title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
浙江鄉試錄序
維
皇嗣極十有三載秋迺浙江鄉試
簡膺守臣聘發維揚渡江而
南巡按御史張子立迓于館
遂會教授何元述教諭易時
中陳全毛豸曾嘉慶吳煥章
===
李梓芳馬呈瑞訓導李彬率
入簾御史曰浙之文其敝乎
敢厪執事簡聞而懼甚試之
明日得卷閱之如御史言迺
曰學術弗正心術罔以端宜
御史有憂也夫今弗圖蔑有
紀矣雖然二三子濬焉爾矣
punctuated:
浙江鄉試錄序

維皇嗣極十有三載秋，迺浙江鄉試。簡膺守臣聘，發維揚，渡江而南。巡按御史張子立迓于館，遂會教授何元述、教諭易時中、陳全、毛豸、曾嘉慶、吳煥章、李梓芳、馬呈瑞、訓導李彬，率入簾。御史曰：「浙之文，其敝乎！敢厪執事。」簡聞而懼甚。試之明日，得卷閱之，如御史言。迺曰：「學術弗正，心術罔以端，宜御史有憂也。夫今弗圖，蔑有紀矣。雖然，二三子濬焉爾矣。」
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Zhejiang Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the thirteenth year since the Emperor ascended the throne, the Zhejiang Provincial Examination was held. I, Jian, accepted an invitation from the provincial authorities, set out from Weiyang, and crossed the Yangzi southward. The Regional Inspector, Zhang Zili, welcomed me at the guesthouse. I then joined the Prefectural School Instructor, He Yuanshu; the County School Instructors, Yi Shizhong, Chen Quan, Mao Zhi, Zeng Jiaqing, Wu Huanzhang, Li Zifang, and Ma Chengrui; and the Assistant Instructor, Li Bin. We all entered the examiners’ enclosure.

The Regional Inspector said, “Has not the writing of Zhejiang fallen into decline? I venture to trouble you with this responsibility.” Hearing this, I was deeply apprehensive. On the day after the examination, I received the scripts and read them: they were just as the Regional Inspector had said. I then said, “When learning is not correct, there is no means of rectifying the workings of the heart. It is fitting that the Regional Inspector should be concerned. If we do not address this now, there will be no standards left. Even so, it rests with you gentlemen to deepen your efforts.”

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
夫文者言之飾也而道之昌
也善言者不勦說以附同不
襲名以亂道獵言匪基誠偽
浮矣詭言無章授受駁矣紕
言異製規度哆矣文之渙也
故稱敝焉是附同而亂道者
也昔者先王之建國也彰六
===
藝以丕文敦三德以崇化習
察而言範物軌而行臧是故
擴聚攄蓄釐澆歸雅摛精掞
華弘其言也而非標也鮮不
程矣今
天子明聖慎德考言垂休彝作人
有司者將之以其
punctuated:
夫文者，言之飾也，而道之昌也。善言者，不勦說以附同，不襲名以亂道。獵言匪基，誠偽浮矣；詭言無章，授受駁矣；紕言異製，規度哆矣。文之渙也，故稱敝焉，是附同而亂道者也。
昔者先王之建國也，彰六藝以丕文，敦三德以崇化。習察而言範，物軌而行臧。是故擴聚攄蓄，釐澆歸雅，摛精掞華，弘其言也，而非標也，鮮不程矣。
今天子明聖，慎德考言，垂休彝，作人。有司者將之以其
translation_en:
Literary composition adorns speech and makes the Way flourish. Those skilled in expression do not plagiarize sayings to echo others, nor appropriate names to confound the Way. When expressions are hunted out without a foundation, sincerity and falsity become unmoored; when words are specious and lack order, what is taught and received becomes confused; when language is erroneous and departs from established forms, rules and measures become lax. This is the disintegration of literary composition, and thus it is called a decline: it consists in echoing others and confounding the Way.
In former times, when the ancient kings established their states, they made the Six Arts manifest to enlarge cultural accomplishment and cultivated the Three Virtues to elevate moral transformation. Through practice and discernment, speech became exemplary; with things properly regulated, conduct became good. Thus they expanded what they had gathered and expressed what they had stored within, corrected superficiality and returned to refinement, and unfolded the essence and displayed the splendor of their learning. They enlarged their expression without mere ostentation, and seldom failed to meet the standards.
Now the Son of Heaven, enlightened and sagely, attends carefully to virtue and examines words, bequeaths excellent enduring norms, and nurtures men of talent. The responsible officials carry this forward by means of its…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
制也未嘗不再三焉維兹全浙
自古在昔文獻足徴其孰以
爲虞而廼敝也不亦甚乎矧
宣治采風匪言奚以故君子
修之於其言也寔昭明德吾
聞之也有德者必有言言之
而罔德斯之謂蹊焉于何其
===
賴文矣將焉用之簡也無良
罔敢攸知罔敢攸受也雖然
二三子淆焉爾矣或有賦鶴
鳴之首章者廼憮然曰命簡
哉兹殫力覈精奭諸弗式諧
以庶言得九十人敷如理如
有孚粲如其吳越之良乎嗚
punctuated:
制也，未嘗不再三焉。維兹全浙，自古在昔，文獻足徴，其孰以爲虞？而廼敝也，不亦甚乎？矧宣治采風，匪言奚以？故君子修之於其言也，寔昭明德。吾聞之也：「有德者必有言。」言之而罔德，斯之謂蹊焉，于何其賴？文矣，將焉用之？簡也無良，罔敢攸知，罔敢攸受也。
雖然，二三子淆焉爾矣。或有賦《鶴鳴》之首章者，廼憮然曰：「命簡哉！」兹殫力覈精，奭諸弗式，諧以庶言，得九十人，敷如、理如、有孚、粲如，其吳越之良乎！嗚
translation_en:
…the prescribed regulations, never failing to give the matter repeated attention. Throughout Zhejiang, from ancient times onward, literary traditions and worthy men have provided ample testimony: who would have thought there was cause for concern? Yet things have deteriorated—is this not grave indeed? Moreover, in proclaiming good government and gathering evidence of local customs, what can one use if not words? Thus, when the gentleman cultivates his speech, he truly makes his luminous virtue manifest. I have heard it said: “Those who possess virtue are sure to have something to say.” To speak without virtue is what is called taking a bypath [?]; what reliance can be placed upon it? It may be polished writing, but what use will it serve? I, Jian [?], lack worthiness and dare neither claim discernment nor presume to accept it.
Even so, it is only a few among you who have become confused. Someone recited the first stanza of “The Crane Cries” (He ming), whereupon I said, with troubled feeling: “This is a charge to me, Jian!” Here we exhausted our strength in scrutinizing the finest distinctions, clearing away what did not conform to the standards [?] and assessing the various writings together. We obtained ninety men: expansive and orderly, sincere and brilliant—surely these are the worthy men of Wu and Yue! Ah…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
呼爾多士固
社稷之隸也毋多爾文其將自
謀也則令名是圖令圖天所
賛也簡寔麗焉而資之以永
也然有爽言之懼矣廼以告
于御史御史曰古之遺訓也
垂之而稽其符也肅而彦約
===
===
而逖胥而不淪是役也御史
子立寔監臨焉維提調則左
布政使党以平左參政洪珠
維監試則按察使路迎副使
陳儒就試之士二千七百有
竒提學僉事徐階簡也維時
理鹺監察御史盧瓚貞勵士
punctuated:
呼！爾多士固社稷之隸也，毋多爾文。其將自謀也，則令名是圖。令圖，天所賛也，簡寔麗焉，而資之以永也。然有爽言之懼矣，廼以告于御史。御史曰：「古之遺訓也，垂之而稽其符也。肅而彦，約而逖，胥而不淪。」
是役也，御史子立寔監臨焉。維提調，則左布政使党以平、左參政洪珠；維監試，則按察使路迎、副使陳儒。就試之士二千七百有竒，提學僉事徐階簡也。維時，理鹺監察御史盧瓚貞勵士
translation_en:
… Ah! You scholars are indeed servants of the state. Do not pride yourselves on your literary accomplishments. If you would plan for your own future, seek an honorable name. An honorable purpose is what Heaven assists; selection truly rests upon this and provides the means to make it enduring [?]. Yet, fearing that these words might prove untrue, I conveyed them to the censor. The censor said: “These are teachings handed down from antiquity. Set them down and examine whether they are fulfilled. Be dignified and accomplished, restrained yet far-reaching, and together avoid falling into decline [?].”
For this examination, Censor Zili served as Supervising Official. The Proctors were Dang Yiping, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Hong Zhu, Left Administration Vice Commissioner. The examination monitors were Lu Ying, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, and Chen Ru, Surveillance Vice Commissioner. More than 2,700 scholars presented themselves for the examination; they had been selected by Xu Jie, Education Intendant and Surveillance Assistant Commissioner. At this time, Lu Zan, the Investigating Censor administering the salt gabelle, steadfastly encouraged the scholars’ …

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
風克敦丕績工部主事程嘉
行南京戶部主事王文儒慶
觀厥成允叶嘉樂右布政使
張原明右叅政萬廷彩郭日
休副使王卿戴金魏綸左叅
議范韶吳山右叅議姜儀僉
事陸冕朱子和莊用賓焦煜
===
方紀達及期原明遷代之者
任忠咸後先賛襄罔或弗共
都指揮僉事李節李光榮署
都指揮僉事張大本湯慶胥
閑衞惟虔法得備書告成事
將歌鹿鳴以好之也併梓廼
文以

translation_en: …the ethos of the scholars, thereby bringing this great undertaking to fruition. Cheng Jiaxing, a Bureau Secretary in the Ministry of Works, and Wang Wenru, a Bureau Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue, joyfully witnessed its completion, fittingly sharing in the celebration. Zhang Yuanming, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner; Wan Tingcai and Guo Rixiu, Right Administration Vice Commissioners; Wang Qing, Dai Jin, and Wei Lun, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; Fan Shao and Wu Shan, Left Administration Assistant Commissioners; Jiang Yi, Right Administration Assistant Commissioner; and Lu Mian, Zhu Zihe, Zhuang Yongbin, Jiao Yu, and Fang Jida, Assistant Surveillance Commissioners, all lent their assistance in succession, none failing to discharge his duties. By the appointed time, Yuanming had been transferred, and Ren Zhong had succeeded him and likewise assisted. Li Jie and Li Guangrong, Assistant Regional Military Commissioners, and Zhang Daben and Tang Qing, acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners, all diligently attended to guarding the examination precincts. Established procedure permits them all to be recorded here [?]. Now that the undertaking is declared complete, we shall sing “The Deer Call” to express our goodwill toward the successful candidates, and shall also have their writings printed from woodblocks in order to …

translation_en:
Zhejiang Provincial Examination, the Thirteenth Year of Jiajing (1534)

Supervising Official
Zhang Zili, Regional Inspector of Zhejiang and Investigating Censor, had the courtesy name Yuanli and was from Huang County, Shandong. He became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the bingxu year.

Proctors
Dang Yiping, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Zhejiang, had the courtesy name Shouheng and was from Junzhou, Henan. He became a metropolitan graduate in the jiaxu year.
Hong Zhu, Left Administration Vice Commissioner of Zhejiang, had the courtesy name Yufang and was from Putian County, Fujian. He became a metropolitan graduate in the xinsi year.

Examination Monitors
Lu Ying, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Zhejiang, had the courtesy name Binyang and was from Wenshang County, Shandong. He became a metropolitan graduate in the wuchen year.
Chen Ru, Surveillance Vice Commissioner of Zhejiang, had the courtesy name Ruzong and was registered in an officer household of the Embroidered-uniform Guard. He became a metropolitan graduate in the guiwei year.

Examiners
Gao Jian, Professor of the Confucian School of Yangzhou Prefecture in the directly administered metropolitan region, had the courtesy name Gongjing and was from Mianzhou, Sichuan. He became a metropolitan graduate in the year transcribed as sichou [?].
He Yuanshu, Professor of the Confucian School of Huizhou Prefecture, Guangdong, had the courtesy name Yuanxiao and was from Jinjiang County, Fujian. He became a metropolitan graduate in the renchen year.

Associate Examiners
Yi Shizhong, Instructor of the Confucian School of Dongliu County, Chizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, had the courtesy name Jiahui. He was registered with Quanzhou Guard, Fujian, and was a native of Nancheng County, Jiangxi; he became a tribute student (gongshi) in the renwu year.
Chen Quan, Instructor of the Confucian School of Xiangfu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, had the courtesy name Renfu and was from Macheng County, Huguang. He became a tribute student in the yiyou year.
Mao Zhi, Instructor of the Confucian School of Tang County, Nanyang Prefecture, Henan, had the courtesy name Wenxian and was from Jingzhou Right Guard, Huguang. He became a tribute student in the bingzi year.
Zeng Jiaqing, Instructor of the Confucian School of Luotian County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, had the courtesy name Ruheng and was from Taihe County, Jiangxi. He became a tribute student in the renwu year.
Wu Huanzhang, Instructor of the Confucian School of Yancheng County, Huai’an Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, had the courtesy name Qinhua and was from Putian County, Fujian. He became a tribute student in the wuzi year.

兩浙都轉運鹽使司運使楊表〔汝志，福建龍溪縣人，甲戌進士〕。嚴州府知府盛應陽〔斯顯，直隸吳縣人，癸未進士〕。寧波府知府鄭威〔伯震，福建閩縣人，丙戌進士〕。台州府知府許繼〔士來，福建閩縣人，癸未進士〕。

受卷官：
杭州府同知李中孚〔伯虛，湖廣江陵縣人，己丑進士〕。温州府推官劉訓〔于伊，河南汝陽縣人，壬辰進士〕。湖州府德清縣知縣謝九儀〔君賜，山東章丘縣人，壬辰進士〕。紹興府上虞縣知縣張光祖〔德徵，河南潁川衛人，壬辰進士〕。嘉興府秀水縣知縣林應亮〔熙載，福建候官縣人，壬辰進士〕。嘉興府崇德縣知縣張守約〔彥博，湖廣華容縣人，丙戌進士〕。
translation_en:
Luan Guifang, Instructor of the Confucian School of Guangshan County, Guang Prefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan, had the courtesy name Zhengfang. Registered in Huarong County, Huguang, he was a native of Anren County, Jiangxi, and a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the wuzi year.

Ma Chengrui, Instructor of the Confucian School of Qingyun County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, had the courtesy name Qianhe. He was a native of Putian County, Fujian, and a tribute scholar of the renwu year.

Li Bin, Assistant Instructor of the Confucian School of Changyuan County, Kai Prefecture, Daming Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, had the courtesy name Xihui. He held official registration in Guizhou Front Guard, was a native of Nanfeng County, Jiangxi, and was a tribute scholar of the bingzi year.

Officials Responsible for Printing Examination Papers

Duan Ying, Registrar in the Registry of the Zhejiang Provincial Administration Commission, had the courtesy name Shijie. He was a native of Langzhong County, Sichuan, and an Imperial University student.

Zhang Jiayi, Registrar in the Registry of the Zhejiang Provincial Surveillance Commission, had the courtesy name Yuankai. He was a native of Heyin County, Henan, and an Imperial University student.

Officials Responsible for Collecting and Keeping Examination Scripts

Yang Biao, Salt Transport Commissioner of the Liangzhe Salt Distribution Commission, had the courtesy name Ruzhi. He was a native of Longxi County, Fujian, and a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the jiaxu year.

Sheng Yingyang, Prefect of Yanzhou Prefecture, had the courtesy name Sixian. He was a native of Wu County in the directly administered metropolitan region and a metropolitan graduate of the guiwei year.

Zheng Wei, Prefect of Ningbo Prefecture, had the courtesy name Bozhen. He was a native of Min County, Fujian, and a metropolitan graduate of the bingxu year.

Xu Ji, Prefect of Taizhou Prefecture, had the courtesy name Shilai. He was a native of Min County, Fujian, and a metropolitan graduate of the guiwei year.

Officials Responsible for Receiving Examination Scripts

Li Zhongfu, Vice Prefect of Hangzhou Prefecture, had the courtesy name Boxu. He was a native of Jiangling County, Huguang, and a metropolitan graduate of the jichou year.

Liu Xun, Prefectural Judge of Wenzhou Prefecture, had the courtesy name Yuyi. He was a native of Ruyang County, Henan, and a metropolitan graduate of the renchen year.

Xie Jiuyi, Magistrate of Deqing County, Huzhou Prefecture, had the courtesy name Junci. He was a native of Zhangqiu County, Shandong, and a metropolitan graduate of the renchen year.

Zhang Guangzu, Magistrate of Shangyu County, Shaoxing Prefecture, had the courtesy name Dezheng. He was from Yingchuan Guard, Henan, and was a metropolitan graduate of the renchen year.

Lin Yingliang, Magistrate of Xiushui County, Jiaxing Prefecture, had the courtesy name Xizai. He was a native of Houguan County, Fujian (written 候官 [?]), and a metropolitan graduate of the renchen year.

Zhang Shouyue, Magistrate of Chongde County, Jiaxing Prefecture, had the courtesy name Yanbo. He was a native of Huarong County, Huguang, and a metropolitan graduate of the bingxu year.

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰賢哉回也一簞食一瓢飲在陋巷人
不堪其憂回也不改其樂賢哉回也
溥博如天淵泉如淵見而民莫不敬言而
民莫不信行而民莫不說
是集義所生者非義襲而取之也
易
休復之吉以下仁也
===
九五有孚惠心勿問元吉有孚惠我德
與天地相似故不違知周乎萬物而道濟
天下故不過旁行而不流樂天知命故
不憂安土敦乎仁故能愛
夫乾天下之至健也德行恒易以知險夫
坤天下之至順也德行恒簡以知阻
書
帝乃誕敷文德舞干羽于兩階七旬有苗
格
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

子曰：「賢哉，回也！一簞食，一瓢飲，在陋巷，人不堪其憂，回也不改其樂。賢哉，回也！」

溥博如天，淵泉如淵，見而民莫不敬，言而民莫不信，行而民莫不說。

是集義所生者，非義襲而取之也。

易

休復之吉，以下仁也。

九五：有孚惠心，勿問，元吉。有孚惠我德。

與天地相似，故不違；知周乎萬物，而道濟天下，故不過；旁行而不流，樂天知命，故不憂；安土敦乎仁，故能愛。

夫乾，天下之至健也，德行恒易以知險；夫坤，天下之至順也，德行恒簡以知阻。

書

帝乃誕敷文德，舞干羽于兩階，七旬，有苗格。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The Master said: “How worthy Hui is! With a single basket of food and a single gourd of water, living in a mean lane, others could not endure such distress, yet Hui does not let it diminish his joy. How worthy Hui is!”

Vast and all-embracing like Heaven, deep and inexhaustible like an abyss: when he appears, none among the people fail to respect him; when he speaks, none fail to trust him; when he acts, none fail to delight in him.

This [vital force, qi] is produced by the accumulation of righteous deeds; it cannot be acquired through an isolated act of righteousness.

Book of Changes (Yijing)

The good fortune of a gracious return comes from placing oneself below the benevolent.

Nine in the fifth place: There is sincerity and a benevolent heart. Without need to inquire, there is supreme good fortune. There is sincerity in recognizing my virtue with gratitude.

He accords with Heaven and Earth and therefore does not run counter to them. His understanding encompasses the myriad things, and his Way benefits all under Heaven; therefore he does not err. He ranges widely without drifting astray. He delights in Heaven and understands his allotted destiny; therefore he has no anxiety. He is content where he dwells and steadfast in benevolence; therefore he can love.

Qian is the utmost strength under Heaven. Its virtuous activity is ever easy, and thereby it knows danger. Kun is the utmost compliance under Heaven. Its virtuous activity is ever simple, and thereby it knows obstruction.

Book of Documents (Shujing)

The emperor then spread his civil virtue far and wide and had dancers perform with shields and feathers between the two stairways. After seventy days, the Youmiao submitted.

In demeanor, reverence; in speech, compliance; in sight, clarity; in hearing, acuity; in thought, wisdom.

Boyi promulgated the statutes and regulated the people through punishments; Yu brought the waters and land into order and took charge of the renowned mountains and rivers; Ji taught sowing and planting, cultivating fine grain. The Lord on High said to King Wen: “Do not waver and stray; do not covet and envy. Be the first to ascend the heights.”

Long ago, in ancient times, our forebears established their precepts: be gentle and reverent morning and evening, and discharge your duties with respect.

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
理天下之男教立六宫以聽天下之内
治以明章婦順此明王之定制也我
朝稽古立法率以道治天下其所以教之者
不惟其身教之懿而言教亦至純備自
今觀之其統治于外以示教者有
祖訓有教民榜有孝順事實爲善陰隲有五倫
書諸書迨我
皇上敬一有箴五箴有註陽教備矣不知與古
帝王之書果有合歟其輔治于内以示
===
順者有
高皇后傳有
仁孝文皇后内訓二十章迨我
章聖皇太后又製爲女訓十二章婦順章矣不
知與古后妃之訓亦相倣歟夫陽教不
修陽事不得適見於天日爲之食陰教
不修陰事不得適見於天月爲之食今
自
宫闈以達天下修齊治平之化亦旣協于一
punctuated: 理天下之男教，立六宫以聽天下之内治，以明章婦順。此明王之定制也。我朝稽古立法，率以道治天下。其所以教之者，不惟其身教之懿，而言教亦至純備。自今觀之，其統治于外以示教者，有祖訓，有教民榜，有孝順事實、爲善陰隲，有五倫書諸書。迨我皇上，敬一有箴，五箴有註，陽教備矣。不知與古帝王之書果有合歟？其輔治于内以示順者，有高皇后傳，有仁孝文皇后内訓二十章。迨我章聖皇太后，又製爲女訓十二章，婦順章矣。不知與古后妃之訓亦相倣歟？夫陽教不修，陽事不得，適見於天，日爲之食；陰教不修，陰事不得，適見於天，月爲之食。今自宫闈以達天下，修齊治平之化亦旣協于一
translation_en:
…to regulate the instruction of men throughout the realm; he establishes the six palaces to attend to the realm’s internal governance and to make manifest women’s obedience. This is the settled institution of enlightened kings. Our dynasty has examined antiquity in establishing its laws and has consistently governed the realm through the Way. Its means of instruction comprise not only the excellence of teaching by personal example: its verbal teachings, too, are supremely pure and comprehensive. Looking at these today, among the works that provide instruction through governance of the outer realm are the Ancestral Injunctions, the Placard for Instructing the People, True Accounts of Filial Obedience, Doing Good and Hidden Merit, and the Book of the Five Human Relationships. Coming down to our present Emperor, there is his Admonition on Reverent Single-mindedness and his commentary on the Five Admonitions: instruction in the yang sphere is complete. We ask whether these indeed accord with the writings of the emperors and kings of antiquity.

As for the works that assist governance within and teach obedience, there are the Biography of Empress Gao and the twenty chapters of the Inner Instructions of Empress Renxiao Wen. Coming down to our Empress Dowager Zhangsheng, she has further composed twelve chapters of Instructions for Women, making women’s obedience manifest. We ask whether these likewise follow the teachings of the empresses and consorts of antiquity.

When instruction in the yang sphere is neglected and affairs of that sphere are improperly conducted, a sign of censure appears in Heaven [?], and the sun is eclipsed on that account. When instruction in the yin sphere is neglected and affairs of that sphere are improperly conducted, a sign of censure appears in Heaven [?], and the moon is eclipsed on that account. Now, from the palace’s inner quarters throughout the realm, the transforming influence of cultivating oneself, ordering the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to the realm has already been brought into unity…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
矣而日月之食猶復見之豈天心仁愛
已至而益求其至歟抑數之適然而無
關於政事之修否歟夫由之而不知者
凡民也爾諸士通古今之故達天人之
蘊請明言之以為
今日治化之助
問選舉考課法之相因者也周禮大司徒
以鄉三物教萬民而賓興之因民之常
而施十有二教其考察而書之者又有
===
鄉大夫黨正之屬有司諫掌糾萬民之
德而勸之夫其所以為教者素矣至於
嚴諸考課廼復有六計有八法太宰於
歲終詔百官廢置之三歲則大計羣吏
之治而誅賞之豈所進者或非賢歟抑
養之未至而賢者或變於初歟然較諸
唐虞法為已密而稱盛治者恒歸諸堯
舜何也隋唐以降取士恒以詞章用士
恒以資格方諸成周之教若有異矣而
punctuated:
矣，而日月之食猶復見之，豈天心仁愛已至而益求其至歟？抑數之適然而無關於政事之修否歟？夫由之而不知者，凡民也。爾諸士通古今之故，達天人之蘊，請明言之，以為今日治化之助。
問：選舉、考課，法之相因者也。《周禮》大司徒以鄉三物教萬民而賓興之，因民之常而施十有二教。其考察而書之者，又有鄉大夫、黨正之屬，有司諫掌糾萬民之德而勸之。夫其所以為教者素矣。至於嚴諸考課，廼復有六計，有八法。太宰於歲終詔百官廢置之，三歲則大計羣吏之治而誅賞之。豈所進者或非賢歟？抑養之未至而賢者或變於初歟？然較諸唐虞，法為已密，而稱盛治者恒歸諸堯舜，何也？隋唐以降，取士恒以詞章，用士恒以資格，方諸成周之教若有異矣，而
translation_en:
…yet eclipses of the sun and moon still occur. Is it that Heaven’s benevolent care, already at its utmost, seeks still greater perfection? Or do these events simply arise from numerical cycles, without connection to whether government is well ordered? Ordinary people follow the way without understanding it. You scholars understand the circumstances of past and present and grasp the profound relations between Heaven and humanity. Please explain these matters clearly, to assist the governance and moral transformation of the present day.
Question: The selection and recommendation of men and the assessment of officials’ performance are mutually dependent institutions. In the Rites of Zhou, the Minister of Education teaches all the people through the three subjects of district instruction and advances the worthy, honoring them as guests. In accordance with the enduring norms of human life, he applies twelve teachings. Among those who examine the people and record their findings are the District Grand Masters and Neighborhood Heads; the Remonstrance Officers are charged with correcting the moral conduct of all the people and encouraging them. Thus, the means of educating them are established well in advance. When it comes to rigorous assessment of officials, there are also the six criteria and the eight regulations. At the end of each year, the Grand Steward advises on the dismissal or retention of the officials; every third year, he comprehensively assesses their administration and punishes or rewards them. Could some of those advanced have been unworthy? Or was their cultivation incomplete, so that worthy men sometimes departed from their original character? Yet although these institutions were already more elaborate than those of Tang and Yu, praise for flourishing government invariably goes to Yao and Shun. Why is this? From the Sui and Tang onward, men have generally been recruited on the basis of literary composition and employed according to formal qualifications and seniority. Compared with the instruction of the Zhou at its height, this seems different, yet…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
亦未嘗乏士者何居豈其所得者非古
之才乎或謂漢舉孝廉茂才庶幾近之
不知其所以教之者何如也方今

子寓射御之學而宴享之會亦具左右
司馬則兵固儒者事也方今天下承平
日久將不知兵兵不知戰武書廢而不

之左氏喜言陣法其載一時卒乘偏兩
之制前茅慮無之警不知果可用於戰

公告武王十勝九敗之詳其說在于六
punctuated:
亦未嘗乏士者，何居？豈其所得者非古之才乎？或謂漢舉孝廉茂才，庶幾近之，不知其所以教之者何如也。方今聖明在上，立賢無方，駸駸乎復古之治矣。翕受敷施，不知有足以副當宁之求者乎？不然，則先王選舉之義、考課之方，其在今日固不可不之講矣。願悉究之，以觀所蘊。
問：天有五財，民並用之，何能去兵？古者君子寓射御之學，而宴享之會亦具左右司馬，則兵固儒者事也。方今天下承平日久，將不知兵，兵不知戰，武書廢而不講，識者憂焉。試舉一二，相與諸士折衷之。左氏喜言陣法，其載一時卒乘偏兩之制、前茅慮無之警，不知果可用於戰歟？觀其不欲廢車，而乃未始及騎，則毁車崇卒、以騎易車，其法亦何所始歟？太公告武王十勝九敗之詳，其說在于六
translation_en:
…yet they never lacked men of talent. Why was this? Surely the men they obtained were not unlike the talented men of antiquity? Some say that the Han recommendation of the Filial and Incorrupt and of Outstanding Talent came close to the ancient practice; but how did they educate these men? Now our sage and enlightened sovereign reigns above, appointing worthy men without restriction and advancing swiftly toward a restoration of ancient governance. With talent broadly welcomed and employed, are there men adequate to meet the sovereign’s demands? If not, then the principles by which the former kings selected men for office and their methods of evaluating performance certainly must be studied today. Examine these matters fully, so that we may see the learning you possess.
Question: Heaven provides the five resources, and the people use them all; how can arms be dispensed with? In antiquity, gentlemen included archery and charioteering in their studies, and even at ceremonial banquets there were Directors of Military Affairs of the Left and Right. Military matters are thus certainly the concern of Confucian scholars. Now the realm has long enjoyed peace: generals do not understand military affairs, soldiers do not know how to fight, and military writings have been neglected and are no longer studied. Those with discernment are troubled by this. Let us raise one or two matters for critical consideration together with you candidates. Master Zuo delights in discussing battle formations. His account records the contemporary organization of infantry and chariots into pian and liang units, and precautions involving forward scouts and vigilance against unforeseen dangers [?]. Could these actually be employed in battle? We observe that he was unwilling to abandon chariots, yet never discussed cavalry. Where, then, did the practices of discarding chariots in favor of infantry and replacing chariots with cavalry originate? The Grand Duke explained to King Wu in detail the ten conditions for victory and the nine for defeat. His account is found in the Six…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
韜武王之時猶用騎戰顧其法絕不見
于春秋至於車戰亦絕不見於後世則
車騎卒伍之戰不知可偏廢歟或曰六
韜非周書戰國知兵之士祖其餘論而
推廣之設爲問答以極兵家之變今觀
其書智畧竒詭雜然横出有鰓鰓然憂
天下諸侯合而軋巳之意則以爲戰國
之書者夫亦有所據歟諸葛武侯好韜
畧岳飛好左氏皆足以摧敵制勝其法
===
異而功同者何歟今之用兵者將祖六
韜三畧而用之歟抑亦取之左氏歟頃
者雲中之變上厪
當宁之慮至屯兵易將始克底平則講武一事
寔惟急務願詳言之將以轉聞于
上
問三代之治名與實相副而享國長久萬
世之所宜法焉者也然其文章制度各
有因革而不甚相沿固其時然爾其亦
punctuated:
韜。武王之時猶用騎戰，顧其法絕不見于春秋，至於車戰，亦絕不見於後世，則車騎卒伍之戰，不知可偏廢歟？或曰：「六韜非周書，戰國知兵之士祖其餘論而推廣之，設爲問答，以極兵家之變。」今觀其書，智畧竒詭，雜然横出，有鰓鰓然憂天下諸侯合而軋巳之意，則以爲戰國之書者，夫亦有所據歟？諸葛武侯好韜畧，岳飛好左氏，皆足以摧敵制勝，其法異而功同者何歟？今之用兵者，將祖六韜三畧而用之歟？抑亦取之左氏歟？頃者雲中之變，上厪當宁之慮，至屯兵易將，始克底平。則講武一事，寔惟急務。願詳言之，將以轉聞于上。
問：三代之治，名與實相副，而享國長久，萬世之所宜法焉者也。然其文章制度，各有因革，而不甚相沿，固其時然爾，其亦
translation_en:
…Tactics. In King Wu’s time, mounted troops were already used in battle, yet this method is entirely absent from the Spring and Autumn Annals; chariot warfare, in turn, is entirely absent from later ages. Can any one of these forms of warfare—with chariots, cavalry, or infantry—be dispensed with? Some say: “The Six Secret Tactics is not a Zhou text. Men versed in warfare during the Warring States period took its surviving teachings as their foundation and expanded upon them, casting them as questions and answers to explore the full range of military adaptations.” Looking at the book now, its ingenious and extraordinary stratagems emerge in profusion, and it conveys an anxious fear that the lords of the realm might unite to crush oneself. Does the claim that it is a Warring States text therefore have some basis? Zhuge Liang, Marquis of Wu, favored the military teachings of the Tactics and Strategies, while Yue Fei favored the Zuo Commentary. Both were able to crush their enemies and secure victory. Why did different methods produce the same success? Should those who employ troops today take the Six Secret Tactics and the Three Strategies as their foundation and apply them, or should they draw upon the Zuo Commentary? Recently, the disturbance at Yunzhong troubled His Majesty; only after troops were stationed there and commanders replaced was peace finally restored. The study of military affairs is thus an urgent task indeed. Please discuss this in detail, so that your views may be transmitted to His Majesty.
Question: Under the government of the Three Dynasties, names and realities corresponded, and their rule endured for a long time. They are models that all subsequent ages ought to follow. Yet their cultural forms and institutions each involved both continuity and change, and they did not closely follow one another. This was certainly due to the circumstances of their respective times; might they also…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
有同焉而可言者乎董仲舒謂三代有
改制之異而無變道之實者其果然乎
由秦而後雖治亂興衰不一其變而英
君碩輔亦代有人卒不聞有致三代之
隆建萬世之長策者何也豈三代制作
不可行於後世矣乎然亦有復井田六
官者矣曾靡裨於治則三代之制果終
不可行歟抑别有其故歟唐太宗號稱
英主考其治庶幾於古而於三代之制
===
未竟其施焉豈所謂善治焉者惟直究
其實而不必於其名歟抑惟循名責實
者而后可以爲善之至也其舉至當之
論以復固將以考材焉
問古有言曰識時務者在俊傑諸士平日
固以俊傑自期也試以時務一二商確
可乎浙爲東南首藩海育地産財賦充
饒食宜無不足也夫何倉廩日虚一遇
水旱之虞爲之牧者輒議勸借勸之誠
punctuated:
有同焉而可言者乎？董仲舒謂三代有改制之異，而無變道之實者，其果然乎？由秦而後，雖治亂興衰不一其變，而英君碩輔亦代有人，卒不聞有致三代之隆、建萬世之長策者，何也？豈三代制作不可行於後世矣乎？然亦有復井田、六官者矣，曾靡裨於治，則三代之制果終不可行歟？抑别有其故歟？唐太宗號稱英主，考其治，庶幾於古，而於三代之制，未竟其施焉。豈所謂善治焉者，惟直究其實，而不必於其名歟？抑惟循名責實者，而后可以爲善之至也？其舉至當之論以復，固將以考材焉。

問：古有言曰：「識時務者在俊傑。」諸士平日固以俊傑自期也，試以時務一二商確，可乎？浙爲東南首藩，海育地産，財賦充饒，食宜無不足也。夫何倉廩日虚，一遇水旱之虞，爲之牧者輒議勸借？勸之誠
translation_en:
…are there also common features that can be discussed? Dong Zhongshu maintained that the Three Dynasties differed in their changes to institutions, but did not in substance alter the Way. Is this indeed so? Since the Qin, although order and disorder, rise and decline have varied in countless ways, outstanding rulers and eminent ministers have appeared in every age. Yet we hear of none who ultimately attained the flourishing rule of the Three Dynasties or established enduring plans for ten thousand generations. Why is this? Could the institutions established by the Three Dynasties be impracticable in later ages? Yet there have also been those who restored the well-field system and the Six Ministries, without bringing any benefit to government. Does this mean that the institutions of the Three Dynasties ultimately cannot be put into practice, or is there some other reason? Emperor Taizong of the Tang is renowned as an outstanding ruler. Examining his government, we find that it approached that of antiquity, yet he did not fully implement the institutions of the Three Dynasties. Could it be that those called good rulers simply pursue the substance, without insisting upon the names? Or can the highest excellence be attained only by holding actual performance accountable to the names? Respond with the most fitting arguments: your abilities will be assessed thereby.

Question: An ancient saying states, “Those who understand the affairs of the times are outstanding men.” You gentlemen have surely always aspired to be such men. May we therefore examine and discuss one or two contemporary matters? Zhejiang is the foremost province of the southeast. With the bounty of its seas and the produce of its land, its wealth and tax revenues are abundant; food ought never to be insufficient. Why, then, do its granaries grow emptier by the day, and why, whenever floods or drought threaten, do those who govern it immediately propose soliciting loans? Such solicitation is indeed…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
是也不知督稅之吏徵輸于官者何在
枕山臂江果悍自負兵宜無不競也夫
何軍伍日耗一遇潢池之警當其事者
輒稱招募招之誠是也不知清戎之官
操練于衞者何為鹽徒海寇備禦終年
然詰捕之擾徒增萑澤之患如故不知
何以弭之山鄉水區勤動終歲然稱貸
之苦徒聞川陸之利未獲不知何以處
之議者多歸咎於歲凶或又以為長吏
===
不得其人茲欲寓兵於農使緩急得有
所賴藏富於民使水旱不能為災如之
何其可也諸士留心世故久矣請著于
篇以觀用世之學
punctuated: 是也，不知督稅之吏徵輸于官者何在？枕山臂江，果悍自負，兵宜無不競也。夫何軍伍日耗，一遇潢池之警，當其事者輒稱招募？招之誠是也，不知清戎之官操練于衞者何為？鹽徒海寇，備禦終年，然詰捕之擾徒增，萑澤之患如故，不知何以弭之？山鄉水區，勤動終歲，然稱貸之苦徒聞，川陸之利未獲，不知何以處之？議者多歸咎於歲凶，或又以為長吏不得其人。茲欲寓兵於農，使緩急得有所賴；藏富於民，使水旱不能為災，如之何其可也？諸士留心世故久矣，請著于篇，以觀用世之學。
translation_en: …is indeed right. Yet where are the revenues that the officials supervising taxation collect and remit to the government? With mountains at its back and rivers at its sides, and with people who pride themselves on their courage and fierceness, the province should surely have strong troops. Why, then, are the ranks depleted day by day, so that whenever an alarm of local rebellion arises, those responsible immediately speak of recruiting men? Recruitment is indeed right, but what are the officials responsible for putting military affairs in order doing about drilling troops in the guards? Defense against salt smugglers and maritime raiders continues throughout the year, yet the harassment caused by investigations and arrests only increases, while the scourge of brigandage remains as before. How can it be quelled? In mountain villages and waterside districts, people labor diligently throughout the year, yet we hear only of the hardships of borrowing, while the benefits of waterways and land remain unrealized. How should this be addressed? Those who discuss these matters mostly blame poor harvests; others hold that the senior local officials are not the right men for their posts. If we now wish to embed the soldiery among the farming population, so that there is something to rely upon in ordinary times and emergencies alike, and to store wealth among the people, so that floods and droughts cannot bring disaster, how can this be accomplished? You gentlemen have long attended to worldly affairs. Please set forth your views in writing, so that we may assess your learning for practical service.

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰賢哉回也一簞食一瓢飲在陋巷人
不堪其憂回也不改其樂賢哉回也
彭輅
同考試官訓導李批淡而不厭蓋慕顏子之
樂者
同考試官教諭吳批顏子非以貧爲樂也蓋
忘貧而樂自得者也此作能盡之故錄
===
考試官教授何批冲澹有味
考試官教授高批清雅
聖人稱大賢必即其安貧者而深賛之焉夫處
貧而不改其樂顏子所以爲賢也固宜夫子賛
之而深致意也如此且君子不隕穫於貧賤不
充詘於富貴顏氏子其殆庶幾乎故夫子曰賢
哉回也蓋自其處貧者而觀之其食也一簞焉
爾矣無餘物也其飲也一瓢焉爾矣無餘味也
方且陋巷爰居而終窶且貧困亦甚矣夫人亦
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

子曰：「賢哉，回也！一簞食，一瓢飲，在陋巷，人不堪其憂，回也不改其樂。賢哉，回也！」

彭輅

同考試官訓導李批：「淡而不厭，蓋慕顏子之樂者。」

同考試官教諭吳批：「顏子非以貧爲樂也，蓋忘貧而樂自得者也。此作能盡之，故錄。」

考試官教授何批：「冲澹有味。」

考試官教授高批：「清雅。」

聖人稱大賢，必即其安貧者而深賛之焉。夫處貧而不改其樂，顏子所以爲賢也。固宜夫子賛之而深致意也如此。且君子不隕穫於貧賤，不充詘於富貴，顏氏子其殆庶幾乎？故夫子曰：「賢哉，回也！」蓋自其處貧者而觀之，其食也，一簞焉爾矣，無餘物也；其飲也，一瓢焉爾矣，無餘味也。方且陋巷爰居，而終窶且貧，困亦甚矣。夫人亦
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The Master said: “How worthy Hui is! With a single basket of food and a single gourd of drink, living in a mean lane—others could not bear such distress, yet Hui did not let it alter his joy. How worthy Hui is!”

Peng Lu

Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor, comments: “Unadorned, yet never tiresome: surely the work of someone who admires Master Yan’s joy.”

Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: “Master Yan did not take poverty itself as a joy. Rather, he forgot his poverty and found joy within himself. This composition fully conveys this, and so it has been selected.”

Examiner He, Instructor, comments: “Serene and understated, yet full of savor.”

Examiner Gao, Instructor, comments: “Pure and elegant.”

When the sage commends a man of great worth, he invariably takes that man’s contentment in poverty as grounds for profound praise. To live in poverty without allowing it to alter his joy was what made Master Yan worthy. It was certainly fitting that the Master should praise him and express such deep feeling. Moreover, the gentleman is neither dismayed by poverty and low station nor puffed up or constrained by wealth and high rank. Did not Master Yan come close to this ideal? Thus the Master said: “How worthy Hui is!” Consider how he lived in poverty: his food was merely a single basketful, with nothing besides; his drink was merely a single gourdful, with no other flavor. Moreover, he dwelt in a mean lane and remained destitute and poor: his hardship was indeed extreme. As for others, too, …

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
孰堪其憂也回也素位而行與簞瓢而順適自
養之貞而莫之有求也素履之往與陋巷而相
忘於土皆安而無所於懷也曷嘗以貧窶累其
心而改其所樂哉蓋回之心誠有見于其大者
是故無喪無得而富貴貧賤處之一也然則回
也其賢矣哉吁再言賢哉回也則夫子所以嘆
美之者意獨至矣考諸易曰困而不失其所亨
其唯君子乎蓋古之聖人無欲故其視天下之
故如寒暑晝夜相代乎前吾豈有二其心哉昔
===
茂叔亦謂顏子見大心泰而歸諸亞聖嗟乎樂
天知命故不憂夫子之謂也不遠復無祗悔固
顏子之庶幾焉者乎學者要當尋孔顏樂處
溥博如天淵泉如淵見而民莫不敬言而
民莫不信行而民莫不說
張志淑
同考試官敎諭陳批言聖德之發見本於充
積之盛親切有味末復歸誠之一言意亦獨至有
本者如是是之取爾
punctuated:
孰堪其憂也？回也素位而行，與簞瓢而順適，自養之貞而莫之有求也；素履之往，與陋巷而相忘，於土皆安而無所於懷也。曷嘗以貧窶累其心而改其所樂哉？蓋回之心誠有見于其大者，是故無喪無得，而富貴貧賤處之一也。然則回也其賢矣哉！吁！再言「賢哉回也」，則夫子所以嘆美之者，意獨至矣。考諸《易》曰：「困而不失其所亨，其唯君子乎！」蓋古之聖人無欲，故其視天下之故，如寒暑晝夜相代乎前，吾豈有二其心哉？昔茂叔亦謂顏子見大心泰，而歸諸亞聖。嗟乎！「樂天知命，故不憂」，夫子之謂也；「不遠復，無祗悔」，固顏子之庶幾焉者乎！學者要當尋孔顏樂處。
溥博如天，淵泉如淵，見而民莫不敬，言而民莫不信，行而民莫不說。
張志淑
同考試官敎諭陳批：言聖德之發見，本於充積之盛，親切有味。末復歸誠之一言，意亦獨至。有本者如是，是之取爾。
translation_en:
…who could endure such distress? Hui acted in accordance with his station, content with his basket of food and gourd of drink; he cultivated his own steadfast rectitude and sought nothing else. He proceeded according to his accustomed conduct, forgetting himself amid his humble alley, at ease wherever he dwelt [?], with nothing weighing upon his mind. When did he ever let poverty burden his heart and alter that in which he delighted? Hui’s heart truly perceived what was great. Thus neither loss nor gain affected him, and he met wealth and honor, poverty and low station alike. Was Hui not indeed worthy? Ah! In repeating “How worthy Hui is!” the Master expressed the utmost depth of his admiration. Consulting the Book of Changes, we find: “In hardship, yet not losing the means of fulfillment—is this not the noble man alone?” The sages of antiquity were free from desire. Thus they regarded the affairs of the world as cold and heat, day and night, succeeding one another before them: how could their hearts become divided? Formerly, Maoshu likewise said that Master Yan perceived what was great and his heart was at peace, and ranked him as second to the Sage. Ah! “Delighting in Heaven and knowing one’s allotted fate, one is therefore without anxiety”: this describes the Master. “Returning before going far, without coming to remorse”: surely this is what Master Yan approached! Students must seek out that in which Confucius and Yan Hui delighted.
“Vast and broad as Heaven, deep as a wellspring, like an abyss: when he appears, none among the people fails to revere him; when he speaks, none fails to trust him; when he acts, none fails to rejoice.”
Zhang Zhishu
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: The essay says that the manifestation of sagely virtue is rooted in the fullness of its accumulation within. Its treatment is apt and rich in meaning. At the end it returns to the single word ‘sincerity,’ an idea also pursued to its fullest depth. Such is writing that has a foundation; for this reason it was selected.

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授何批是有見者
考試官教授高批溫裕
中庸於至聖之德必申賛其體用之全焉蓋充
積極其盛而發見當其可德之體用所以爲全
也非天下至聖其孰能與於此中庸三十一章
言至聖之德以明天道及此復申言之謂夫言
天下之至德者存乎聖言天下之至感者存乎
時其積中發外之盛何如哉蓋自其溥博言之
萬物皆備而充周不可窮天德純全而廣大不
===
可禦擬諸形容固即天之爲天而蕩蕩難名者
矣自其淵泉言之寂然不動有以通天下之故
渾然在中有以立天下之本擬諸形容固即淵
之爲淵而淵淵莫測者矣充積之極其盛也蓋
如此由是時而見也則爲德容恭已之施固天
下之所觀而化者而莫有不敬者焉時而言也
則爲德言巽命之申固天下之所訓而行者而
莫有不信者焉又時而行也則爲德行而聲敎
所訖有以丕冒乎天下媚茲一人亦自有不能
punctuated:
考試官教授何批：是有見者。
考試官教授高批：溫裕。
中庸於至聖之德，必申賛其體用之全焉。蓋充積極其盛，而發見當其可，德之體用所以爲全也。非天下至聖，其孰能與於此？中庸三十一章言至聖之德，以明天道。及此復申言之，謂夫言天下之至德者存乎聖，言天下之至感者存乎時，其積中發外之盛何如哉！蓋自其溥博言之，萬物皆備，而充周不可窮；天德純全，而廣大不可禦。擬諸形容，固即天之爲天而蕩蕩難名者矣。自其淵泉言之，寂然不動，有以通天下之故；渾然在中，有以立天下之本。擬諸形容，固即淵之爲淵而淵淵莫測者矣。充積之極其盛也，蓋如此。由是時而見也，則爲德容，恭已之施，固天下之所觀而化者，而莫有不敬者焉。時而言也，則爲德言，巽命之申，固天下之所訓而行者，而莫有不信者焉。又時而行也，則爲德行，而聲敎所訖，有以丕冒乎天下，媚茲一人，亦自有不能
translation_en:
Examiner He, an Instructor, comments: “This shows insight.”
Examiner Gao, an Instructor, comments: “Gentle and ample.”
In discussing the virtue of the utmost sage, the Doctrine of the Mean necessarily further praises its completeness in both substance and function. For inward accumulation reaches its fullest abundance, while outward manifestation accords with what is fitting: this is what makes virtue complete in substance and function. Who but the utmost sage under Heaven could attain this? Chapter thirty-one of the Doctrine of the Mean speaks of the virtue of the utmost sage to illuminate the Way of Heaven. Here it elaborates further: the highest virtue under Heaven resides in sagehood, and the most profound power to move others resides in timeliness. How abundant must be what accumulates within and manifests without!
Consider his breadth and expansiveness: all things are fully present within him, and his all-pervading fullness is inexhaustible; Heaven’s virtue is pure and complete within him, and its vastness cannot be restrained. Seeking an image to describe this, it is precisely what makes Heaven Heaven—so vast that it is difficult to name. Consider his depth, like a deep spring: still and unmoving, he can comprehend the workings of all under Heaven; wholly integrated within, he can establish the foundation of all under Heaven. Seeking an image to describe this, it is precisely what makes an abyss an abyss—so profoundly deep that it cannot be fathomed. Such is the utmost abundance of his inward accumulation.
Thus, when he appears at the proper time, his appearance embodies virtue. His bearing of personal reverence [?] is indeed what all under Heaven behold and are transformed by, and none fail to revere him. When he speaks at the proper time, his words embody virtue. His promulgation of gently persuasive commands is indeed what all under Heaven receive as instruction and put into practice, and none fail to trust him. Again, when he acts at the proper time, his actions embody virtue; wherever his proclamations and teaching reach, they abundantly extend their shelter over all under Heaven. Loving this one man, they naturally cannot…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
已於悅焉發見之當其可也又如此固皆積盛
致然爾非聖人而能若是乎吁此聖人之所以
為天道也雖然聖人亦何以得此也哉維天之
命於穆不已於乎不顯文王之德之純聖人之
德一誠而已矣然則學者欲造於聖人亦求之
戒懼慎獨去不誠以復於誠而已矣誠復而體
立焉用行焉蘊之為德行發之為事業是固一
以貫之者也故曰誠者天之道也誠之者人之
道也
===
是集義所生者非義襲而取之也
張元
同考試官教諭毛批沉渾而不浮圓融而不
滯子固集義而有得者因其文可想見其人
同考試官教諭易批講是集義所生處甚是
纔一著力便不是矣且文亦昌大惇厚非襲取者
所能及
考試官教授何批是善養其氣者
考試官教授高批讀之充如
punctuated:
已於悅焉。發見之當其可也，又如此。固皆積盛致然爾，非聖人而能若是乎？吁！此聖人之所以為天道也。雖然，聖人亦何以得此也哉？「維天之命，於穆不已！」「於乎不顯，文王之德之純！」聖人之德，一誠而已矣。然則學者欲造於聖人，亦求之戒懼慎獨，去不誠以復於誠而已矣。誠復而體立焉，用行焉；蘊之為德行，發之為事業，是固一以貫之者也。故曰：「誠者，天之道也；誠之者，人之道也。」

是集義所生者，非義襲而取之也。
張元

同考試官教諭毛批：「沉渾而不浮，圓融而不滯。子固集義而有得者，因其文可想見其人。」
同考試官教諭易批：「講『是集義所生』處甚是，纔一著力便不是矣。且文亦昌大惇厚，非襲取者所能及。」
考試官教授何批：「是善養其氣者。」
考試官教授高批：「讀之充如。」
translation_en:
… refrain from delighting in him. Such, too, are his manifestations, each appearing at its proper moment. All this results from the abundance accumulated within him. Could anyone but a sage achieve this? Ah! This is why the sage embodies the Way of Heaven. Yet how does the sage attain this? “Heaven’s mandate—how profound and unceasing!” “Ah, how illustrious is the purity of King Wen’s virtue!” The sage’s virtue is nothing more than sincerity alone. Thus, if learners wish to attain sagehood, they need only seek it through vigilance and apprehension and through watchfulness over themselves when alone, removing insincerity so as to return to sincerity. Once sincerity is restored, its substance is established and its functioning proceeds. Stored within, it constitutes virtuous conduct; expressed outwardly, it constitutes achievements. These are indeed pervaded by a single principle. Hence it is said: “Sincerity is the Way of Heaven; making oneself sincere is the human way.”

“It is produced by the accumulation of righteousness; it cannot be seized through an isolated act of righteousness.”
By Zhang Yuan 張元.

Comment by Associate Examiner Mao, Instructor: “Deep and substantial without being superficial; rounded and harmonious without being obstructed. You are surely someone who has accumulated righteousness and attained something thereby. Through your writing one can envision the person you are.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Yi, Instructor: “The explanation of ‘it is produced by the accumulation of righteousness’ is entirely correct: the slightest forced effort would make it wrong. Moreover, the writing is expansive and generous, earnest and substantial—beyond the reach of anyone seeking to seize it through an isolated act.”

Comment by Examiner He, Professor: “Here is someone who knows well how to nourish his vital force.”

Comment by Examiner Gao, Professor: “Reading it, one feels a fullness of vital force.”

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
大賢指言氣之所由充所以示養氣之始事也
夫氣生於集義而不可以襲取然則養氣者其
可不於義焉求之哉此孟子所以爲公孫丑告
也其意若曰理之與氣每相須而成其功效亦
相因而見是故配義與道人知夫氣之充耳而
其養之之始何如哉蓋由事之行也義以爲質
達諸萬變而皆協善之動也持以有常聚焉百
順而無斁則內而反於身也常直而事爲有本
外而形於氣也常充而操之有要盛大流行之
===
勢殆將日新月盛塞天地而配道義此其本矣
乃若於義積習之未深謂可以偶合而盡推行
之不豫謂可以襲取而充則徇外者遺內將何
以爲體驗擴充之地正助者心忘亦何以收直
養無害之功至大至剛之氣吾見隨得隨失塞
天地而配道義無是理也氣其可以義襲而取
哉是則義也者集也而非襲也故氣也者生也
而非取也功效之得失如此養氣者亦維善事
其心而已抑於是而知集義養氣體用一原之
punctuated: 大賢指言氣之所由充，所以示養氣之始事也。夫氣生於集義，而不可以襲取，然則養氣者，其可不於義焉求之哉？此孟子所以爲公孫丑告也。其意若曰：理之與氣，每相須而成，其功效亦相因而見。是故配義與道，人知夫氣之充耳，而其養之之始何如哉？蓋由事之行也，義以爲質；達諸萬變而皆協，善之動也，持以有常；聚焉百順而無斁，則內而反於身也常直，而事爲有本；外而形於氣也常充，而操之有要。盛大流行之勢，殆將日新月盛，塞天地而配道義，此其本矣。乃若於義積習之未深，謂可以偶合而盡；推行之不豫，謂可以襲取而充，則徇外者遺內，將何以爲體驗擴充之地？正助者心忘，亦何以收直養無害之功？至大至剛之氣，吾見隨得隨失，塞天地而配道義，無是理也。氣其可以義襲而取哉？是則義也者，集也而非襲也；故氣也者，生也而非取也。功效之得失如此，養氣者亦維善事其心而已。抑於是而知集義養氣，體用一原之
translation_en:
The great worthy points out how vital force (qi) becomes full, thereby showing the first task in nourishing it. Vital force arises from accumulating righteousness; it cannot be seized through an isolated righteous act. How, then, could those who nourish their vital force fail to seek it in righteousness? This is why Mengzi instructed Gongsun Chou as he did. His meaning was something like this: principle and vital force always depend upon one another for their fulfillment, and their efficacy likewise becomes manifest through their mutual operation. Thus, when vital force accompanies righteousness and the Way, people recognize only its fullness. But how does its nourishment begin?

In carrying out affairs, one takes righteousness as their substance. In extending one's conduct through myriad changes, one ensures that all accords with what is right; in putting goodness into action, one maintains constancy. When one accumulates a hundred instances of accordance without wearying, inwardly, in reflecting upon oneself, one is always upright, and one's actions have a foundation; outwardly, in what manifests as vital force, one is always full, and one's means of sustaining it has an essential guiding principle. Its mighty, flowing momentum will then grow fresh each day and flourish each month, filling Heaven and Earth and accompanying the Way and righteousness. This is its foundation.

But suppose one's accumulated practice of righteousness is not yet deep, and one claims that an occasional accord with it suffices to fulfill it; or one's efforts to put it into practice have not been made beforehand, and one claims that vital force can be filled by seizing it through an isolated act. Those who pursue what is external then neglect what is internal: what basis will they have for personally realizing and extending it? Those who anticipate results or force growth, whose minds forget [?]—how can they achieve the effect of nourishing it with uprightness and doing it no harm? I see that their supremely great and supremely firm vital force will be lost as soon as it is gained. That it should fill Heaven and Earth and accompany the Way and righteousness is impossible. Can vital force really be seized through an isolated act of righteousness?

Righteousness, then, must be accumulated, not suddenly appropriated; accordingly, vital force is generated, not seized. Such are success and failure in achieving the desired effect. Those who nourish their vital force need only tend their minds well. Moreover, from this we understand that accumulating righteousness and nourishing vital force exemplify substance and function sharing a single source …

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
理也自反而縮體用合矣孟子之不動心其原
蓋在於此告子以義爲外故亦外心與氣而不
求其於體用舉無所屬則亦冥然悍然而已爾
此孟子告子不動心之異也學之者深求其原
固盡心知性知天之學矣其何異端得而亂之
易
九五有孚惠心勿問元吉有孚惠我德
陳善
同考試官教諭毛批寫出王者得民氣象可
以爲文矣
同考試官教諭易批易義潔淨精微此作得
之
考試官教授何批彖傳中正有慶是如此
考試官教授高批典實
聖人於益之九五而著以交孚之義也蓋孚而
曰交則一德之相感者深矣上下以此爲益吉
又何待於問邪周公繫辭之意有如此且夫人
君有相之道求無媿也已生民有欲之道求無
punctuated:
理也。自反而縮，體用合矣。孟子之不動心，其原蓋在於此。告子以義爲外，故亦外心與氣，而不求其於體用，舉無所屬，則亦冥然悍然而已爾。此孟子、告子不動心之異也。學之者深求其原，固盡心知性知天之學矣，其何異端得而亂之？

易
九五，有孚惠心，勿問，元吉；有孚惠我德。
陳善

同考試官教諭毛批：寫出王者得民氣象，可以爲文矣。
同考試官教諭易批：易義潔淨精微，此作得之。
考試官教授何批：彖傳中正有慶，是如此。
考試官教授高批：典實。

聖人於益之九五而著以交孚之義也。蓋孚而曰交，則一德之相感者深矣。上下以此爲益，吉又何待於問邪？周公繫辭之意有如此。且夫人君有相之道，求無媿也已；生民有欲之道，求無
translation_en:
…the principle that substance and function have a single source. When one examines oneself and finds oneself upright, substance and function are united. Here, surely, lies the source of Mengzi’s unperturbed mind. Gaozi regarded righteousness as external; hence he also treated the mind and vital energy as external, without seeking their relation to substance and function. With neither grounded in anything, he was merely uncomprehending and obstinate. This is the difference between the unperturbed minds of Mengzi and Gaozi. If students inquire deeply into their source, theirs will indeed be the learning that fully develops the mind, knows human nature, and knows Heaven. How could heterodox teachings disrupt it?

Book of Changes
Nine in the fifth place: “With sincerity and a benevolent heart, there is no need to inquire: supreme good fortune. With sincerity, they cherish my virtue.”
By Chen Shan.

Associate Examiner Mao, Instructor, comments: “It portrays the bearing of a true king winning the people’s allegiance. This qualifies as accomplished writing.”
Associate Examiner Yi, Instructor, comments: “The meaning of the Changes is pure, refined, and subtle. This composition captures it.”
Examiner He, Professor, comments: “This is what the Commentary on the Judgments means by ‘central and correct, there is cause for rejoicing.’”
Examiner Gao, Professor, comments: “Grounded in the classics and substantial.”

In the nine in the fifth place of Increase, the sage sets forth the meaning of mutual sincerity. When sincerity is described as mutual, the reciprocal response arising from a shared virtue is profound. When those above and below take this as their means of bringing increase, what need is there to inquire about good fortune? Such was the Duke of Zhou’s intention in appending these words. Now, the ruler has a way of assisting the people: he seeks only to be free of shame. The people have a way of desiring: they seek that there should be no …

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
拂也已是故以益之九五言之陽剛中正以居
尊位矣而又當益下之時是其所以爲益也視
民如傷心旣純於天德矣即以其心而推之務
使下究之澤眞足以怙冒乎羣生而不徒襲之
以仁聲也愛民如子心旣純於王道矣即以其
心而擴之務俾大賚之恩眞足以覃敷乎庶物
而不徒隆之以仁聞也上之惠下如此則信以
發志有不疾而速之機孚乃化邦有無遠弗届
之妙其爲大善固不待於占筮也吾見遺以樂
===
也民樂之而不忍忘蓋翊戴之爲元后殆有中
心悅而不假於其貌者矣導以利也民利之而
不忍負蓋親愛之如父母殆有內志誠而非華
於其面者矣是固所謂大善也而亦奚俟於問
邪爻義如此占在其中矣抑考之書曰民非后
罔克胥匡以生后非民罔以辟四方又曰爾惟
風下民惟草則知一體之義其相須也甚殷而
其相感也甚速否則志乖而道睽矣乖與睽聖
人不由也故曰王者之民皞皞如也霸者之民
punctuated: 拂也已。是故以益之九五言之，陽剛中正以居尊位矣，而又當益下之時，是其所以爲益也。視民如傷，心旣純於天德矣，即以其心而推之，務使下究之澤眞足以怙冒乎羣生，而不徒襲之以仁聲也。愛民如子，心旣純於王道矣，即以其心而擴之，務俾大賚之恩眞足以覃敷乎庶物，而不徒隆之以仁聞也。上之惠下如此，則信以發志，有不疾而速之機；孚乃化邦，有無遠弗届之妙。其爲大善，固不待於占筮也。吾見遺以樂也，民樂之而不忍忘，蓋翊戴之爲元后，殆有中心悅而不假於其貌者矣。導以利也，民利之而不忍負，蓋親愛之如父母，殆有內志誠而非華於其面者矣。是固所謂大善也，而亦奚俟於問邪？爻義如此，占在其中矣。抑考之《書》曰：「民非后，罔克胥匡以生；后非民，罔以辟四方。」又曰：「爾惟風，下民惟草。」則知一體之義，其相須也甚殷，而其相感也甚速。否則志乖而道睽矣。乖與睽，聖人不由也。故曰：「王者之民皞皞如也，霸者之民
translation_en:
…thwarting them, and that is all. Thus, to speak of the nine in the fifth place of Increase: with the strength of yang, centrality, and correctness, he occupies the exalted position, and moreover encounters a time for benefiting those below. This is how he brings increase. He regards the people as though they were wounded: his heart already accords wholly with Heaven’s virtue. He extends this heart, striving to ensure that the beneficence reaching those below truly suffices to shelter all living people, rather than merely covering them with proclamations of benevolence. He loves the people as his children: his heart already accords wholly with the kingly Way. He enlarges this heart, striving to ensure that the grace of his generous gifts truly spreads to all things, rather than merely magnifying his reputation for benevolence.

When the ruler benefits those below in this manner, his trustworthiness gives expression to his intentions, possessing the capacity to act swiftly without haste; his sincerity transforms the realm, possessing the wondrous efficacy of reaching even the most distant places. That this constitutes great goodness certainly does not await divination by stalks. I see that when he bestows joy upon the people, they rejoice in it and cannot bear to forget him. Supporting and honoring him as their sovereign, they surely feel delight in their hearts without putting on an outward show. When he guides them toward benefit, they benefit from it and cannot bear to betray him. Loving him as their parents, they surely possess inward sincerity, rather than a merely pleasing expression on their faces. This indeed is what is called great goodness; why should it await inquiry through divination? Such is the meaning of the line, and its divinatory judgment is contained within it.

Furthermore, examining the Book of Documents, we find: “Without a sovereign, the people cannot help one another to live; without the people, the sovereign has no means to rule the four quarters.” It also says: “You are the wind; the people below are the grass.” Thus we know that, according to the principle that ruler and people form one body, their mutual dependence is exceedingly profound, and their influence upon one another exceedingly swift. Otherwise, their intentions diverge and their ways become estranged. Divergence and estrangement are paths the sage does not follow. Hence it is said: “The people under a true king are spacious and at ease; the people under a hegemon…”

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
驩虞如也公私之辯讀易者詳之
與天地相似故不違知周乎萬物而道濟
天下故不過旁行而不流樂天知命故
不憂安土敦乎仁故能愛
愼蒙
同考試官敎諭毛批知周以下說聖人智仁
與天地合德良是
同考試官敎諭易批聖人盡性事發得明潔
錄之
===
考試官敎授何批得旨
考試官敎授高批沖澹
大傳言聖人盡性之事以見其用易也蓋知仁
合德而與天地參易之能事備矣聖人以之而
盡性焉謂非善於用易者邪大傳之意蓋如此
且天地設位而易行乎其中矣聖人盡性于易
者也而崇效天焉卑法地焉則固與之克肖矣
而亦奚有于違邪何者天陽化也其道曰知地
陰變也其道曰仁聖人知仁合德者也故有以
punctuated:
驩虞如也。公私之辯，讀易者詳之。

與天地相似，故不違；知周乎萬物，而道濟天下，故不過；旁行而不流，樂天知命，故不憂；安土敦乎仁，故能愛。

愼蒙

同考試官敎諭毛批：知周以下，說聖人智仁與天地合德，良是。

同考試官敎諭易批：聖人盡性事，發得明潔，錄之。

考試官敎授何批：得旨。

考試官敎授高批：沖澹。

大傳言聖人盡性之事，以見其用易也。蓋知仁合德，而與天地參，易之能事備矣。聖人以之而盡性焉，謂非善於用易者邪？大傳之意，蓋如此。且天地設位，而易行乎其中矣。聖人盡性于易者也，而崇效天焉，卑法地焉，則固與之克肖矣，而亦奚有于違邪？何者？天陽化也，其道曰知；地陰變也，其道曰仁。聖人知仁合德者也，故有以
translation_en:
…are joyful and content. Those who read the Book of Changes should examine closely this distinction between public-mindedness and private interest.

“He resembles Heaven and Earth and therefore does not act contrary to them. His wisdom encompasses the myriad things, and his Way brings aid to all under Heaven; therefore he does not go beyond what is fitting. He acts in every direction without going astray. He delights in Heaven and understands destiny; therefore he is free from anxiety. He is at peace where he dwells and steadfast in benevolence; therefore he is able to love.”

Shen Meng 愼蒙

Comment by Associate Examiner Mao, Instructor: “From ‘His wisdom encompasses’ onward, the explanation that the sage’s wisdom and benevolence accord in virtue with Heaven and Earth is indeed correct.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Yi, Instructor: “The sage’s fulfillment of his nature is expounded clearly and cleanly. Include this answer.”

Comment by Examiner He, Professor: “Captures the purport.”

Comment by Examiner Gao, Professor: “Serene and restrained.”

The Great Commentary speaks of the sage’s fulfillment of his nature to show how he puts the Changes into practice. When wisdom and benevolence unite in virtue, and one stands alongside Heaven and Earth as a third, the capacities of the Changes are fully realized. The sage fulfills his nature through it: can one say that he is not adept at putting the Changes into practice? Such, broadly, is the meaning of the Great Commentary.

Now Heaven and Earth take their appointed positions, and change operates between them. The sage fulfills his nature through the Changes. In loftiness he emulates Heaven; in lowliness he models himself on Earth. Thus he truly resembles them: how could he act contrary to them? Why is this so? Heaven transforms through yang, and its Way is called wisdom; Earth changes through yin, and its Way is called benevolence. The sage unites wisdom and benevolence in virtue, and therefore has the means to…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
見天下之賾而知無不周尤必大其道以濟之
則明而且當有以協于中矣夫何過焉亦有以
見天下之動而權無不達尤必正其經以守之
則貞而不諒有以偕於時矣夫何流焉及其至
而言之理所自出者曰天命則禀于天之數也
惟其樂天知命則心無累于物而見不惑于私
故能無憂而知益深矣身所素居者曰土仁則
根于心之德也惟其安土敦仁則志不願乎外
而欲不留于內故能愛而仁益篤矣夫知仁如
===
天地矣又推之以達經權極之而妙神化則性
于是盡殆如子之事親善繼其志善述其事矣
豈不成位乎中而與天地參哉雖然厥彰厥微
匪靈弗瑩在聖人固誠無不明而能用夫易矣
然人不能皆聖也則思誠之功獨可少之哉有
志于學易者亦曰自慎動始
書
帝乃誕敷文德舞干羽于兩階七旬有苗
格
punctuated:
見天下之賾，而知無不周，尤必大其道以濟之，則明而且當，有以協于中矣，夫何過焉？亦有以見天下之動，而權無不達，尤必正其經以守之，則貞而不諒，有以偕於時矣，夫何流焉？及其至而言之，理所自出者曰天命，則禀于天之數也。惟其樂天知命，則心無累于物，而見不惑于私，故能無憂，而知益深矣。身所素居者曰土仁，則根于心之德也。惟其安土敦仁，則志不願乎外，而欲不留于內，故能愛，而仁益篤矣。夫知仁如天地矣，又推之以達經權，極之而妙神化，則性于是盡，殆如子之事親，善繼其志，善述其事矣。豈不成位乎中，而與天地參哉？雖然，厥彰厥微，匪靈弗瑩。在聖人，固誠無不明，而能用夫易矣。然人不能皆聖也，則思誠之功獨可少之哉？有志于學易者，亦曰自慎動始。

書

帝乃誕敷文德，舞干羽于兩階，七旬有苗格。
translation_en:
…to perceive the intricacies of all under Heaven, so that their wisdom encompasses everything. Above all, they must broaden their Way to bring this to fulfillment; then, discerning and fitting in their judgments, they can accord with the mean. How could they go too far? They can also perceive the movements of all under Heaven, so that their discretionary judgment reaches every circumstance. Above all, they must hold fast to properly established constant principles; then, steadfast without being rigidly bound to their word, they can act in keeping with the times. How could they drift astray?

To speak of its utmost realization: that from which principle issues is called Heaven’s mandate—the allotted order received from Heaven. Precisely because they delight in Heaven and understand its mandate, their minds are unburdened by things, and their perceptions are not confused by selfishness. Thus they can be free from anxiety, and their wisdom grows ever deeper. That in which one ordinarily dwells is called “land and benevolence” [?], rooted in the virtue of the heart. Precisely because they are content where they dwell and steadfast in benevolence, their aspirations do not seek anything outside, and desires do not linger within. Thus they can love, and their benevolence grows ever more profound.

Their wisdom and benevolence thus resemble Heaven and Earth. They extend these further to comprehend constant principles and discretionary judgment, carrying them to the utmost so as to attain the subtle workings of spiritual transformation. In this way they fully realize their nature. It is much like children serving their parents, skillfully carrying forward their intentions and continuing their undertakings. Do they not thereby establish their place between Heaven and Earth and form a triad with them?

Nevertheless, whether manifest or subtle, these matters cannot be illuminated without spiritual discernment. In the sage, sincerity indeed leaves nothing unilluminated, enabling him to employ the Changes. Yet not everyone can be a sage: can the effort to attain sincerity possibly be dispensed with? Those who aspire to study the Changes must likewise begin by taking care in their actions.

Book of Documents

The emperor then spread his civil virtue far and wide, and had dancers perform with shields and feathers between the two stairways. After seventy days, the Youmiao came to submit.

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
孫汝賢
同考試官教諭李批宣武功而徵諸文德帝
王柔遠之道也此作足以發之槩見其盛
同考試官教諭曾批苗人格化聖人動物之
誠也揭以繹之有見矣為之擊節
考試官教授何批能悉聖人來遠之化
考試官教授高批整肅
史臣紀聖世内治修而遠人服以見其盛也甚
矣威武之未可以服人也帝舜之修文德而有
===
苗格也有以夫昔禹之征有苗也因益之賛而
班師矣帝之當是時也夫何為哉是故四方風
動九功惟叙文教之成於天下者久矣玆乃誕
而布之凡五教之敷與好生之洽者方惟日不
足而無逺弗届矣夫何有于止極邪帝之敷是
德也抑何見哉是故武舞以干文舞以羽文物
之昭於朝廷者素矣玆乃發而揚之或舞之阼
階或舞之賔階者惟進退有度而泰和可象矣
夫何如其雍容邪是惟盡其在我帝之心初不
punctuated:
孫汝賢

同考試官教諭李批：「宣武功而徵諸文德，帝王柔遠之道也。此作足以發之，槩見其盛。」

同考試官教諭曾批：「苗人格化，聖人動物之誠也。揭以繹之，有見矣，為之擊節。」

考試官教授何批：「能悉聖人來遠之化。」

考試官教授高批：「整肅。」

史臣紀聖世内治修而遠人服，以見其盛也。甚矣，威武之未可以服人也！帝舜之修文德而有苗格也，有以夫！昔禹之征有苗也，因益之賛而班師矣。帝之當是時也，夫何為哉？是故四方風動，九功惟叙，文教之成於天下者久矣。玆乃誕而布之，凡五教之敷與好生之洽者，方惟日不足，而無逺弗届矣。夫何有于止極邪？帝之敷是德也，抑何見哉？是故武舞以干，文舞以羽，文物之昭於朝廷者素矣。玆乃發而揚之，或舞之阼階，或舞之賔階者，惟進退有度，而泰和可象矣。夫何如其雍容邪？是惟盡其在我，帝之心初不
translation_en:
Sun Ruxian

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “To set forth military achievements and trace their basis to civil virtue is to explain the way emperors and kings bring distant peoples into willing submission. This composition adequately elucidates it, giving an overall view of its magnificence.”

Associate Examiner Zeng, Instructor, comments: “The Miao people's submission to transformation reveals the sincerity through which the sage moves other beings. The essay brings this out and unfolds its meaning with insight. I applaud it.”

Examiner He, Professor, comments: “It fully explains the sage's transforming influence that draws distant peoples to him.”

Examiner Gao, Professor, comments: “Orderly and dignified.”

The court historian records how, in the age of the sage, internal governance was well ordered and distant peoples submitted, thereby displaying that age's flourishing greatness. How utterly inadequate military might is to secure people's submission! There was indeed a reason why Emperor Shun's cultivation of civil virtue brought the Youmiao into submission. Formerly, when Yu campaigned against the Youmiao, he withdrew his troops following Yi's counsel. What, then, did the emperor do at this time? His influence had already stirred the four quarters like the wind, and the nine achievements were duly ordered: civil instruction had long been established throughout the world. Now he spread it abroad on a grand scale. In disseminating the five teachings and extending his life-loving benevolence, he seemed to find each day too short, and no place was so distant that his influence did not reach it. How could there be any stopping point or limit?

And how was the emperor's dissemination of this virtue made manifest? Shields were used in the martial dance and feathers in the civil dance: the court had long shone with these cultural forms. Now he displayed and exalted them. Some danced at the host's steps and others at the guest's steps; their advances and retreats followed proper measures, making supreme harmony visible. How gracious and composed it all was! This was simply to do fully what lay within his own power; the emperor's heart had never…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
期於苗之格者迨夫逆自班師甫七旬耳蠢茲
有苗漸被干聲教者皆相率而來王于以觀中
國文物之盛焉鼓舞乎德化者皆革心而效順
于以被天地覆載之仁焉由是而懷柔之有加
也由是而分北之可行也是蓋誠能動物苗之
格亦有莫能自已者耳夫文德之敷不在於禹
班師之後而有苗之格適會於舞干羽之時有
虞之盛信千載而一見矣抑征伐之道上世以
德末世以力而舒慘隨之雖以湯武之聖有慙
===
德之論而爰及干戈義士猶不滿焉况其下者
乎史稱三苗有洞庭彭蠡之險若未易圖者而
帝舜竟以文德格之然則威武何用哉後世有
銳志雪耻致海内虚耗窮兵以貽晚年之悔者
惜乎無以此語之
貌曰恭言曰從視曰明聽曰聰思曰睿
來日升
同考試官教諭李批五事各具一德也而一
以貫之者也子能言之有見矣受形受性亦有本
punctuated:
期於苗之格者。迨夫逆自班師，甫七旬耳，蠢茲有苗，漸被干聲教者，皆相率而來王，于以觀中國文物之盛焉；鼓舞乎德化者，皆革心而效順，于以被天地覆載之仁焉。由是而懷柔之有加也，由是而分北之可行也。是蓋誠能動物，苗之格亦有莫能自已者耳。夫文德之敷，不在於禹班師之後，而有苗之格，適會於舞干羽之時。有虞之盛，信千載而一見矣！抑征伐之道，上世以德，末世以力，而舒慘隨之。雖以湯武之聖，有慙德之論，而爰及干戈，義士猶不滿焉，况其下者乎？史稱三苗有洞庭、彭蠡之險，若未易圖者，而帝舜竟以文德格之，然則威武何用哉？後世有銳志雪耻，致海内虚耗，窮兵以貽晚年之悔者，惜乎無以此語之！
貌曰恭，言曰從，視曰明，聽曰聰，思曰睿。
來日升
同考試官教諭李批：「五事各具一德也，而一以貫之者也。子能言之，有見矣。受形受性，亦有本
translation_en:
…expect the Miao to submit. When barely seventy days had passed since the army’s return [?], those among the unruly Miao who were gradually reached by the civilizing instruction all led one another to acknowledge the sovereign, thereby witnessing the flourishing cultural institutions of the Central Kingdom. Those inspired by his transforming virtue all changed their hearts and offered allegiance, thereby receiving the benevolence that shelters and sustains all things like Heaven and Earth. Thus his gracious measures to win them over could be increased, and their division and banishment could be carried out. This was surely because sincerity can move others: the Miao, too, could not help but submit. The spreading of civil virtue did not begin only after Yu withdrew the army; rather, the submission of the Miao happened to coincide with the performance of the dance with shields and feathers. The splendor of Shun’s reign was truly something seen but once in a thousand years!
Now, in the way of punitive warfare, the earliest ages relied on virtue, and later ages on force; leniency and harshness followed accordingly. Even with the sageliness of Tang and Wu, there was talk of virtue tinged with shame; when it came to taking up arms, righteous men still felt dissatisfied. How much more so with rulers beneath them! The histories say that the Sanmiao possessed the natural defenses of Dongting and Pengli, so that they seemed difficult to subdue. Yet Emperor Shun ultimately brought them to submission through civil virtue. What use, then, was military might? In later ages there were rulers who, intent on avenging humiliation, depleted the realm and exhausted their armies, leaving themselves regrets in old age. What a pity that no one conveyed these words to them!
“Demeanor is to be reverent; speech, compliant; sight, clear; hearing, acute; thought, discerning.”
Lai Risheng
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: “Each of the five activities possesses its own virtue, yet a single principle runs through them all. You have been able to articulate this and have shown insight. Your discussion of receiving bodily form and receiving one’s nature also has a basis…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之說也
同考試官敎諭曾批讀此作四體不言而喻
矣心服
考試官敎授何批敷暢
考試官敎授高批是嘗有誠身之功者
君子叙五事而各著其德誠身之義昭矣蓋天
生蒸民有物必有則也君子隨在而能敬以從
事焉身有不誠者乎箕子演五事之疇以告武
王意蓋如此且夫天以五行生人也與之以形
===
而理即賦焉人以五事爲德也能踐其形而身
斯誠矣何以言之人之始生而形色具是則所
謂貌也貌之澤者水之爲也而其德則恭焉莊
敬之節不忒於臨下之儀祗恪之容罔愆於人
望之度是有此貌則有此恭矣恭非貌之德乎
人之形色具而聲音發是則所謂言也言之揚
者火之爲也而其德則從焉心聲之發因言以
宣者無鄙倍之氣德音之布託辭以達者無躁
妄之失是有此言則有此從矣從非言之德乎
punctuated:
之說也。
同考試官敎諭曾批：讀此作，四體不言而喻矣，心服。
考試官敎授何批：敷暢。
考試官敎授高批：是嘗有誠身之功者。
君子叙五事而各著其德，誠身之義昭矣。蓋天生蒸民，有物必有則也。君子隨在而能敬以從事焉，身有不誠者乎？箕子演五事之疇以告武王，意蓋如此。且夫天以五行生人也，與之以形，而理即賦焉。人以五事爲德也，能踐其形，而身斯誠矣。何以言之？人之始生而形色具，是則所謂貌也。貌之澤者，水之爲也，而其德則恭焉。莊敬之節，不忒於臨下之儀；祗恪之容，罔愆於人望之度。是有此貌則有此恭矣，恭非貌之德乎？人之形色具而聲音發，是則所謂言也。言之揚者，火之爲也，而其德則從焉。心聲之發，因言以宣者，無鄙倍之氣；德音之布，託辭以達者，無躁妄之失。是有此言則有此從矣，從非言之德乎？
translation_en:
…an explanation of this.
Associate Examiner Zeng, Instructor, comments: Reading this composition, one understands how the four limbs convey meaning without words. I am convinced at heart.
Examiner He, Professor, comments: Expansive and fluent.
Examiner Gao, Professor, comments: This is someone who has indeed worked at making his person sincere.
The gentleman sets forth the five activities and makes manifest the virtue proper to each; thus the meaning of making one's person sincere becomes clear. Heaven brings forth the multitude of people: wherever there is a thing, there must be a norm. If the gentleman can attend reverently to his affairs in every situation, could his person fail to be sincere? Such, surely, was Jizi's meaning when he expounded the category of the five activities to King Wu. Heaven produces human beings through the Five Phases, giving them bodily form and, at the same time, endowing them with principle. Human beings cultivate virtue through the five activities: if they can fulfill what their bodily form entails, their persons become sincere.
How may this be explained? When a human being is first born, bodily form and complexion are complete: this is what is called appearance. The lustre of appearance is the working of water, and its virtue is reverence. The discipline of solemn respect never departs from the deportment appropriate to dealing with those below; a demeanour of reverent attentiveness never falls short of the standards others expect. Thus, where there is this appearance, there is this reverence. Is reverence not the virtue of appearance?
Once bodily form and complexion are complete, the voice issues forth: this is what is called speech. The projection of speech is the working of fire, and its virtue is accordance. When the voice of the heart issues forth and is expressed through speech, it has no air of vulgarity or perversity; when virtuous utterances are disseminated and conveyed through words, they contain no fault of rashness or recklessness. Thus, where there is this speech, there is this accordance. Is accordance not the virtue of speech?

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
能言而後能視矣視所以爲木之散也視而曰
明蓋其貞明不昧之體不爲淺近所蔽以通神
明之德以類萬物之情是故明之所受出其視
焉而天下無遁形矣謂非視之德邪能視而後
能聽矣聽所以爲金之收也聽而曰聰蓋其至
虛能通之神不爲疑似所惑以涵萬象之感以
收萬物之聲是故聰之所受出其聽焉而天下
無遺響矣謂非聽之德邪至於思能通土心之
官也精氣之會也思則清明之體有以見天下
===
之賾如神之知有以達天下之故寂然不動感
而遂通恭從明聰一以貫之而無遺矣思不曰
睿乎是則觀五事則知受形之原天之所以命
諸人也觀五德則知受性之原人之所以合諸
天也君子誠身可不於其敬焉圖之抑理氣之
相承也久矣人惟不思耳是以舉物而遺則言
人而昧天道之大原荒矣大禹因數第疇以人
合天諄諄以敬爲言則學問之極功聖人之能
事不外是也故曰大禹開萬世心學之源
punctuated: 能言而後能視矣。視所以爲木之散也。視而曰明，蓋其貞明不昧之體，不爲淺近所蔽，以通神明之德，以類萬物之情。是故明之所受，出其視焉，而天下無遁形矣。謂非視之德邪？能視而後能聽矣。聽所以爲金之收也。聽而曰聰，蓋其至虛能通之神，不爲疑似所惑，以涵萬象之感，以收萬物之聲。是故聰之所受，出其聽焉，而天下無遺響矣。謂非聽之德邪？至於思，能通土，心之官也，精氣之會也。思則清明之體有以見天下之賾，如神之知有以達天下之故。寂然不動，感而遂通，恭從明聰一以貫之而無遺矣。思不曰睿乎？是則觀五事，則知受形之原，天之所以命諸人也；觀五德，則知受性之原，人之所以合諸天也。君子誠身，可不於其敬焉圖之？抑理氣之相承也久矣，人惟不思耳。是以舉物而遺則，言人而昧天，道之大原荒矣。大禹因數第疇，以人合天，諄諄以敬爲言，則學問之極功、聖人之能事，不外是也。故曰：大禹開萬世心學之源。
translation_en:
Once one can speak, one can see. Sight manifests the dispersive action of Wood. The virtue attributed to sight is clarity: its steadfastly luminous, unobscured substance is not veiled by what is shallow and immediate, and thus penetrates the potency of spiritual illumination and comprehends the dispositions of the myriad things by analogy. Hence what clarity apprehends comes through sight, and nothing under Heaven can conceal its form. Could this not be the virtue of sight? Once one can see, one can hear. Hearing manifests the gathering action of Metal. The virtue attributed to hearing is acuity: its utterly receptive and penetrating spirit is not confused by doubtful appearances, and thus embraces the impressions of the myriad phenomena and gathers the sounds of the myriad things. Hence what acuity apprehends comes through hearing, and no sound under Heaven is missed. Could this not be the virtue of hearing?

As for thought, it communicates with Earth; it is the function of the heart and the convergence of vital essence and qi. Through thought, the heart’s clear and luminous substance can perceive the profundities of all under Heaven, and its spiritlike understanding can penetrate the causes of things under Heaven. Still and unmoving, it responds to stimuli and thereby comprehends. Reverence, compliance, clarity, and acuity are threaded together by a single principle, with nothing left out. Is thought not therefore called sagacity? Thus, by examining the Five Activities, we understand the source from which we receive bodily form—what Heaven bestows upon human beings. By examining the Five Virtues, we understand the source from which we receive our nature—how human beings accord with Heaven. In making himself sincere, can the gentleman fail to pursue this through reverence?

Indeed, principle and qi have long sustained one another; people merely fail to reflect upon them. Thus they discuss things while overlooking their governing norms, and speak of humanity while remaining ignorant of Heaven: the great source of the Way is left neglected. Yu the Great followed the numbers in ordering the categories, bringing humanity into accord with Heaven, and repeatedly urged reverence. The ultimate accomplishment of learning and the full capacity of the sage lie within this. Hence it is said: Yu the Great opened the source of the learning of the heart for all ages.

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
詩
