Every three years he conducted a comprehensive assessment of the officials’ administration and punished or rewarded them. How rigorous were the means by which they were assessed! Precisely because instruction was provided beforehand, people had resources on which to draw in advancing toward goodness; because assessment was rigorous, they had warnings to spur them to greater efforts toward goodness. This was how the Zhou obtained worthy men and achieved good government.
You, honored examiners, say that the methods of selection and performance assessment are mutually dependent. This is correct. Yet, because those who discuss government invariably turn to the ages of Tang Yao and Yu Shun, you harbor doubts about Zhou performance assessment; and, in view of the shortcomings of Sui and Tang recruitment and employment of men, you find merit in the Han nomination of the filially pious and incorrupt and of outstanding talents, as approximating ancient practice. In my humble opinion, however, performance assessment did not first become rigorous under the Zhou. In the time of Yu Shun, it was said: “Have them present their proposals in words, clearly test them through accomplishments, and grant carriages and robes according to their service.” It was also said: “Assess achievements every three years; after three assessments, demote the benighted and promote the enlightened.” Thus these practices had a long history. As for those who discuss government and turn exclusively to Tang Yao and Yu Shun, could it be that the descent from august sovereigns to emperors, and from emperors to kings, was brought about by the circumstances of their times? This cannot be held against the Zhou. Although Emperor Wu of Han’s nomination of the filially pious and incorrupt and of outstanding talents differed slightly …

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
異於隋唐也顧在當時挾書之律再世始
除禮樂之請謙讓未遑然則為教可知矣
彼其屢詔邦國夫亦因董仲舒之對慕古
之名姑為是文具乎未可與周並也審如
是選舉之義考課之方大略可知矣我
國家取士以文而三試之若循文詞之舊矣
其用人稽其年勞而叙遷之若循資格之
舊矣然社有學郡縣有學而其為教又皆
宗六經首德行是黨正閭胥教民之意也
===
郡縣有守令提調之而總於藩司是州長
攷勸糾戒之意也畿輔諸省有憲臣督視
之是司諫糾民之意也士三歲試於鄉論
其秀者而升之禮部是鄉長鄉大夫大司
徒賓興之意也而選舉即周之法矣況懷
材抱德賢良方正之士訪延徵辟不專為
文夫豈倚於文詞者所可擬乎內外百司
三載一考績各書其功過而奏之銓曹是
受會致事之意也考功第其殿最而黜陟
punctuated:
異於隋唐也。顧在當時，挾書之律再世始除，禮樂之請謙讓未遑，然則為教可知矣。彼其屢詔邦國，夫亦因董仲舒之對，慕古之名，姑為是文具乎？未可與周並也。審如是，選舉之義、考課之方，大略可知矣。
我國家取士以文而三試之，若循文詞之舊矣；其用人，稽其年勞而叙遷之，若循資格之舊矣。然社有學，郡縣有學，而其為教又皆宗六經、首德行，是黨正、閭胥教民之意也。郡縣有守令提調之，而總於藩司，是州長攷勸糾戒之意也。畿輔諸省有憲臣督視之，是司諫糾民之意也。士三歲試於鄉，論其秀者而升之禮部，是鄉長、鄉大夫、大司徒賓興之意也。而選舉即周之法矣。況懷材抱德、賢良方正之士，訪延徵辟，不專為文，夫豈倚於文詞者所可擬乎？內外百司三載一考績，各書其功過而奏之銓曹，是受會致事之意也。考功第其殿最而黜陟
translation_en:
…different from those of the Sui and Tang. Yet at that time, the prohibition on possessing books was not repealed until two reigns had passed, while proposals concerning rites and music were met with modest disclaimers that there had not yet been time to attend to them. From this one can judge the state of instruction. As for the repeated edicts issued throughout the realm, were these perhaps merely prompted by Dong Zhongshu’s response to the throne—a desire for the reputation of emulating antiquity, provisionally satisfied by these formalities on paper? They cannot be placed on a par with Zhou practice. If this assessment is sound, the principles of selecting men for office and the methods of evaluating their performance can be understood in broad outline.
Our dynasty selects men through written compositions and examines them three times, seemingly following the old reliance on literary composition. In employing men, it considers their years of service and promotes them in sequence, seemingly following the old reliance on seniority and qualifications. Yet there are schools in the local communities and in the prefectures and counties, and their instruction invariably takes the Six Classics as its authority and gives priority to virtuous conduct. This embodies the intention behind the district rectifiers (dangzheng) and neighborhood heads (lüxu) instructing the people. In the prefectures and counties, prefects and magistrates oversee this instruction, under the general direction of the Provincial Administration Commission. This embodies the intention behind the district chiefs (zhouzhang) examining and encouraging, correcting and admonishing. In the metropolitan region and the provinces, censorial officials supervise it. This embodies the intention behind the remonstrance officials (sijian) correcting the people. Every three years, scholars take the Provincial Examination; the outstanding among them are assessed and advanced to the Ministry of Rites. This embodies the intention behind the township heads (xiangzhang), township grandees (xiangdafu), and Minister of Education (da situ) honoring worthy men as guests and advancing them. Thus our selection of men for office follows the methods of Zhou. Moreover, men possessing talent and virtue, worthiness and uprightness, are sought out, invited, summoned, and appointed: selection is not confined to written compositions. How could this be compared with a system dependent on literary expression alone? The officials of all agencies, both in the capital and outside it, undergo a performance evaluation once every three years. Their merits and faults are individually recorded and reported to the Ministry of Personnel. This embodies the intention behind receiving accounts and submitting reports of official duties. The Bureau of Evaluations ranks their performance from worst to best and demotes or promotes…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之是六計弊治之意也其在內者復五年
一考察之在外者復三年一考察之是三
歲大計之意也又臺諫時以所聞舉劾之
太宰請於
上而去留之是歲終詔王廢置之意也而考課
即周之法矣况竒才異能精忠大節之士
超遷特拜不專以資又豈倚於資格者所
可擬乎百六十年士有成材官有成績而
海內乂安有由然矣而執事猶欲講求其
===
法者愚以為成周之法未必不可行於今
也隋唐之事又非所以為訓也為今之計
豈可以他求哉亦惟守吾
祖宗之法而時振飭之而已矣是故學校之敎
或隳於士習之浮薄或敗於師儒之怠弛
則
申勅中外本實必敦遴選必愼去其害吾敎
者可也黜陟之典或亂於毁譽之失真或
誤於形迹之疑似則
punctuated:
之，是六計弊治之意也。其在內者，復五年一考察之；在外者，復三年一考察之，是三歲大計之意也。又臺諫時以所聞舉劾之，太宰請於上而去留之，是歲終詔王廢置之意也。而考課即周之法矣。况竒才異能、精忠大節之士，超遷特拜，不專以資，又豈倚於資格者所可擬乎？百六十年，士有成材，官有成績，而海內乂安，有由然矣。而執事猶欲講求其法者，愚以為成周之法未必不可行於今也，隋唐之事又非所以為訓也。為今之計，豈可以他求哉？亦惟守吾祖宗之法而時振飭之而已矣。
是故學校之敎，或隳於士習之浮薄，或敗於師儒之怠弛，則申勅中外，本實必敦，遴選必愼，去其害吾敎者可也。黜陟之典，或亂於毁譽之失真，或誤於形迹之疑似，則
translation_en:
…them: this embodies the intent of judging administration by the six criteria. Those serving in the capital are additionally reviewed once every five years, and those serving outside it once every three years: this embodies the intent of the great triennial reckoning. Moreover, the censors and remonstrance officials periodically recommend or impeach them on the basis of what they have heard, and the Minister of Personnel petitions His Majesty to dismiss or retain them: this embodies the intent of informing the king at year’s end whom to dismiss or appoint. Thus, the assessment of officials follows the methods of the Zhou. Furthermore, men of exceptional talent and ability, consummate loyalty and outstanding integrity receive accelerated promotions and special appointments, without exclusive regard for seniority. How could those who rely on their qualifications and seniority compare with them? For one hundred and sixty years, scholars have developed their talents, officials have achieved results, and all within the seas has enjoyed peace and order. There are reasons why this has been so. Yet you, sir, still wish to investigate these methods. In my humble view, the methods of the flourishing Zhou are not necessarily impracticable today, while the practices of the Sui and Tang should not serve as models. In devising policy for the present, how could we seek elsewhere? We need only uphold the methods of our imperial ancestors and periodically reinvigorate and rectify their implementation.
Thus, if education in the schools is undermined by the frivolous and shallow habits of scholars, or impaired by the indolence and laxity of teachers, it will suffice to renew injunctions to officials in the capital and the provinces: substantial learning and conduct must be fostered, selection must be careful, and whatever harms our teaching must be removed. If the procedures for demotion and promotion are confused by untruthful praise and blame, or distorted by outward appearances that invite uncertain judgments, then…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
申勅所司事求其實聽求其公去其害吾政
者可也如是則選舉考課豈復有失人之
患而成周之治有不可再見於今哉愚不
敏敢執此以復
第三問
張志淑
同考試官教諭陳批書生談兵亹亹若老將
他日為文武全才者子豈其人邪主司為
國得賢可預慶矣庸執此以驗
===
考試官教授何批六韜左氏互相為用孔
明武穆各有所長子能指而言之有見矣錄之
考試官教授高批是亦胷中有甲兵者
平邦國之治存乎兵備之不可不豫馭天
下之兵存乎法講之不可不明備不豫則
倉卒應變無以成折衝禦侮之功講不明
則淺率寡謀何以收戰勝攻取之效是故
先王謀其始也睽乖取象則弧矢利夫天
下師嚴以律則地水制于剛中皆以潛消
punctuated:
申勅所司，事求其實，聽求其公，去其害吾政者可也。如是，則選舉考課豈復有失人之患，而成周之治有不可再見於今哉？愚不敏，敢執此以復。
第三問
張志淑
同考試官教諭陳批：書生談兵，亹亹若老將。他日為文武全才者，子豈其人邪？主司為國得賢，可預慶矣。庸執此以驗。
考試官教授何批：《六韜》、《左氏》互相為用，孔明、武穆各有所長。子能指而言之，有見矣。錄之。
考試官教授高批：是亦胷中有甲兵者。
平邦國之治，存乎兵備之不可不豫；馭天下之兵，存乎法講之不可不明。備不豫，則倉卒應變，無以成折衝禦侮之功；講不明，則淺率寡謀，何以收戰勝攻取之效？是故先王謀其始也，睽乖取象，則弧矢利夫天下；師嚴以律，則地水制于剛中。皆以潛消
translation_en:
… instruct the responsible offices to seek the facts in every matter and impartiality in hearing cases, and remove whatever harms our government. If this is done, how could selection for office and assessments of officials’ performance still suffer from failures to obtain the right men? And could the good government of the Zhou in its maturity not appear again today? Though I am slow of understanding, I venture to offer this in reply.
Third Question
Zhang Zhishu
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: A scholar discussing warfare, speaking fluently like a veteran general! Might you be the man who will one day possess complete talents in both civil and military affairs? We may already congratulate the examination authorities on obtaining a worthy man for the state. Let this assessment stand for future verification.
Comment by Examiner He, Professor: The Six Secret Teachings and the Zuo Commentary complement one another in their application; Kongming and Wumu each had their particular strengths. You can identify and explain these: you have insight. Accept this essay.
Comment by Examiner Gao, Professor: Here too is a man who carries armored troops within his breast.
The orderly government that brings peace to the states depends upon making military preparations in advance; commanding the armies of the realm depends upon clearly studying and explaining military methods. Without advance preparation, when suddenly called upon to respond to an emergency, one has no means of repelling attacks and resisting aggression. Without clear study and explanation, one is superficial, rash, and deficient in planning: how can one achieve victory in battle and success in assault? Thus, when the former kings laid their plans at the outset, they drew upon the image of estrangement in the Kui hexagram, and bows and arrows benefited the realm; they made armies strict through discipline, and in the Shi hexagram—earth above water—control rested with the firm line in the central position. All this was intended quietly to eliminate…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
暴亂陰奪不軌輔弼敎化宣昭文德歸于
無亂以成君之仁初非必於用武以毒天
下也是故泥焉者敗變焉者神弛焉者弗
可振也然則備之其可以弗豫講之其可
以弗明邪執事以文策士而以武事相與
講明豈以書生亦有識達時務者乎請試
言之兵也者天地之義氣也天無是氣則
不成歲功人無是氣則不成人道故宋子
罕曰天有五財民並用之廢一不可何能
===
去兵夫兵金象也五財無金則木煩而不
制水煩而不化五行擧乖其用則兵固天
道之不可廢者聖人明於天道故五射五
御之學備於周官而夾谷之會雖孔子大
聖亦具左右司馬以從則兵尤儒者事也
自軒轅制五陣以生克爲勝負太公爲六
韜以極陰陽之變化而兵法始著於天下
矣夫五陣五行之理也六韜八卦之象也
其法出于河圖洛書後世兵家者流雖出
punctuated:
暴亂，陰奪不軌，輔弼敎化，宣昭文德，歸于無亂，以成君之仁，初非必於用武以毒天下也。是故泥焉者敗，變焉者神，弛焉者弗可振也。然則備之其可以弗豫，講之其可以弗明邪？執事以文策士，而以武事相與講明，豈以書生亦有識達時務者乎？請試言之。

兵也者，天地之義氣也。天無是氣，則不成歲功；人無是氣，則不成人道。故宋子罕曰：「天有五財，民並用之，廢一不可，何能去兵？」夫兵，金象也。五財無金，則木煩而不制，水煩而不化，五行擧乖其用，則兵固天道之不可廢者。聖人明於天道，故五射五御之學備於《周官》，而夾谷之會，雖孔子大聖，亦具左右司馬以從，則兵尤儒者事也。自軒轅制五陣，以生克爲勝負，太公爲《六韜》，以極陰陽之變化，而兵法始著於天下矣。夫五陣，五行之理也；六韜，八卦之象也。其法出于《河圖》《洛書》。後世兵家者流，雖出
translation_en:
…violence and disorder, forestall unlawful designs, assist moral instruction, and make civil virtue manifest, bringing about freedom from disorder and thereby fulfilling the ruler’s benevolence. The original purpose was certainly not to insist on using military force to bring suffering upon the world. Thus those who cling rigidly to military methods fail; those who adapt them achieve wondrous results; and those who let military preparedness lapse cannot recover. How, then, could preparations fail to be made in advance, or military methods fail to be clearly studied? You, sir, examine scholars through literary policy questions, yet invite us to elucidate military affairs together. Is this because you believe that among scholars there may also be men whose understanding encompasses the affairs of the time? Allow me to attempt an explanation.

Military force is the righteous vital energy of Heaven and Earth. Without this energy, Heaven could not bring the year’s work to completion; without it, human beings could not fulfill the human Way. Thus Zihan of Song said: “Heaven has provided five resources, and the people use them all. Not one can be discarded. How could arms be abolished?” Arms correspond to Metal. If the five resources lacked Metal, Wood would proliferate without restraint, and Water would abound without transformation; all Five Phases would be thrown out of their proper functioning. Military force is thus something that the Way of Heaven cannot dispense with. The sages understood the Way of Heaven, and so instruction in the five forms of archery and the five skills of charioteering is fully provided for in the Offices of Zhou. At the meeting at Jiagu, even the great sage Confucius had Majors of the Left and Right accompany him. Military affairs are therefore particularly a concern of Confucian scholars. Xuanyuan devised the five battle formations, making victory and defeat depend on the cycles of generation and conquest; the Grand Duke composed the Six Secret Teachings to explore fully the transformations of yin and yang. From these beginnings, military methods became known throughout the world. The five formations embody the principles of the Five Phases; the Six Secret Teachings embody the images of the Eight Trigrams. Their methods derive from the River Chart and the Luo Writing. Although military strategists of later ages devised…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
竒效詭縱横經緯至于百千萬變不可勝
窮然終不能有出於五行八卦之外者迨
夫一變而為春秋則左氏得其意觀其叙
晉敗狄曰兩於前伍於後專為右角參為
左角偏為前拒則步戰之五陣也其叙楚
敗晉曰軍行右轅左追蓐前茅慮無中權後
勁則車戰之五陣也其法純用軒轅蒙馬
遁荆採樵致絞左氏以叙事寓兵法用之
於戰其可乎哉左氏去周未遠古法猶存
===
故有車戰而無騎戰當時有車而無騎也
自鄭莊公用徒兵中行穆子毀車崇卒趙
武靈王用胡騎而車騎步卒始並用于天
下矣又變而為戰國則武經七書得其精
觀其載太公論戰騎有必走必懼必敗必
饑必亂可克可擒可虜之十勝焉有敗地
圍地死地沒地竭地艱地困地患地隅地
之九敗焉其法載于六韜然而不用于周
不見于春秋其深謀妙法反出于孫武子
punctuated:
竒效詭，縱横經緯，至于百千萬變，不可勝窮，然終不能有出於五行八卦之外者。迨夫一變而為春秋，則左氏得其意。觀其叙晉敗狄曰：「兩於前，伍於後，專為右角，參為左角，偏為前拒。」則步戰之五陣也。其叙楚敗晉曰：「軍行，右轅，左追蓐，前茅慮無，中權後勁。」則車戰之五陣也。其法純用軒轅。蒙馬遁荆，採樵致絞，左氏以叙事寓兵法，用之於戰，其可乎哉？左氏去周未遠，古法猶存，故有車戰而無騎戰，當時有車而無騎也。自鄭莊公用徒兵，中行穆子毀車崇卒，趙武靈王用胡騎，而車騎步卒始並用于天下矣。
又變而為戰國，則武經七書得其精。觀其載太公論戰騎，有必走、必懼、必敗、必饑、必亂、可克、可擒、可虜之十勝焉；有敗地、圍地、死地、沒地、竭地、艱地、困地、患地、隅地之九敗焉。其法載于六韜，然而不用于周，不見于春秋，其深謀妙法反出于孫武子
translation_en:
…unorthodox devices and deceptive practices, deploying and arranging them in hundreds, thousands, and myriads of inexhaustible variations, ultimately none can go beyond the Five Phases and Eight Trigrams. When a further transformation brought the Spring and Autumn period, Master Zuo grasped their meaning. Consider his account of Jin’s defeat of the Di: “Pairs in front, groups of five behind; single units formed the right wing, triple units the left wing, and detached units the forward defensive line.” These were the five formations for infantry warfare. His account of Chu’s defeat of Jin says: “On the march, chariots were on the right, men gathering bedding on the left; scouts went ahead to guard against unforeseen dangers, the command occupied the center, and strong troops brought up the rear.” These were the five formations for chariot warfare. Their methods followed Xuanyuan entirely. Covering horses to put the forces of Jing to flight, and gathering firewood to lure out the forces of Jiao—Master Zuo embedded military methods in his narration of events. Could these be applied in battle? Master Zuo lived not far removed from the Zhou, and ancient methods still survived. Thus there was chariot warfare but no cavalry warfare, for at that time there were chariots but no cavalry. Only after Duke Zhuang of Zheng employed infantry, Zhonghang Muzi destroyed chariots and favored foot soldiers, and King Wuling of Zhao employed Hu cavalry did chariots, cavalry, and infantry begin to be used together throughout the realm.
With a further transformation came the Warring States period, and the Seven Military Classics captured the essence of these methods. Consider their account of the Grand Duke’s discussion of cavalry warfare: there are ten conditions for victory, including circumstances in which the enemy must flee, must be frightened, must be defeated, must go hungry, or must fall into disorder, and those in which the enemy can be overcome, captured, or taken prisoner [the text lists only eight of the ten]. There are nine conditions for defeat: ruinous terrain, encircled terrain, deadly terrain, engulfing terrain, exhausting terrain, difficult terrain, confining terrain, perilous terrain, and cornered terrain. These methods are recorded in the Six Secret Teachings (Liu tao), yet they were not employed under the Zhou and do not appear in the Spring and Autumn period. Its profound plans and ingenious methods, on the contrary, rank …

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之下蘇子謂六韜非周書則其所言亦有
據矣誠為戰國知兵之士祖其餘論而推
廣之設為問答以極兵家之變也然蹂轢
彊陣遏禦奔衝不可以無車乘亂搗虛追
敗結離不可以無騎短戟相交投石超距
不可以無卒而車騎步卒不可偏廢于天
下矣是故用兵貴乎有紀尚節制也決勝
至于無形尚權變也二者兵家之大權左
氏多古法尚近節制之兵六韜多變法已
===
極權謀之秘武侯八陣本六韜而其節制
則得諸左氏故武侯之兵極天下之至深
岳飛兵法本左氏而其運用則得諸六韜
故岳飛之兵極天下之至變兵志曰凡兵
之道莫貴乎一一者能獨往獨來階於道
幾於神用之在於機顯之在於勢所謂奇
正相生循環無端者也此又兵家之至要
二公之所獨得也今觀武侯八陣擊首則
尾至擊尾則首至擊中則首尾皆至岳飛
punctuated:
之下。蘇子謂《六韜》非周書，則其所言亦有據矣。誠為戰國知兵之士祖其餘論而推廣之，設為問答，以極兵家之變也。然蹂轢彊陣，遏禦奔衝，不可以無車；乘亂搗虛，追敗結離，不可以無騎；短戟相交，投石超距，不可以無卒。而車騎步卒不可偏廢于天下矣。是故用兵貴乎有紀，尚節制也；決勝至于無形，尚權變也。二者，兵家之大權。《左氏》多古法，尚近節制之兵；《六韜》多變法，已極權謀之秘。武侯八陣本《六韜》，而其節制則得諸《左氏》，故武侯之兵極天下之至深。岳飛兵法本《左氏》，而其運用則得諸《六韜》，故岳飛之兵極天下之至變。
《兵志》曰：「凡兵之道，莫貴乎一。」一者，能獨往獨來，階於道，幾於神，用之在於機，顯之在於勢，所謂奇正相生，循環無端者也。此又兵家之至要，二公之所獨得也。今觀武侯八陣，擊首則尾至，擊尾則首至，擊中則首尾皆至。岳飛
translation_en:
…below Master Sun Wu. Master Su said that the Six Secret Teachings (Liu tao) was not a Zhou work; his assertion thus has grounds. Indeed, it was produced by men versed in warfare during the Warring States period, who took the surviving teachings as their basis and expanded upon them, casting them as questions and answers to explore the full range of military adaptation. Yet chariots are indispensable for crushing strong formations and checking headlong charges; cavalry is indispensable for exploiting disorder, striking undefended positions, pursuing defeated troops, and engaging separated forces [?]; infantry is indispensable for fighting at close quarters with short halberds, throwing stones, and leaping distances. Thus none of these—chariots, cavalry, or infantry—can be neglected in warfare throughout the realm. Accordingly, valuing order in the employment of troops means esteeming discipline and control; securing victory without discernible form means esteeming flexible adaptation. These two are the great instruments of military command. The Zuo Commentary contains many ancient methods and remains close to warfare governed by discipline and control; the Six Secret Teachings contains many adaptive methods and fully explores the secrets of stratagem. The Marquis of Wu’s eight formations were based on the Six Secret Teachings, while his discipline and control derived from the Zuo Commentary. Thus the warfare of the Marquis of Wu, Zhuge Liang, attained the utmost profundity. Yue Fei’s military methods were based on the Zuo Commentary, while his practical deployment derived from the Six Secret Teachings. Thus Yue Fei’s warfare attained the utmost adaptability.
The Records of Warfare says: “In the way of warfare, nothing is more valuable than unity.” Through unity, one can advance and withdraw independently, ascend toward the Way, and approach the divine. Its application lies in grasping the critical moment; its manifestation lies in strategic configuration. This is what is meant by the unorthodox and orthodox generating each other in an endless cycle. This, moreover, is the supreme essential of military practice, which these two men alone grasped. Now, examining the Marquis of Wu’s eight formations: when the head was attacked, the tail came to its aid; when the tail was attacked, the head came to its aid; when the center was attacked, both head and tail came to its aid. Yue Fei…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
行陣兵識將意將識士情人人各自爲戰
此皆會于一而幾于神者也摧敵制勝有
以哉法異功同一者基之矣是故以兵法
言則左氏不如六韜之盡而深六韜不如
左氏之約而大以知兵言則岳飛不如武
侯之深而安武侯亦當以岳飛之兵爲變
且神也使今之爲兵者學六韜皆如武侯
之得其深學左氏皆如岳飛之得其變則
用左氏可也用六韜可也使學六韜而徒
===
得其數學左氏而徒尚其辭則左氏固陳
言也六韜亦陳言也所謂徒讀父書者耳
其何以應天下之變哉洪惟我
朝稽古定制擇將備邊其置兵也内設兵部
五府以統之外設都司衛所以翼之大小
相維犬牙相制備至豫矣其訓兵也内則
嚴團營操練之典外則慎考較演習之法
調度有時開闔有方講至明矣一或有變
則又命將出師擇人任勢使騎步相參五
punctuated:
行陣，兵識將意，將識士情，人人各自爲戰，此皆會于一而幾于神者也。摧敵制勝，有以哉！法異功同，一者基之矣。是故以兵法言，則左氏不如六韜之盡而深，六韜不如左氏之約而大；以知兵言，則岳飛不如武侯之深而安，武侯亦當以岳飛之兵爲變且神也。使今之爲兵者學六韜皆如武侯之得其深，學左氏皆如岳飛之得其變，則用左氏可也，用六韜可也。使學六韜而徒得其數，學左氏而徒尚其辭，則左氏固陳言也，六韜亦陳言也，所謂徒讀父書者耳，其何以應天下之變哉？
洪惟我朝稽古定制，擇將備邊。其置兵也，内設兵部、五府以統之，外設都司、衛所以翼之，大小相維，犬牙相制，備至豫矣。其訓兵也，内則嚴團營操練之典，外則慎考較演習之法，調度有時，開闔有方，講至明矣。一或有變，則又命將出師，擇人任勢，使騎步相參，五
translation_en:
…in his battle formations, the soldiers understood their commanders’ intentions, and the commanders understood their men’s dispositions; each man fought on his own initiative. These are all instances of attaining unity and approaching the divine. There was indeed a basis for crushing the enemy and securing victory! Their methods differed, but their achievements were the same: unity was their foundation. Thus, in terms of military methods, the Zuo Commentary does not equal the Six Secret Teachings in comprehensiveness and depth, while the Six Secret Teachings does not equal the Zuo Commentary in concision and scope. In terms of understanding warfare, Yue Fei does not equal the Marquis Wu in profundity and steadiness; yet the Marquis Wu, too, would surely regard Yue Fei’s military practice as adaptable and divine. If those who conduct warfare today could all study the Six Secret Teachings and grasp its depths as the Marquis Wu did, and study the Zuo Commentary and grasp its adaptability as Yue Fei did, then either the Zuo Commentary or the Six Secret Teachings could serve them. But if, in studying the Six Secret Teachings, they acquire only its techniques, and in studying the Zuo Commentary, they merely prize its language, then the Zuo Commentary is indeed nothing but stale words, and the Six Secret Teachings is likewise nothing but stale words. Such men are merely what is called ‘those who only read their father’s books.’ How could they respond to the changing circumstances of the world?
We reverently reflect that our dynasty has examined antiquity to establish its institutions, selected commanders, and provided for the defense of the frontiers. In organizing its forces, it has established the Ministry of War and the Five Chief Military Commissions at the center to command them, and Regional Military Commissions, Guards, and Battalions in the provinces to support them. Larger and smaller units sustain one another and hold one another in check, interlocking like dogs’ teeth: preparations have been made with the utmost foresight. In training its forces, at the center it rigorously enforces the regulations for drilling the consolidated camps, while in the provinces it carefully implements the rules for assessment and exercises. Mobilization and deployment have their appointed times; opening and closing formations have their prescribed methods. These matters have been explained with the utmost clarity. Should any disturbance arise, it further appoints commanders and dispatches troops, selecting suitable men and making use of the strategic situation, so that cavalry and infantry support one another, and the five…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
兵互用兵識將意將識士情百六十年以
來兵威强盛邊境肅清有由然矣然而承
平日久邊卒漸驕日者雲中之變至厪
宵旰之憂屯兵易將始克底平豈兵威未豫而
使之狎兵謀不素而使之縱邪故愚謂宜
於學校之中别立戎敎科舉取士試以兵
務又於武學武舉之外别立講武一司隸
諸禁籍博采天下文臣武將謀略智勇之
士延置其中使之日講韜略推演八陣極
===
深研幾制器尚象皆可以施於實用如孔
明之深也以盡天下之變又時以其法閲
練軍士使皆知將意而識士情有若一身
之於四肢如岳飛之變也以盡天下之神
則今之兵猶夫古也而古今人豈不相及
哉矧我
國家至仁有道神武不殺威德所加無遠弗
届若涖戎者法自昭明而不可犯事有豫
備而不失宜則赳赳武夫足爲公侯腹心
punctuated: 兵互用，兵識將意，將識士情。百六十年以來，兵威强盛，邊境肅清，有由然矣。然而承平日久，邊卒漸驕。日者雲中之變，至厪宵旰之憂，屯兵易將，始克底平。豈兵威未豫而使之狎，兵謀不素而使之縱邪？故愚謂宜於學校之中别立戎敎，科舉取士，試以兵務；又於武學武舉之外，别立講武一司，隸諸禁籍，博采天下文臣武將謀略智勇之士，延置其中，使之日講韜略，推演八陣，極深研幾，制器尚象，皆可以施於實用。如孔明之深也，以盡天下之變；又時以其法閲練軍士，使皆知將意而識士情，有若一身之於四肢。如岳飛之變也，以盡天下之神。則今之兵猶夫古也，而古今人豈不相及哉？矧我國家至仁有道，神武不殺，威德所加，無遠弗届。若涖戎者法自昭明而不可犯，事有豫備而不失宜，則赳赳武夫足爲公侯腹心
translation_en:
…the five kinds of weapons are used in conjunction; soldiers understand their commanders’ intentions, and commanders understand their soldiers’ dispositions. For a hundred and sixty years, our military might has been strong and our frontiers peaceful: there are reasons why this has been so. Yet after a long period of peace, the frontier troops have gradually grown unruly. Recently, the disturbance at Yunzhong caused His Majesty such anxiety that he rose before dawn and ate only after dark. Only after troops were stationed there and commanders replaced was peace finally restored. Could it be that military authority had not been established beforehand, allowing them to become insolent, and that military planning had not been undertaken in advance, allowing them to run unchecked?

Thus, in my humble view, special military instruction should be instituted in the schools, and candidates selected through the civil service examinations should be tested on military affairs. In addition to the military schools and military examinations, a separate office for the study of warfare should be established and entered on the registers of the imperial establishment [?]. Civil officials and military commanders throughout the realm who possess strategic ability, intelligence, and courage should be broadly recruited and invited to serve in it. They should discuss military strategy daily, work out the applications of the Eight Formations, probe the profound and investigate the first signs of change, and fashion implements according to symbolic patterns, so that all these things may be put to practical use. With depth like that of Kongming, they would encompass every possible change under Heaven. They should also periodically use these methods to inspect and train the troops, so that soldiers understand their commanders’ intentions and commanders understand their soldiers’ dispositions, like the relation of a body to its four limbs. With adaptability like that of Yue Fei, they would fully realize the wondrous efficacy of warfare. Then the soldiers of today would be like those of antiquity: how could people today fail to equal the ancients?

Moreover, our dynasty is supremely benevolent and possesses the Way; its divine martial power prevails without killing, and no place is too distant for its authority and virtue to reach. If those who administer military affairs have regulations that are clear and cannot be transgressed, and prepare for contingencies in advance so that their actions remain appropriate, then valiant warriors will be fit to serve as the trusted confidants of dukes and lords…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而桓桓甲胄足為
王室屏翰矣尚何外患之足慮乎抑又聞宋
儒之告其君曰聖王制御夷狄之道其本
不在乎威强而在乎德業其任不在乎邊
境而在乎朝廷其具不在乎兵食而在乎
紀綱則所以斡旋化機以為長治久安之
圖者其尚有進於是者乎草茅之見固有
欲言而未盡者執事其與進之
第四問
===
同考試官訓導李 批 名實一策正驗儒生用
世之志子以法其意不泥其迹立說蓋識治體而
有卓見者
同考試官教諭吴 批 有議論有斷制終篇復
歸以格致誠正之學即此可占子之所蘊矣
考試官教授何 批 循名責實正
今日急務是作敷陳詳盡録之不獨以其文也
考試官教授高 批 是精於名實之辨者
banxin: 郷試録 七十三 楊機
punctuated:
而桓桓甲胄足為王室屏翰矣，尚何外患之足慮乎？抑又聞宋儒之告其君曰：「聖王制御夷狄之道，其本不在乎威强而在乎德業，其任不在乎邊境而在乎朝廷，其具不在乎兵食而在乎紀綱。」則所以斡旋化機，以為長治久安之圖者，其尚有進於是者乎？草茅之見，固有欲言而未盡者，執事其與進之。
第四問
同考試官訓導李批：名實一策，正驗儒生用世之志。子以法其意、不泥其迹立說，蓋識治體而有卓見者。
同考試官教諭吴批：有議論，有斷制，終篇復歸以格致誠正之學，即此可占子之所蘊矣。
考試官教授何批：循名責實，正今日急務。是作敷陳詳盡，録之不獨以其文也。
考試官教授高批：是精於名實之辨者。
translation_en:
…and the valiant men in armor will suffice as the royal house’s shield and bulwark. What external threat need then cause concern? Yet I have also heard that a Song Confucian scholar told his ruler: “In the sage king’s way of controlling the Yi and Di, the foundation lies not in military might but in virtuous achievement; responsibility lies not at the frontier but at court; the means lie not in troops and provisions but in the governing order and discipline.” Might there therefore be something beyond what I have proposed, by which to turn the workings of transformation toward lasting order and enduring peace? In the humble views of this commoner, there are indeed things I wish to say that I have not fully expressed. May you, honored officials, permit me to put them forward.
Fourth Question
Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor, comments: This policy essay on names and realities truly tests a Confucian scholar’s aspiration to serve the world. You base your argument on emulating the underlying intent without being bound by outward forms. You evidently understand the essentials of governance and possess outstanding insight.
Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: There is reasoned discussion and decisive judgment. At the end, the essay returns to the learning of investigating things, extending knowledge, making intentions sincere, and rectifying the mind. From this alone, we can discern what you have within you.
Examiner He, Professor, comments: Requiring actual performance to accord with nominal responsibilities is precisely today’s urgent task. This composition sets out its arguments thoroughly and fully. We select it not solely for its literary merit.
Examiner Gao, Professor, comments: This is the work of someone accomplished in distinguishing names from realities.

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
善爲治者法古之意而不泥其迹者也夫
意也者制作之所由出也迹也者制作之
所由寓也是本非二物也而何以曰意可
法迹不可泥哉蓋天下之勢其變無常形
而吾之治之不可以膠於一定故古昔帝
王之有所制作也由其初言之治如其時
事如其意固所謂名實相副者及行之既
久勢以時變向之制作有所窒礙而不可
復行則雖帝王身當其任亦且視爲陳迹
===
推其意而更爲之矣況治於其後者尚可
以泥乎是故法其意則雖事不相沿無所
往而非實泥其迹則雖行之舉相似無所
往而非名是名實之辯也請因明問所及
而陳其槩世之論名實者其於名類能知
之至所謂實則吾猶惑焉立官而命之曰
是冢宰是司徒是宗伯司馬司寇司空以
爲六官之實在是矣取民之田而限之曰
母過百畝割其巔以畀鄉里九族以爲井
punctuated:
善爲治者，法古之意而不泥其迹者也。夫意也者，制作之所由出也；迹也者，制作之所由寓也。是本非二物也，而何以曰意可法、迹不可泥哉？蓋天下之勢，其變無常形，而吾之治之，不可以膠於一定。故古昔帝王之有所制作也，由其初言之，治如其時，事如其意，固所謂名實相副者。及行之既久，勢以時變，向之制作有所窒礙而不可復行，則雖帝王身當其任，亦且視爲陳迹，推其意而更爲之矣。況治於其後者，尚可以泥乎？是故法其意，則雖事不相沿，無所往而非實；泥其迹，則雖行之舉相似，無所往而非名。是名實之辯也。請因明問所及而陳其槩。
世之論名實者，其於名，類能知之；至所謂實，則吾猶惑焉。立官而命之曰：「是冢宰，是司徒，是宗伯、司馬、司寇、司空。」以爲六官之實在是矣。取民之田而限之曰：「母過百畝。」割其巔以畀鄉里九族，以爲井
translation_en:
Those skilled in government follow the intent of antiquity without clinging to its outward forms. Intent is the source from which institutions arise; outward forms are that in which institutions find embodiment. These are fundamentally not two separate things. Why, then, do we say that intent should be followed, but outward forms should not be rigidly adhered to? The circumstances of the world change without any fixed pattern, and our government cannot be bound to one unchanging arrangement. Thus, when the emperors and kings of antiquity established institutions, considered at their inception, their government suited the times and their measures accorded with their intent. This was indeed what is called correspondence between name and substance. Once those institutions had been in operation for a long time, however, circumstances changed with the times, and the earlier arrangements encountered obstacles that made their continued implementation impossible. Even if those emperors and kings themselves had been in charge, they would have regarded these arrangements as relics of the past and, carrying forward their intent, established them anew. How much less should those governing afterward cling to them? Hence, if one follows their intent, even when particular measures do not continue earlier practices, everything has substance. If one clings to their outward forms, even when every action resembles earlier practice, everything is merely a name. Such is the distinction between name and substance. Allow me to set out its broad outlines with reference to the matters raised in your discerning question.
Those who discuss name and substance nowadays generally understand names; but as for what they call substance, I remain perplexed. They establish offices and designate them, saying: “This is the Grand Steward, this the Minister of Education, and these the Minister of Rites, Minister of War, Minister of Justice, and Minister of Works.” They suppose that the substance of the Six Offices lies in this. They take the people's fields and impose a limit, saying: “They must not exceed one hundred mu.” They cut off their “tops” [?] and distribute these to the local communities and the nine degrees of kinship, supposing that the substance of the well-field …

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
田之實在是矣嗚呼此其所謂實乃正吾
所謂名也夫六官之所由設何為也哉以
治民焉耳井田之所由畫何為也哉以養
民焉耳治也養也是帝王制作之實也而
其曰六官曰井田陳迹之存乎簡編者皆
所謂名也使為國家者興賢而用之擇能
而使之邦治果修也邦教果敷也邦禮果
秩也邦政果舉也邦禁果章也邦土果奠
也雖不立六官其實六官也不然獨名而
===
已矣因民之利而興之擇民之害而去之
强不得凌弱也衆不得暴寡也富不得兼
併於貧也吏不得多取於下也雖不畫井
田其實井田也不然亦名而已矣古之帝
王有見於此是故唐虞建官惟百夏商官
倍周官三百六十周固無所襲於夏商而
夏商亦自不襲唐虞之舊夏貢殷助周徹
文王九一武王十一三代固不相沿而武
王亦自不沿其父之制苟益於民則帝王
punctuated: 田之實在是矣。嗚呼！此其所謂實，乃正吾所謂名也。夫六官之所由設，何為也哉？以治民焉耳。井田之所由畫，何為也哉？以養民焉耳。治也，養也，是帝王制作之實也。而其曰六官、曰井田，陳迹之存乎簡編者，皆所謂名也。使為國家者興賢而用之，擇能而使之，邦治果修也，邦教果敷也，邦禮果秩也，邦政果舉也，邦禁果章也，邦土果奠也，雖不立六官，其實六官也。不然，獨名而已矣。因民之利而興之，擇民之害而去之，强不得凌弱也，衆不得暴寡也，富不得兼併於貧也，吏不得多取於下也，雖不畫井田，其實井田也。不然，亦名而已矣。古之帝王有見於此，是故唐虞建官惟百，夏商官倍，周官三百六十。周固無所襲於夏商，而夏商亦自不襲唐虞之舊。夏貢，殷助，周徹，文王九一，武王十一。三代固不相沿，而武王亦自不沿其父之制。苟益於民，則帝王
translation_en:
…the substance of the well-field system lies in this. Alas! What they call substance is precisely what I call name. Why were the six offices established? Simply to govern the people. Why were the well-fields laid out? Simply to sustain the people. Governing and sustaining: these are the substance of the institutions created by emperors and kings. As for what are called the six offices and the well-fields—the surviving traces of the past preserved in books—these are all what I call names. If those who govern the realm promote and employ the worthy, select and appoint the capable, and thereby truly put the state's administration in order, extend its instruction, regulate its rites, carry out its military affairs, make its prohibitions clear, and secure its lands, then even without establishing the six offices, they possess the substance of the six offices. Otherwise, they have only the name.

If they develop what benefits the people and identify and remove what harms them, so that the strong cannot oppress the weak, the many cannot tyrannize over the few, the rich cannot engross the property of the poor, and officials cannot exact excessive levies from those below, then even without laying out well-fields, they possess the substance of the well-field system. Otherwise, this too is merely a name.

The emperors and kings of antiquity understood this. Thus Tang and Yu established only one hundred offices; Xia and Shang doubled that number; and Zhou had three hundred and sixty. Zhou certainly did not simply copy Xia and Shang, and Xia and Shang themselves did not copy the old arrangements of Tang and Yu. Xia used the tribute system (gong), Yin the labor-assistance system (zhu), and Zhou the shared-levy system (che). King Wen levied one part in nine, and King Wu one in ten. The Three Dynasties certainly did not simply follow one another, and King Wu himself did not follow his father's institutions. Provided that something benefits the people, then the emperors and kings…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之意也昔者周公之思兼三王以施四事
也其有不合仰而思之坐以待旦而孟子
之論井地曰若夫潤澤之則在君與子變
通以盡利神化以宜民聖賢之所爲蓋如
此至於後世時益以降則勢宜益以殊而
顧泥六官井田之迹思舉而復之於數千
載之下徇其名不責其實此其爲莽歟此
其爲宇文歟夫莽之事自其迹觀之不可
謂非井田也宇文之事自其迹觀之不可
===
謂非六官也然卒之六官無救於周之亡
而井田適以促新之滅然則其效可覩矣
自孟子以下善論治者愚於漢得董仲舒
焉其告武帝曰三王之道所祖不同非其
相反將以捄溢扶衰故王者有改制之名
無變道之實斯言也非無所見而云也殷
因於夏禮所損益可知周因於殷禮所損
益可知是魯論之旨而精於名實之辯者
也周公以下善爲治者愚於唐得太宗焉
punctuated:
之意也。昔者周公之思兼三王以施四事也，其有不合，仰而思之，坐以待旦。而孟子之論井地曰：「若夫潤澤之，則在君與子。」變通以盡利，神化以宜民，聖賢之所爲蓋如此。至於後世，時益以降，則勢宜益以殊，而顧泥六官井田之迹，思舉而復之於數千載之下，徇其名，不責其實，此其爲莽歟？此其爲宇文歟？夫莽之事，自其迹觀之，不可謂非井田也；宇文之事，自其迹觀之，不可謂非六官也。然卒之六官無救於周之亡，而井田適以促新之滅，然則其效可覩矣。
自孟子以下善論治者，愚於漢得董仲舒焉。其告武帝曰：「三王之道，所祖不同，非其相反，將以捄溢扶衰，故王者有改制之名，無變道之實。」斯言也，非無所見而云也。「殷因於夏禮，所損益可知；周因於殷禮，所損益可知。」是《魯論》之旨，而精於名實之辯者也。周公以下善爲治者，愚於唐得太宗焉。
translation_en:
…the intention of emperors and kings. In former times, the Duke of Zhou sought to combine the ways of the Three Kings in implementing four practices. Whenever something did not accord with them, he looked upward in thought and sat awaiting dawn. Yet when Mengzi discussed the well-field system, he said: “As for refining and adapting it, that rests with your ruler and you.” Adapting institutions to realize their full benefits, effecting subtle transformations to suit the people—such was the practice of sages and worthies. In later ages, as time advanced, circumstances necessarily differed ever more. Yet some clung to the outward forms of the Six Ministries and the well-field system, hoping to restore them thousands of years later. They pursued the names without demanding the substance. Was this not what Wang Mang did? Was this not what the Yuwen rulers did? Judged by its outward form, Wang Mang’s undertaking could indeed be called the well-field system; judged by its outward form, the Yuwen undertaking could indeed be called the Six Ministries. Yet in the end the Six Ministries could not save the Northern Zhou from falling, while the well-field system served only to hasten the destruction of the Xin. Their results are thus plain to see.
Among those after Mengzi who discussed government well, I humbly find Dong Zhongshu of the Han. He told Emperor Wu: “The ways of the Three Kings differed in what they took as their precedent. This was not because they contradicted one another, but because they sought to correct excess and shore up decline. Thus kings nominally change institutions, but in substance do not change the Way.” These words were not spoken without insight. “The Yin followed the rites of the Xia; what they subtracted and added can be known. The Zhou followed the rites of the Yin; what they subtracted and added can be known.” This is the purport of the Lu Analects, and it shows a precise understanding of the distinction between names and realities. Among those after the Duke of Zhou who governed well, I humbly find Emperor Taizong of the Tang.

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
口分世業以授民租庸調以取民而天下
稱治斯義也非無所本而然也聖人不先
天以開人各因時以立政是春秋之旨而
深有得於名實之辯者也執事發策乃不
能無疑於仲舒之論而惜太宗之不竟其
施其亦小泥焉矣至謂三代制作不可行
於後世意若有深諱焉者愚以為是無損
於三代也蓋今所謂三代制作皆其迹也
未有能得其意也誠得其意則豈惟今之
===
世行之無弊哉雖千百世可矣故愚嘗竊
譬之帝王制作之意歷千百世而可行者
猶天之元氣流通運行無有止息者也其
制作之迹隨時改易者猶天之五行二象
始終升降循環而不窮者也而烏能一之
是故善為治者法古之意而不泥其迹如
是而止矣雖然欲法古必先自治使徒欲
得帝王之意而己之所以為意者或牽於
有我則不能舍以從天下之公或蔽於自
punctuated:
口分、世業以授民，租、庸、調以取民，而天下稱治。斯義也，非無所本而然也。聖人不先天以開人，各因時以立政，是《春秋》之旨，而深有得於名實之辯者也。執事發策，乃不能無疑於仲舒之論，而惜太宗之不竟其施，其亦小泥焉矣。至謂三代制作不可行於後世，意若有深諱焉者，愚以為是無損於三代也。蓋今所謂三代制作，皆其迹也，未有能得其意也。誠得其意，則豈惟今之世行之無弊哉？雖千百世可矣。故愚嘗竊譬之：帝王制作之意，歷千百世而可行者，猶天之元氣流通運行，無有止息者也；其制作之迹，隨時改易者，猶天之五行二象，始終升降，循環而不窮者也。而烏能一之？是故善為治者，法古之意而不泥其迹，如是而止矣。

雖然，欲法古，必先自治。使徒欲得帝王之意，而己之所以為意者，或牽於有我，則不能舍以從天下之公；或蔽於自
translation_en:
…He distributed lifetime allotments and hereditary holdings to the people, and levied grain taxes, labor service or its commutation, and textile taxes upon them; all under Heaven was acclaimed as well governed. This approach was not without a foundation. The sages did not anticipate Heaven in initiating human affairs, but each established government according to the needs of his time. This is the purport of the Spring and Autumn Annals, and it shows a profound grasp of the distinction between names and realities. Yet in setting your policy question, you retain doubts about Zhongshu’s argument and regret that Taizong did not carry his measures through to completion. This, too, is somewhat inflexible. As for saying that the institutions established by the Three Dynasties cannot be implemented in later ages, you seem to regard this as something deeply taboo. In my humble view, it does no discredit to the Three Dynasties. For what we now call the institutions of the Three Dynasties are all merely their outward forms; no one has yet grasped their underlying intent. If that intent were truly grasped, could it be put into practice without ill effects only in our own age? It could be so applied even for hundreds and thousands of generations. Thus I have ventured to draw this analogy: the intent behind the institutions established by the ancient emperors and kings, which can be put into practice through hundreds and thousands of generations, resembles Heaven’s primordial vital energy, circulating and moving without cessation. The outward forms of their institutions, which change with the times, resemble Heaven’s Five Phases and two manifestations of yin and yang, beginning and ending, rising and falling, cycling without exhaustion. How could these be made uniform? Thus those skilled in governing emulate the intent of antiquity without clinging to its outward forms. That is all.

Nevertheless, anyone who wishes to emulate antiquity must first govern himself. Suppose one merely wishes to grasp the intent of the ancient emperors and kings, while one’s own intentions are perhaps constrained by attachment to self: then one cannot relinquish that attachment and follow the common good of all under Heaven. Or, if one is blinded by self-…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
用則不能虛以稽衆論之是或狃於柔懦
則不能斷以袪浮議之惑或蔽於近小則
不能明以燭幽隱之情彼其執以爲古之
意者將出於一巳之見而非帝王之本然
其因仍故事也必失於偷惰變易法制也
必失於紛更雖有過人之資必爲之志亦
終爲漢文之謙讓未遑宋神之偏信獨斷
而可不戒哉故爲人君者必有格致之學
以明乎天下之理必有誠正之功以踐乎
===
天下之理然後能識古帝王之意而所謂
致三代之隆建萬世之長策者可得而言
焉是又執事未發之意也謹對
第五問
潘仲驂
同考試官教諭馬批足食足兵國政之大也
子能區處得宜是有先憂之志者詞亦足以發之
參之他策俱優錄此鼎甞一臠矣
考試官教授何批其人存則其政舉注之
punctuated:
用，則不能虛以稽衆論之是；或狃於柔懦，則不能斷以袪浮議之惑；或蔽於近小，則不能明以燭幽隱之情。彼其執以爲古之意者，將出於一巳之見，而非帝王之本然。其因仍故事也，必失於偷惰；變易法制也，必失於紛更。雖有過人之資、必爲之志，亦終爲漢文之謙讓未遑、宋神之偏信獨斷，而可不戒哉？故爲人君者，必有格致之學，以明乎天下之理；必有誠正之功，以踐乎天下之理。然後能識古帝王之意，而所謂致三代之隆、建萬世之長策者，可得而言焉。是又執事未發之意也。謹對。

第五問
潘仲驂

同考試官教諭馬批：足食足兵，國政之大也。子能區處得宜，是有先憂之志者，詞亦足以發之。參之他策，俱優，錄此鼎甞一臠矣。

考試官教授何批：「其人存，則其政舉。」注之
translation_en:
…reliance on his own judgment, he cannot approach matters with an open mind to examine what is right in the opinions of others. If habituated to weakness and timidity, he cannot act decisively to dispel the confusion of idle discussions; if confined to immediate and petty concerns, he cannot see clearly into hidden circumstances. What he insists is the intent of antiquity will then arise from his own individual views, rather than from the true intentions of the ancient emperors and kings. In adhering to precedents, he will inevitably lapse into indolence; in altering laws and institutions, he will inevitably lapse into disruptive changes. Even with exceptional abilities and a determination to act, he will ultimately fall into Emperor Wen of Han’s modest deference and failure to find time to act, or Emperor Shenzong of Song’s one-sided trust and arbitrary decisions. Can one fail to take warning?

Thus a ruler must pursue the learning of investigating things and extending knowledge, so as to understand the principles of the world, and undertake the work of making his intentions sincere and rectifying his mind, so as to put those principles into practice. Only then can he recognize the intentions of the ancient emperors and kings, and only then can one speak of attaining the flourishing rule of the Three Dynasties and establishing enduring policies for all ages. This, too, is an intention that you, honored examiners, have left unstated. Respectfully submitted in reply.

Fifth Question
Pan Zhongcan

Comment by Associate Examiner Ma, Instructor: Ensuring sufficient food and sufficient troops are great affairs of state. You have planned their management appropriately, showing an aspiration to be the first to take thought for the realm’s troubles; your language also adequately expresses this aspiration. Comparing this with your other policy essays, all are excellent. Recording this one is like tasting a single morsel from the cauldron.

Comment by Examiner He, Professor: “When the right men are present, their government is put into effect.” [The following fragment, 注之, is unclear.] …

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
弊何患焉此文盡之
考試官教授高批是識時務者
對財猶水也水勢易渙以瀦之而為利兵
猶火也火勢易潜以煽之而為明夫亦因
其勢而利導之非有求於水火之外者也
明此則可與論救弊之理不必求新於常
法之外苦用力於其法之所無而更張之
唯於常法之所有者順逆而整齊之則因
地之利可以足國因人之力可以足兵執
===
事愛民體國之心可無終慮矣何則海育
地產財賦充饒浙固東南之富區也乃今
一遇水旱輒議勸借夫勸借之法亦黃香
之不得已於漢者耳追呼之苦倍于徵需
濡沫之利豈堪賑貸毋亦有因其勢而順
導之者乎蓋浙之民浮而侈夫其導之以
質乎專逐末者驅之於田畝尚奢侈者教
之以節儉而又以身先之痛加抑損力為
節制用民之財若取諸家用民之力若出
punctuated:
弊何患焉？此文盡之。
考試官教授高批：是識時務者。
對：財猶水也，水勢易渙，以瀦之而為利；兵猶火也，火勢易潜，以煽之而為明。夫亦因其勢而利導之，非有求於水火之外者也。明此，則可與論救弊之理，不必求新於常法之外，苦用力於其法之所無而更張之。唯於常法之所有者，順逆而整齊之，則因地之利可以足國，因人之力可以足兵，執事愛民體國之心可無終慮矣。何則？海育地產，財賦充饒，浙固東南之富區也。乃今一遇水旱，輒議勸借。夫勸借之法，亦黃香之不得已於漢者耳。追呼之苦倍于徵需，濡沫之利豈堪賑貸？毋亦有因其勢而順導之者乎？蓋浙之民浮而侈，夫其導之以質乎？專逐末者，驅之於田畝；尚奢侈者，教之以節儉。而又以身先之，痛加抑損，力為節制。用民之財若取諸家，用民之力若出
translation_en:
…what need is there to fear abuses? This essay treats the matter fully.
Examiner Gao, a Professor, comments: This is someone who understands the affairs of the times.
Your servant replies: Wealth is like water: water readily disperses, but when impounded it becomes useful. Military strength is like fire: fire readily subsides, but when fanned it gives light. One need only guide their inherent tendencies to beneficial ends, without seeking anything beyond water and fire themselves. Whoever understands this can discuss the principles of remedying abuses. There is no need to seek innovations beyond established methods, laboriously striving after what those methods lack in order to alter them. Simply work with what established methods already contain, encouraging or checking their tendencies to bring them into order. Then the advantages of the land can amply provision the state, and the strength of the people can amply supply the army. You, sir, with your concern for the people and devotion to the state, need no longer be troubled by endless anxiety.
Why is this? With the sea's bounty and the land's produce, wealth and tax revenues are abundant: Zhejiang has always been a rich region of the southeast. Yet nowadays, whenever flood or drought occurs, proposals immediately arise to solicit loans. Soliciting loans was merely a measure to which Huang Xiang resorted under the Han when he had no alternative. The hardship of repeated official summonses is twice that of ordinary exactions; how can such meager mutual aid suffice for relief grants and loans? Might there not be a way to work with prevailing tendencies and guide them appropriately? The people of Zhejiang are frivolous and extravagant; should they not be guided toward simplicity? Those devoted exclusively to secondary occupations should be directed to the fields, and those who prize extravagance should be taught thrift. Moreover, one must lead them by personal example, rigorously curbing expenditure and exerting oneself to maintain restraint. Use the people's wealth as though taking it from one's own household; use the people's labor as though it came from…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
諸身所謂冗役冗費凡可以蠹吾財者皆
盡去而不靳又必於預備倉之法而廣之
如李悝之平糴熟則斂之於官饑則散之
於民耿壽昌之常平賤則增價以糴貴則
減價以糶隨處可設也若然則民財可阜
倉廩可實有備無患而勸借之議容可免
矣枕山臂江果悍自負浙固東南之巨鎮
也乃今一遇有警輒稱招募夫招募之法
亦韓愈之不得已於唐者耳供給勞費倍
===
干養兵經歷騷擾比諸剽掠毋亦有因其
法而整齊之者乎蓋浙之兵惰而驕夫其
整之以經乎壯者在伍毋役以私富者在
行毋縱以賄而又必身先之甲胄與同甘
苦與同月給之餉無後其時日練以法無
惰其力而其為商為賈凡所以荒武事者
皆痛懲而必革又必合吾民兵而教之如
吳子所謂一人教十人十人教百人百人
教千人千人教萬人孫子所謂教目知形
punctuated:
諸身。所謂冗役冗費，凡可以蠹吾財者，皆盡去而不靳。又必於預備倉之法而廣之，如李悝之平糴，熟則斂之於官，饑則散之於民；耿壽昌之常平，賤則增價以糴，貴則減價以糶，隨處可設也。若然，則民財可阜，倉廩可實，有備無患，而勸借之議容可免矣。
枕山臂江，果悍自負，浙固東南之巨鎮也。乃今一遇有警，輒稱招募。夫招募之法，亦韓愈之不得已於唐者耳。供給勞費倍干養兵，經歷騷擾比諸剽掠，毋亦有因其法而整齊之者乎？蓋浙之兵惰而驕，夫其整之以經乎？壯者在伍，毋役以私；富者在行，毋縱以賄。而又必身先之，甲胄與同，甘苦與同。月給之餉，無後其時；日練以法，無惰其力。而其為商為賈，凡所以荒武事者，皆痛懲而必革。又必合吾民兵而教之，如吳子所謂一人教十人，十人教百人，百人教千人，千人教萬人；孫子所謂教目知形
translation_en:
…from one's own person. All superfluous labor services and expenditures—everything that can drain our resources—must be eliminated without reluctance. The system of reserve granaries must also be expanded. There is Li Kui's system of equitable grain purchases: in abundant years, grain is gathered into government stores; in famine years, it is distributed to the people. There is also Geng Shouchang's ever-normal granary system: when grain is cheap, the purchase price is raised; when it is dear, the selling price is lowered. These arrangements can be established everywhere. In this way, the people's resources can increase and the granaries can be filled. With preparations made, calamity need not be feared, and proposals to solicit loans may be dispensed with.
With mountains at its back and rivers at its arms, bold and fierce in its self-confidence, Zhejiang is indeed a great stronghold of the southeast. Yet nowadays, whenever an alarm arises, there is immediately talk of recruiting troops. Recruitment was, after all, only a measure to which Han Yu resorted out of necessity under the Tang. The labor and expense of provisioning recruits are twice those of maintaining troops [?], and the disturbance they cause wherever they pass is comparable to plunder. Might there not be a way to put them in order by working through the existing system? Zhejiang's soldiers are indolent and arrogant: should they not be brought to order through regular discipline? Let the able-bodied remain in the ranks, without employing them for private service; let the wealthy remain in their units, without excusing them in return for bribes. One must also lead them personally, sharing the wearing of armor and helmet, and sharing their hardships and comforts. Their monthly pay must not be late; they must drill daily according to prescribed methods, without slackening their efforts. Their engagement in trade and commerce, and everything else that causes them to neglect military duties, must be sternly punished and resolutely abolished. Our militia must also be assembled and trained, as Master Wu says: one man trains ten, ten train a hundred, a hundred train a thousand, and a thousand train ten thousand; and as Master Sun says: train the eyes to recognize shapes…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
色之旗敎耳知號令之數敎足知進退之
度敎手知長短之兵敎心知賞罰之用者
無日可廢也若然則習熟藝精志定氣飽
有備無患而招募之議容可免矣乃若鹽
徒起於商販海寇起於番舶皆以死覓利
愈撲而不可滅者也漢人牢盆之法旣不
足以盡其奸則整齊之不可以已也何則
鹽法之弊所禁不在於鹽徒當在於竈戶
鹽徒之禁又不當在於所治當在於他方
===
故在所治則當盡弛挑負之禁凡欲市者
皆給之引輕其直以抵月報之數其在竈
戶當嚴私賣之法凡欲市於人者皆驗之
引時其直以爲竈戶之利捕鹽徒兵不必
獲挑負之鹽徒特令查私賣之竈戶仍令
出鹽地方一切居民得互相舉發有私賣
者治以重典則他方鹽徒入吾境已無可
市之鹽出其境又有盤獲之禁無利可趨
有害可畏自將歸干故土以業生矣若海
punctuated:
色之旗，敎耳知號令之數，敎足知進退之度，敎手知長短之兵，敎心知賞罰之用者，無日可廢也。若然，則習熟藝精，志定氣飽，有備無患，而招募之議容可免矣。
乃若鹽徒起於商販，海寇起於番舶，皆以死覓利，愈撲而不可滅者也。漢人牢盆之法旣不足以盡其奸，則整齊之不可以已也。何則？鹽法之弊，所禁不在於鹽徒，當在於竈戶；鹽徒之禁，又不當在於所治，當在於他方。
故在所治，則當盡弛挑負之禁，凡欲市者，皆給之引，輕其直，以抵月報之數。其在竈戶，當嚴私賣之法，凡欲市於人者，皆驗之引，時其直，以爲竈戶之利。捕鹽徒兵，不必獲挑負之鹽徒，特令查私賣之竈戶。仍令出鹽地方一切居民得互相舉發，有私賣者，治以重典。則他方鹽徒入吾境，已無可市之鹽；出其境，又有盤獲之禁。無利可趨，有害可畏，自將歸干故土，以業生矣。若海
translation_en:
…the colors of flags; teaching the ears to recognize the system of signals and commands; teaching the feet the prescribed movements for advancing and retreating; teaching the hands the use of long and short weapons; and teaching the mind how rewards and punishments operate—none of this may be neglected for a single day. If this is done, practice will become familiar and skills refined, resolve will be steady and morale full. With preparations made, there will be no cause for anxiety, and proposals to recruit additional troops may perhaps be dispensed with.
As for salt smugglers, they arise from traders, while maritime raiders arise from foreign shipping. All risk death in pursuit of profit; however vigorously they are suppressed, they cannot be eradicated. Since the Han system of government salt-boiling pans was insufficient to eliminate all such illicit practices, efforts to bring them under orderly control must not cease. Why is this? In addressing abuses of the salt laws, restrictions should target salt-producing households rather than salt smugglers. Restrictions on salt smugglers, moreover, should be enforced elsewhere rather than within the jurisdiction under one's administration.
Thus, within one's jurisdiction, all prohibitions on carrying salt should be relaxed. Everyone wishing to purchase it should receive a permit, and the price should be lowered, with the proceeds counted toward the amount reported monthly. For salt-producing households, the laws against private sales should be strictly enforced. Whenever they wish to sell to someone, the buyer's permit should be inspected; prices should be adjusted to the time [?], to benefit the salt-producing households. Troops charged with apprehending salt smugglers need not arrest those carrying salt; they should simply be ordered to investigate salt-producing households making private sales. All residents of salt-producing localities should also be permitted to report one another's violations, and anyone making private sales should be punished under severe statutes. Salt smugglers from elsewhere would then enter our territory and find no salt available for illicit purchase; on leaving it, they would also face prohibitions enforced by inspection and arrest. With no profit to pursue and penalties to fear, they would naturally return to their native places [?] and pursue occupations for their livelihood. As for maritime…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
宼弗靖則武職之罪也泊蒙衝于近地而
威望不著老弱守舟而巡警不嚴又有陽
爲詰捕而陰受其賂者是以海宼時生無
所忌畏使船皆在鎭軍皆在船又時習水
戰以示之威時出遊𪈠而警之備則何萑
澤之弗靖哉乃若小民稱貸起於饑寒地
利未獲由之兼併皆忍死求生欲已而不
能自己者宋人青苗之法旣不可行之於
官則利導之不可以已也何則民窮之弊
===
在官居其十九富豪居其十一法外徵求
剥膚椎髓則其勢不得不稱貸而輸之官
非時之役勞筋苦骨而其力不得以自盡
於南畝終歲勤動少有所獲則追呼之吏
峻其科所貸之家索其息則又哀呼求假
於富豪之前矣負息旣多勢必有訟大吏
則臨之刑威而責償旦夕小吏則受人賄
賂而淹禁逾年二者相因展轉交害如之
何民不窮且盜也則民財就盡非長吏之
punctuated: 宼弗靖，則武職之罪也。泊蒙衝于近地，而威望不著；老弱守舟，而巡警不嚴；又有陽爲詰捕而陰受其賂者，是以海宼時生，無所忌畏。使船皆在鎭，軍皆在船，又時習水戰以示之威，時出遊𪈠而警之備，則何萑澤之弗靖哉？乃若小民稱貸，起於饑寒；地利未獲，由之兼併。皆忍死求生，欲已而不能自己者。宋人青苗之法旣不可行之於官，則利導之不可以已也。何則？民窮之弊，在官居其十九，富豪居其十一。法外徵求，剥膚椎髓，則其勢不得不稱貸而輸之官；非時之役，勞筋苦骨，而其力不得以自盡於南畝。終歲勤動，少有所獲，則追呼之吏峻其科，所貸之家索其息，則又哀呼求假於富豪之前矣。負息旣多，勢必有訟。大吏則臨之刑威，而責償旦夕；小吏則受人賄賂，而淹禁逾年。二者相因，展轉交害，如之何民不窮且盜也？則民財就盡，非長吏之
translation_en:
…if the pirates are not subdued, the fault lies with the military officers. Their armored warships lie anchored nearby, yet inspire no awe; the old and weak guard the vessels, while patrols and watches are lax. There are even those who openly claim to investigate and arrest the pirates while secretly accepting their bribes. Thus pirates repeatedly arise, with nothing to restrain or frighten them. If every ship were stationed at its garrison and every soldier aboard his ship, if they regularly practiced naval warfare to display their might and regularly went out on patrol [?] to maintain vigilant readiness, how could these bandit haunts remain unpacified?

As for ordinary people, they borrow because they suffer hunger and cold; they fail to enjoy the yield of the land because of its engrossment by the powerful [?]. They all endure the threat of death in their struggle to survive, wishing to stop borrowing but unable to do so. Since the Green Sprouts system of the Song cannot be implemented by the authorities, efforts to guide the people toward beneficial means of livelihood must not cease. Why is this? Of the causes of the people's impoverishment, officials account for nine-tenths, and wealthy magnates for one-tenth. Exactions beyond the law strip their skin and pound their marrow, leaving them no choice but to borrow in order to pay the authorities. Labor services imposed at improper seasons strain their sinews and torment their bones, preventing them from devoting their full strength to the fields. After toiling all year, they obtain a little, only for the clerks who pursue them for payment to press their assessments harshly, and for the households from which they borrowed to demand interest. Once again they must plead pitifully before the wealthy for loans.

Once their interest debts have mounted, litigation inevitably follows. Senior officials confront them with the threat of punishment and demand repayment within a day; subordinate clerks accept bribes and keep them imprisoned for more than a year. These two practices reinforce each other, inflicting harm in an ever-turning cycle. How could the people fail to become impoverished and turn to banditry? When the people's resources are thus nearly exhausted, is this not the local magistrates'…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
責乎必於山郷水區凡可以厚其生者與
之無禁使得以盡自然之利賦稅徭役凡
所以需于上者徵之以時使得以受一分
之賜事為之制曲為之防無名征求一切
可罷也貪暴多取悉力與裁也則又何民
瘼之弗蘇哉是故財以裕民非推所有以
與之也兵以止盜非取諸外以昌之也民
自有財導之則源開國自有兵整之則威
振特患濟之者之無其人耳有其人矣或
===
病於職業之弗專有其職矣又病於遷徙
之無常或以議論之不一或以奉行之弗
稱是以法久弊生財殫兵弱以至於此苟
忠惠公清上下皆有其人節制奉行上下
皆一其心相與利導而整齊之則兵寓于
農緩急得有所賴富藏于民水旱不能為
災此其可行之道固不在遠也未識以為
何如
punctuated: 責乎？必於山郷水區，凡可以厚其生者，與之無禁，使得以盡自然之利；賦稅徭役，凡所以需于上者，徵之以時，使得以受一分之賜。事為之制，曲為之防，無名征求，一切可罷也；貪暴多取，悉力與裁也。則又何民瘼之弗蘇哉？是故財以裕民，非推所有以與之也；兵以止盜，非取諸外以昌之也。民自有財，導之則源開；國自有兵，整之則威振。特患濟之者之無其人耳。有其人矣，或病於職業之弗專；有其職矣，又病於遷徙之無常；或以議論之不一，或以奉行之弗稱。是以法久弊生，財殫兵弱，以至於此。苟忠惠公清，上下皆有其人；節制奉行，上下皆一其心，相與利導而整齊之，則兵寓于農，緩急得有所賴；富藏于民，水旱不能為災。此其可行之道，固不在遠也。未識以為何如？
translation_en:
…the responsibility of the local administrators? In mountain villages and waterside districts, whatever can enrich the people's livelihood must be made available to them without prohibition, so that they may fully enjoy nature's benefits. Taxes and labor services—all that is exacted to meet the needs of those above—must be levied at the proper times, so that the people may receive some measure of relief. Establish regulations for every matter and safeguards for every contingency. All unauthorized exactions can be abolished, and every effort must be made to curb the excessive demands of greedy and oppressive officials. What suffering of the people would then remain unrelieved?

Thus, using wealth to enrich the people does not mean handing over everything one possesses to them; using troops to suppress bandits does not mean drawing upon outside resources to strengthen them. The people already have sources of wealth: guide them, and those sources will open up. The state already has troops: put them in order, and their might will be manifest. The sole concern is the lack of suitable men to carry this through. Even when suitable men are found, their duties may be insufficiently focused; even when they have appropriate posts, they may be transferred unpredictably. Sometimes deliberations fail to yield agreement; sometimes implementation falls short. Thus, as institutions endure, abuses arise, wealth is exhausted, and military strength declines, until matters reach their present state.

If loyal, benevolent, impartial, and incorruptible men held office at every level, and if those above and below were of one mind in command and implementation, working together to guide resources to beneficial use and bring affairs into order, then soldiers would be incorporated among the farmers, providing a dependable force in times of need; wealth would be stored among the people, so that floods and droughts could not bring disaster. This practicable course is surely close at hand. I wonder what you think of it?

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
浙江鄉試錄後序
嘉靖甲午八月癸亥浙江鄉
試錄成故事元述宜有言以
勗多士曰夫士幸而生
聖明之世又幸以其藝升於有司
將進而立於
天子之廷以其氏名與其文詞梓
===
而為錄將登諸
天府傳示海內及於無窮若爾多
士今日之事其可謂至榮也
已雖然人榮之則必有以責
之責之而不副則必罪且尤
之是故其升於有司進而立
於
punctuated:
浙江鄉試錄後序

嘉靖甲午八月癸亥，浙江鄉試錄成。故事，元述宜有言以勗多士，曰：「夫士幸而生聖明之世，又幸以其藝升於有司，將進而立於天子之廷，以其氏名與其文詞梓而為錄，將登諸天府，傳示海內，及於無窮。若爾多士今日之事，其可謂至榮也已。雖然，人榮之，則必有以責之；責之而不副，則必罪且尤之。是故，其升於有司，進而立於
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Zhejiang Provincial Examination

On the guihai day of the eighth month in the jiawu year of the Jiajing reign (1534), the Record of the Zhejiang Provincial Examination was completed. Following precedent, I, Yuanshu, ought to offer some words to encourage the assembled scholars:

“A scholar is fortunate to be born in an age of sage and enlightened rule, and fortunate again to be selected by the responsible officials for his literary skill. He will advance to stand at the court of the Son of Heaven. His name and compositions are carved on woodblocks and printed as a record, which will be deposited in the imperial archives and circulated throughout the realm for all time. What you scholars have attained today may indeed be called the highest honor. Nevertheless, when people honor someone, they necessarily expect something of him. If he fails to meet their expectations, they will surely condemn and reproach him. Thus, when he is selected by the responsible officials and advances to stand at …

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
天子之廷也善固藉以顯而惡亦
因之以彰其梓而為錄登諸
天府傳示廣遠也善固資之有聞
而惡亦無以自覆然則夫人
之所謂榮乃吾所深懼者也
爾多士亦嘗思所以居其榮
者乎古稱太上有立德其次
===
有立功其次有立言三者謂
之不朽
國家之制每三歲一舉士每舉
合海内之衆蓋千餘人至考
其所終有能具是三者寡矣
夫然吾未見榮之能居也而
況反道敗德自速戾以負於
punctuated:
天子之廷也，善固藉以顯，而惡亦因之以彰。其梓而為錄，登諸天府，傳示廣遠也，善固資之有聞，而惡亦無以自覆。然則夫人之所謂榮，乃吾所深懼者也。爾多士亦嘗思所以居其榮者乎？古稱太上有立德，其次有立功，其次有立言，三者謂之不朽。

國家之制，每三歲一舉士，每舉合海内之衆，蓋千餘人。至考其所終，有能具是三者寡矣。夫然，吾未見榮之能居也，而況反道敗德，自速戾，以負於
translation_en:
…at the Son of Heaven’s court, their goodness indeed gains prominence thereby, but their wickedness likewise becomes manifest. When their names and writings are printed in a record, deposited in the imperial repository, and circulated far and wide, their goodness indeed becomes known thereby, but neither can their wickedness remain concealed. Thus, what others call an honor is precisely what I deeply fear. Have you, assembled scholars, ever considered how to prove worthy of that honor? An ancient saying holds that the highest achievement is to establish virtue, the next to establish meritorious deeds, and the next to establish enduring words. These three are called imperishable.

Under the institutions of the state, scholars are selected every three years. Each selection brings together more than a thousand men from throughout the realm. Yet when one examines what they ultimately accomplish, few have been able to achieve all three of these things. Such being the case, I have yet to see that they can prove worthy of their honor—how much less those who turn against the Way, corrupt their virtue, and bring guilt upon themselves, thereby failing…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
聖明者歟爾多士勉之毋溺於榮
知以為懼焉可也夫浙天下
首藩也
聖天子在上豈弟作人觀文成化
浙之漸被尤深士養於庠序
既充然有所蘊乃試之日監
臨御史于立朝夕儆于簾内
===
外之吏惟公惟慎以仰副
聖天子側席求賢之心爾多士又
皆選而拔其尤固足以居其
榮而無慊者元述獨慮夫志
之怠也故有以勗多士其尚
毋以予言為贅也哉遂次其
說書諸末簡
punctuated:
聖明者歟？爾多士勉之，毋溺於榮，知以為懼焉可也。
夫浙，天下首藩也。聖天子在上，豈弟作人，觀文成化，浙之漸被尤深。士養於庠序，既充然有所蘊，乃試之日，監臨御史于立朝夕儆于簾内外之吏，惟公惟慎，以仰副聖天子側席求賢之心。爾多士又皆選而拔其尤，固足以居其榮而無慊者。元述獨慮夫志之怠也，故有以勗多士，其尚毋以予言為贅也哉！遂次其說，書諸末簡。
translation_en:
…the sagely and enlightened sovereign? You scholars must exert yourselves. Do not become absorbed in honor; recognize in it a cause for apprehension, and that will suffice.
Zhejiang is the foremost province of the realm. The sagely Son of Heaven reigns above, nurturing men of talent with gracious benevolence and bringing about moral transformation through cultivated learning. Zhejiang has received these influences especially deeply. Its scholars, nurtured in the schools, have already accumulated substantial learning and virtue. When the examination took place, the Supervising Official, Censor Yu Li, admonished the officials within and outside the examination curtain morning and evening to act with impartiality and care, thereby fulfilling the sagely Son of Heaven’s eager desire to seek worthy men. You scholars have all been selected as the outstanding among your fellows, and certainly deserve to enjoy this honor without misgivings. I, Yuanshu, worry only that your resolve may slacken. Thus I have offered these words to encourage you scholars; may you not regard my words as superfluous! I have accordingly arranged these remarks and written them on the concluding leaves.

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
浙江鄉試錄序
維
皇嗣極十有三載秋迺浙江鄉試
簡膺守臣聘發維揚渡江而
南巡按御史張子立迓于館
遂會敎授何元述敎諭易時
中陳全毛豸曾嘉慶吳煥章
===
李粹芳馬呈瑞訓導李彬率
入簾御史曰浙之文其敝乎
敢厪執事簡聞而懼甚試之
明日得卷閱之如御史言迺
曰學術弗正心術罔以端宜
御史有憂也失今弗圖蔑有
紀矣雖然二三子淆焉爾矣
punctuated:
浙江鄉試錄序

維皇嗣極十有三載秋，迺浙江鄉試。簡膺守臣聘，發維揚，渡江而南。巡按御史張子立迓于館，遂會敎授何元述、敎諭易時中、陳全、毛豸、曾嘉慶、吳煥章、李粹芳、馬呈瑞、訓導李彬，率入簾。御史曰：「浙之文，其敝乎！敢厪執事。」簡聞而懼甚。試之明日，得卷閱之，如御史言。迺曰：「學術弗正，心術罔以端，宜御史有憂也。失今弗圖，蔑有紀矣。雖然，二三子淆焉爾矣。
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Zhejiang Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the thirteenth year since the Emperor succeeded to the throne, the Zhejiang Provincial Examination was held. I, Jian, accepted an invitation from the provincial authorities, set out from Weiyang, and crossed the Yangzi southward. The Regional Inspector, Zhang Zili, welcomed me at my lodgings. I then joined Professor He Yuanshu; Instructors Yi Shizhong, Chen Quan, Mao Zhi, Zeng Jiaqing, Wu Huanzhang, Li Cuifang, and Ma Chengrui; and Assistant Instructor Li Bin, and we entered the examiners’ enclosure together. The censor said: “The writing of Zhejiang—has it not fallen into decline? I venture to trouble you with this responsibility.” Hearing this, I, Jian, was deeply apprehensive. On the day after the examination, I received the scripts and read them; they were as the censor had said. I then said: “When the pursuit of learning is not correct, the disposition of the mind cannot be set right. It is fitting that the censor should be concerned. If we miss this opportunity and do not address the matter now, there will be no standards left. Even so, it is only a few among you who are confused.…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
夫文者言之飾也而道之昌
也善言者不勦說以附同不
襲名以亂道獵言匪基誠僞
浮矣詭言無章授受駮矣紕
言異製規度侈矣文之渙也
故稱敝焉是附同而亂道者
也昔者先王之建國也彰六
===
藝以丕文敦三德以崇化習
察而言範物軌而行臧是故
擴聚攄蓄釐澆歸雅摛精掞
華弘其言也而非摽也鮮不
程矣今
天子明聖慎德考言垂休彝作人
有司者將之以其
punctuated:
夫文者，言之飾也，而道之昌也。善言者，不勦說以附同，不襲名以亂道。獵言匪基，誠僞浮矣；詭言無章，授受駮矣；紕言異製，規度侈矣。文之渙也，故稱敝焉，是附同而亂道者也。昔者先王之建國也，彰六藝以丕文，敦三德以崇化。習察而言範，物軌而行臧。是故擴聚攄蓄，釐澆歸雅，摛精掞華，弘其言也，而非摽也，鮮不程矣。
今天子明聖，慎德考言，垂休彝，作人。有司者將之以其
translation_en:
Writing embellishes speech and brings the Way to flourishing expression. Those skilled in expression do not plagiarize others’ explanations merely to agree with them, nor appropriate established names to confound the Way. When words are scavenged without a foundation, sincerity and falsehood become superficial [?]; when speech is aberrant and lacks order, what is taught and received becomes contradictory; when faulty expressions depart from established forms, standards and measures become excessive. Such is the dissolution of writing, and hence it is called corrupt: it follows others in agreement while confounding the Way. In ancient times, when the former kings established their states, they made the Six Arts manifest to magnify culture and strengthened the Three Virtues to elevate moral transformation. Through practice and discernment, speech became exemplary; affairs followed proper rules, and conduct became good [?]. Thus, they expanded what they gathered and expressed what they had stored, corrected frivolity and returned to refinement, and unfolded the essence and displayed the splendor of their learning. They enlarged their expression without ostentation, and little failed to serve as a model.
The present Son of Heaven is enlightened and sagely. He attends carefully to virtue and examines speech, bequeaths admirable enduring norms, and cultivates men of talent. The responsible officials carry this forward according to his…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
制也未嘗不再三焉維茲全浙
自古在昔文獻足徵其孰以
爲虞而迺敝也不亦甚乎矧
宣治采風匪言奚以故君子
修之於其言也寔昭明德吾
聞之也有德者必有言言之
而罔德斯之謂蹊焉于何其
===
賴文矣將焉用之簡也無良
罔敢攸知罔敢攸受也雖然
二三子淆焉爾矣或有賦鶴
鳴之首章者迺憮然曰命簡
哉茲殫力覈精𫔎諸弗式諧
以庶言得九十人敷如理如
有孚粲如其吳越之良乎嗚
punctuated:
制也，未嘗不再三焉。維茲全浙，自古在昔，文獻足徵，其孰以爲虞？而迺敝也，不亦甚乎？矧宣治采風，匪言奚以？故君子修之於其言也，寔昭明德。吾聞之也：「有德者必有言。」言之而罔德，斯之謂蹊焉，于何其賴？文矣，將焉用之？簡也無良，罔敢攸知，罔敢攸受也。
雖然，二三子淆焉爾矣。或有賦《鶴鳴》之首章者，迺憮然曰：「命簡哉！」茲殫力覈精，𫔎諸弗式，諧以庶言，得九十人，敷如，理如，有孚，粲如，其吳越之良乎！嗚
translation_en:
…the prescribed regulations, never failing to attend to them repeatedly. Throughout Zhejiang, from ancient times onward, writings and worthy men have furnished ample testimony. Who would have thought there was cause for concern? Yet matters have deteriorated—is this not extreme? Moreover, in making good government manifest and gathering evidence of local customs, what could one use if not words? Thus, when the gentleman cultivates his speech, he truly makes his luminous virtue manifest. I have heard it said: “Those who possess virtue invariably have words.” To speak without virtue is to take a bypath [?]; what reliance can be placed upon it? There may be literary refinement, but what use will it serve? I, Jian, lack worth, and dare neither claim discernment nor accept such writing [?].
Even so, it is only a few among you who have become confused. Someone recited the first stanza of “The Crane Cries” from the Book of Odes, whereupon I said with troubled reflection: “The charge falls to me, Jian!” Accordingly, we exhausted our strength in scrutinizing the finest points, rejecting what failed to conform to the standards [?], and reaching agreement through our various assessments. We selected ninety men: expansive and orderly in expression, possessing sincerity and resplendent in accomplishment—surely these are the worthy men of Wu and Yue! Ah …

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
呼爾多士固
社稷之隸也毋多爾文其將自
謀也則令名是圖令圖天所
賛也簡寔麗焉而資之以永
也然有爽言之懼矣廼以告
于御史御史曰古之遺訓也
垂之而稽其符也肅而彥約
===
而逖胥而不淪是役也御史
子立寔監臨焉維提調則左
布政使党以平左參政洪珠
維監試則按察使路迎副使
陳儒就試之士二千七百有
竒提學僉事徐階簡也維時
理鹺監察御史盧瓚貞勵士
punctuated:
呼！爾多士固社稷之隸也，毋多爾文，其將自謀也，則令名是圖。令圖，天所賛也，簡寔麗焉，而資之以永也。然有爽言之懼矣，廼以告于御史。御史曰：「古之遺訓也，垂之而稽其符也。」肅而彥，約而逖，胥而不淪。
是役也，御史子立寔監臨焉。維提調則左布政使党以平、左參政洪珠，維監試則按察使路迎、副使陳儒。就試之士二千七百有竒，提學僉事徐階簡也。維時理鹺監察御史盧瓚貞勵士
translation_en:
…Alas! You scholars are indeed servants of the altars of soil and grain. Do not take excessive pride in your literary accomplishments. If you would plan for yourselves, seek a worthy reputation. Worthy aspirations receive Heaven’s approval. I, Jian [?], am truly bound to this principle and draw upon it to secure lasting worth. Yet I feared that my words might prove mistaken, so I reported them to the censor. The censor said: “These are teachings bequeathed by the ancients. Hand them down and examine how they are borne out.” Reverent and accomplished, restrained and far-reaching, together avoiding decline [?].
For this examination, Censor Zili served as Supervising Official. The Proctors were Dang Yiping, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Hong Zhu, Left Administration Vice Commissioner. The examination overseers were Lu Ying, Surveillance Commissioner, and Chen Ru, Surveillance Vice Commissioner. More than 2,700 scholars presented themselves for examination; they had been selected by Xu Jie, Surveillance Assistant Commissioner in charge of education. At this time, Lu Zan, Investigating Censor administering the salt monopoly, steadfastly encouraged the scholars’ …

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
風克敦丕績工部主事程嘉
行南京戶部主事王文儒慶
觀厥成允叶嘉樂右布政使
張原明右叅政萬廷彩郭日
休副使王卿戴金魏綸左叅
議范韶吳山右叅議姜儀僉
事陸冕朱子和莊用賓焦煜
===
方紀達及期原明遷代之者
任忠咸後先賛襄罔或弗共
都指揮僉事李節李光榮署
都指揮僉事張大本湯慶胥
閑衛惟虔法得備書告成事
將歌鹿鳴以好之也併梓廼
文以
punctuated: 風，克敦丕績。工部主事程嘉行、南京戶部主事王文儒慶觀厥成，允叶嘉樂。右布政使張原明、右叅政萬廷彩、郭日休，副使王卿、戴金、魏綸，左叅議范韶、吳山，右叅議姜儀，僉事陸冕、朱子和、莊用賓、焦煜、方紀達，及期原明遷，代之者任忠，咸後先賛襄，罔或弗共。都指揮僉事李節、李光榮，署都指揮僉事張大本、湯慶，胥閑衛惟虔，法得備書。告成事，將歌《鹿鳴》以好之也，併梓廼文以
translation_en:
…conduct among the scholars, successfully advancing this great undertaking. Cheng Jiaxing, Secretary in the Ministry of Works, and Wang Wenru, Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue, rejoiced to witness its completion, sharing fully in the happy occasion.
Zhang Yuanming, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner; Wan Tingcai and Guo Rixiu, Right Administration Vice Commissioners; Wang Qing, Dai Jin, and Wei Lun, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; Fan Shao and Wu Shan, Left Administration Assistant Commissioners; Jiang Yi, Right Administration Assistant Commissioner; and Lu Mian, Zhu Zihe, Zhuang Yongbin, Jiao Yu, and Fang Jida, Surveillance Assistant Commissioners, all contributed their assistance in succession, with none failing in his duties. By the appointed time, Yuanming had been transferred, and Ren Zhong succeeded him and likewise assisted.
Li Jie and Li Guangrong, Assistant Regional Military Commissioners, and Zhang Daben and Tang Qing, acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners, all diligently attended to guarding the examination precincts. In accordance with the prescribed form, they may all be recorded here [?]. Now that the undertaking has been brought to completion, we shall sing “The Deer Call” to express our goodwill toward the successful candidates, and together print their compositions in order to…

translation_en:
Zhejiang Provincial Examination of the Thirteenth Year of Jiajing (1534).

Supervising Official:
Zhang Zili, Regional Inspector of Zhejiang serving as Investigating Censor, had the courtesy name Yuanli and was a native of Huang County, Shandong. He became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the bingxu year.

Proctors:
Dang Yiping, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Zhejiang, had the courtesy name Shouheng and was a native of Jun Subprefecture, Henan. He became a metropolitan graduate in the jiaxu year.
Hong Zhu, Left Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner of Zhejiang, had the courtesy name Yufang and was a native of Putian County, Fujian. He became a metropolitan graduate in the xinsi year.

Examination Monitors:
Lu Ying, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Zhejiang, had the courtesy name Binyang and was a native of Wenshang County, Shandong. He became a metropolitan graduate in the wuchen year.
Chen Ru, Provincial Surveillance Vice Commissioner of Zhejiang, had the courtesy name Ruzong and was registered in an officer household of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard. He became a metropolitan graduate in the guiwei year.

Examiners:
Gao Jian, Professor of the Confucian School of Yangzhou Prefecture in the directly administered metropolitan region, had the courtesy name Gongjing and was a native of Mian Subprefecture, Sichuan. He became a metropolitan graduate in the jichou year.
He Yuanshu, Professor of the Confucian School of Huizhou Prefecture, Guangdong, had the courtesy name Yuanxiao and was a native of Jinjiang County, Fujian. He became a metropolitan graduate in the renchen year.

Associate Examiners:

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰賢哉回也一簞食一瓢飲在陋巷人
不堪其憂回也不改其樂賢哉回也
溥博如天淵泉如淵見而民莫不敬言而
民莫不信行而民莫不說
是集義所生者非義襲而取之也
易
休復之吉以下仁也
===
九五有孚惠心勿問元吉有孚惠我德
與天地相似故不違知周乎萬物而道濟
天下故不過旁行而不流樂天知命故
不憂安土敦乎仁故能愛
夫乾天下之至健也德行恒易以知險夫
坤天下之至順也德行恒簡以知阻
書
帝乃誕敷文德舞干羽于兩階七旬有苗
格
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

子曰：「賢哉，回也！一簞食，一瓢飲，在陋巷，人不堪其憂，回也不改其樂。賢哉，回也！」

溥博如天，淵泉如淵。見而民莫不敬，言而民莫不信，行而民莫不說。

是集義所生者，非義襲而取之也。

易

休復之吉，以下仁也。

九五：有孚惠心，勿問元吉。有孚惠我德。

與天地相似，故不違；知周乎萬物，而道濟天下，故不過；旁行而不流，樂天知命，故不憂；安土敦乎仁，故能愛。

夫乾，天下之至健也，德行恒易以知險；夫坤，天下之至順也，德行恒簡以知阻。

書

帝乃誕敷文德，舞干羽于兩階，七旬有苗格。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The Master said: “How worthy Hui is! With a single basket of food and a single gourd of drink, living in a humble lane, others could not endure the distress, yet Hui does not let it alter his joy. How worthy Hui is!”

He is all-encompassing and vast like Heaven, deep and inexhaustible like an abyss. When he appears, none among the people fail to respect him; when he speaks, none fail to trust him; when he acts, none fail to delight in him.

This [flood-like vital energy] is born of the accumulation of righteous deeds; it cannot be acquired through an isolated act of righteousness.

Book of Changes

The good fortune of a beautiful return comes from placing oneself below a benevolent person.

Nine in the fifth place: There is sincerity and a benevolent heart. Without needing to inquire, there is supreme good fortune. There is sincerity in cherishing my virtue.

He resembles Heaven and Earth and therefore does not run counter to them. His knowledge encompasses the myriad things, and his Way brings aid to all under Heaven; therefore he does not err. He ranges widely without drifting astray. He delights in Heaven and understands its mandate; therefore he has no anxiety. He is content where he dwells and steadfast in benevolence; therefore he is able to love.

Qian [the Creative] is the utmost strength under Heaven. Its virtuous activity is always easy, and thereby it knows danger. Kun [the Receptive] is the utmost compliance under Heaven. Its virtuous activity is always simple, and thereby it knows obstruction.

Book of Documents

The emperor then spread civil virtue far and wide and had dancers perform with shields and plumes between the two stairways. After seventy days, the Youmiao came to submit.

text:
理天下之男敎立六宮以聽天下之內
治以明章婦順此明王之定制也我
朝稽古立法率以道治天下其所以敎之者

書諸書迨我

===

高皇后傳有

punctuated: 理天下之男敎，立六宮以聽天下之內治，以明章婦順。」此明王之定制也。我朝稽古立法，率以道治天下。其所以敎之者，不惟其身敎之懿，而言敎亦至純備。自今觀之，其統治于外以示敎者，有《祖訓》，有《敎民榜》，有《孝順事實》《爲善陰隲》，有《五倫書》諸書。迨我皇上，敬一有箴，五箴有註，陽敎備矣。不知與古帝王之書果有合歟？其輔治于內以示順者，有《高皇后傳》，有仁孝文皇后《內訓》二十章。迨我章聖皇太后，又製爲《女訓》十二章，婦順章矣。不知與古后妃之訓亦相倣歟？夫陽敎不修，陽事不得，適見於天，日爲之食；陰敎不修，陰事不得，適見於天，月爲之食。今自宮闈以達天下，修齊治平之化亦旣協于一
translation_en:
…to regulate the instruction of the men of the realm; he establishes the Six Palaces to attend to the realm’s internal governance and to make manifest women’s obedience.” This is the established institution of enlightened kings. Our dynasty examines antiquity in establishing its laws and consistently governs the realm through the Way. Its means of instruction comprise not only the excellence of personal example: its verbal teachings, too, are utterly pure and comprehensive. Looking at these today, the works that provide instruction through the unified governance of external affairs include the Ancestral Injunctions, the Placard for Instructing the People, True Accounts of Filial Obedience, Doing Good and Hidden Merit, and the Book of the Five Human Relationships. Under our present emperor, there is an admonition on reverent concentration on the One and commentary on the Five Admonitions. Instruction in the yang sphere is thus complete. We ask: do these truly accord with the writings of the emperors and kings of antiquity?

The works that assist internal governance by exemplifying obedience include the Biography of Empress Gao and the twenty chapters of the Inner Instructions by Empress Renxiao Wen. Now our Empress Dowager Zhangsheng has also composed twelve chapters of Instructions for Women, making women’s obedience manifest. We ask: do these likewise resemble the instructions of the empresses and consorts of antiquity?

When instruction in the yang sphere is neglected and yang affairs are not properly ordered, the corresponding manifestation appears in Heaven: the sun is eclipsed on that account. When instruction in the yin sphere is neglected and yin affairs are not properly ordered, the corresponding manifestation appears in Heaven: the moon is eclipsed on that account. Now, from the palace quarters throughout the realm, the transforming influence of cultivating oneself, regulating the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to the realm has already been harmonized into one…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄

===

德而勸之夫其所以為教者素矣至於
嚴諸考課迺復有六計有八法太宰於
