恒以資格方諸成周之教若有異矣而
punctuated:
矣，而日月之食猶復見之，豈天心仁愛已至而益求其至歟？抑數之適然而無關於政事之修否歟？夫由之而不知者，凡民也。爾諸士通古今之故，達天人之蘊，請明言之，以為今日治化之助。
問：選舉考課，法之相因者也。《周禮》大司徒以鄉三物教萬民而賓興之，因民之常而施十有二教，其考察而書之者，又有鄉大夫、黨正之屬；有司諫，掌糾萬民之德而勸之。夫其所以為教者素矣，至於嚴諸考課，迺復有六計，有八法。太宰於歲終詔百官廢置之，三歲則大計羣吏之治而誅賞之。豈所進者或非賢歟？抑養之未至而賢能或變於初歟？然較諸唐虞，法為已密，而稱盛治者恒歸諸堯舜，何也？隋唐以降，取士恒以詞章，用士恒以資格，方諸成周之教，若有異矣，而
translation_en:
…yet eclipses of the sun and moon still occur. Is it that Heaven’s benevolent concern, though already most fully expressed, seeks still greater perfection? Or are these merely occurrences determined by numerical cycles, unrelated to whether affairs of government are well ordered? Those who follow the way without understanding it are the common people. You scholars understand the circumstances of past and present and comprehend the profound workings of Heaven and humankind. Explain this clearly, please, to assist the governance and moral transformation of the present day.
Question: Selection and promotion, and the assessment of official performance, are mutually dependent institutions. According to the Rituals of Zhou, the Minister of Education instructed the people through the three subjects of township education and promoted the worthy with the ceremonial honors accorded to guests. Following the constant principles of human relations, he implemented twelve forms of instruction. There were also Township Grandees, District Heads, and other such officials who examined the people and recorded their findings; Remonstrance Officials were charged with correcting the people’s moral conduct and encouraging them. Thus the means of educating them were established well in advance. Yet when it came to rigorous assessment, there were also the six criteria of evaluation and the eight regulations. At the end of each year, the Grand Administrator directed the dismissal or retention of the various officials; every third year he conducted a comprehensive assessment of their administration and punished or rewarded them. Could it be that some of those promoted were not worthy? Or was their cultivation incomplete, so that the worthy and capable sometimes departed from what they had originally been? Compared with the institutions of Tang and Yu, however, these regulations were already more detailed. Why, then, do those who praise flourishing government invariably turn to Yao and Shun? From the Sui and Tang onward, men were generally selected for office on the basis of literary composition and employed according to their qualifications and seniority. Compared with the education of the Zhou at its height, this seems different, yet…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
亦未嘗乏士者何居豈其所得者非古
之才乎或謂漢舉孝廉茂才庶幾近之
不知其所以教之者何如也方今
聖明在上立賢無方駸駸乎復古之治矣翕受
敷施不知有足以副
當宁之求者乎不然則先王選舉之義考課之
方其在今日固不可不之講矣願悉究
之以觀所蘊
問天有五財民並用之何能去兵古者君
===
子為射御之學而宴享之會亦具左右
司馬則兵固儒者事也方今天下承平
日久將不知兵兵不知戰武書廢而不
講識者憂焉試舉一二相與諸士折衷
之左氏喜言陣法其載一時卒乘偏兩
之制前茅慮無之警不知果可用於戰
歟觀其不欲廢車而乃未始及騎則毀
車崇卒以騎易車其法亦何所始歟太
公告武王十勝九敗之詳其說在于六
punctuated:
亦未嘗乏士者，何居？豈其所得者非古之才乎？或謂漢舉孝廉茂才，庶幾近之，不知其所以教之者何如也。方今聖明在上，立賢無方，駸駸乎復古之治矣。翕受敷施，不知有足以副當宁之求者乎？不然，則先王選舉之義、考課之方，其在今日，固不可不之講矣。願悉究之，以觀所蘊。

問：天有五財，民並用之，何能去兵？古者君子為射御之學，而宴享之會亦具左右司馬，則兵固儒者事也。方今天下承平日久，將不知兵，兵不知戰，武書廢而不講，識者憂焉。試舉一二，相與諸士折衷之。左氏喜言陣法，其載一時卒乘偏兩之制、前茅慮無之警，不知果可用於戰歟？觀其不欲廢車，而乃未始及騎，則毀車崇卒、以騎易車，其法亦何所始歟？太公告武王十勝九敗之詳，其說在于六
translation_en:
…yet there was never a shortage of capable men. Why was this? Could the men they obtained have lacked the talents of antiquity? Some say that the Han recommendation of the Filial and Incorrupt and of Outstanding Talent came close to the ancient practice; but how, we wonder, were these men educated? Today our sagely and enlightened sovereign reigns above, appointing worthy men without restriction and advancing swiftly toward a restoration of ancient governance. Talent is broadly received and put to use: are there men adequate to meet the reigning sovereign’s expectations? If not, then the principles by which the former kings selected men and their methods of evaluating performance certainly demand examination today. We ask you to investigate these fully, so that we may see the understanding you possess.

Question: Heaven provides five material resources, and the people use them all; how could weapons be dispensed with? In antiquity, gentlemen studied archery and charioteering, and even ceremonial banquets had Directors of Military Affairs of the Left and Right. Military affairs were therefore properly the concern of Confucian scholars. Today the realm has enjoyed peace for many years. Commanders do not understand warfare, soldiers do not know how to fight, and military writings lie neglected and unstudied. Those with discernment are troubled by this. Let us raise one or two matters for critical consideration together with you candidates. Master Zuo readily discusses battle formations. Could the contemporary arrangements he records for infantry and chariots, and for units called pian and liang, and the precautions involving advance scouts and vigilance against unforeseen dangers, actually be employed in battle? We observe that he did not wish to abandon chariots, yet never discussed cavalry. Where, then, did the practices of dismantling chariots and favoring infantry, and of replacing chariots with cavalry, originate? Taigong explained to King Wu the details of the ten means of victory and nine causes of defeat. His account is contained in the Six …

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
韜武王之時猶用騎戰顧其法絕不見
于春秋至於車戰亦絕不見於後世則
車騎卒伍之戰不知可偏廢歟或曰六
韜非周書戰國知兵之士祖其餘論而
推廣之設爲問答以極兵家之變今觀
其書智畧竒詭雜然横出有鰓鰓然憂
天下諸侯合而軋已之意則以爲戰國
之書者夫亦有所據歟諸葛武侯好韜
畧岳飛好左氏皆足以摧敵制勝其法
===
異而功同者何歟今之用兵者將祖六
韜三畧而用之歟抑亦取之左氏歟頃
者雲中之變上厪
當宁之慮至屯兵易將始克底平則講武一事
寔惟急務願詳言之將以轉聞于
上
問三代之治名與實相副而享國長乆萬
世之所宜法焉者也然其文章制度各
有因革而不甚相沿固其時然爾其亦
punctuated:
韜。武王之時猶用騎戰，顧其法絕不見于春秋。至於車戰，亦絕不見於後世，則車騎卒伍之戰，不知可偏廢歟？或曰：「《六韜》非周書，戰國知兵之士祖其餘論而推廣之，設爲問答，以極兵家之變。」今觀其書，智畧竒詭，雜然横出，有鰓鰓然憂天下諸侯合而軋已之意，則以爲戰國之書者，夫亦有所據歟？諸葛武侯好韜畧，岳飛好左氏，皆足以摧敵制勝，其法異而功同者何歟？今之用兵者，將祖《六韜》《三畧》而用之歟？抑亦取之左氏歟？頃者雲中之變，上厪當宁之慮，至屯兵易將，始克底平。則講武一事，寔惟急務，願詳言之，將以轉聞于上。

問：三代之治，名與實相副，而享國長乆，萬世之所宜法焉者也。然其文章制度，各有因革，而不甚相沿，固其時然爾，其亦
translation_en:
…Secret Teachings (Liu tao). In King Wu’s time, mounted troops were already used in battle, yet this method is entirely absent from accounts of the Spring and Autumn period. Chariot warfare, in turn, is entirely absent from later ages. Among warfare employing chariots, cavalry, and infantry, can any one form be dispensed with? Some say: “The Six Secret Teachings is not a Zhou work. Men versed in warfare during the Warring States period took the surviving teachings as their foundation and expanded upon them, arranging questions and answers to explore the full range of military variations.” Looking at the book now, we find ingenious and extraordinary stratagems appearing in profusion, together with an anxious concern that the feudal lords throughout the realm might unite to crush oneself [?]. Does the view that it is a Warring States work thus have some basis? Zhuge Liang, Marquis of Wu, favored military strategy, while Yue Fei favored Zuo’s Commentary. Both were fully capable of crushing enemies and securing victory. Why did their different methods produce the same achievements? Should those who command troops today take the Six Secret Teachings and the Three Strategies (San lüe) as their models and put them into practice? Or should they draw upon Zuo’s Commentary? Recently, the disturbance at Yunzhong caused His Majesty concern; only after troops were stationed there and commanders replaced could order finally be restored. The study of military affairs is therefore an urgent task indeed. Please discuss it in detail, so that your views may be conveyed to His Majesty.

Question: Under the Three Dynasties, name and reality accorded, and their rule endured for a long time: theirs is an example that all subsequent ages ought to follow. Yet their cultural forms and institutions each combined continuity and change, without closely following those of their predecessors. This was certainly due to the circumstances of their times; might they also…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
有同焉而可言者乎董仲舒謂三代有
改制之異而無變道之實者其果然乎
由秦而後雖治亂興衰不一其變而英
君碩輔亦代有人卒不聞有致三代之
隆建萬世之長策者何也豈三代制作
不可行於後世矣乎然亦有復井田六
官者矣曾靡裨於治則三代之制果終
不可行歟抑別有其故歟唐太宗號稱
英主考其治庶幾於古而於三代之制
===
未竟其施焉豈所謂善治焉者惟宜究
其實而不必於其名歟抑惟循名責實
者而后可以爲善之至也其舉至當之
論以復固將以考材焉
問古有言曰識時務者在俊傑諸士平日
固以俊傑自期也試以時務一二商確
可乎浙爲東南首藩海育地産財賦充
饒食宜無不足也夫何倉廩日虛一遇
水旱之虞爲人牧者輒議勸借勸之誠
punctuated:
有同焉而可言者乎？董仲舒謂三代有改制之異，而無變道之實者，其果然乎？由秦而後，雖治亂興衰不一其變，而英君碩輔亦代有人，卒不聞有致三代之隆、建萬世之長策者，何也？豈三代制作不可行於後世矣乎？然亦有復井田、六官者矣，曾靡裨於治，則三代之制果終不可行歟？抑別有其故歟？唐太宗號稱英主，考其治，庶幾於古，而於三代之制未竟其施焉。豈所謂善治焉者，惟宜究其實而不必於其名歟？抑惟循名責實者，而后可以爲善之至也？其舉至當之論以復，固將以考材焉。

問：古有言曰：「識時務者在俊傑。」諸士平日固以俊傑自期也，試以時務一二商確，可乎？浙爲東南首藩，海育地産，財賦充饒，食宜無不足也。夫何倉廩日虛，一遇水旱之虞，爲人牧者輒議勸借？勸之誠
translation_en:
…are there also common features that can be discussed? Dong Zhongshu maintained that the Three Dynasties differed in their changes to institutions, but did not actually alter the Way. Was this indeed so? Since the Qin, although order and disorder, flourishing and decline have varied in many ways, outstanding rulers and eminent ministers have appeared in every age. Yet we never hear of any who attained the greatness of the Three Dynasties or established a lasting policy for ten thousand generations. Why is this? Could the institutions established by the Three Dynasties be impracticable in later ages? Yet there have been those who restored the well-field system and the Six Offices, without contributing anything to good government. Does this mean that the institutions of the Three Dynasties are ultimately unworkable, or is there some other reason? Taizong of the Tang was acclaimed as an outstanding ruler. On examining his government, we find that it approached that of antiquity, yet he never fully implemented the institutions of the Three Dynasties. Does this mean that those who govern well need only pursue the substance, without insisting on the names? Or can the highest excellence be attained only by holding actual performance accountable to its stated name? Present the most fitting argument in reply; it will serve to assess your abilities.

Question: An ancient saying declares: “Those who understand the affairs of the times are outstanding men.” You gentlemen have surely always aspired to be such men. May we discuss and examine one or two matters of current concern? Zhejiang is the foremost province of the southeast. With the bounty of its seas and the produce of its land, its wealth and tax revenues are abundant; there should be no shortage of food. Why, then, do its granaries grow emptier by the day, so that whenever flood or drought threatens, those charged with tending the people immediately propose soliciting loans? To solicit them is indeed …

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
是也不知督税之吏徴輸于官者何在
枕山臂江果悍自負兵宜無不競也夫
何軍伍日耗一遇潢池之警當其事者
輒稱招募招之誠是也不知清戎之官
操練于衛者何為鹽徒海寇備禦終年
然詰捕之擾徒增萑澤之患如故不知
何以弭之山鄉水區勤動終嵗然稱貸
之苦徒聞川陸之利未獲不知何以處
之議者多歸咎於嵗凶或又以為長吏
===
不得其人茲欲寓兵於農使緩急得有
所賴藏富於民使水旱不能為災如之
何其可也諸士留心世故久矣請著于
篇以觀用世之學
punctuated: 是也。不知督税之吏徴輸于官者何在？枕山臂江，果悍自負，兵宜無不競也。夫何軍伍日耗，一遇潢池之警，當其事者輒稱招募？招之誠是也，不知清戎之官操練于衛者何為？鹽徒海寇，備禦終年，然詰捕之擾徒增，萑澤之患如故，不知何以弭之？山鄉水區，勤動終嵗，然稱貸之苦徒聞，川陸之利未獲，不知何以處之？議者多歸咎於嵗凶，或又以為長吏不得其人。茲欲寓兵於農，使緩急得有所賴；藏富於民，使水旱不能為災，如之何其可也？諸士留心世故久矣，請著于篇，以觀用世之學。
translation_en:
…is indeed right. Yet where are the officials charged with supervising taxes and collecting payments for the government? With mountains at their backs and rivers at their flanks, and proud of their courage and fierceness, their troops ought surely to be strong. Why, then, do the ranks dwindle daily, and why, whenever an alarm of local rebellion arises, do those responsible immediately call for recruitment? Recruiting is indeed right; yet what are the officials charged with putting military affairs in order and drilling troops in the guards doing?

Defense against illicit salt dealers and sea raiders continues throughout the year. Yet the disruption caused by investigations and arrests only increases, while the scourge of banditry remains unchanged. How can it be quelled? In mountain villages and waterside districts, people toil throughout the year. Yet we hear only of the hardships of borrowing, while the benefits of waterways and land remain unrealized. How can this be addressed? Those who discuss these matters mostly blame poor harvests; others hold that the wrong men have been appointed as local administrators.

We now wish to incorporate soldiers within the farming population, so that there will be forces to rely upon whenever needed, and to store wealth among the people, so that floods and droughts cannot bring disaster. How can this be accomplished? You gentlemen have long attended to worldly affairs. Please set forth your views in writing, so that we may assess your learning for practical service.

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
中式舉人九十名
第一名張志淑台州府學生春秋
第二名陳善錢塘縣學增廣生易
第三名潘仲驂湖州府學生禮記
第四名楊機寧波府學附學生詩
第五名孫汝賢餘姚縣學生書
第六名慎蒙歸安縣學生易
第七名查秉鉞海寧縣學生詩
===
第八名來日升蕭山縣學生書
第九名汪呂之黃巖縣學增廣生春秋
第十名胡采嵊縣學生禮記
第十一名茅坤歸安縣學生書
第十二名張鳴鶴錢塘縣學生易
第十三名沈棐德清縣學生詩

第十五名彭輅嘉興縣學生詩
第十六名唐禹海寧縣學增廣生易
punctuated:
中式舉人九十名。

第一名，張志淑，台州府學生，《春秋》。第二名，陳善，錢塘縣學增廣生，《易》。第三名，潘仲驂，湖州府學生，《禮記》。第四名，楊機，寧波府學附學生，《詩》。第五名，孫汝賢，餘姚縣學生，《書》。第六名，慎蒙，歸安縣學生，《易》。第七名，查秉鉞，海寧縣學生，《詩》。第八名，來日升，蕭山縣學生，《書》。第九名，汪呂之，黃巖縣學增廣生，《春秋》。第十名，胡采，嵊縣學生，《禮記》。第十一名，茅坤，歸安縣學生，《書》。第十二名，張鳴鶴，錢塘縣學生，《易》。第十三名，沈棐，德清縣學生，《詩》。第十四名，張元，餘姚縣學生，《易》。第十五名，彭輅，嘉興縣學生，《詩》。第十六名，唐禹，海寧縣學增廣生，《易》。
translation_en:
Ninety successful provincial graduates (juren).

First: Zhang Zhishu, a student of the Taizhou Prefectural School. His examination classic was the Spring and Autumn Annals.

Second: Chen Shan, an added student of the Qiantang County School. His examination classic was the Book of Changes.

Third: Pan Zhongcan, a student of the Huzhou Prefectural School. His examination classic was the Book of Rites.

Fourth: Yang Ji, an attached student of the Ningbo Prefectural School. His examination classic was the Book of Odes.

Fifth: Sun Ruxian, a student of the Yuyao County School. His examination classic was the Book of Documents.

Sixth: Shen Meng, a student of the Gui'an County School. His examination classic was the Book of Changes.

Seventh: Zha Bingyue, a student of the Haining County School. His examination classic was the Book of Odes.

Eighth: Lai Risheng, a student of the Xiaoshan County School. His examination classic was the Book of Documents.

Ninth: Wang Lüzhi, an added student of the Huangyan County School. His examination classic was the Spring and Autumn Annals.

Tenth: Hu Cai, a student of the Sheng County School. His examination classic was the Book of Rites.

Eleventh: Mao Kun, a student of the Gui'an County School. His examination classic was the Book of Documents.

Twelfth: Zhang Minghe, a student of the Qiantang County School. His examination classic was the Book of Changes.

Thirteenth: Shen Fei, a student of the Deqing County School. His examination classic was the Book of Odes.

Fourteenth: Zhang Yuan, a student of the Yuyao County School. His examination classic was the Book of Changes.

Fifteenth: Peng Lu, a student of the Jiaxing County School. His examination classic was the Book of Odes.

Sixteenth: Tang Yu, an added student of the Haining County School. His examination classic was the Book of Changes.

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
第十七名吳一儒歸安縣學生書
第十八名徐袍蘭谿縣學生易
第十九名張輻山陰縣學生詩
第二十名葉選餘姚縣學附學生易
第二十一名林夔臨海縣學生詩
第二十二名應奎杭州府學增廣生易
第二十三名周鼎溫州府學增廣生詩
第二十四名徐文通永康縣學附學生書
第二十五名李廷元縉雲縣學增廣生易
===
第二十六名朱佐海鹽縣學生春秋
第二十七名馮覲杭州府學生詩
第二十八名王宗聖義烏縣學生書
第二十九名張堯年慈谿縣學增廣生詩
第三十名盧璘餘姚縣學附學生易
第三十一名韓應龍餘姚縣學附學生禮記
第三十二名商璉會稽縣學生詩

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰賢哉回也一簞食一瓢飲在陋巷人
不堪其憂回也不改其樂賢哉回也
彭輅
同考試官訓導李批淡而不厭蓋慕顏子之
樂者
同考試官教諭吳批顏子非以貧爲樂也蓋
忘貧而樂自得者也此作能盡之故錄
===
考試官教授何批冲澹有味
考試官教授高批清雅
聖人稱大賢必即其安貧者而深賛之焉夫處
貧而不改其樂顏子所以爲賢也固宜夫子賛
之而深致意也如此且君子不隕穫於貧賤不
充詘於富貴顏氏子其殆庶幾乎故夫子曰賢
哉回也蓋自其處貧者而觀之其食也一簞焉
爾矣無餘物也其飲也一瓢焉爾矣無餘味也
方且陋巷爰居而終窶且貧困亦甚矣夫人亦
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

子曰：「賢哉，回也！一簞食，一瓢飲，在陋巷，人不堪其憂，回也不改其樂。賢哉，回也！」

彭輅

同考試官訓導李批：「淡而不厭，蓋慕顏子之樂者。」

同考試官教諭吳批：「顏子非以貧爲樂也，蓋忘貧而樂自得者也。此作能盡之，故錄。」

考試官教授何批：「冲澹有味。」

考試官教授高批：「清雅。」

聖人稱大賢，必即其安貧者而深賛之焉。夫處貧而不改其樂，顏子所以爲賢也。固宜夫子賛之而深致意也如此。且君子不隕穫於貧賤，不充詘於富貴，顏氏子其殆庶幾乎？故夫子曰：「賢哉，回也！」蓋自其處貧者而觀之，其食也，一簞焉爾矣，無餘物也；其飲也，一瓢焉爾矣，無餘味也。方且陋巷爰居，而終窶且貧，困亦甚矣。夫人亦
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The Master said: “How worthy Hui is! With a single bamboo basket of food and a single gourd of drink, living in a humble lane—others could not endure such distress, yet Hui did not let it alter his joy. How worthy Hui is!”

Peng Lu 彭輅

Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor, comments: “Plain yet never wearisome: surely the work of one who admires Master Yan’s joy.”

Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: “Master Yan did not take poverty itself as a source of joy. Rather, he forgot his poverty, and his joy came of itself. This composition fully expresses this, and so it is included.”

Examiner He, Professor, comments: “Serene and understated, yet full of flavor.”

Examiner Gao, Professor, comments: “Pure and elegant.”

When the sage praises a person of great worth, he grounds his profound commendation in that person’s contentment in poverty. To live in poverty without letting it alter his joy was what made Master Yan worthy. It was indeed fitting that the Master should praise him and express such deep appreciation. Moreover, the gentleman is neither dismayed by poverty and low station nor unsettled by wealth and high rank. Did not the son of the Yan family come close to this ideal? Thus the Master said: “How worthy Hui is!” Consider how he lived in poverty: his food was merely a single bamboo basketful, with nothing else besides; his drink was merely a single gourdful, with no other flavors to enjoy. Furthermore, he dwelt in a humble lane and remained destitute and poor. His hardship was indeed extreme. As for other people, they too …

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
孰堪其憂也回也素位而行與簞瓢而順適自
養之貞而莫之有求也素履之往與陋巷而相
忘於土皆安而無所於懷也曷嘗以貧窶累其
心而改其所樂哉蓋回之心誠有見于其大者
是故無喪無得而富貴貧賤處之一也然則回
也其賢矣哉吁再言賢哉回也則夫子所以嘆
美之者意獨至矣考諸易曰困而不失其所亨
其唯君子乎蓋古之聖人無欲故其視天下之
故如寒暑晝夜相代乎前吾豈有二其心哉昔
===
茂叔亦謂顏子見大心泰而歸諸亞聖嗟乎樂
天知命故不憂夫子之謂也不遠復無祇悔固
顏子之庶幾焉者乎學者要當尋孔顏樂處
溥博如天淵泉如淵見而民莫不敬言而
民莫不信行而民莫不說
張志淑
同考試官教諭陳批言聖德之發見本於充
積之盛親切有味末復歸誠之一言意亦獨至有
本者如是是以取爾
punctuated:
孰堪其憂也？回也素位而行，與簞瓢而順適，自養之貞而莫之有求也；素履之往，與陋巷而相忘，於土皆安而無所於懷也。曷嘗以貧窶累其心而改其所樂哉？蓋回之心誠有見于其大者，是故無喪無得，而富貴貧賤處之一也。然則回也其賢矣哉！吁！再言「賢哉回也」，則夫子所以嘆美之者，意獨至矣。考諸《易》曰：「困而不失其所亨，其唯君子乎！」蓋古之聖人無欲，故其視天下之故，如寒暑晝夜相代乎前，吾豈有二其心哉？昔茂叔亦謂顏子見大心泰，而歸諸亞聖。嗟乎！「樂天知命，故不憂」，夫子之謂也；「不遠復，無祇悔」，固顏子之庶幾焉者乎！學者要當尋孔顏樂處。
溥博如天，淵泉如淵，見而民莫不敬，言而民莫不信，行而民莫不說。
張志淑
同考試官教諭陳批：言聖德之發見，本於充積之盛，親切有味。末復歸誠之一言，意亦獨至。有本者如是，是以取爾。
translation_en:
…who could bear such distress? Hui acted according to his station, content with his basket of food and gourd of drink, steadfast in cultivating himself and seeking nothing else. He proceeded in unadorned conduct, forgetting himself amid the narrow lanes, at ease wherever he dwelt [?], with nothing weighing upon his mind. When did he ever allow poverty to burden his heart and change what he delighted in? Hui’s heart truly perceived what was great; thus neither loss nor gain affected him, and he met wealth and honor, poverty and lowliness alike. Was Hui not indeed worthy? Ah! By saying once again, “How worthy Hui is!” the Master expressed the utmost depth of his admiration. Consider the statement in the Book of Changes: “Beset by hardship yet not losing that through which he attains fulfillment—is this not the superior man alone?” The sages of antiquity were free of desires. They therefore regarded the events of the world as they did cold and heat, day and night, alternating before them. How could they let their hearts become divided?
In former times, Maoshu likewise said that Master Yan perceived what was great and his heart was at ease, and accordingly ranked him as second to the sage. Ah! “Delighting in Heaven and understanding fate, he therefore has no anxiety”—this describes the Master. “Returning before going far, without coming to regret”—surely Master Yan came close to this! Students must seek out that in which Kongzi and Yan Hui found their delight.
“Broad and vast as Heaven, deep and flowing as an abyss: when he appears, none among the people fails to respect him; when he speaks, none fails to trust him; when he acts, none fails to be pleased.”
Zhang Zhishu
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, School Instructor: The essay explains that the manifestation of sagely virtue is rooted in the fullness of its accumulation. Its treatment is pertinent and rich in meaning. At the close it returns to the single word ‘sincerity,’ showing exceptional depth of thought. Such is writing that has a foundation; this is why I have selected it.

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎授何批是有見者
考試官敎授高批溫裕
中庸於至聖之德必申贊其體用之全焉蓋充
積極其盛而發見當其可德之體用所以爲全
也非天下至聖其孰能與於此中庸三十一章
言至聖之德以明天道及此復申言之謂夫言
天下之至德者存乎聖言天下之至感者存乎
時其積中發外之盛何如哉蓋自其溥博言之
萬物皆備而充周不可窮天德純全而廣大不
===
可禦擬諸形容固即天之爲天而蕩蕩難名者
矣自其淵泉言之寂然不動有以通天下之故
渾然在中有以立天下之本擬諸形容固即淵
之爲淵而淵淵莫測者矣充積之極其盛也蓋
如此由是時而見也則爲德容恭己之施固天
下之所觀而化者而莫有不敬者焉時而言也
則爲德言巽命之申固天下之所訓而行者而
莫有不信者焉又時而行也則爲德行而聲敎
所訖有以丕冒乎天下媚兹一人亦自有不能
punctuated:
考試官敎授何批：是有見者。
考試官敎授高批：溫裕。
中庸於至聖之德，必申贊其體用之全焉。蓋充積極其盛，而發見當其可，德之體用所以爲全也。非天下至聖，其孰能與於此？中庸三十一章言至聖之德，以明天道，及此復申言之。謂夫言天下之至德者存乎聖，言天下之至感者存乎時，其積中發外之盛何如哉！蓋自其溥博言之，萬物皆備而充周不可窮，天德純全而廣大不可禦。擬諸形容，固即天之爲天而蕩蕩難名者矣。自其淵泉言之，寂然不動，有以通天下之故；渾然在中，有以立天下之本。擬諸形容，固即淵之爲淵而淵淵莫測者矣。充積之極其盛也，蓋如此。由是時而見也，則爲德容，恭己之施，固天下之所觀而化者，而莫有不敬者焉。時而言也，則爲德言，巽命之申，固天下之所訓而行者，而莫有不信者焉。又時而行也，則爲德行，而聲敎所訖，有以丕冒乎天下，媚兹一人，亦自有不能
translation_en:
Examiner He, Prefectural School Instructor, comments: “This shows insight.”
Examiner Gao, Prefectural School Instructor, comments: “Gentle and ample.”
In discussing the virtue of the consummate sage, the Doctrine of the Mean further extols its completeness in both substance and function. For its inward accumulation reaches the utmost fullness, while its outward manifestation accords with what is fitting: this is what makes virtue complete in substance and function. Who but the consummate sage of the world could attain this? Chapter thirty-one of the Doctrine of the Mean discusses the virtue of the consummate sage to elucidate the Way of Heaven; at this point it further develops that discussion. It means that the highest virtue in the world resides in sagehood, and the highest power to move others depends upon timeliness. How abundant is what accumulates within and manifests itself without!
Speaking of its breadth and vastness, all things are fully present within it, and its all-pervading fullness is inexhaustible. Heavenly virtue is pure and complete, and its breadth and greatness cannot be checked. If one seeks a likeness to describe it, it is precisely that which makes Heaven Heaven—so boundless that it is difficult to name. Speaking of its depth as a fountain, it is still and unmoving, yet thereby comprehends the affairs of the world; it abides within as an undivided whole, yet thereby establishes the foundation of the world. If one seeks a likeness to describe it, it is precisely that which makes an abyss an abyss—so deep as to be unfathomable. Such is the utmost fullness of its inward accumulation.
Thus, when the sage appears at the proper time, his appearance embodies virtue. His practice of holding himself reverently is what all under Heaven behold and are transformed by, and none fail to revere him. When he speaks at the proper time, his words embody virtue. His reiteration of gentle commands is what all under Heaven receive as instruction and act upon, and none fail to trust him. Again, when he acts at the proper time, his conduct embodies virtue. Wherever his proclaimed teachings reach, they broadly shelter all under Heaven. Loving this one man, the people likewise cannot help but…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
已於悅焉發見之當其可也又如此固皆積盛
致然爾非聖人而能若是乎吁此聖人之所以
爲天道也雖然聖人亦何以得此也哉維天之
命於穆不已於乎不顯文王之德之純聖人之
德一誠而已矣然則學者欲造於聖人亦求之
戒懼愼獨去不誠以復於誠而已矣誠復而體
立焉用行焉蘊之爲德行發之爲事業是固一
以貫之者也故曰誠者天之道也誠之者人之
道也
===
是集義所生者非義襲而取之也
張元
同考試官敎諭毛批沉渾而不浮圓融而不
滯子固集義而有得者因具文可想見其人
同考試官敎諭易批講是集義所生處甚是
纔一著力便不是矣且文亦昌大惇厚非襲取者
所能及
考試官敎授何批是善養其氣者
考試官敎授高批讀之充如
punctuated:
已於悅焉。發見之當其可也，又如此，固皆積盛致然爾。非聖人而能若是乎？吁！此聖人之所以爲天道也。雖然，聖人亦何以得此也哉？「維天之命，於穆不已。於乎不顯，文王之德之純。」聖人之德，一誠而已矣。然則學者欲造於聖人，亦求之戒懼愼獨，去不誠以復於誠而已矣。誠復而體立焉，用行焉；蘊之爲德行，發之爲事業，是固一以貫之者也。故曰：「誠者，天之道也；誠之者，人之道也。」

是集義所生者，非義襲而取之也。
張元

同考試官敎諭毛批：沉渾而不浮，圓融而不滯。子固集義而有得者，因具文可想見其人。

同考試官敎諭易批：講是集義所生處甚是，纔一著力便不是矣。且文亦昌大惇厚，非襲取者所能及。

考試官敎授何批：是善養其氣者。

考試官敎授高批：讀之充如。
translation_en:
…cannot help delighting in him. Such, too, is the fitting timeliness of its manifestation. All this results from virtue accumulated in abundance. Could anyone but a sage attain this? Ah! This is how the sage embodies the Way of Heaven. Yet how does the sage attain it? “Heaven’s mandate—how profound and unceasing! Ah, how illustrious is the purity of King Wen’s virtue!” The sage’s virtue is nothing more than sincerity alone. Thus, if learners wish to attain sagehood, they need only seek it through vigilance and apprehension and watchfulness when alone, removing insincerity to return to sincerity. Once sincerity is restored, the underlying substance is established and its functioning comes into operation. Stored within, it constitutes virtuous conduct; expressed outwardly, it constitutes achievements. A single principle indeed runs through it all. Hence it is said: “Sincerity is the Way of Heaven; making oneself sincere is the way of humanity.”

“It is produced by accumulating righteousness, not acquired through a sudden act of righteousness.”
By Zhang Yuan.

Comment by Associate Examiner Mao, Instructor: Substantial and profound without being superficial; rounded and integrated without being obstructed. You are assuredly someone who has gained something through accumulating righteousness. From this essay [?], one can picture its author.

Comment by Associate Examiner Yi, Instructor: The explanation of “produced by accumulating righteousness” is thoroughly correct: the moment one applies force, it is already wrong. Moreover, the writing is expansive and substantial, earnest and generous—beyond the reach of anyone seeking to acquire it through a sudden act.

Comment by Examiner He, Professor: This is someone skilled at nourishing his vital force, qi.

Comment by Examiner Gao, Professor: Reading it, one feels a sense of fullness.

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
大賢指言氣之所由充所以示養氣之始事也
夫氣生於集義而不可以襲取然則養氣者其
可不於義焉求之哉此孟子所以爲公孫丑告
也其意若曰理之與氣每相須而成其功效亦
相因而見是故配義與道人知夫氣之充耳而
其養之之始何如哉蓋由事之行也義以爲質
達諸萬變而皆恊善之動也持以有常聚爲百
順而無斁則內而反於身也常直而事爲有本
外而形於氣也常充而操之有要盛大流行之
===
勢殆將日新月盛塞天地而配道義此其本矣
乃若於義積習之未深謂可以偶合而盡推行
之不豫謂可以襲取而充則徇外者遺內將何
以爲體驗擴充之地正助者心忘亦何以收直
養無害之功至大至剛之氣吾見隨得隨失塞
天地而配道義無是理也氣其可以義襲而取
哉是則義也者集也而非襲也故氣也者生也
而非取也功效之得失如此養氣者亦維善事
其心而已抑於是而知集義養氣體用一原之
punctuated:
大賢指言氣之所由充，所以示養氣之始事也。夫氣生於集義，而不可以襲取，然則養氣者，其可不於義焉求之哉？此孟子所以爲公孫丑告也。其意若曰：理之與氣，每相須而成，其功效亦相因而見。是故配義與道，人知夫氣之充耳，而其養之之始何如哉？蓋由事之行也，義以爲質；達諸萬變而皆恊，善之動也，持以有常；聚爲百順而無斁。則內而反於身也，常直而事爲有本；外而形於氣也，常充而操之有要。盛大流行之勢，殆將日新月盛，塞天地而配道義，此其本矣。
乃若於義積習之未深，謂可以偶合而盡；推行之不豫，謂可以襲取而充。則徇外者遺內，將何以爲體驗擴充之地？正助者心忘，亦何以收直養無害之功？至大至剛之氣，吾見隨得隨失，塞天地而配道義，無是理也。氣其可以義襲而取哉？
是則義也者，集也而非襲也；故氣也者，生也而非取也。功效之得失如此，養氣者亦維善事其心而已。抑於是而知集義養氣、體用一原之
translation_en:
The great worthy explains directly how qi becomes full, thereby showing the initial work of nourishing it. Qi arises from the accumulation of righteousness and cannot be seized through an isolated act. How, then, could anyone nourishing qi fail to seek it in righteousness? This is why Mengzi addressed Gongsun Chou. His meaning was as follows: principle and qi always depend upon one another for their fulfillment, and their effects likewise become manifest through their mutual dependence. Thus, when qi accords with righteousness and the Way, people recognize only its fullness. But how does the work of nourishing it begin? In carrying out affairs, one takes righteousness as their substance, extending it through myriad changes so that all are in accord. In putting goodness into action, one maintains constancy, accumulating a hundred instances of accordance without weariness. Inwardly, when one examines oneself, one is always upright, and one’s conduct has a foundation. Outwardly, as this manifests in qi, it is always full, and one has grasped the essentials of maintaining it. Its vast and flowing momentum will then renew itself daily and grow monthly, filling Heaven and Earth and according with the Way and righteousness. This is its foundation.
But suppose one has not deeply cultivated righteousness through repeated practice, yet thinks that an occasional coincidence with it can exhaust its requirements; or has not prepared oneself to put it into practice, yet thinks that qi can be made full by seizing it through an isolated act. Those who pursue the outward neglect the inward: what basis will they have for personally realizing and expanding it? Those who anticipate results or force its growth forget the heart [?]: how can they achieve the result of nourishing it with uprightness and doing it no harm? As for qi, supremely great and supremely firm, I see them losing it as soon as they gain it. That it should fill Heaven and Earth and accord with the Way and righteousness under such circumstances is impossible. Can qi really be acquired by an isolated act of righteousness?
Thus righteousness must be accumulated, rather than appropriated in a single act; qi therefore arises, rather than being seized. Since success and failure in this work are like this, those who nourish qi need only attend properly to their hearts. From this, moreover, one understands that accumulating righteousness and nourishing qi, and substance and function having a single source …

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
理也自反而縮體用合矣孟子之不動心其原
蓋在於此告子以義爲外故亦外心與氣而不
求其於體用擧無所屬則亦冥然悍然而已爾
此孟子告子不動心之異也學之者深求其原
固盡心知性知天之學矣其何異端得而亂之
易
九五有孚惠心勿問元吉有孚惠我德
陳善
同考試官教諭毛批寫出王者得民氣象可
===
以爲文矣
同考試官教諭易批易義潔淨精微此作得
之
考試官教授何批彖傳中正有慶是如此
考試官教授高批典實
聖人於益之九五而著以交孚之義也蓋孚而
曰交則一德之相感者深矣上下以此爲益吉
又何待於問邪周公繫辭之意有如此且夫人
君有相之道求無媿也已生民有欲之道求無
punctuated:
理也。自反而縮，體用合矣。孟子之不動心，其原蓋在於此。告子以義爲外，故亦外心與氣，而不求其於體用，擧無所屬，則亦冥然悍然而已爾。此孟子、告子不動心之異也。學之者深求其原，固盡心知性知天之學矣，其何異端得而亂之？
《易》
九五：有孚惠心，勿問，元吉。有孚惠我德。
陳善
同考試官教諭毛批：寫出王者得民氣象，可以爲文矣。
同考試官教諭易批：易義潔淨精微，此作得之。
考試官教授何批：彖傳中正有慶，是如此。
考試官教授高批：典實。
聖人於益之九五，而著以交孚之義也。蓋孚而曰交，則一德之相感者深矣。上下以此爲益，吉又何待於問邪？周公繫辭之意有如此。且夫人君有相之道，求無媿也已；生民有欲之道，求無
translation_en:
…the principle. When one examines oneself and finds oneself upright, substance and function are united. Here, surely, lies the source of Mengzi’s unperturbed mind. Gaozi regarded righteousness as external; thus he also treated the mind and vital energy as external and did not seek their relation in terms of substance and function. With neither having any grounding, he was merely uncomprehending and obstinate. This is the difference between the unperturbed minds of Mengzi and Gaozi. Those who study this and search deeply for its source are indeed pursuing the learning of fully realizing the mind, knowing human nature, and knowing Heaven. How could heterodox teachings succeed in confusing them?

Book of Changes

“Nine in the fifth place: With sincerity and a beneficent heart, there is no need to inquire: supreme good fortune. With sincerity, they cherish my virtue.”

Chen Shan

Associate Examiner Mao, Instructor, comments: “It conveys the bearing of a true king winning the people’s allegiance. This qualifies as accomplished writing.”

Associate Examiner Yi, Instructor, comments: “The meaning of the Changes is pure, refined, and subtle. This composition captures it.”

Examiner He, Professor, comments: “This is what the Commentary on the Judgments means by ‘central and correct, bringing blessings.’”

Examiner Gao, Professor, comments: “Classically grounded and substantial.”

In the ninth line in the fifth place of Increase, the sage makes manifest the meaning of mutual sincerity. When sincerity is described as mutual, the reciprocal response arising from a shared virtue is profound indeed. When those above and below take this as their increase, what need is there to inquire about good fortune? Such was the Duke of Zhou’s intention in appending these words. Now, the ruler has a way of aiding the people and seeks only to be free from shame; the people have a way of expressing their desires and seek only to be free from…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
拂也已是故以益之九五言之陽剛中正以居
尊位矣而又當益下之時是其所以爲益也視
民如傷心旣純於天德矣即以其心而推之務
使下究之澤真足以怙冒乎羣生而不徒襲之
以仁聲也愛民如子心旣純於王道矣即以其
心而擴之務俾大賚之恩真足以覃敷乎庶物
而不徒隆之以仁聞也上之惠下如此則信以
發志有不疾而速之機孚乃化邦有無遠弗届
之妙其爲大善固不待於占筮也吾見遺以樂
===
也民樂之而不忍忘蓋翊戴之爲元后殆有中
心悅而不假於其貌者矣導以利也民利之而
不忍負蓋親愛之如父母殆有內志誠而非革
於其面者矣是固所謂大善也而亦奚俟於問
邪爻義如此占在其中矣抑考之書曰民非后
罔克胥匡以生后非民罔以辟四方又曰爾惟
風下民惟草則知一體之義其相須也甚殷而
其相感也甚速否則志乖而道睽矣乖與睽聖
人不由也故曰王者之民皞皞如也霸者之民
punctuated:
拂也已。是故以益之九五言之，陽剛中正以居尊位矣，而又當益下之時，是其所以爲益也。視民如傷，心旣純於天德矣，即以其心而推之，務使下究之澤真足以怙冒乎羣生，而不徒襲之以仁聲也。愛民如子，心旣純於王道矣，即以其心而擴之，務俾大賚之恩真足以覃敷乎庶物，而不徒隆之以仁聞也。上之惠下如此，則信以發志，有不疾而速之機；孚乃化邦，有無遠弗届之妙。其爲大善，固不待於占筮也。吾見遺以樂也，民樂之而不忍忘，蓋翊戴之爲元后，殆有中心悅而不假於其貌者矣。導以利也，民利之而不忍負，蓋親愛之如父母，殆有內志誠而非革於其面者矣。是固所謂大善也，而亦奚俟於問邪？爻義如此，占在其中矣。
抑考之《書》曰：「民非后，罔克胥匡以生；后非民，罔以辟四方。」又曰：「爾惟風，下民惟草。」則知一體之義，其相須也甚殷，而其相感也甚速。否則志乖而道睽矣。乖與睽，聖人不由也。故曰：「王者之民皞皞如也，霸者之民
translation_en:
…not to thwart them, and that is all. Thus, speaking of the nine in the fifth place of Increase (Yi), it occupies the honored position with yang strength, centrality, and correctness, and moreover comes at a time for benefiting those below. This is how it brings increase. Regarding the people as though they were injured, the ruler’s heart is already wholly in accord with Heaven’s virtue. He extends that heart, striving to ensure that the beneficence reaching those below truly suffices to shelter all living beings, rather than merely clothing his actions in a reputation for benevolence. Loving the people as his children, his heart is already wholly in accord with the kingly Way. He enlarges that heart, striving to ensure that the grace of his generous gifts truly spreads to all things, rather than merely magnifying his reputation for benevolence. When the ruler benefits those below in this way, trust gives expression to his intentions, with the efficacy of being swift without haste; sincerity transforms the realm, with the wondrous power of reaching even the remotest places. That this constitutes great good certainly need not await divination by stalks or shells. I see that when he bestows happiness upon them, the people delight in him and cannot bear to forget him. Supporting and honoring him as their sovereign, they surely feel delight in their innermost hearts, without putting on a mere outward show. When he guides them toward benefit, the people benefit from him and cannot bear to betray him. Loving him as their own parents, they surely possess sincerity of inward purpose, rather than a change merely on the surface. This assuredly is what is called great good: why should it await inquiry? Such is the meaning of the line, and the divinatory judgment is contained within it.
Moreover, examining the Book of Documents, we find: “Without a sovereign, the people cannot help one another to live; without the people, the sovereign has no means to rule the four quarters.” It also says: “You are the wind; the common people are the grass.” Thus we know that, by the principle that they form one body, their mutual dependence is profound, and their response to one another is very swift. Otherwise, their purposes diverge and their ways part. Divergence and separation are paths the sage does not follow. Hence it is said: “The people of a true king are expansive and at ease; the people of a hegemon…”

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
驩虞如也公私之辯讀易者詳之
與天地相似故不違知周乎萬物而道濟
天下故不過旁行而不流樂天知命故
不憂安土敦乎仁故能愛
愼蒙
同考試官教諭毛批知周以下說聖人智仁
與天地合德良是
同考試官教諭易批聖人盡性事發得明潔
錄之
===
考試官教授何批得旨
考試官教授高批冲澹
大傳言聖人盡性之事以見其用易也蓋知仁
合德而與天地參易之能事備矣聖人以之而
盡性焉謂非善於用易者邪大傳之意蓋如此
且天地設位而易行乎其中矣聖人盡性于易
者也而崇效天焉卑法地焉則固與之克肖矣
而亦奚有于違邪何者天陽化也其道曰知地
陰變也其道曰仁聖人知仁合德者也故有以
punctuated:
驩虞如也。公私之辯，讀易者詳之。
與天地相似，故不違；知周乎萬物，而道濟天下，故不過；旁行而不流；樂天知命，故不憂；安土敦乎仁，故能愛。
愼蒙
同考試官教諭毛批：知周以下，說聖人智仁與天地合德，良是。
同考試官教諭易批：聖人盡性事，發得明潔，錄之。
考試官教授何批：得旨。
考試官教授高批：冲澹。
大傳言聖人盡性之事，以見其用易也。蓋知仁合德，而與天地參，易之能事備矣。聖人以之而盡性焉，謂非善於用易者邪？大傳之意蓋如此。且天地設位，而易行乎其中矣。聖人盡性于易者也，而崇效天焉，卑法地焉，則固與之克肖矣，而亦奚有于違邪？何者？天陽化也，其道曰知；地陰變也，其道曰仁。聖人知仁合德者也，故有以
translation_en:
…are full of delight and pleasure. Those who read the Changes should examine closely this distinction between public-mindedness and self-interest.

“He resembles Heaven and Earth and therefore does not run counter to them. His wisdom encompasses the myriad things, and his Way benefits all under Heaven; therefore he does not err. He ranges widely without going astray. He delights in Heaven and understands fate; therefore he does not worry. He rests content in his place and is steadfast in benevolence; therefore he can love.”

Shen Meng 愼蒙

Associate Examiner Mao, Instructor, comments: “From ‘his wisdom encompasses’ onward, the explanation that the sage’s wisdom and benevolence unite in virtue with Heaven and Earth is indeed correct.”

Associate Examiner Yi, Instructor, comments: “The sage’s complete realization of his nature is expounded clearly and lucidly. Include this.”

Examiner He, Professor, comments: “Grasps the purport.”

Examiner Gao, Professor, comments: “Serene and restrained.”

The Great Commentary speaks of the sage’s complete realization of his nature to show how he employs the Changes. When wisdom and benevolence unite in virtue and stand alongside Heaven and Earth as a third, all that the Changes can accomplish is fully realized. Through this the sage completely realizes his nature. Could one say that he is not adept at employing the Changes? Such, broadly, is the meaning of the Great Commentary.

Moreover, Heaven and Earth take their positions, and change operates between them. The sage completely realizes his nature through the Changes: in loftiness he emulates Heaven, and in lowliness he models himself on Earth. Thus he truly resembles them; how could he run counter to them? Why is this so? Heaven transforms through yang, and its Way is called wisdom; Earth changes through yin, and its Way is called benevolence. The sage unites wisdom and benevolence in virtue, and therefore is able to…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
見天下之賾而知無不周尤必大其道以濟之
則明而且當有以協于中矣夫何過焉亦有以
見天下之動而權無不達尤必正其經以守之
則貞而不諒有以偕於時矣夫何流焉及其至
而言之理所自出者曰天命則稟于天之數也
惟其樂天知命則心無累于物而見不惑于私
故能無憂而知益深矣身所素居者曰土仁則
根于心之德也惟其安土敦仁則志不願乎外
而欲不留于內故能愛而仁益篤矣夫知仁如
===
天地矣又推之以達經權極之而妙神化則性
于是盡殆如子之事親善繼其志善述其事矣
豈不成位乎中而與天地參哉雖然厥彰厥微
匪靈弗瑩在聖人固誠無不明而能用夫易矣
然人不能皆聖也則思誠之功獨可少之哉有
志于學易者亦曰自愼動始
書
帝乃誕敷文德舞干羽于兩階七旬有苗
格
punctuated:
見天下之賾而知無不周，尤必大其道以濟之，則明而且當，有以協于中矣，夫何過焉？亦有以見天下之動而權無不達，尤必正其經以守之，則貞而不諒，有以偕於時矣，夫何流焉？及其至而言之，理所自出者曰天，命則稟于天之數也。惟其樂天知命，則心無累于物而見不惑于私，故能無憂而知益深矣。身所素居者曰土，仁則根于心之德也。惟其安土敦仁，則志不願乎外而欲不留于內，故能愛而仁益篤矣。夫知仁如天地矣，又推之以達經權，極之而妙神化，則性于是盡，殆如子之事親，善繼其志，善述其事矣。豈不成位乎中而與天地參哉？雖然，厥彰厥微，匪靈弗瑩。在聖人固誠無不明，而能用夫易矣。然人不能皆聖也，則思誠之功獨可少之哉？有志于學易者，亦曰自愼動始。
書
帝乃誕敷文德，舞干羽于兩階，七旬有苗格。
translation_en:
…to perceive the hidden complexities of all under Heaven, so that his wisdom encompasses everything. Yet he must also broaden his Way to bring this to fruition; then he is discerning and fitting in his judgments, able to accord with the mean. How could he go too far? He can likewise perceive all the movements under Heaven, so that his discretionary judgment reaches everywhere. Yet he must also rectify the constant principles by which he holds firm; then he is steadfast without being rigidly bound to his word, able to act in keeping with the times. How could he drift astray?
To speak of this at its utmost: that from which principle issues is called Heaven; destiny is the allotted course received from Heaven. Precisely because he delights in Heaven and understands destiny, his mind is unburdened by things and his insight is not confused by selfish concerns. Thus he can be free of anxiety, and his wisdom grows ever deeper. The place where one ordinarily dwells is called one’s land; benevolence is the virtue rooted in the heart. Precisely because he is content in his land and steadfast in benevolence, his aspirations do not reach outward in longing, nor do desires linger within. Thus he can love, and his benevolence grows ever more profound.
His wisdom and benevolence thus resemble Heaven and Earth. He further extends them to comprehend constant principles and discretionary judgment, and carries them to their utmost to achieve the subtle workings of spiritual transformation. His nature is thereby fully realized. This is much like a son serving his parents, skillfully carrying forward their intentions and continuing their undertakings. Does he not thereby establish his place between Heaven and Earth and form a triad with them?
Nevertheless, what is manifest and what is hidden cannot be illuminated without spiritual intelligence. In the sage, sincerity indeed leaves nothing unilluminated, and he can therefore put the Changes to use. Yet not everyone can be a sage: can the effort to attain sincerity possibly be dispensed with? Those intent on studying the Changes must begin by being circumspect in their actions.
Book of Documents
The emperor then widely displayed his civil virtue, having dancers perform with shields and feather plumes between the two stairways. After seventy days, the Youmiao submitted.

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
孫汝賢
同考試官教諭李批宣武功而徵諸文德帝
王柔遠之道也此作足以發之槩見其盛
同考試官教諭曾批苗人格化聖人動物之
誠也揭以繹之有見矣為之擊節
考試官教授何批能悉聖人來遠之化
考試官教授高批整肅
史臣紀聖世內治修而遠人服以見其盛也甚
矣威武之未可以服人也帝舜之修文德而有
===
苗格也有以夫昔禹之征有苗也因益之贊而
班師矣帝之當是時也夫何為哉是故四方風
動九功惟叙文教之成於天下者久矣玆乃誕
而布之凡五教之敷與好生之洽者方惟日不
足而無遠弗届矣夫何有于止極邪帝之敷是
德也抑何見哉是故武舞以干文舞以羽文物
之昭於朝廷者素矣玆乃發而揚之或舞之阼
階或舞之賓階者惟進退有度而泰和可象矣
夫何如其雍容邪是惟盡其在我帝之心初不
punctuated:
孫汝賢

同考試官教諭李批：「宣武功而徵諸文德，帝王柔遠之道也。此作足以發之，槩見其盛。」
同考試官教諭曾批：「苗人格化，聖人動物之誠也。揭以繹之，有見矣，為之擊節。」
考試官教授何批：「能悉聖人來遠之化。」
考試官教授高批：「整肅。」

史臣紀聖世內治修而遠人服，以見其盛也。甚矣，威武之未可以服人也！帝舜之修文德而有苗格也，有以夫！昔禹之征有苗也，因益之贊而班師矣。帝之當是時也，夫何為哉？是故四方風動，九功惟叙，文教之成於天下者久矣。玆乃誕而布之，凡五教之敷與好生之洽者，方惟日不足，而無遠弗届矣。夫何有于止極邪？帝之敷是德也，抑何見哉？是故武舞以干，文舞以羽，文物之昭於朝廷者素矣。玆乃發而揚之，或舞之阼階，或舞之賓階者，惟進退有度，而泰和可象矣。夫何如其雍容邪？是惟盡其在我，帝之心初不
translation_en:
Sun Ruxian

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: “To set forth martial achievement and trace it to civil virtue is to show the way emperors and kings cherish distant peoples. This composition adequately elucidates it, giving a broad view of its magnificence.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Zeng, Instructor: “The Miao people’s coming over and being transformed demonstrates the sage’s sincerity, which moves other beings. The author brings this out and expounds it with insight. I applaud him.”
Comment by Examiner He, Professor: “He fully conveys the sage’s transforming influence, which draws distant peoples to him.”
Comment by Examiner Gao, Professor: “Orderly and dignified.”

The court historian records how, in the age of the sage, internal government was well ordered and distant peoples submitted, thereby displaying its greatness. How utterly inadequate martial might is to secure people’s submission! There was indeed a reason why Emperor Shun cultivated civil virtue and the Youmiao came over! Formerly, when Yu campaigned against the Youmiao, he withdrew his army following Yi’s counsel. What, then, did the emperor do at that time?

His influence stirred the four quarters like the wind, and the nine achievements were duly ordered: civil instruction had long since been established throughout the realm. Now he spread it abroad on a grand scale. In disseminating the five teachings and extending his life-loving benevolence, he felt that each day afforded insufficient time, and there was no place so distant that his influence did not reach it. What limit could there be to it? Yet how was the emperor’s dissemination of this virtue made manifest?

Shields were used in the martial dance and feathers in the civil dance: the emblems of cultivated order had long shone at court. Now he brought them forth and displayed them. Some danced at the host’s steps, others at the guests’ steps; their advances and retreats were measured, and supreme harmony found visible expression. How gracious and composed it all was! This was simply to do to the utmost what lay within his own power. The emperor’s intention from the outset was not…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
期於苗之格者迨夫遡自班師甫七旬耳蠢玆
有苗漸被乎聲敎者皆相率而來王于以覩中
國文物之盛焉鼓舞乎德化者皆革心而效順
于以被天地覆載之仁焉由是而懷柔之有加
也由是而分北之可行也是蓋誠能動物苗之
格亦有莫能自已者耳夫文德之敷不在於禹
班師之後而有苗之格適會於舞干羽之時有
虞之盛信千載而一見矣抑征伐之道上世以
德末世以力而舒慘隨之雖以湯武之聖有慙
德之論而爰及干戈義士猶不滿焉況其下者
乎史稱三苗有洞庭彭蠡之險若未易圖者而
帝舜竟以文德格之然則威武何用哉後世有
銳志雪恥致海內虛耗窮兵以貽晚年之悔者
惜乎無以此語之
貌曰恭言曰從視曰明聽曰聰思曰睿
來日升
同考試官敎諭李批五事各具一德也而一
以貫之者也子能言之有見矣受形受性亦有本
punctuated:
期於苗之格者。迨夫遡自班師，甫七旬耳，蠢玆有苗，漸被乎聲敎者，皆相率而來王，于以覩中國文物之盛焉；鼓舞乎德化者，皆革心而效順，于以被天地覆載之仁焉。由是而懷柔之有加也，由是而分北之可行也。是蓋誠能動物，苗之格亦有莫能自已者耳。夫文德之敷，不在於禹班師之後，而有苗之格，適會於舞干羽之時。有虞之盛，信千載而一見矣。抑征伐之道，上世以德，末世以力，而舒慘隨之。雖以湯武之聖，有慙德之論，而爰及干戈，義士猶不滿焉，況其下者乎？史稱三苗有洞庭、彭蠡之險，若未易圖者，而帝舜竟以文德格之。然則威武何用哉？後世有銳志雪恥，致海內虛耗，窮兵以貽晚年之悔者，惜乎無以此語之！

貌曰恭，言曰從，視曰明，聽曰聰，思曰睿。

來日升

同考試官敎諭李批：五事各具一德也，而一以貫之者也。子能言之，有見矣。受形受性，亦有本
translation_en:
…expect the Miao to submit. Yet, reckoning from the army’s return, barely seventy days had passed when these unruly Miao, gradually touched by his civilizing teachings, led one another to acknowledge his sovereignty and thereby witnessed the splendor of the Central Kingdom’s culture and institutions. Inspired by his transforming virtue, they changed their hearts and pledged obedience, thereby receiving a benevolence like that of Heaven and Earth, which shelter and sustain all things. Thus his care for those afar grew still greater, and thus their division and removal could be carried out. This was surely because sincerity can move others: the Miao could not help but submit. The dissemination of civil virtue did not begin only after Yu withdrew his army; rather, the Miao’s submission happened to coincide with the dance of shields and feathers. The flourishing rule of Youyu was indeed something witnessed only once in a thousand years.

Moreover, in the conduct of punitive expeditions, the earliest ages relied on virtue, while later ages relied on force; leniency and harshness followed accordingly. Even with the sagehood of Tang and Wu, there was talk of virtue that gave cause for shame; when recourse was made to arms, righteous men still expressed dissatisfaction. How much more so with lesser rulers! The histories say that the Sanmiao possessed the natural defenses of Dongting and Pengli, making them seemingly difficult to overcome. Yet Emperor Shun ultimately brought them to submission through civil virtue. What use, then, was military might? In later ages, there were rulers whose determination to avenge humiliation exhausted the realm, and whose relentless warfare left them with regrets in old age. Alas, no one imparted these words to them!

“Demeanor should be reverent; speech, compliant; sight, clear; hearing, acute; thought, discerning.”

Lai Risheng

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: “Each of the five activities possesses its own virtue, yet a single principle runs through them all. You have been able to articulate this and have shown insight. Your discussion of receiving physical form and receiving one’s nature also has a basis …”

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之說也
同考試官教諭曾批讀此作四體不言而喻
矣心服
考試官教授何批敷暢
考試官教授高批是嘗有誠身之功者
君子叙五事而各著其德誠身之義昭矣蓋天
生蒸民有物必有則也君子隨在而能敬以從
事焉身有不誠者乎箕子演五事之疇以告武
王意蓋如此且夫天以五行生人也與之以形
===
而理即賦焉人以五事爲德也能踐其形而身
斯誠矣何以言之人之始生而形色具是則所
謂貌也貌之澤者水之爲也而其德則恭焉莊
敬之節不忒於臨下之儀祗恪之容罔愆於人
望之度是有此貌則有此恭矣恭非貌之德乎
人之形色具而聲音發是則所謂言也言之揚
者火之爲也而其德則從焉心聲之發因言以
宣者無鄙倍之氣德音之布託辭以達者無躁
妄之失是有此言則有此從矣從非言之德乎
punctuated:
之說也。
同考試官教諭曾批：讀此作，四體不言而喻矣，心服。
考試官教授何批：敷暢。
考試官教授高批：是嘗有誠身之功者。
君子叙五事而各著其德，誠身之義昭矣。蓋天生蒸民，有物必有則也。君子隨在而能敬以從事焉，身有不誠者乎？箕子演五事之疇以告武王，意蓋如此。且夫天以五行生人也，與之以形，而理即賦焉。人以五事爲德也，能踐其形，而身斯誠矣。何以言之？人之始生而形色具，是則所謂貌也。貌之澤者，水之爲也，而其德則恭焉。莊敬之節，不忒於臨下之儀；祗恪之容，罔愆於人望之度。是有此貌則有此恭矣，恭非貌之德乎？人之形色具而聲音發，是則所謂言也。言之揚者，火之爲也，而其德則從焉。心聲之發，因言以宣者，無鄙倍之氣；德音之布，託辭以達者，無躁妄之失。是有此言則有此從矣，從非言之德乎？
translation_en:
…is an explanation with a basis.

Associate Examiner Zeng, Instructor, comments: “Reading this composition, one understands how the four limbs convey meaning without words. I am convinced at heart.”

Examiner He, Professor, comments: “Expansive and fluent.”

Examiner Gao, Professor, comments: “This is someone who has worked at making himself sincere.”

The gentleman sets forth the Five Activities and makes manifest the virtue belonging to each; thus the meaning of making oneself sincere becomes clear. Heaven gives birth to the multitude of people, and wherever there is a thing, there must be its governing principle. If the gentleman can act with reverence in every circumstance, how could he fail to be sincere in his person? This was surely Jizi’s intention when he expounded the category of the Five Activities to King Wu. Heaven brings human beings into existence through the Five Phases: in giving them bodily form, it also endows them with principle. Human beings cultivate virtue through the Five Activities: by fully realizing what their bodily form entails, they make themselves sincere.

How may this be explained? When a person is first born and possesses bodily form and complexion, this is what is called appearance. The lustre of appearance is the work of water, and its virtue is reverence. The discipline of solemn respect admits no error in one’s bearing toward those below; a reverent demeanour does not fall short of the standard others look to. Thus, where there is this appearance, there is this reverence. Is reverence not the virtue of appearance?

Once a person possesses bodily form and complexion and produces sounds, this is what is called speech. The outward projection of speech is the work of fire, and its virtue is accordance. When the voice of the heart issues forth and is expressed in speech, it contains no trace of vulgarity or perversity; when virtuous utterances are disseminated and conveyed through words, they contain no fault of impetuousness or recklessness. Thus, where there is this speech, there is this accordance. Is accordance not the virtue of speech?

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
能言而後能視矣視所以爲木之散也視而曰
明蓋其貞明不昧之體不爲淺近所蔽以通神
明之德以類萬物之情是故明之所受出其視
焉而天下無遁形矣謂非視之德邪能視而後
能聽矣聽所以爲金之收也聽而曰聰蓋其至
虛能通之神不爲疑似所惑以涵萬象之感以
收萬物之聲是故聰之所受出其聽焉而天下
無遺響矣謂非聽之德邪至於思能通土心之
官也精氣之會也思則清明之體有以見天下
===
之賾如神之知有以達天下之故寂然不動感
而遂通恭從明聰一以貫之而無遺矣思不曰
睿乎是則觀五事則知受形之原天之所以命
諸人也觀五德則知受性之原人之所以合諸
天也君子誠身可不於其敬焉圖之抑理氣之
相承也久矣人惟不思耳是以舉物而遺則言
人而昧天道之大原荒矣大禹因數第疇以人
合天諄諄以敬爲言則學問之極功聖人之能
事不外是也故曰大禹開萬世心學之源
punctuated: 能言而後能視矣。視所以爲木之散也。視而曰明，蓋其貞明不昧之體，不爲淺近所蔽，以通神明之德，以類萬物之情。是故明之所受，出其視焉，而天下無遁形矣，謂非視之德邪？能視而後能聽矣。聽所以爲金之收也。聽而曰聰，蓋其至虛能通之神，不爲疑似所惑，以涵萬象之感，以收萬物之聲。是故聰之所受，出其聽焉，而天下無遺響矣，謂非聽之德邪？至於思，能通土，心之官也，精氣之會也。思則清明之體有以見天下之賾，如神之知有以達天下之故，寂然不動，感而遂通，恭從明聰，一以貫之而無遺矣。思不曰睿乎？是則觀五事，則知受形之原，天之所以命諸人也；觀五德，則知受性之原，人之所以合諸天也。君子誠身，可不於其敬焉圖之？抑理氣之相承也久矣，人惟不思耳。是以舉物而遺則，言人而昧天，道之大原荒矣。大禹因數第疇，以人合天，諄諄以敬爲言，則學問之極功、聖人之能事，不外是也。故曰：「大禹開萬世心學之源。」
translation_en:
Only after being able to speak can one see. Sight embodies the dispersive action of Wood. The virtue assigned to sight is clarity: its steadfastly luminous and unclouded substance is not obscured by what is shallow or near at hand, enabling one to comprehend the powers of spiritual illumination and to discern by analogy the dispositions of the myriad things. Thus the clarity one receives emerges through sight, and nothing under Heaven can conceal its form. Could this be anything other than the virtue of sight? Only after being able to see can one hear. Hearing embodies the gathering action of Metal. The virtue assigned to hearing is acuity: its utterly receptive and penetrating spiritual capacity is not confused by doubtful appearances, enabling one to encompass the impressions of the myriad phenomena and gather the sounds of the myriad things. Thus the acuity one receives emerges through hearing, and no sound under Heaven is missed. Could this be anything other than the virtue of hearing?

As for thought, it connects with Earth; it is the function of the heart and the meeting place of vital essence and qi. Through thought, the clear and luminous substance can perceive the intricacies of all under Heaven, and spirit-like understanding can penetrate the reasons for all that happens under Heaven. Still and unmoving, it responds to stimuli and thereby comprehends. Reverence, compliance, clarity, and acuity are all threaded together by a single principle, with nothing left out. Is not the virtue of thought called sagacity? Thus, by observing the Five Activities, one understands the source from which bodily form is received—how Heaven endows human beings. By observing the Five Virtues, one understands the source from which human nature is received—how human beings accord with Heaven. If the gentleman would make himself sincere, can he fail to pursue this through reverent attentiveness?

Indeed, principle and qi have long sustained one another; people simply fail to reflect. Thus they discuss things while overlooking their governing standards, and speak of humanity while remaining ignorant of Heaven: the great source of the Way is neglected. Yu the Great followed the numbers in ordering the categories, bringing humanity into accord with Heaven, and earnestly and repeatedly spoke of reverent attentiveness. The highest achievement of learning and the full accomplishment of the sage lie within this. Hence it is said: “Yu the Great opened the wellspring of the learning of the heart for all ages.”

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
詩
帝謂文王無然畔援無然歆羨誕先登于
岸
楊機
同考試官訓導李批聖人造道處不數語而
足蓋亦深有得者
同考試官教諭吳批只平平說去而義理自
見刻之為務纖麗者式
考試官教授何批是作雅義者取之
===
考試官教授高批典重
天命聖人以天德之純其寓意深矣夫德未純
私心累之也文王無是焉其斯造位乎天德歟
此詩言文王伐密之事而推本於天也故設為
帝命文王之詞曰利害相形而畔援生焉人心
至難制也爾其以理制欲相忘於彼此之分一
取一舍惟其可而不容心焉情欲相感而歆羨
生焉己私未易克也爾其以道御氣虛心於物
我之交欲也惡也視之理而不妄動焉夫人心
punctuated:
詩

帝謂文王：「無然畔援，無然歆羨，誕先登于岸。」

楊機

同考試官訓導李批：「聖人造道處，不數語而足，蓋亦深有得者。」

同考試官教諭吳批：「只平平說去，而義理自見，刻之為務纖麗者式。」

考試官教授何批：「是作雅義者，取之。」

考試官教授高批：「典重。」

天命聖人以天德之純，其寓意深矣。夫德未純，私心累之也。文王無是焉，其斯造位乎天德歟？此詩言文王伐密之事，而推本於天也。故設為帝命文王之詞曰：「利害相形而畔援生焉，人心至難制也。爾其以理制欲，相忘於彼此之分，一取一舍，惟其可而不容心焉。情欲相感而歆羨生焉，己私未易克也。爾其以道御氣，虛心於物我之交，欲也惡也，視之理而不妄動焉。夫人心
translation_en:
Book of Odes

“God said to King Wen: ‘Do not thus reject one thing and cling to another; do not thus covet and envy. Be the first to ascend the shore in greatness.’”

Yang Ji

Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor, comments: “A few words suffice to convey how the sage attains the Way. The writer, too, evidently has a deep understanding.”

Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: “The exposition proceeds quite plainly, yet its moral principles emerge of themselves. Print it as a model for those who pursue delicate ornament.”

Examiner He, Professor, comments: “Those who compose elegant expositions should adopt this as a model.”

Examiner Gao, Professor, comments: “Classical and dignified.”

Heaven enjoins the sage to possess the purity of Heaven’s virtue: profound indeed is the meaning conveyed. When virtue is not yet pure, it is encumbered by selfish thoughts. King Wen was free of these. Was this how he attained a place in Heaven’s virtue [?]? This ode speaks of King Wen’s campaign against Mi and traces its ultimate source to Heaven. It therefore frames these words as God’s command to King Wen:

“When advantage and harm are set against each other, rejection and attachment arise. The human heart is exceedingly difficult to govern. You should use principle to restrain desire, forgetting the distinction between this and that. In every acceptance and rejection, follow only what is fitting, allowing no private intention to intrude. When feelings and desires stir one another, covetousness and envy arise. One’s selfishness is not easily overcome. You should use the Way to govern your vital energies and keep your heart free of preconceptions in the encounters between things and yourself. Whether desiring or disliking, attend to principle and do not act rashly. Now, the human heart…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
有所畔援則不得其正有所歆羨則不得其正
欲造道也難矣爾惟無是二者是以物不為撓
而天賦之知識以盡獨能精思力踐與太極為
全體凡道之極至爾蓋超衆人而先得之矣外
無所動而自然之明覺不虧獨能融會貫通與
天德為一致凡道之涯涘爾其先天下而獨濟
之矣吁此文王之德所以為盛蓋天實命之而
非人力之所及也其伐密也夫豈有所作惡於
其間哉抑考伐密伐崇皆文王事也而詩人每
===
原諸天者見帝王行師非出於得已乃所以奉
天也而己不與焉其訓嚴矣後世不此之務伐
楚以圖霸攻秦以洩停蓄之憤是皆聖人之棄
也而天理之在人心者亦滅矣噫此春秋之所
以作乎
自古在昔先民有作温恭朝夕執事有恪
查秉鉞
同考試官訓導李批辭不浮而理自足可謂
善頌者矣
punctuated:
有所畔援，則不得其正；有所歆羨，則不得其正。欲造道也，難矣！爾惟無是二者，是以物不為撓，而天賦之知識以盡，獨能精思力踐，與太極為全體。凡道之極至，爾蓋超衆人而先得之矣。外無所動，而自然之明覺不虧，獨能融會貫通，與天德為一致。凡道之涯涘，爾其先天下而獨濟之矣。吁！此文王之德所以為盛，蓋天實命之，而非人力之所及也。其伐密也，夫豈有所作惡於其間哉？抑考伐密、伐崇，皆文王事也，而詩人每原諸天者，見帝王行師非出於得已，乃所以奉天也，而己不與焉。其訓嚴矣！後世不此之務，伐楚以圖霸，攻秦以洩停蓄之憤，是皆聖人之棄也，而天理之在人心者亦滅矣。噫！此春秋之所以作乎？

自古在昔，先民有作；温恭朝夕，執事有恪。
查秉鉞
同考試官訓導李批：辭不浮而理自足，可謂善頌者矣。
translation_en:
…Whenever the heart inclines toward partisan attachments, it loses its proper balance; whenever it harbors covetous admiration, it loses its proper balance. How difficult it then becomes to attain the Way! You alone are free of these two faults. Thus external things do not disturb you, and your Heaven-endowed understanding is fully realized. You alone can reflect deeply and practice earnestly, forming a complete unity with the Supreme Ultimate. Whatever the ultimate reaches of the Way, you have surely surpassed the multitude and attained them first. Nothing external moves you, and your innate clarity of awareness remains unimpaired. You alone can comprehend all things in their interconnected unity and become one with Heaven’s virtue. Whatever the farthest bounds of the Way, you alone have reached them ahead of all under Heaven.

Ah! This is what made King Wen’s virtue so abundant. Heaven itself indeed ordained it; it lay beyond the reach of human effort. In his campaign against Mi, could any personal likes or dislikes [?] have entered into it? Now, the campaigns against Mi and Chong were both King Wen’s undertakings. Yet the poet invariably traces them to Heaven, showing that when sage kings and emperors deploy their armies, they do so only when they have no alternative. They thereby serve Heaven, without allowing their own interests to enter. How strict this teaching is! Later generations neglected this duty: they attacked Chu to seek hegemony and assaulted Qin to vent accumulated resentment. These are all acts that the sage rejects, and through them the heavenly principle within the human heart is also extinguished. Alas! Was this why the Spring and Autumn Annals was composed?

“From antiquity, in ages past, the forebears established their practices; gentle and reverent morning and evening, they performed their duties with respect.”

Zha Bingyue.

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor: “The language is not extravagant, yet the reasoning is fully sufficient. He may indeed be called skilled in praise.”

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭吳批說詩人不敢忘敬之意
宛然當是作手
考試官教授何批典雅
考試官教授高批文字嚴整錄之
商人於祀先之敬必推本其所傳者遠也蓋敬
也者所以祀乎其先也商人奉祭而歸諸古焉
其亦思所以繼之矣舊說以此為祀成湯之樂
也蓋曰宗廟之祭樂為大而所以將之者敬為
大顧茲升歌清廟而一敬是承豈自我作古哉
===
蓋自古在昔之時有開物成務之道曰先民也
者有以盡性命之微而制為典常是故俟后聖
而不惑有以萃天下之渙而肇稱殷禮足以昭
懿範于無窮故自其祀事言之精白乃心有嚴
於夙夜在公之際淑慎爾止祗承於奏假無言
之餘儼陟降之求而慎乃攸司薦其俎豆序其
禮樂勿勿乎欲其饗之也蓋自一獻以至九獻
而罔有弗欽者矣篤思成之綏而修乃常職對
越在天奔走在廟業業乎如將弗勝也蓋自一
punctuated:
同考試官教諭吳批：說詩人不敢忘敬之意，宛然，當是作手。
考試官教授何批：典雅。
考試官教授高批：文字嚴整，錄之。
商人於祀先之敬，必推本其所傳者遠也。蓋敬也者，所以祀乎其先也。商人奉祭而歸諸古焉，其亦思所以繼之矣。舊說以此為祀成湯之樂也。蓋曰：宗廟之祭，樂為大，而所以將之者，敬為大。顧茲升歌清廟，而一敬是承，豈自我作古哉？
蓋自古在昔之時，有開物成務之道。曰先民也者，有以盡性命之微而制為典常，是故俟后聖而不惑；有以萃天下之渙而肇稱殷禮，足以昭懿範于無窮。故自其祀事言之，精白乃心，有嚴於夙夜在公之際；淑慎爾止，祗承於奏假無言之餘。儼陟降之求，而慎乃攸司，薦其俎豆，序其禮樂，勿勿乎欲其饗之也。蓋自一獻以至九獻，而罔有弗欽者矣。篤思成之綏，而修乃常職，對越在天，奔走在廟，業業乎如將弗勝也。蓋自一
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: “The poet’s sense that he dare not forget reverence is vividly conveyed. This must be the work of an accomplished writer.”
Examiner He, Professor, comments: “Classical and elegant.”
Examiner Gao, Professor, comments: “The writing is disciplined and well ordered. Accept it.”
In their reverence when sacrificing to their ancestors, the people of Shang necessarily traced its origins far back through the tradition they had received. Reverence is that by which one sacrifices to one’s ancestors. In offering sacrifices and referring their practice back to antiquity, the people of Shang were surely also considering how to carry on that tradition. The old interpretation regards this poem as music for sacrifices to Cheng Tang. Its meaning is this: in sacrifices at the ancestral temple, music is of great importance; yet in that which sustains the music, reverence is of greatest importance. Now, as we ascend to sing in the pure temple and carry forward this single-minded reverence, could we ourselves have originated the precedent?
From ancient times there was a Way of opening up the potential of things and bringing affairs to completion. Those called the men of old could fathom the subtleties of human nature and Heaven’s mandate and establish enduring institutions and norms; thus they could await a later sage without misgivings. They could gather together the scattered people of the realm and first institute the rites of Yin, thereby illuminating an admirable example for all time. Thus, speaking of their sacrificial service: purify your heart, maintaining solemnity as you serve morning and night; be good and circumspect in your conduct, reverently attending even beyond the wordless presentation of offerings to the spirits. Solemnly seek the spirits as they ascend and descend, and carefully discharge your responsibilities. Present the sacrificial stands and vessels, arrange the rites and music in their proper order, and eagerly [?] desire that the spirits partake of them. From the first offering to the ninth, there was nothing performed without reverence. Earnestly seek the peace brought by thoughts fulfilled, and attend to your regular duties. Respond to those in Heaven and hasten about the temple, apprehensive as though you could not bear the charge. Indeed, from the first …

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
成以至九成而罔有或黷者矣古人恭敬之傳
蓋如此顧予烝嘗其敢以或忘哉吁此商人之
樂所以爲盛也抑商人尚聲而那之詩乃卒歸
之一敬者何哉記曰心怵而奉之以禮唯賢者
能盡祭之義必受其福蓋禮樂行乎陰陽而通
乎鬼神有不可偏廢者是故恭敬之傳商人以
之而魯祭不欲觀者豈獨以其禘之僭也哉嗚
呼知禮樂之情者能作識禮樂之文者能述乃
今知三代之治弗可及也已
===
春秋
冬十有二月丙子齊侯衛侯鄭伯來戰于
郎〔桓公十年〕春正月齊人衛人鄭人盟
于惡曹〔桓公十有一年〕
張志淑
同考試官教諭陳批夫子罪三國意或如此
叙事核而有條文亦稱之諸君可作當失辯矣
考試官教授何批是公穀之餘也
考試官教授高批斷案不謬於聖人
punctuated:
成以至九成，而罔有或黷者矣。古人恭敬之傳蓋如此，顧予烝嘗，其敢以或忘哉？吁！此商人之樂所以爲盛也。抑商人尚聲，而《那》之詩乃卒歸之一敬者，何哉？《記》曰：「心怵而奉之以禮，唯賢者能盡祭之義，必受其福。」蓋禮樂行乎陰陽而通乎鬼神，有不可偏廢者。是故恭敬之傳，商人以之，而魯祭不欲觀者，豈獨以其禘之僭也哉？嗚呼！知禮樂之情者能作，識禮樂之文者能述。乃今知三代之治弗可及也已。

春秋

冬十有二月丙子，齊侯、衛侯、鄭伯來戰于郎。〔桓公十年〕春正月，齊人、衛人、鄭人盟于惡曹。〔桓公十有一年〕

張志淑

同考試官教諭陳批：「夫子罪三國，意或如此。叙事核而有條，文亦稱之。諸君可作當失辯矣。」

考試官教授何批：「是公穀之餘也。」

考試官教授高批：「斷案不謬於聖人。」
translation_en:
…from the first musical completion through the ninth, there was never any irreverence. Such was the tradition of reverence and respect among the ancients. As for our winter and autumn sacrifices, would we dare ever to forget it? Ah! This is what made the music of the Shang so splendid. Yet the Shang prized sound: why, then, does the hymn Na ultimately return to the single principle of reverence? The Record of Rites says: “With an apprehensive heart, one presents offerings according to ritual. Only the worthy can fully realize the meaning of sacrifice, and they will assuredly receive its blessings.” Ritual and music operate through yin and yang and communicate with ghosts and spirits; neither may be neglected. Thus the Shang put this tradition of reverence and respect into practice. When Confucius was unwilling to watch the sacrifices of Lu, was it solely because their performance of the di sacrifice usurped a prerogative beyond their station? Alas! Those who understand the essential nature of ritual and music can create them; those who recognize their outward forms can transmit them. Only now do I understand that the governance of the Three Dynasties cannot be equaled.

Spring and Autumn Annals

“In winter, in the twelfth month, on the bingzi day, the Marquis of Qi, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Zheng came to fight at Lang.” 〔Tenth year of Duke Huan〕 “In spring, in the first month, men of Qi, Wei, and Zheng made a covenant at Ecao.” 〔Eleventh year of Duke Huan〕

Zhang Zhishu 張志淑

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “The Master's intention in condemning the three states may indeed have been like this. The account of events is accurate and orderly, and the writing matches it. You gentlemen may compose [such an answer?]; there would be no further argument [?].”

Comment by Examiner He, Professor: “This carries on the legacy of the Gongyang and Guliang commentaries.”

Comment by Examiner Gao, Professor: “Its judgment does not depart from that of the Sage.”

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
春秋變詞以責諸侯忿以興兵而黨以結信也
夫忿則失道黨則非義三國寔為之固王法之
禁乎此齊鄭衛也于郎曷戰乎爾鄭人釋憾之
請也主三國奈何歸惡於諸侯也魯後鄭班鄭
人讐焉摟而戰其皆褊心之肆乎先王之制兵
也亂略惟遏匪是則觀釁焉矣同惡其孰敢廼
玆異邦之涉悖道而恣焉以逞法也如之何或
以鍾巫之難桓故之以此固甘心焉者然越之
盟稷之會其誰尸之舍大憝而爰問放餼不亦
===
顛乎斯之謂不知類也噫諸侯非用兵之患也
而無義問之難不然瀦宮污室周法具在也而
奚有於三國是故不言侵伐而特以來戰為文
著罪也以其事而惡之者也猶夫齊衛鄭也惡
曹曷盟乎爾三國自固之謀也窮諸人奈何分
惡於諸侯也魯師戰衂三國虞焉要而歃其皆
忮心之崇乎先王之設盟也王室是藩匪是則
善鄰焉矣濟惡其孰敢廼今徇師而誓蔑義而
羣焉匪臧法也如之何或以門庭之耻桓是之
punctuated:
春秋變詞以責諸侯，忿以興兵，而黨以結信也。夫忿則失道，黨則非義，三國寔為之，固王法之禁乎！此齊鄭衛也，于郎曷戰乎爾？鄭人釋憾之請也。主三國奈何？歸惡於諸侯也。魯後鄭班，鄭人讐焉，摟而戰，其皆褊心之肆乎！先王之制兵也，亂略惟遏，匪是則觀釁焉矣。同惡其孰敢？廼玆異邦之涉，悖道而恣焉以逞，法也如之何？或以鍾巫之難，桓故之，以此固甘心焉者。然越之盟、稷之會，其誰尸之？舍大憝而爰問放餼，不亦顛乎！斯之謂不知類也。噫！諸侯非用兵之患也，而無義問之難。不然，瀦宮污室，周法具在也，而奚有於三國？是故不言侵伐，而特以來戰為文，著罪也，以其事而惡之者也。
猶夫齊衛鄭也，惡曹曷盟乎爾？三國自固之謀也。窮諸人奈何？分惡於諸侯也。魯師戰衂，三國虞焉，要而歃，其皆忮心之崇乎！先王之設盟也，王室是藩，匪是則善鄰焉矣。濟惡其孰敢？廼今徇師而誓，蔑義而羣焉，匪臧，法也如之何？或以門庭之耻，桓是之
translation_en:
The Spring and Autumn Annals varies its wording to censure the feudal lords for raising armies out of anger and pledging mutual trust through factional alliances. Anger departs from the Way, and factionalism violates righteousness. The three states indeed committed these acts: surely royal law forbade them! These were Qi, Zheng, and Wei. Why did they fight at Lang? At the request of the men of Zheng, who wished to vent their resentment. Why identify the rulers of the three states as the principals? To lay the blame upon the feudal lords. Lu had placed Zheng lower in precedence, and the men of Zheng bore it a grudge. They drew the others into battle: was this not an unbridled indulgence of narrow-mindedness on the part of all three?
When the former kings regulated military action, its purpose was to check disorder and aggression; otherwise, one was to watch for an occasion that warranted intervention. Who would dare join others in wrongdoing? Yet here they crossed into another state, defying the Way and acting without restraint to satisfy themselves. How could the law countenance this? Some might invoke the calamity at Zhongwu, for which Duke Huan was responsible: on these grounds, they certainly had cause to seek satisfaction. Yet who had presided over the covenant at Yue and the meeting at Ji? To set aside the great malefactor and instead call someone to account for releasing provisions [?]—was this not to turn things upside down? This is what is meant by failing to distinguish categories. Alas! The trouble with the feudal lords was not their use of arms; the difficulty was their lack of righteous grounds for calling another to account. Otherwise, the Zhou laws prescribing the flooding of a palace and the destruction of its chambers were fully available: what obstacle would there have been for the three states? Thus the text does not speak of an invasion or punitive expedition, but specifically writes that they “came to fight,” exposing their guilt. It condemns them through the deed itself.
These were likewise Qi, Wei, and Zheng. Why did they make a covenant at Ecao? It was a plan by the three states to secure themselves. Why reduce them to the designation “men”? To apportion blame among the feudal lords. Lu’s army had suffered defeat, and the three states grew apprehensive. They bound one another by a blood oath: was this not an elevation of their malicious intentions? When the former kings instituted covenants, their purpose was to defend the royal house; otherwise, they served to maintain good relations with neighboring states. Who would dare use them to further wrongdoing? Yet now they swore an oath in support of their military undertaking [?], disregarding righteousness and banding together in wrongdoing. How could the law countenance this? Some might invoke the humiliation at his very gates, which Duke Huan sought to…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
圖此固戒心焉者然兵于郎外於桃丘其誰甚
之略修睦而徼福明神不亦鄙乎斯之謂不知
務也噫諸侯非有盟之患也而無義舉之難不
然定亂平怨周官可稽也而何靳於一盟是故
不錄諸侯特以人稱示貶也以其事而微之者
也聖人律三國也其諸勅法乎是役也始禍者
鄭忽習姦者齊之祿父衛晉也奚糊其口於四
方桃丘之約亦既何爲迺二三其德殄邦禮而
厚鄰怨民弗與也於逮嗣世相鼠賦焉昭業允
===
休其文公乎君子謂衛宣免也幸矣
夏楚子蔡侯陳侯鄭伯許男徐子滕子頓
子胡子沈子小邾子宋世子佐淮夷會
于申〔昭公四年〕
汪呂之
同考試官教諭陳批晉平之世伯業其不競
乎申之會夷夏盛衰之迹可考也讀子之作有餘
慨焉錄之
考試官教授何批知脫時格
punctuated:
圖，此固戒心焉者。然兵于郎，外於桃丘，其誰甚之？略修睦而徼福明神，不亦鄙乎？斯之謂不知務也。噫！諸侯非有盟之患也，而無義舉之難。不然，定亂平怨，周官可稽也，而何靳於一盟？是故不錄諸侯，特以人稱，示貶也，以其事而微之者也。聖人律三國也，其諸勅法乎？是役也，始禍者鄭忽，習姦者齊之祿父、衛晉也。奚糊其口於四方？桃丘之約，亦既何爲？迺二三其德，殄邦禮而厚鄰怨，民弗與也。於逮嗣世，《相鼠》賦焉。昭業允休，其文公乎？君子謂衛宣免也，幸矣。
夏，楚子、蔡侯、陳侯、鄭伯、許男、徐子、滕子、頓子、胡子、沈子、小邾子、宋世子佐、淮夷會于申。〔昭公四年〕
汪呂之
同考試官教諭陳批：晉平之世，伯業其不競乎？申之會，夷夏盛衰之迹可考也。讀子之作，有餘慨焉，錄之。
考試官教授何批：知脫時格。
translation_en:
…to plan for this was certainly to exercise vigilance. Yet which was worse: the fighting at Lang or exclusion at Taoqiu? To neglect the cultivation of amity while seeking blessings from the bright spirits—is this not contemptible? This is what is meant by failing to understand what matters. Alas! The lords’ trouble was not that they made covenants; their difficulty was that they undertook nothing righteous. Otherwise, the Offices of Zhou provides precedents for settling disorder and reconciling grievances: why begrudge a single covenant? Thus the text does not record them by their titles as lords, but calls them merely “men,” indicating censure. It diminishes them on account of their conduct. In judging the three states, was the Sage not enforcing the rules?
In this campaign, the one who initiated the calamity was Hu of Zheng; those practiced in wrongdoing were Lufu of Qi and Jin of Wei. How could they silence the mouths of the four quarters [?]? What, after all, had the agreement at Taoqiu accomplished? They were instead inconstant in their virtue, destroying interstate ritual propriety and deepening their neighbors’ resentment. The people did not support them. By the succeeding generation, “Look at the Rat” was composed. Surely it was Duke Wen whose illustrious achievements were truly splendid? The gentleman says that Duke Xuan of Wei was fortunate to escape.
In summer, the Viscount of Chu, the Marquis of Cai, the Marquis of Chen, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Viscount of Xu, the Viscount of Teng, the Viscount of Dun, the Viscount of Hu, the Viscount of Shen, the Viscount of Xiaozhu, Zuo, Heir Apparent of Song, and the Huai Yi met at Shen. 〔Fourth year of Duke Zhao〕
Wang Lüzhi
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “In the time of Duke Ping of Jin, was not the hegemonic enterprise failing? In the meeting at Shen, one can trace the rise and decline of the Yi and the Xia. Reading your composition leaves me with lingering sorrow. I select it for inclusion.”
Comment by Examiner He, Professor: “He knows how to break free of the conventional style of the day.”

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎授高批不俗
春秋於中國崇夷之信責君而備及其臣焉此
申之會中國君臣失而夷也不亦傷乎且于申
曷會楚虔請之晉而得諸侯有是會也其狄中
國曷虔也弗軌於君矣而胥戴焉是之狄爾及
大夫曷蔽其罪也夫陳蔡諸國王室之衞也寔
共命焉幾盡乎人殘執之刑其誰屬之玆維罔
克作休將焉用會矧以時祭而魯辭以疾而衞
辭以難而曹邾辭俾皆若而人虔不惴焉恐乎
===
而歸之天道祇見其誣也已無亦利其芘與事
襲召陵赦焉爾矣何禮之爲爰以淪於夷而莫
之諭也其奚以辭於四方致其身若此舛孰甚
焉猶有異焉者向戌列卿諸侯之良也寔服事
焉何以爲國沐浴之請其誰圖之玆維匪克夾
乂毋庸于從矧廼叔向以君無辱命有獻廼向
戌以薦聞有獻廼僑如以薦守有獻僉之若而
人虔不矯焉肆乎而委諸天命祇見其謬也已
無亦怵于勢與度以十年億焉爾矣何智之爲
punctuated:
考試官敎授高批：不俗。

春秋於中國崇夷之信，責君而備及其臣焉。此申之會，中國君臣失而夷也，不亦傷乎？且于申曷會？楚虔請之晉而得諸侯，有是會也。其狄中國曷？虔也弗軌於君矣，而胥戴焉，是之狄爾。及大夫曷？蔽其罪也。夫陳蔡諸國，王室之衞也，寔共命焉，幾盡乎人？殘執之刑，其誰屬之？玆維罔克作休，將焉用會？矧以時祭而魯辭，以疾而衞辭，以難而曹邾辭，俾皆若而人，虔不惴焉恐乎？而歸之天道，祇見其誣也已。無亦利其芘與？事襲召陵，赦焉爾矣，何禮之爲？爰以淪於夷而莫之諭也，其奚以辭於四方？致其身若此，舛孰甚焉！猶有異焉者，向戌列卿，諸侯之良也，寔服事焉，何以爲國？沐浴之請，其誰圖之？玆維匪克夾乂，毋庸于從。矧廼叔向以君無辱命有獻，廼向戌以薦聞有獻，廼僑如以薦守有獻，僉之若而人，虔不矯焉肆乎？而委諸天命，祇見其謬也已。無亦怵于勢與？度以十年，億焉爾矣，何智之爲？
translation_en:
Examiner Gao, Professor, comments: “Free of vulgarity.”

In the Spring and Autumn Annals’ record of the central states’ honoring the barbarians, it censures the rulers and extends its full demands to their ministers. At this meeting at Shen, the rulers and ministers of the central states erred and became barbarians. Is this not lamentable? Why, then, did they meet at Shen? Qian of Chu requested permission from Jin and obtained the attendance of the regional lords; thus this meeting took place. Why does the text treat the central states as barbarians? Qian had acted lawlessly toward his ruler, yet they all upheld him: that is why it treats them as barbarians. Why does the censure extend to the grandees? Because they concealed his crime.

The states of Chen, Cai, and the others were defenders of the royal house, yet they obeyed his commands. How nearly had they fulfilled their obligations as human beings [?]? To whom should the punishment for murderous violence and seizure be assigned [?]? Since they could accomplish nothing good in this, what use was there in attending the meeting? Moreover, Lu declined on grounds of seasonal sacrifices, Wei on grounds of illness, and Cao and Zhu on grounds of troubles at home. Had all been like these men, would Qian not have trembled in fear? Yet they attributed the matter to the Way of Heaven, revealing only their own falsehood. Was it not that they sought the advantage of his protection? They followed the precedent of Shaoling and simply pardoned him. What sort of ritual propriety was that? Thus they sank into barbarism without anyone admonishing them. How could they justify themselves before the four quarters? To bring themselves to such a condition—what error could be greater!

Yet there is something further to distinguish here. Xiang Xu, a ranked minister, was an outstanding man among the regional states, yet he served Qian. How could he thereby serve his own state? Who among them contemplated bathing before requesting punitive action against the regicide? Since they could not assist in bringing order, they should not have followed him. Moreover, Shuxiang offered his views concerning his ruler’s not dishonoring his charge; Xiang Xu offered his views concerning presenting what had been heard; and Qiaoru offered his views concerning presenting what was to be preserved [?]. Had they all been men of this kind, would Qian not have behaved high-handedly and without restraint [?]? Yet they consigned the matter to Heaven’s mandate, revealing only their own error. Was it not that they were intimidated by his power? They reckoned on ten years: it was merely conjecture. What sort of wisdom was that?

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
遄以變於夷而不可由也其奚以謝諸天下謀
其國至此恥孰大焉是故春秋累數諸侯而淮
夷不殊以夷諸國以責備賢者聖人於此所甚
隱也抑椒舉之謀范山之餘智也北方可圖楚
之愿其未蒐乎申之役闚天下之大也合諸侯
執徐子圍朱方遷賴而縣陳蔡天寔殷其毒也
畀而崇亂申亥之變天固斁而降之罰也文襄
之業嗣是焉晉其弗克靈承矣嗚呼聖人憂之
也至巳
===
禮記
爲人君者謹其所好惡而已矣君好之則
臣爲之上行之則民從之
潘仲驂
同考試官教諭馬批結以夫子告顏子爲邦
意印證儘有發明
考試官教授何批詞理精明可錄
考試官教授高批錄此以勵夫囿於說樂
者
punctuated:
遄以變於夷而不可由也，其奚以謝諸天下？謀其國至此，恥孰大焉？是故《春秋》累數諸侯而淮夷不殊，以夷諸國，以責備賢者，聖人於此所甚隱也。抑椒舉之謀，范山之餘智也。北方可圖，楚之愿，其未蒐乎？申之役，闚天下之大也。合諸侯，執徐子，圍朱方，遷賴，而縣陳蔡，天寔殷其毒也。畀而崇亂，申亥之變，天固斁而降之罰也。文襄之業嗣是焉，晉其弗克靈承矣。嗚呼！聖人憂之也至巳！

《禮記》
爲人君者，謹其所好惡而已矣。君好之，則臣爲之；上行之，則民從之。

潘仲驂

同考試官教諭馬批：結以夫子告顏子爲邦意印證，儘有發明。
考試官教授何批：詞理精明，可錄。
考試官教授高批：錄此以勵夫囿於說樂者。
translation_en:
…swiftly becoming like the barbarians, so that their course could no longer be followed. How could they answer to all under Heaven? In planning for their states, they had come to this: what disgrace could be greater? Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals lists the regional lords together without distinguishing the Huai barbarians from them, thereby treating the various states as barbarian and demanding full responsibility of the worthy. This was a matter that deeply distressed the Sage.

Moreover, Jiao Ju’s plan merely drew on the remnants of Fan Shan’s wisdom. The north could be schemed against: had Chu’s ambitions not yet been mustered [?]? The undertaking at Shen was an attempt to spy out the vast realm under Heaven. Convening the regional lords, seizing the Viscount of Xu, besieging Zhufang, relocating Lai, and making Chen and Cai into counties—Heaven was indeed allowing his perniciousness to grow. By granting him success, it magnified his disorder; with the upheaval involving Shen Hai, Heaven indeed rejected him and sent down punishment. The enterprise of Dukes Wen and Xiang was to be carried on thereafter, but Jin could no longer worthily inherit it. Alas! The Sage’s concern over this was profound indeed!

Record of Rites

“One who rules others need only be careful about what he likes and dislikes. What the ruler likes, his ministers will do; what those above practice, the people will follow.”

Pan Zhongcan

Comment by Associate Examiner Ma, Instructor: “The conclusion corroborates its argument with the meaning of the Master’s advice to Yan Zi on governing a state. It offers considerable illumination.”

Comment by Examiner He, Professor: “The wording and reasoning are refined and clear. Worth selecting.”

Comment by Examiner Gao, Professor: “Selected to encourage those whose interpretations remain confined to discussing music.”

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
人君當致愼於感人者以其所關者大也夫人
心之從感視上之好惡以為之趨耳君人者其
欲無愼得乎子夏告魏文侯以古樂新樂至此
欲其審於好惡之幾也以為德音之正溺音之
邪其道雖有不同然音感於外而情動於中豈
能自已乎使於此而好惡無節於內則易流者
益以蕩矣君人者夫亦察之於微以致其決之
其所可好也而好之必歸諸道所以章好而象
德者在是之其所可惡也而惡之必歸諸非道
===
所以癉惡而綴淫者在是若是果何為哉蓋以
君者臣之則也心之所好雖未大於聲色然臣
將近而法之是訓是行從厥攸好蓋有不率而
勸者矣苟所好或非其正寧能免於首惡之名
邪上者民之表也身之所行雖未修之播告然
民將遠而效之而康而色惟皇之極殆有不戒
以孚者矣使所行弗順於道豈能已其效尤之
弊邪是則好惡雖微而係於臣民之重如此吾
君聽音可不愼於所擇以為感人動物之本乎
punctuated: 人君當致愼於感人者，以其所關者大也。夫人心之從感，視上之好惡以為之趨耳。君人者，其欲無愼得乎？子夏告魏文侯以古樂新樂，至此欲其審於好惡之幾也。以為德音之正、溺音之邪，其道雖有不同，然音感於外而情動於中，豈能自已乎？使於此而好惡無節於內，則易流者益以蕩矣。君人者，夫亦察之於微，以致其決。之其所可好也，而好之必歸諸道，所以章好而象德者在是；之其所可惡也，而惡之必歸諸非道，所以癉惡而綴淫者在是。若是，果何為哉？蓋以君者，臣之則也。心之所好，雖未大於聲色，然臣將近而法之，是訓是行，從厥攸好，蓋有不率而勸者矣。苟所好或非其正，寧能免於首惡之名邪？上者，民之表也。身之所行，雖未修之播告，然民將遠而效之，而康而色，惟皇之極，殆有不戒以孚者矣。使所行弗順於道，豈能已其效尤之弊邪？是則好惡雖微，而係於臣民之重如此。吾君聽音，可不愼於所擇，以為感人動物之本乎？
translation_en:
The ruler should exercise the utmost care over what influences others, because so much depends upon it. When people’s hearts respond to an influence, they merely look to the preferences and aversions of those above them for the direction they should take. Can one who rules others afford to be careless? In speaking to Marquis Wen of Wei about ancient and modern music, Zixia at this point wished him to examine closely the subtle beginnings of his preferences and aversions. His meaning was that although the upright sounds of virtuous music and the perverse sounds of depraved music follow different paths, sound acts upon us from without and feelings stir within: how could these responses cease of themselves? If preferences and aversions are not restrained within, dispositions already prone to drift will become still more unrestrained. The ruler must therefore examine these things at their subtlest beginnings and reach a firm decision. In turning toward what deserves to be liked, he must direct his liking toward the Way: herein lies the means to make manifest what is good and give visible expression to virtue. In turning toward what deserves to be disliked, he must direct his dislike toward what violates the Way: herein lies the means to condemn evil and restrain excess. Why, indeed, should he act thus?

It is because the ruler is the standard for his ministers. Although the preferences of his heart may not yet have been conspicuously expressed in voice or countenance, his ministers, close at hand, will take them as their model. They heed them and act upon them, following what he likes; thus they may be encouraged without being expressly led. If what he likes should be improper, how could he escape the name of an instigator of evil? Those above are the example for the people. Although their personal conduct may not yet have been set forth in public proclamations [?], the people at a distance will imitate it. “Your ease and your countenance” must accord with “the sovereign’s highest standard”: thus the people may respond with trust even without admonition. If his conduct does not accord with the Way, how could he prevent the harm of their imitating his faults? Preferences and aversions may be subtle, yet their consequences for ministers and people are as weighty as this. When our lord listens to music, can he fail to choose carefully, making that choice the foundation for influencing people and moving other beings?

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
抑古樂之作聖人本之性情均之律度以宣暢
其和心終而格人神感天地順氣成象而太和
興焉其視鄭衛之音蓋霄壤矣大音寖微日趨
靡曼文侯聽古樂而恐臥聽溺音而不知倦何
足咎哉故子夏終陳謹於好惡之言以開悟之
豈非夫子告顏子爲邦之道而欲其用韶舞放
鄭聲之意歟嗚呼以此爲坊後世猶有芝房寶
鼎霓裳羽衣之作如漢唐之君者
先王之所以治天下者五貴有德貴貴貴
===
老敬長慈幼此五者先王之所以定天
下也
胡采
同考試官教諭馬批形容王者氣象得出蓋
留心經學者
考試官教授何批五者關係世道風俗故
能定天下此作發揮明盡錄之
考試官教授高批題常而意新可取
先王治道有其要而因著治之所由成也夫貴
punctuated:
抑古樂之作，聖人本之性情，均之律度，以宣暢其和心，終而格人神，感天地，順氣成象，而太和興焉。其視鄭衛之音，蓋霄壤矣。大音寖微，日趨靡曼，文侯聽古樂而恐臥，聽溺音而不知倦，何足咎哉？故子夏終陳謹於好惡之言以開悟之，豈非夫子告顏子爲邦之道，而欲其用韶舞、放鄭聲之意歟？嗚呼！以此爲坊，後世猶有芝房、寶鼎、霓裳羽衣之作，如漢唐之君者。

先王之所以治天下者五：貴有德，貴貴，貴老，敬長，慈幼。此五者，先王之所以定天下也。

胡采

同考試官教諭馬批：形容王者氣象得出，蓋留心經學者。

考試官教授何批：五者關係世道風俗，故能定天下。此作發揮明盡，錄之。

考試官教授高批：題常而意新，可取。

先王治道有其要，而因著治之所由成也。夫貴
translation_en:
Furthermore, in creating ancient music, the sages rooted it in human nature and feeling and regulated it by pitch standards and measures, thereby giving full expression to their harmonious hearts. Ultimately it reached humans and spirits, moved Heaven and Earth, brought the vital energies into accord and gave them patterned form, so that supreme harmony arose. Compared with the music of Zheng and Wei, it was as far apart as heaven and earth.
