As the great music gradually declined and tastes turned daily toward seductive refinement, what cause is there for surprise that Marquis Wen feared falling asleep when listening to ancient music, yet never tired of listening to debauched sounds? Thus Zixia concluded by urging him to exercise care in his likes and dislikes, seeking to awaken his understanding. Was this not the very intention of the Master when he instructed Master Yan in governing a state, wishing him to employ the Shao dance and banish the sounds of Zheng? Alas! Even with this as a safeguard, later ages still produced such works as “The Fungus Chamber,” “The Precious Tripod,” and “Rainbow Skirts and Feathered Robes,” under rulers such as those of the Han and Tang.

“The former kings governed All under Heaven through five things: honoring the virtuous, honoring the noble, honoring the aged, respecting elders, and cherishing the young. Through these five things the former kings brought stability to All under Heaven.”

Hu Cai

Comment by Associate Examiner Ma, Instructor: “He succeeds in portraying the bearing of a true king. He is evidently someone who devotes attention to the study of the Classics.”

Comment by Examiner He, Professor: “These five things bear upon the moral condition of the age and its customs; hence they can bring stability to All under Heaven. This composition expounds the matter clearly and fully. Selected for inclusion.”

Comment by Examiner Gao, Professor: “The topic is familiar, but the conception is fresh. Worth selecting.”

The former kings’ way of governing had its essentials, and here the means by which their government achieved success are accordingly made clear. Now, honoring…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
德貴貴貴老敬長慈幼皆先王治天下之要也
而治道之成亦豈外是哉且夫先王之治天下
法天作則而後世莫能及者固非徧物以為智
也亦非博施以為功也其要則有五者已矣彼
道充於己謂之有德先王則尊而尚之嚴惟丕
式毋敢慢焉貴則朝廷之爵不容於或褻必隆
之而示其體貌之尊老則鄉黨之齒不可以或
遺必惇之而修其孝養之義以至行吾敬而祗
事之罔違所以長長也推吾恩而撫字之不失
===
所以幼幼也先王為治之道如此而何以定天
下哉蓋天下之人有此五者雖各異其分而能
施之有道使各當其欲則賢才用而爵位崇世
道底隆平之盛齒讓行而慈愛洽風俗著淳美
之休自將各止其所而天下平矣是知聖人固
未嘗外天下以為治而天下卒不能外于聖人
以安其所治焉可見治道出於人心之所同然
而非意之也此先王之教因而弗改所以領天
下國家也歟雖然尊賢育才敬老慈幼無忘賓
punctuated:
德、貴貴、貴老、敬長、慈幼，皆先王治天下之要也，而治道之成亦豈外是哉？且夫先王之治天下，法天作則，而後世莫能及者，固非徧物以為智也，亦非博施以為功也，其要則有五者已矣。彼道充於己，謂之有德，先王則尊而尚之，嚴惟丕式，毋敢慢焉。貴則朝廷之爵，不容於或褻，必隆之而示其體貌之尊；老則鄉黨之齒，不可以或遺，必惇之而修其孝養之義。以至行吾敬而祗事之罔違，所以長長也；推吾恩而撫字之不失，所以幼幼也。
先王為治之道如此，而何以定天下哉？蓋天下之人有此五者，雖各異其分，而能施之有道，使各當其欲，則賢才用而爵位崇，世道底隆平之盛；齒讓行而慈愛洽，風俗著淳美之休。自將各止其所而天下平矣。是知聖人固未嘗外天下以為治，而天下卒不能外于聖人以安其所治焉。可見治道出於人心之所同然，而非意之也。此先王之教，因而弗改，所以領天下國家也歟？雖然，尊賢育才，敬老慈幼，無忘賓
translation_en:
…esteeming virtue, honoring the noble, valuing the aged, respecting elders, and caring for the young: these were all essentials by which the former kings governed all under Heaven. Could the accomplishment of good government lie outside them? In governing all under Heaven, the former kings took Heaven as their model and established standards that later ages could not match. This certainly did not mean knowing every single thing and calling that wisdom, nor dispensing benefits everywhere and calling that achievement. The essentials amounted to these five alone. Those in whom the Way was fully realized were said to possess virtue; the former kings honored and esteemed them, reverently taking them as great exemplars and never daring to slight them. Nobility pertains to the ranks conferred by the court, which must never be treated with disrespect: the kings necessarily exalted their holders and displayed the honor due to them through courteous treatment. Old age pertains to seniority within local communities, which must never be neglected: the kings necessarily treated the aged generously and fulfilled the duty of filial support. Extending their reverence and serving elders respectfully without transgression was how they treated elders as elders; extending their kindness and nurturing the young without neglect was how they treated the young as young.
Such was the former kings’ way of governing. How, then, did it bring stability to all under Heaven? Among the people of the realm are these five categories, each with its distinct station. If these practices are applied properly, so that each receives what they desire, the worthy and talented will be employed and ranks and offices held in esteem, bringing the world to flourishing peace. Deference according to age will prevail and loving care will reach everyone, giving social customs the beauty of simplicity and goodness. Each will naturally find their proper place, and all under Heaven will be at peace. From this we know that the sage never sought to govern apart from the people of the realm, while the people, in turn, could never secure peace in the realm under his governance apart from the sage. Clearly, the way of government arises from what human hearts agree upon; it is not arbitrarily contrived. Is this why the teaching of the former kings, followed without alteration, serves to guide all under Heaven, its states, and its ruling houses? Nevertheless, honoring the worthy and nurturing talent, respecting the aged and caring for the young, not forgetting guests…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
旅桓文嘗以是盟五伯矣卒不能淑季世於三
代何邪善乎孔子告哀公曰凡爲天下國家有
九經所以行之者一也後世有願治之君而皆
非本於誠意雖有所爲不過藻飾之虛耳何益
於治哉故曰有天德者然後可以語王道其要
只在謹獨
第貳場
論
君子尊德性而道問學
===
張志淑
同考試官教諭陳批精一之訓昉於虞廷萬
世之言學者莫加焉子思子之言夫亦有所受也
是作反覆論議而聖賢體用之學讀之躍如豈深
造而有得者邪噫是未可以科舉文字目之矣
考試官教授何批昔人謂文章須明白正
大此作近之可以式矣
考試官教授高批只就本題發明而紆徐
曲折綽有法度是理到之言
punctuated:
旅，桓文嘗以是盟五伯矣，卒不能淑季世於三代，何邪？善乎孔子告哀公曰：「凡爲天下國家有九經，所以行之者一也。」後世有願治之君，而皆非本於誠，意雖有所爲，不過藻飾之虛耳，何益於治哉？故曰：「有天德者，然後可以語王道。」其要只在謹獨。
第貳場
論
君子尊德性而道問學
張志淑
同考試官教諭陳批：精一之訓昉於虞廷，萬世之言學者莫加焉。子思子之言，夫亦有所受也。是作反覆論議，而聖賢體用之學，讀之躍如，豈深造而有得者邪？噫！是未可以科舉文字目之矣。
考試官教授何批：昔人謂文章須明白正大，此作近之，可以式矣。
考試官教授高批：只就本題發明，而紆徐曲折，綽有法度，是理到之言。
translation_en:
…travelers. Dukes Huan and Wen once used these principles in the covenants of the Five Hegemons, yet ultimately could not bring their declining age to the goodness of the Three Dynasties. Why was this? How aptly Confucius told Duke Ai: “There are nine guiding principles for governing the world, states, and families, but that by which they are put into practice is one.” In later ages there were rulers who desired good government, yet none grounded their efforts in sincerity. Though they intended to accomplish something, their efforts amounted only to empty embellishment. What benefit could this bring to government? Thus it is said: “Only one who possesses heavenly virtue can be spoken to about the Kingly Way.” Its essential requirement lies solely in vigilance over oneself when alone.
Second Session
Discourse
“The gentleman honors his moral nature and pursues inquiry and learning.”
Zhang Zhishu
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: The teaching of discernment and single-mindedness originated at the court of Shun. Among all who have spoken of learning throughout the ages, none has surpassed it. Master Zisi’s words, too, surely derived from a transmitted teaching. This composition examines the matter from many sides; as one reads, the sages’ and worthies’ learning concerning substance and function comes vividly to life. Could its author be someone who has studied deeply and attained understanding? Ah! This cannot be regarded merely as examination writing.
Comment by Examiner He, Professor: Writers of old said that prose must be clear, upright, and grand. This composition approaches that standard and may serve as a model.
Comment by Examiner Gao, Professor: It expounds the set topic alone, yet proceeds with an unhurried flow and varied turns, displaying ample command of compositional rules. These are words that reach the underlying principle.

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
君子學以會道之全則其功固不容有所
偏廢矣何則道原於天而備於聖人其大
也極於無外也然而無不體焉未始有遺
於小也其小也極於無內也然而無不統
焉未始不足於大也合小與大渾然一以
貫之是道之所以爲全也君子於此語大
而畧其小則弊也淪於空語小而昧其大
則弊也滯於物二者以言乎失道均也而
豈君子之所謂學哉是故其大無外其小
===
無內道本如是其全也尊德性而道問學
學亦本如是其全也循其尊與道者而無
有偏廢焉夫是謂學之全功而道之全者
於是乎會焉矣君子尊德性而道問學子
思子其善言學者乎雖然此非子思之言
也孔子曰君子博學於文約之以禮文也
者問學之資也禮也者德性之蘊也博文
約禮乃所謂尊德性而道問學也雖然亦
非孔子之言也舜之命禹曰惟精惟一允
punctuated: 君子學以會道之全，則其功固不容有所偏廢矣。何則？道原於天而備於聖人，其大也極於無外也，然而無不體焉，未始有遺於小也；其小也極於無內也，然而無不統焉，未始不足於大也。合小與大，渾然一以貫之，是道之所以爲全也。君子於此，語大而畧其小，則弊也淪於空；語小而昧其大，則弊也滯於物。二者以言乎失道，均也，而豈君子之所謂學哉？是故其大無外，其小無內，道本如是其全也；尊德性而道問學，學亦本如是其全也。循其尊與道者而無有偏廢焉，夫是謂學之全功，而道之全者於是乎會焉矣。君子尊德性而道問學，子思子其善言學者乎！雖然，此非子思之言也。孔子曰：「君子博學於文，約之以禮。」文也者，問學之資也；禮也者，德性之蘊也。博文約禮，乃所謂尊德性而道問學也。雖然，亦非孔子之言也。舜之命禹曰：「惟精惟一，允
translation_en:
The gentleman studies in order to comprehend the Way in its entirety; his efforts must therefore admit no one-sided neglect. Why is this? The Way originates in Heaven and is fully embodied in the sage. In its greatness, it reaches the point beyond which nothing lies outside it; yet it embodies everything, omitting nothing small. In its minuteness, it reaches the point within which nothing further lies; yet it encompasses everything, lacking nothing great. Uniting the small and the great, one principle runs through them as an undivided whole: this is what makes the Way complete. If the gentleman speaks of its greatness but neglects its minuteness, the resulting fault is to lapse into emptiness. If he speaks of its minuteness but fails to understand its greatness, the resulting fault is to become mired in things. In departing from the Way, these two are alike. How could either be what the gentleman calls learning?
Thus, in its greatness nothing lies outside it, and in its minuteness nothing lies within it: such is the inherent completeness of the Way. To honor one’s moral nature and pursue inquiry and study: such, too, is the inherent completeness of learning. To follow both this honoring and this pursuit without neglecting either is what is meant by the complete work of learning; through this, the Way in its entirety is comprehended. “The gentleman honors his moral nature and pursues inquiry and study”: was Master Zisi not adept at speaking of learning! Yet these were not Zisi’s own words. Kongzi said: “The gentleman learns broadly from cultural writings and disciplines himself through ritual.” Cultural writings provide the resources for inquiry and study; ritual contains the substance of moral nature. Learning broadly from cultural writings and disciplining oneself through ritual are precisely what is meant by honoring one’s moral nature and pursuing inquiry and study. Yet neither were these Kongzi’s own words. In his charge to Yu, Shun said: “Be discerning; be single-minded; truly…”

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
執厥中精也者道問學以致其察也一也
者尊德性以守其正也精之一之而中者
常不失焉乃所以會道之全也故道之全
者會而聖可幾聖可幾而學之事盡焉矣
自今言之發育萬物峻極于天聖人之道
其大何如也禮儀三百威儀三千聖人之
道其小何如也然而大也非空也萬殊之
一本也小也非物也一本之萬殊也自其
發育峻極也析而言之則所謂三千三百
===
===
矣大而未始有遺於小也自其三千三百
也統而言之則所謂發育峻極矣小而未
始不足於大也蓋道之所以為全而吾之
得於天者其體本如是也顧道之得於天
者本如是其全而卒未有能會焉者何也
廣大之弗致高明之弗極故者弗温而厚
者弗敦則性真喪而無以極乎道之大也
精微之弗盡中庸之弗道新有弗知而禮
有弗崇則問學荒而無以盡乎道之小也
punctuated:
執厥中。」精也者，道問學以致其察也；一也者，尊德性以守其正也。精之、一之，而中者常不失焉，乃所以會道之全也。故道之全者會，而聖可幾；聖可幾，而學之事盡焉矣。
自今言之，發育萬物，峻極于天，聖人之道其大何如也！禮儀三百，威儀三千，聖人之道其小何如也！然而大也非空也，萬殊之一本也；小也非物也，一本之萬殊也。自其發育峻極也，析而言之，則所謂三千三百矣，大而未始有遺於小也；自其三千三百也，統而言之，則所謂發育峻極矣，小而未始不足於大也。蓋道之所以為全，而吾之得於天者，其體本如是也。
顧道之得於天者，本如是其全，而卒未有能會焉者，何也？廣大之弗致，高明之弗極，故者弗温，而厚者弗敦，則性真喪，而無以極乎道之大也；精微之弗盡，中庸之弗道，新有弗知，而禮有弗崇，則問學荒，而無以盡乎道之小也。
translation_en:
…hold fast to that mean.” Refinement means pursuing inquiry and learning to attain full discernment; singleness means honoring one’s moral nature to preserve its rectitude. Through refinement and singleness, the mean is never lost: this is how one comprehends the Way in its entirety. Thus, when the entirety of the Way is comprehended, sagehood becomes attainable; when sagehood becomes attainable, the work of learning is fully accomplished.
To speak of it now: nourishing and developing the myriad things, towering to the height of Heaven—how vast is the Way of the sage! Three hundred ceremonial observances and three thousand rules of deportment—how minute is the Way of the sage! Yet its vastness is no empty abstraction: it is the single root of myriad distinctions. Its minuteness is no mere collection of things: it is the myriad distinctions of a single root. If we analyze its nourishing, developing, and towering reach, these are precisely what are called the three thousand and the three hundred. In its vastness, nothing minute is ever omitted. If we consider the three thousand and the three hundred as a unified whole, these are precisely what is called nourishing, developing, and towering reach. In its minuteness, it is never deficient in vastness. Such, fundamentally, is the constitution of the Way in its entirety, which we receive from Heaven.
Yet if the Way received from Heaven is fundamentally complete in this manner, why is it that people nevertheless fail to comprehend it? When breadth and greatness are not fully attained, loftiness and clarity are not pursued to their utmost, old learning is not reviewed, and substantial virtue is not deepened, the genuineness of one’s nature is lost, leaving no means of reaching the utmost vastness of the Way. When the subtle and minute are not fully explored, the constant mean is not followed, new knowledge remains unacquired, and ritual propriety is not honored, inquiry and learning fall into neglect, leaving no means of fully comprehending the minuteness of the Way.

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
夫惟道之大有未極也於是徒泥其小而
其學局焉而不能通道之小有未盡也於
是徒慕其大而其學蕩焉而無所歸宿或
失則空或失則物而道之全者病矣嗚呼
斯道之全其得之於天我與聖人一也聖
人者以其道參天地賛化育而我乃以其
學為道病夫獨能無所愧怍乎是故君子
尊德性而道問學其功不容以偏廢也然
所謂尊德性者非求諸玄虛寂滅如世之
===
禪伯之為也廣大吾致焉高明吾極焉故
者吾温厚者吾敦焉蓋無所加於性分之
外而事皆下學也所謂道問學者非求諸
詞章訓詁如世之俗儒之為也精微吾盡
焉中庸吾道焉新也吾知禮也吾崇焉蓋
將以究性命之奧而事皆上達也故自夫
德性之尊也則有以極道之大而物不足
言矣自夫問學之道也則有以盡道之小
而空不足言矣自夫尊德性而事皆下
punctuated:
夫惟道之大有未極也，於是徒泥其小，而其學局焉而不能通；道之小有未盡也，於是徒慕其大，而其學蕩焉而無所歸宿。或失則空，或失則物，而道之全者病矣。嗚呼！斯道之全，其得之於天，我與聖人一也。聖人者，以其道參天地、賛化育，而我乃以其學為道病，夫獨能無所愧怍乎？是故君子尊德性而道問學，其功不容以偏廢也。
然所謂尊德性者，非求諸玄虛寂滅，如世之禪伯之為也。廣大吾致焉，高明吾極焉，故者吾温，厚者吾敦焉。蓋無所加於性分之外，而事皆下學也。所謂道問學者，非求諸詞章訓詁，如世之俗儒之為也。精微吾盡焉，中庸吾道焉，新也吾知，禮也吾崇焉。蓋將以究性命之奧，而事皆上達也。
故自夫德性之尊也，則有以極道之大，而物不足言矣；自夫問學之道也，則有以盡道之小，而空不足言矣；自夫尊德性而事皆下
translation_en:
It is precisely because the greatness of the Way has not been fully realized that one merely becomes mired in its details: one’s learning becomes confined and cannot attain comprehensive understanding. Because the details of the Way have not been fully explored, one merely admires its greatness: one’s learning becomes unbounded and has nowhere to come to rest. One error leads to emptiness, the other to fixation on things, and the integrity of the Way is impaired. Alas! In receiving this Way in its entirety from Heaven, I am no different from the sage. Through his Way, the sage forms a triad with Heaven and Earth and assists their transforming and nurturing work; yet through my learning I impair the Way. Can I alone have no cause for shame? Thus the gentleman honors his moral nature and pursues inquiry and learning; neither aspect of this effort may be neglected.
Yet honoring moral nature does not mean seeking it in abstruse emptiness and quiescent extinction, as the Chan masters of this age do. I extend breadth and greatness to their fullest reach; I carry loftiness and clarity to their utmost; I review what is already known and deepen what is substantial. Nothing is added beyond what is allotted to one’s nature, and these activities are all learning in ordinary affairs. Pursuing inquiry and learning does not mean seeking it in literary composition and textual glosses, as the vulgar scholars of this age do. I explore the subtle and minute to the full; I follow the Mean; I come to know what is new and esteem ritual. The purpose is to fathom the mysteries of human nature and Heaven’s mandate, and these activities all lead to higher understanding.
Thus, through honoring moral nature, one can fully realize the greatness of the Way, and fixation on things is no longer at issue. Through pursuing inquiry and learning, one can fully explore the details of the Way, and emptiness is no longer at issue. And insofar as one honors moral nature while all one’s activities consist in learning in ordinary affairs…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
學也則舉其大而小無不該道問學而事
皆上達也則舉其小而大亦無不具矣又
自其小大之互舉也則萬殊一本語用而
體存焉一本萬殊語體而用備焉而體用
出於一矣又自其體用之一也則致飭於
外而未始遺内致養於内而未始遺外而
顯微内外無不出於一矣道之全者不於
是會焉矣乎道之全者會則所謂發育峻
極者又將由我乎出三千三百者又將由
===
我乎裁而聖人之能事在我矣學之全功
豈復有加於此乎是故道必全而後可謂
之道學必會道之全而後可謂之學其功
固不容有所偏廢也雖然孔子之告哀公
曰博學之審問之慎思之明辨之篤行之
此其言乃若專於道問學孟子曰學問之
道無他求其放心而已此其言又若專於
尊德性何也蓋既曰學之問之則所謂問
學者必有所在而不容舍德性以為宗既
punctuated:
學也，則舉其大而小無不該；道問學而事皆上達也，則舉其小而大亦無不具矣。又自其小大之互舉也，則萬殊一本，語用而體存焉；一本萬殊，語體而用備焉，而體用出於一矣。又自其體用之一也，則致飭於外而未始遺内，致養於内而未始遺外，而顯微内外無不出於一矣。道之全者不於是會焉矣乎？道之全者會，則所謂發育峻極者，又將由我乎出；三千三百者，又將由我乎裁，而聖人之能事在我矣。學之全功，豈復有加於此乎？是故道必全而後可謂之道，學必會道之全而後可謂之學，其功固不容有所偏廢也。
雖然，孔子之告哀公曰：「博學之，審問之，慎思之，明辨之，篤行之。」此其言乃若專於道問學。孟子曰：「學問之道無他，求其放心而已。」此其言又若專於尊德性，何也？蓋既曰學之問之，則所謂問學者必有所在，而不容舍德性以為宗。既
translation_en:
…learning at the ordinary level, then, by taking up what is great, one encompasses everything small. When one pursues inquiry and learning and all one's endeavors reach upward to higher understanding, then, by taking up what is small, one also possesses everything great. Moreover, since the small and the great each embrace the other, the myriad particulars have a single root: in speaking of function, substance is present within it. The single root has myriad particulars: in speaking of substance, function is fully furnished within it. Thus substance and function issue from one source. Further, since substance and function are one, attending to one's outward conduct never entails neglecting the inward self, and nurturing the inward self never entails neglecting outward conduct. Thus the manifest and the subtle, the inward and the outward, all issue from one source. Is this not where the Way in its entirety is brought together? When the Way in its entirety is brought together, then what is called its nurturing of all things and its towering height will proceed from me; the three thousand and three hundred rites will be regulated by me, and the capacities of the sage will reside in me. Could the full achievement of learning go any further than this? Thus the Way must be whole before it can be called the Way, and learning must bring together the entirety of the Way before it can be called learning. Such effort certainly permits no one-sided neglect.
Nevertheless, Confucius told Duke Ai: “Study broadly, inquire closely, reflect carefully, discriminate clearly, and practice earnestly.” These words seem to concern exclusively the pursuit of inquiry and learning. Mengzi said: “The way of learning is nothing other than seeking one's lost heart.” These words, in turn, seem to concern exclusively honoring one's moral nature. Why is this? Since Confucius speaks of studying and inquiring, what he calls inquiry and learning must have something upon which to rest; one cannot dispense with moral nature as its guiding principle. Since…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
曰求其放心則所謂求者必有所事而不
容舍問學以為功初未嘗有偏廢也然則
學者如之何程子曰涵養須用敬進學則
在致知朱子曰非存心無以致知而存心
者又不可以不致知取以為法焉可矣
表
擬
聖駕重幸太學羣臣
賀表
茅坤
同考試官教諭李批我
皇上崇儒重道之意是如此且知
國家典禮可以稱
賀矣
同考試官教諭曾批能揄揚我
皇上禮重
先師之盛可謂識其大者
考試官教授何批得賀表體
punctuated:
曰求其放心，則所謂求者必有所事，而不容舍問學以為功，初未嘗有偏廢也。然則學者如之何？程子曰：「涵養須用敬，進學則在致知。」朱子曰：「非存心無以致知，而存心者又不可以不致知。」取以為法焉，可矣。

表

擬聖駕重幸太學羣臣賀表

茅坤

同考試官教諭李批：「我皇上崇儒重道之意是如此，且知國家典禮，可以稱賀矣。」

同考試官教諭曾批：「能揄揚我皇上禮重先師之盛，可謂識其大者。」

考試官教授何批：「得賀表體。」
translation_en:
… once one speaks of recovering the mind that has strayed, the recovery in question must involve something to be done; one cannot dispense with inquiry and learning as the means of accomplishing it. From the outset, neither aspect has ever been neglected. How, then, should students proceed? Master Cheng said: “Nurturing oneself requires reverent attentiveness; advancing in learning lies in extending knowledge.” Master Zhu said: “Without preserving the mind, there is no means of extending knowledge; yet those who preserve the mind must also extend their knowledge.” It will suffice to take these statements as one's rule.

Memorial

Draft congratulatory memorial from the assembled officials on His Majesty's renewed visit to the Imperial University

Mao Kun

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: “Such is our emperor's intention in honoring Confucian learning and esteeming the Way. The writer also understands the state's ceremonial institutions and can thus offer fitting congratulations.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Zeng, Instructor: “He ably extols the magnificence of our emperor's ceremonial reverence for the First Teacher [Confucius]. He may be said to understand what is most important.”

Comment by Examiner He, Professor: “He has captured the proper form of a congratulatory memorial.”

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎授葛批雅而麗
具官臣某等嘉靖十二年某月某日恭遇
聖駕重幸太學者伏以
華蓋天臨久快虞文之覩
辟雍日麗載瞻周典之光一代會通百王斯
盛臣某等誠懽誠抃稽首頓首上言竊以
至化昭聖人之道太學迺賢士所關丕闡人
文誕宣王度故視學之禮先警衆於大昕
而釋奠之規寔興誠乎秩節哲王先敎必
===
慎德以考材治世右文遹化民而成俗五
典惇慎徽之叙四術極造士之科體乾坤
而峻發育之仁懋詩書而著綏猷之化粤
徵殷法斯養老以乞言相古虞庠固承師
而問道慨風聲之既逖遂文敎之失湮馬
上從戎徒廑過魯園中習射竊比臨雍敎
化不聞於西京典籍奚裨於東觀談經而
徐張𡷈幕論難而輙齒沙門學乏身心罔
敦率履敎惟口耳匪克摳衣永式良猷無
punctuated:
考試官敎授葛批：雅而麗。

具官臣某等，嘉靖十二年某月某日，恭遇聖駕重幸太學者，伏以：華蓋天臨，久快虞文之覩；辟雍日麗，載瞻周典之光。一代會通，百王斯盛。臣某等誠懽誠抃，稽首頓首上言。竊以至化昭聖人之道，太學迺賢士所關。丕闡人文，誕宣王度。故視學之禮，先警衆於大昕；而釋奠之規，寔興誠乎秩節。哲王先敎，必慎德以考材；治世右文，遹化民而成俗。五典惇慎徽之叙，四術極造士之科。體乾坤而峻發育之仁，懋詩書而著綏猷之化。粤徵殷法，斯養老以乞言；相古虞庠，固承師而問道。慨風聲之既逖，遂文敎之失湮。馬上從戎，徒廑過魯；園中習射，竊比臨雍。敎化不聞於西京，典籍奚裨於東觀？談經而徐張𡷈幕，論難而輙齒沙門。學乏身心，罔敦率履；敎惟口耳，匪克摳衣。永式良猷，無
translation_en:
Examiner Ge, an instructor, comments: “Elegant and splendid.”

Your servants, so-and-so and others, holding their respective offices, on a certain day of a certain month in the twelfth year of Jiajing, respectfully mark the occasion of Your Majesty’s renewed visit to the Imperial University. We humbly reflect: Your flowered canopy descends from Heaven, long gratifying our sight with the cultural splendor of Shun; the imperial academy shines like the sun, and once again we behold the radiance of Zhou institutions. The achievements of an entire age converge here; among a hundred kings, such is this occasion’s magnificence. Your servants, so-and-so and others, truly rejoicing and applauding, bow our heads and knock them upon the ground as we submit these words.

We venture to consider that consummate transformation makes manifest the Way of the sages, and that the Imperial University is where the cultivation of worthy scholars is centered. It greatly illuminates human culture and broadly proclaims royal standards. Thus, in the rites for an imperial visit to the school, the assembly is first alerted at daybreak; and the regulations for the sacrificial offering to the ancient teachers truly inspire sincerity through their ordered observances. Wise kings give priority to instruction, attending carefully to virtue when assessing talent; well-governed ages honor culture, thereby transforming the people and establishing good customs. The five teachings concerning human relationships reinforce the order of earnestness, circumspection, and excellence; the four arts fulfill the curriculum for forming scholars. Emulating Heaven and Earth, they exalt the benevolence that nurtures all things; promoting the Poetry and Documents, they manifest the transforming influence of principles that bring peace.

If we examine the institutions of Yin, elders were supported so that their counsel might be sought; if we consider the ancient schools of Shun, teachers were indeed honored and questioned about the Way. Alas, as the influence of those examples grew remote, cultural instruction consequently fell into obscurity. Campaigning on horseback, a ruler merely took the trouble to pass through Lu; practicing archery in a garden, another presumptuously likened this to visiting the imperial academy. Moral transformation was unheard of in the Western Capital; what benefit did the classical writings bring in the Eastern Observatory? When discussing the classics, they would slowly spread a curtain [?]; when debating difficult points, they would readily rank Buddhist monks among the participants. Learning failed to engage the self and mind, and did not encourage earnest practice; instruction passed only from mouth to ear, and could not inspire the reverence of a pupil lifting his robe before his teacher. For making sound principles an enduring model, none …

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
如
昭代玆蓋伏遇
皇帝陛下
聰明振古
神聖憲天
本三代而明人倫
繼百年而興禮樂
帝王列祀允正師資
敬一傳心遠紹道統重念
===
先師之尊莫足追崇載稽前代之規詎容襲
陋爰從塑像遂及爵封釐彼弗經率爾歸
正肅昭明薦躬屈
至尊景耀祥輝萬國依
彤幃之近聲傳
清蹕
九重回黃道之開
文圭祗謁於宫墻榮生爼豆
黼座端臨於胄監
banxin: 山東鄉試錄 七十三
punctuated: 如昭代。玆蓋伏遇皇帝陛下，聰明振古，神聖憲天，本三代而明人倫，繼百年而興禮樂。帝王列祀，允正師資；敬一傳心，遠紹道統。重念先師之尊，莫足追崇；載稽前代之規，詎容襲陋？爰從塑像，遂及爵封，釐彼弗經，率爾歸正。肅昭明薦，躬屈至尊。景耀祥輝，萬國依彤幃之近；聲傳清蹕，九重回黃道之開。文圭祗謁於宫墻，榮生爼豆；黼座端臨於胄監。
translation_en:
…can compare with this illustrious dynasty. We have reverently encountered Your Majesty the Emperor, whose intelligence surpasses antiquity and whose divine sagacity takes Heaven as its model. Taking the Three Dynasties as your foundation, you clarify human relationships; continuing a century of rule, you bring rites and music to flourishing perfection. By arranging sacrifices to emperors and kings, you duly establish the models from whom to learn; by transmitting the teaching of reverent unity from mind to mind, you carry forward the succession of the Way from remote antiquity.
You have further reflected that no retrospective honors could adequately exalt the Former Teacher, Confucius. Having examined the precedents of earlier dynasties, how could you permit their defective practices to be perpetuated? Beginning with sculpted images and extending to noble titles, you rectified what lacked canonical warrant and brought all back into proper order. Solemnly presenting the radiant offerings, you personally condescended from your supreme eminence. Splendor shone and auspicious radiance spread, as the myriad realms drew close to the vermilion curtains. The cries clearing the imperial way resounded, and the ninefold palace opened onto the imperial route [?]. Bearing the patterned jade tablet [?], you reverently paid homage within the temple walls, lending glory to the sacrificial vessels; your august throne presided in dignity over the Directorate of Education…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
寵被章縫
命坐而講易書均拜宫袍之
錫侍席而憲文武普沾珍茗之頒千官傾聽
於圜橋多士願來於鼓篋禮逮神明之裔
其維象賢班聯誦法之臣兹欽扈
聖日垂
天語風教星敷知爲治不在多言俾讀書大有
所益唐宗漢制帝典王謨奚啻丁寧於再
三有儼寅承乎萬一聿敷文命亶開太平
===
臣某等仰覿
闕模躬逢
曠典慶斯文之鼎重四海攸同履世道而泰
來萬邦作乂百辟駿奔而蒞止諸生鵠立
以顒觀肆未選於前聞豈謾修於故事協
正己率人之誼懷開物成務之功播載聲
名篤崇彝訓思皇多士於昭培植之方有
孚作人不盡網羅之意志貞顓靜風俗大
略同焉至治和平禮樂庶幾備矣煥乎唐
punctuated:
寵被章縫。命坐而講易書，均拜宫袍之錫；侍席而憲文武，普沾珍茗之頒。千官傾聽於圜橋，多士願來於鼓篋。禮逮神明之裔，其維象賢；班聯誦法之臣，兹欽扈聖。日垂天語，風教星敷。知爲治不在多言，俾讀書大有所益。唐宗漢制，帝典王謨，奚啻丁寧於再三，有儼寅承乎萬一。聿敷文命，亶開太平。

臣某等仰覿闕模，躬逢曠典。慶斯文之鼎重，四海攸同；履世道而泰來，萬邦作乂。百辟駿奔而蒞止，諸生鵠立以顒觀。肆未選於前聞，豈謾修於故事？協正己率人之誼，懷開物成務之功。播載聲名，篤崇彝訓。思皇多士，於昭培植之方；有孚作人，不盡網羅之意。志貞顓靜，風俗大略同焉；至治和平，禮樂庶幾備矣。煥乎唐
translation_en:
…Imperial favor reaches the scholars in their ceremonial caps. Commanded to sit and expound the Changes and the Documents, they all receive the gift of palace robes; attending the imperial seat and taking Kings Wen and Wu as their models, they all share in the distribution of precious tea. The assembled officials listen intently at the circular bridge, and the many scholars eagerly come, their book baskets ready for study. Ceremonial honors extend to the descendant of the divinely enlightened sage, honoring ancestral worth in his person; ranked among the ministers who recite and follow the ancient teachings, he reverently attends the sage sovereign. Each day imperial words descend, and moral instruction spreads like the stars. Recognizing that governing does not depend on many words, you ensure that reading brings substantial benefit. The precedents of the Tang emperors and the institutions of the Han, the canons of the ancient emperors and the counsels of the kings—these receive far more than repeated earnest admonition; with solemn reverence, even a fraction of their wisdom is received. Thus you spread civilizing instruction and truly inaugurate Great Peace.

Your servants, So-and-so and the others, look up to the example set by the imperial court and personally encounter this extraordinary ceremony. We rejoice in the exalted standing of this cultural tradition, a joy shared throughout the Four Seas; as the course of the age turns toward prosperity, the myriad states attain good order. The assembled dignitaries hasten to arrive, and the students stand erect like swans, gazing with reverence. Such a ceremony has scarcely been heard of before [?]; how could it be merely a perfunctory revival of old precedent? It accords with the principle of rectifying oneself to lead others and embraces the achievement of illuminating things and bringing undertakings to completion. Your renown spreads abroad, and you profoundly honor the enduring teachings. The splendid company of scholars makes manifest your means of nurturing talent; your sincerity in fostering worthy men expresses an inexhaustible desire to gather them all. Their aspirations are upright, concentrated, and tranquil, and customs broadly conform to this standard. Under consummate government, harmony and peace prevail, and rites and music approach completeness. Resplendent is the flourishing age of Tang…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
虞之盛燁如金玉其相顯服
鴻圖私深雀躍伏願
道承精一惟
聖人允執厥中
學懋緝熈幸
天子躬行於上
日新晉飾
天啓離明臣某等瞻
天仰
===
聖不勝欣躍舞抃之至謹奉
表稱
賀以
聞
第叁場
策
第一問
孫汝賢
同考試官教諭李批我
punctuated:
虞之盛，燁如金玉其相，顯服鴻圖，私深雀躍。伏願道承精一，惟聖人允執厥中；學懋緝熈，幸天子躬行於上。日新晉飾，天啓離明。臣某等瞻天仰聖，不勝欣躍舞抃之至，謹奉表稱賀以聞。
第叁場
策
第一問
孫汝賢
同考試官教諭李批：我
translation_en:
…the flourishing age of Yu, radiant as gold and jade in its substance, rendering distinguished service to the grand imperial enterprise: in our hearts we leap with profound joy. We humbly wish that, in transmitting the Way through refinement and single-mindedness, the Sage may faithfully hold to the Mean; and that, in diligently pursuing ever-brightening learning, the Son of Heaven may personally put it into practice from above. May each day bring renewal and advancing refinement, and may Heaven unfold resplendent illumination. We, your servants So-and-so and the others, gaze toward Heaven and look up to the Sage, unable to contain our utmost joy, leaping, dancing, and clapping our hands. We respectfully submit this memorial of congratulation for Your Majesty’s hearing.

Policy Essays
First Question
Sun Ruxian
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: Our …

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
祖宗刑家化國之道今古罕儷直逼唐虞而上之逮我
皇上遠繼道統垂範作則四方有風動之休子書生也而能鋪張揄
揚其盛且文頗莊重亦竒矣故薦
同考試官教諭曾批我
國家治教隆盛民日由之而不知也蓋自宫壼以達
朝廷莫不有訓故兹内外稱治焉此作足昭
聖製之懿是科得人矣
考試官教授何批策以
國朝典章者試諸士以明習耳得子之作不覺愕然
===
考試官教授高批觀是作和而雅足鳴我
國家之盛
聖人之治法天者也天之道曰陰與陽而
聖人之治曰内與外内外者陰陽之象也
陰陽備而天之道以立内外和而聖人之
治以成嗚呼此聖人所以為法天者乎執
事發策秋闈首以我
國家治外治内者為問此固愚所謂法天者
也然而其本原之邃功用之神非愚所能
punctuated:
祖宗刑家化國之道，今古罕儷，直逼唐虞而上之。逮我皇上遠繼道統，垂範作則，四方有風動之休。子書生也，而能鋪張揄揚其盛，且文頗莊重，亦竒矣，故薦。
同考試官教諭曾批：我國家治教隆盛，民日由之而不知也。蓋自宫壼以達朝廷，莫不有訓，故兹内外稱治焉。此作足昭聖製之懿，是科得人矣。
考試官教授何批：策以國朝典章者，試諸士以明習耳。得子之作，不覺愕然。
考試官教授高批：觀是作，和而雅，足鳴我國家之盛。
聖人之治，法天者也。天之道曰陰與陽，而聖人之治曰内與外。内外者，陰陽之象也。陰陽備而天之道以立，内外和而聖人之治以成。嗚呼！此聖人所以為法天者乎？執事發策秋闈，首以我國家治外治内者為問，此固愚所謂法天者也。然而其本原之邃、功用之神，非愚所能
translation_en:
…The way our imperial ancestors ordered their households and transformed the realm has scarcely had an equal, ancient or modern; it closely approaches, and even surpasses, that of Tang Yao and Yu Shun. Now our Emperor carries forward the distant succession of the Way, setting examples and establishing standards, with the blessed result that all quarters respond as grass bends before the wind. You are a student, yet you can expound and celebrate this flourishing achievement; moreover, your writing is quite dignified. This is indeed remarkable, and so I recommend you.
Associate Examiner Zeng, Instructor, comments: Our dynasty’s governance and moral instruction flourish greatly; the people follow them daily without being aware of it. From the palace’s inner quarters to the court, nowhere lacks instruction. Thus both inner and outer spheres are said to be well governed. This composition amply reveals the excellence of the imperial writings. This examination has indeed found a worthy man.
Examiner He, Professor, comments: In posing a policy question on the institutions and regulations of our dynasty, we intended merely to test the candidates’ understanding and familiarity. Upon receiving your composition, I could not help being astonished.
Examiner Gao, Professor, comments: This composition is harmonious and elegant, fully worthy to proclaim our dynasty’s flourishing achievements.
The sage’s governance takes Heaven as its model. The Way of Heaven consists of yin and yang, while the sage’s governance comprises the inner and outer spheres. Inner and outer are the images of yin and yang. When yin and yang are complete, the Way of Heaven is established; when inner and outer are harmonious, the sage’s governance is accomplished. Ah! Is this not how the sage takes Heaven as his model? You, honored examiners, have issued policy questions for the autumn Provincial Examination, asking first about our dynasty’s governance of the outer and inner spheres. This is precisely what I, in my humble understanding, call taking Heaven as one’s model. Yet the profundity of its foundations and the wondrous efficacy of its operation are beyond my ability to …

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
識也獨嘗莊誦
太祖高皇帝所製
祖訓教民榜
太宗文皇帝所製為善陰騭孝順事實
宣宗章皇帝所製五倫書及我
皇上所製敬一箴五箴註而有以仰窺其治外
之迹焉
祖訓為目十有二曰持守曰嚴祭祀曰謹出入
曰慎國政曰禮儀曰法律曰內令曰內官
===
曰職制曰兵衛曰營繕曰供用至弘規大
要則別舉以為首章而制治保邦之道備
教民榜為語凡六曰孝順父母曰尊敬長
上曰和睦鄉里曰教訓子孫曰各安生理
曰毋作非為而修身教家之綱舉為善陰
騭為卷凡十而福善禍淫之理明孝順事
實為卷亦十而孝子順孫之式具五倫書
有總論以冠於前有嘉言善行以實於後
而綱常之義著敬一箴有曰匪敬弗純匪
punctuated:
識也。獨嘗莊誦太祖高皇帝所製《祖訓》《教民榜》，太宗文皇帝所製《為善陰騭》《孝順事實》，宣宗章皇帝所製《五倫書》，及我皇上所製《敬一箴》《五箴註》，而有以仰窺其治外之迹焉。
《祖訓》為目十有二：曰持守，曰嚴祭祀，曰謹出入，曰慎國政，曰禮儀，曰法律，曰內令，曰內官，曰職制，曰兵衛，曰營繕，曰供用。至弘規大要，則別舉以為首章，而制治保邦之道備。《教民榜》為語凡六：曰孝順父母，曰尊敬長上，曰和睦鄉里，曰教訓子孫，曰各安生理，曰毋作非為，而修身教家之綱舉。《為善陰騭》為卷凡十，而福善禍淫之理明。《孝順事實》為卷亦十，而孝子順孫之式具。《五倫書》有總論以冠於前，有嘉言善行以實於後，而綱常之義著。《敬一箴》有曰：「匪敬弗純，匪
translation_en:
…comprehend. Yet I have reverently read the Ancestral Instructions (Zuxun) and the Placard for Instructing the People (Jiaomin bang), composed by Emperor Taizu Gao; Doing Good and Hidden Merit (Weishan yinzhi) and Accounts of Filial Obedience (Xiaoshun shishi), composed by Emperor Taizong Wen; the Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu), composed by Emperor Xuanzong Zhang; and the Admonition on Reverence and Oneness (Jingyi zhen) and the Commentaries on the Five Admonitions (Wuzhen zhu), composed by our reigning emperor. Through these I have been able to glimpse, with reverence, the manifestations of their ordering of the external realm.
The Ancestral Instructions has twelve sections: maintaining what has been established; solemnity in sacrifices; care in going out and coming in; caution in affairs of state; ritual and ceremony; laws; regulations for the inner palace; palace eunuchs; official organization; military guards; construction and repairs; and supplies and expenditure. Its broad principles and essential provisions are set apart as the opening chapter, thus fully presenting the way to establish good government and preserve the state. The Placard for Instructing the People contains six injunctions: be filial and obedient to your parents; respect your elders and superiors; live harmoniously with your fellow villagers; instruct your children and grandchildren; let each attend peaceably to their livelihood; and commit no wrongful deeds. Thus it sets forth the guiding principles for cultivating oneself and instructing one’s family. Doing Good and Hidden Merit comprises ten fascicles and makes clear the principle that good is rewarded with blessings and wickedness with calamity. Accounts of Filial Obedience likewise comprises ten fascicles and supplies models of filial sons and obedient grandsons. The Book of the Five Human Relationships begins with a general discussion, followed by exemplary sayings and good deeds that give it substance, thereby making manifest the meaning of the cardinal relationships and constant moral norms. The Admonition on Reverence and Oneness says: “Without reverence there is no purity; without…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
一弗聚有曰咨爾諸侯卿與大夫以至士
庶一遵斯謨而大易之微闡心箴註惜宋
君之未能體察四箴註歸重於人君之視
聽言動而君人之責彰是製作也以垂示
子孫則所謂禹貽之典則以頒示臣庶則
所謂皇極之敷言也而所以治外者何至
乎又嘗莊誦
孝慈高皇后傳
仁孝文皇后所製內訓及我
===
章聖皇太后所製女訓而有以仰窺其治內之
迹焉
高皇后傳稱造次顛沛恪遵婦道完緝衣鞋助
給將士左右規畫動中事機而深有裨於
皇祖創業之功夙興夜寐無時豫怠勸
帝親賢講學隨事幾諫訪求古訓諭告六宮孜
孜不倦而深有裨於
皇祖致理之績內訓為章二十曰德性曰修身
曰慎言曰謹行曰勤勵曰警戒曰節儉曰
punctuated:
一弗聚。」有曰：「咨爾諸侯、卿與大夫，以至士庶，一遵斯謨。」而大易之微闡。《心箴註》惜宋君之未能體察，《四箴註》歸重於人君之視聽言動，而君人之責彰。是製作也，以垂示子孫，則所謂禹貽之典則；以頒示臣庶，則所謂皇極之敷言也。而所以治外者何至乎！又嘗莊誦《孝慈高皇后傳》、仁孝文皇后所製《內訓》，及我章聖皇太后所製《女訓》，而有以仰窺其治內之迹焉。
《高皇后傳》稱：「造次顛沛，恪遵婦道，完緝衣鞋，助給將士，左右規畫，動中事機。」而深有裨於皇祖創業之功。「夙興夜寐，無時豫怠，勸帝親賢講學，隨事幾諫，訪求古訓，諭告六宮，孜孜不倦。」而深有裨於皇祖致理之績。《內訓》為章二十，曰德性，曰修身，曰慎言，曰謹行，曰勤勵，曰警戒，曰節儉，曰
translation_en:
…without unity, nothing comes together.” It also says: “Hear this, you feudal lords, ministers, and grandees, down to scholars and commoners: all shall follow this counsel.” Thus the subtle meaning of the great Book of Changes is elucidated. The Commentary on the Admonition of the Mind (Xin zhen zhu) deplores the Song ruler’s failure to apprehend and examine its teaching. The Commentary on the Four Admonitions (Si zhen zhu) places particular weight upon the ruler’s looking, listening, speaking, and acting. Thus the responsibilities of ruling others are made manifest. These writings, handed down to instruct descendants, are what is meant by the statutes and rules bequeathed by Yu; promulgated to instruct officials and commoners, they are what is meant by the broadly proclaimed words of the Sovereign’s Standard. How consummate are these means of governing the outer realm! I have also reverently read the Biography of Empress Xiaoci Gao, the Instructions for the Inner Quarters (Nei xun) composed by Empress Renxiao Wen, and the Instructions for Women (Nü xun) composed by our Empress Dowager Zhangsheng. Through these I have been able reverently to glimpse their achievements in governing the inner realm.
The Biography of Empress Gao states: “Even in haste and hardship, she scrupulously followed the way of a wife, making and mending clothes and shoes to help supply the officers and soldiers. She assisted with planning, and her actions invariably suited the needs of the moment.” She thereby contributed greatly to the Imperial Ancestor’s achievement in founding the dynasty. “She rose early and retired late, never indulging in ease or idleness. She urged the emperor to draw close to worthy men and pursue learning, offering tactful remonstrance as occasions arose. She sought out ancient teachings and conveyed them to the six palaces, diligently and tirelessly.” She thereby contributed greatly to the Imperial Ancestor’s achievement of good government. The Instructions for the Inner Quarters comprises twenty chapters, entitled “Moral Nature,” “Cultivating Oneself,” “Care in Speech,” “Caution in Conduct,” “Diligent Endeavor,” “Vigilance,” “Frugality,” and …

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
積善曰遷善曰崇聖訓曰景賢範曰事父
母曰事君曰事舅姑曰奉祭祀曰母儀曰
睦親曰慈幼曰逮下曰待外戚而條目之
詳先後之次備見於自序之辭女訓爲章
十有二曰閨訓曰修德曰受命曰夫婦曰
孝舅姑曰敬夫曰愛妾曰慈幼曰姪子曰
敎子曰慎靜曰節儉而其檃括乎經史參
驗乎古今矯制乎情質歆警乎貞悔備見
於
===
恭穆獻皇帝之序是製作也以體諸身則思媚
思齊之德以見諸言則葛覃卷耳之詠也
而所以治内者何至乎夫是以百六十年
語内則有樛木之仁有小星之義鷄鳴思
警魚貫順序而家之齊者猶諸媯汭周京
之盛也語外則有靖共之節有敬讓之忠
庶績咸熙百揆時叙而國之治者猶諸唐
虞三代之盛也蓋我
國家之治與天無極而外内和理則旣法天
punctuated:
積善，曰遷善，曰崇聖訓，曰景賢範，曰事父母，曰事君，曰事舅姑，曰奉祭祀，曰母儀，曰睦親，曰慈幼，曰逮下，曰待外戚。而條目之詳、先後之次，備見於自序之辭。《女訓》爲章十有二，曰閨訓，曰修德，曰受命，曰夫婦，曰孝舅姑，曰敬夫，曰愛妾，曰慈幼，曰姪子，曰敎子，曰慎靜，曰節儉。而其檃括乎經史，參驗乎古今，矯制乎情質，歆警乎貞悔，備見於恭穆獻皇帝之序。
是製作也，以體諸身，則思媚思齊之德；以見諸言，則《葛覃》《卷耳》之詠也。而所以治内者何至乎！夫是以百六十年，語内，則有《樛木》之仁，有《小星》之義，《鷄鳴》思警，魚貫順序，而家之齊者猶諸媯汭、周京之盛也；語外，則有靖共之節，有敬讓之忠，庶績咸熙，百揆時叙，而國之治者猶諸唐虞三代之盛也。蓋我國家之治與天無極，而外内和理，則旣法天
translation_en:
…“Accumulating Goodness,” “Turning toward Goodness,” “Honoring the Sagely Instructions,” “Admiring Worthy Models,” “Serving Parents,” “Serving the Ruler,” “Serving Parents-in-Law,” “Conducting Sacrifices,” “Maternal Exemplarity,” “Maintaining Harmony among Kin,” “Showing Kindness to the Young,” “Extending Care to Those Below,” and “Treating Imperial Affinal Relatives.” The detailed contents and their sequence are fully set forth in the author’s own preface. Instructions for Women (Nüxun) comprises twelve chapters: “Instructions for the Inner Chambers,” “Cultivating Virtue,” “Receiving Commands,” “Husband and Wife,” “Showing Filial Devotion to Parents-in-Law,” “Respecting One’s Husband,” “Loving the Concubines,” “Showing Kindness to the Young,” “Nephews,” “Teaching Children,” “Being Circumspect and Quiet,” and “Practicing Frugality.” How it draws together the classics and histories, tests them against ancient and modern experience, disciplines disposition and character, and offers encouragement and admonition concerning steadfastness and regret [?] is fully set forth in the preface by Emperor Gongmu Xian.
When embodied in personal conduct, these writings express the virtues celebrated in “Thinking Fondly” and “Thinking of Her Dignity”; when expressed in words, they are the songs “The Spreading Kudzu” (Ge tan) and “The Cocklebur” (Juan er). How consummate is their provision for governing the inner quarters! Thus, for a hundred and sixty years, within the palace there have been the benevolence of “The Drooping Tree” (Jiu mu) and the righteousness of “The Small Stars” (Xiao xing), the vigilant concern of “The Cock Crows” (Ji ming), and orderly succession like fish proceeding in a line. The ordering of the imperial household has thus rivaled the flourishing examples of the bend of the Gui River and the Zhou capital. In the outer realm, there have been steadfast devotion to duty and the loyalty expressed through respect and deference; all undertakings have prospered, and the hundred offices have been duly ordered. The government of the realm has thus rivaled the flourishing ages of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties. Indeed, the good government of our dynasty is as boundless as Heaven; in bringing harmony and order to both the outer and inner realms, it has already taken Heaven as its model…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
矣禮曰天子修男敎后修女順男敎者父
之道也陽之事也象見於天則爲之日女
順者母之道也陰之事也象見於天則爲
之月是故敎順修而後陰陽不忒陰陽不
忒而日月順則矣惟我
皇上全體太極合德陰陽敎順成俗
國家理治而又何加焉迺日月之常猶或有
忒其度者豈漢仲舒所謂天心之仁愛與
不然則行有常度或災而非異也是未可
===
知也雖然嘗聞之陽之爲象
君也陰之爲象
后也而或爲君子焉或爲中國焉則亦陽之屬
也或爲小人焉或爲夷狄焉則亦陰之屬
也方
今崇賢之途雖廓而君子之道或未光柔夷
之化雖孚而中國之靈或未震官或庀於
承德之辟釁或修於通道之蠻則陰陽之
動容有爲之適者是亦未可知也昔在哲
punctuated:
矣。《禮》曰：「天子修男敎，后修女順。」男敎者，父之道也，陽之事也；象見於天，則爲之日。女順者，母之道也，陰之事也；象見於天，則爲之月。是故敎順修而後陰陽不忒，陰陽不忒而日月順則矣。惟我皇上全體太極，合德陰陽，敎順成俗，國家理治，而又何加焉？迺日月之常猶或有忒其度者，豈漢仲舒所謂天心之仁愛與？不然，則行有常度，或災而非異也，是未可知也。

雖然，嘗聞之：陽之爲象，君也；陰之爲象，后也。而或爲君子焉，或爲中國焉，則亦陽之屬也；或爲小人焉，或爲夷狄焉，則亦陰之屬也。方今崇賢之途雖廓，而君子之道或未光；柔夷之化雖孚，而中國之靈或未震。官或庀於承德之辟，釁或修於通道之蠻，則陰陽之動容有爲之適者，是亦未可知也。昔在哲
translation_en:
…indeed. The Book of Rites says: “The Son of Heaven cultivates instruction for men; the empress cultivates obedience among women.” Instruction for men is the way of the father and the province of yang; its manifestation in Heaven is the sun. Obedience among women is the way of the mother and the province of yin; its manifestation in Heaven is the moon. Thus, only when instruction and obedience are cultivated do yin and yang remain free from deviation; when yin and yang do not deviate, the sun and moon follow their proper rules. Our August Sovereign fully embodies the Supreme Ultimate and unites his virtue with yin and yang. Instruction and obedience have become established customs, and the state is well governed. What more could be added? Yet the sun and moon sometimes still depart from their regular courses. Could this be what Dong Zhongshu of the Han called the benevolent love of Heaven’s heart? Otherwise, their movements have fixed courses, and such occurrences may be calamities rather than anomalies. This cannot yet be known.

Nevertheless, I have heard that yang symbolizes the ruler and yin symbolizes the empress. Worthy men and the Central Kingdom likewise belong to yang; petty men and the Yi and Di peoples likewise belong to yin. At present, although the avenues for honoring the worthy have been opened wide, the way of worthy men may not yet shine forth. Although the transforming influence that pacifies foreign peoples has won their trust, the might of the Central Kingdom may not yet inspire awe. Officials may be appointed under rulers who receive our virtuous influence [?], and provocations may arise among the Man peoples with whom routes of communication have been opened [?]. The movements of yin and yang might therefore correspond to these matters; this too cannot yet be known. In former times, wise…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
王克謹天戒則雖有其象而無其應而聖
人兢兢業業之心則又與草茅之憂有不
同者惟我
皇上萬幾之暇深思而慎省之則祈天永命之
功日以配天而承嘏者詒之億萬無疆之
休胥在是矣愚何幸身親見之
第二問
陳善
同考試官教諭毛批選舉考課我
===
國家監成周之制而為之良法美意可謂歷萬世而無弊俟後聖
而不惑者矣子能言之足占用世之學
同考試官教諭易批選課之法以教之在豫
考之在嚴立說可謂知本之論矣末復有所歸重
不有憫時之君子則子言得無傷於激乎
考試官教授何批叙事平實措辭雅重子
之所養可知矣
考試官教授高批議論切中肯綮是通達
治體者
punctuated:
王克謹天戒，則雖有其象而無其應。而聖人兢兢業業之心，則又與草茅之憂有不同者。惟我皇上萬幾之暇，深思而慎省之，則祈天永命之功，日以配天，而承嘏者詒之億萬無疆之休，胥在是矣。愚何幸身親見之！

第二問
陳善

同考試官教諭毛批：「選舉考課，我國家監成周之制而為之，良法美意，可謂歷萬世而無弊，俟後聖而不惑者矣。子能言之，足占用世之學。」

同考試官教諭易批：「選課之法，以教之在豫、考之在嚴立說，可謂知本之論矣。末復有所歸重，不有憫時之君子，則子言得無傷於激乎？」

考試官教授何批：「叙事平實，措辭雅重，子之所養可知矣。」

考試官教授高批：「議論切中肯綮，是通達治體者。」
translation_en:
…kings could heed Heaven’s warnings with due care; thus, although the portents appeared, the calamities they presaged did not follow. Yet the sage’s vigilant and apprehensive concern differs from the anxieties of those outside office. If our Emperor, amid the respite from his myriad affairs, reflects deeply and examines these matters carefully, his efforts to pray to Heaven for an enduring mandate will daily bring him into accord with Heaven. Receiving its blessings and bequeathing boundless prosperity for countless ages—all this rests here. How fortunate I would be to witness it myself!

Second Policy Question
Chen Shan

Comment by Associate Examiner Mao, Instructor: “For selecting and promoting men and evaluating their performance, our dynasty has taken the institutions of the Zhou as its model. These excellent methods and fine intentions may indeed be said to endure for ten thousand generations without ill effects and to await a future sage without giving rise to doubt. Your ability to explain them sufficiently demonstrates learning suited to practical service.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Yi, Instructor: “In discussing the methods of selection and evaluation, you base your argument on providing instruction in advance and conducting evaluations rigorously. This may indeed be called an argument that grasps the fundamentals. At the end, you again identify where the chief responsibility lies. Unless there are gentlemen who share your concern for the times, might your words not incur criticism for excessive vehemence?”

Comment by Examiner He, Professor: “Your account is straightforward and sound, and your diction elegant and dignified. From this one can discern your cultivation.”

Comment by Examiner Gao, Professor: “Your argument strikes precisely at the crucial points. Here is someone who thoroughly understands the principles of governance.”

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
人君欲得人以成治其始也敎之不可不
豫也其終也考之不可不嚴也敎之豫故
人有所資以進於善而無乏材之憂考之
嚴故人有所儆以益勵於善而無匪人之
譏豫以始之嚴以終之此選舉考課之法
所以常相因而圖治者之不可忽也今夫
人材之生古今不甚相遠大抵上智恒少
而中材者恒多夫以中材之多也而始也
敎之不豫則或局於小而不能成其大狃
===
於近而不能究其遠如是而卒然欲得夫
豪傑之士彼必無以應吾之求而吾又欲
苟以充任於是有舉非其人者矣終也考
之不嚴則或志盈於小得官怠於宦成如
是而居然欲得夫靖共之臣彼必無以副
吾之望而吾又欲强以不能於是有任非
其人者矣故欲舉之而無以敎之猶欲木
之生而不培其根也既舉之而無以考之
猶木之既生而不虞蠹之或生乎其間也
punctuated:
人君欲得人以成治，其始也，敎之不可不豫也；其終也，考之不可不嚴也。敎之豫，故人有所資以進於善，而無乏材之憂；考之嚴，故人有所儆以益勵於善，而無匪人之譏。豫以始之，嚴以終之，此選舉考課之法所以常相因，而圖治者之不可忽也。

今夫人材之生，古今不甚相遠，大抵上智恒少，而中材者恒多。夫以中材之多也，而始也敎之不豫，則或局於小而不能成其大，狃於近而不能究其遠。如是而卒然欲得夫豪傑之士，彼必無以應吾之求，而吾又欲苟以充任，於是有舉非其人者矣。終也考之不嚴，則或志盈於小得，官怠於宦成。如是而居然欲得夫靖共之臣，彼必無以副吾之望，而吾又欲强以不能，於是有任非其人者矣。故欲舉之而無以敎之，猶欲木之生而不培其根也；既舉之而無以考之，猶木之既生而不虞蠹之或生乎其間也。
translation_en:
If a ruler wishes to obtain capable men to achieve good government, he must begin by educating them in advance and conclude by examining them rigorously. Education provided in advance gives men the resources to advance in goodness, removing the worry that talent will be scarce. Rigorous examination gives men a warning that spurs them to greater effort in goodness, removing grounds for criticism that unsuitable men hold office. Beginning with advance preparation and concluding with rigor: this is why the methods of selecting men for office and assessing their performance always depend upon one another, and why those who seek good government cannot neglect them.

The emergence of talented men differs little between antiquity and the present. Generally, men of the highest wisdom are always few, while those of middling ability are always numerous. Given how numerous men of middling ability are, if they are not educated in advance at the outset, some will remain confined to small matters and be unable to achieve anything great, or become accustomed to what lies near at hand and be unable to explore what lies beyond. If, under these circumstances, we suddenly wish to obtain outstanding men, they will certainly be unable to meet our demands. Yet if we still wish to fill positions indiscriminately, we will end up recommending unsuitable men. If their performance is not rigorously assessed afterward, some will become satisfied with small gains and grow negligent in office once their careers are established. If, under these circumstances, we simply expect to obtain conscientious and dutiful ministers, they will certainly be unable to fulfill our hopes. Yet if we still wish to force them to undertake what they cannot do, we will end up entrusting responsibilities to unsuitable men. Thus, wishing to recommend men without providing for their education is like wishing a tree to grow without nourishing its roots. Having recommended them, failing to provide for their assessment is like having a tree grow without guarding against wood-boring insects that might develop within it.

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
是二者其無以致木之用均也然則選擧
考課之義可不慎歟粤自唐虞以降稱長
治久安者莫如周稱法制之備者亦莫如
周今自其選擧考課載在周禮者言之大
司徒以六德六行六藝敎萬民而賓興之
鄉大夫攷民之德行道藝而興賢者能者
此其擧之固已異後世之文詞矣然其敎
之於始也大司徒因民之常而施十有二
敎曰祀曰陽曰陰曰樂曰儀曰俗曰刑曰
===
誓曰度曰世事曰賢曰庸總之於上如此
州長攷德行道藝而勸之糾其過惡而戒
之黨正屬民讀法而書其德行道藝族師
書其孝弟睦婣有學者閭胥書其敬敏任
恤者分以敎之於下如此而又有司諫掌
糾萬民之德而勸之所以敎之者何如其
豫也使民興賢出使長之使民興能入使
治之此其用之固已異後世之資格矣至
其考之於終也太宰以八法治官府其七
punctuated: 是二者，其無以致木之用均也。然則選擧考課之義，可不慎歟？粤自唐虞以降，稱長治久安者莫如周，稱法制之備者亦莫如周。今自其選擧考課載在《周禮》者言之，大司徒以六德、六行、六藝敎萬民而賓興之，鄉大夫攷民之德行道藝而興賢者能者，此其擧之固已異後世之文詞矣。然其敎之於始也，大司徒因民之常而施十有二敎，曰祀、曰陽、曰陰、曰樂、曰儀、曰俗、曰刑、曰誓、曰度、曰世事、曰賢、曰庸，總之於上如此。州長攷德行道藝而勸之，糾其過惡而戒之；黨正屬民讀法而書其德行道藝；族師書其孝弟睦婣有學者；閭胥書其敬敏任恤者，分以敎之於下如此。而又有司諫掌糾萬民之德而勸之，所以敎之者何如其豫也！使民興賢，出使長之；使民興能，入使治之，此其用之固已異後世之資格矣。至其考之於終也，太宰以八法治官府，其七
translation_en:
…These two cases are alike in failing to make the tree useful. How, then, could one fail to give careful attention to the principles of selecting and recommending men and assessing their performance? From the time of Tang Yao and Yu Shun onward, no dynasty equaled the Zhou in its reputation for enduring order and lasting peace; nor did any equal it in the completeness of its laws and institutions. To speak now of its selection and performance assessment as recorded in the Rites of Zhou: the Minister of Education (da situ) taught all the people the six virtues, six forms of conduct, and six arts, and recommended worthy men with the ceremonial honors accorded to guests. The District Grand Masters (xiang dafu) examined the people's virtue, conduct, learning, and skills, and recommended the worthy and the capable. Their recommendations thus already differed from those of later ages, which relied on literary composition.
Yet, in educating them at the outset, the Minister of Education followed the enduring norms of human life and applied twelve kinds of instruction: sacrificial rites, yang rites, yin rites, music, deportment, customs, punishments, solemn pledges, standards, hereditary occupations, worthiness, and meritorious service. Such was the overall direction provided from above. The Department Chiefs (zhou zhang) examined virtue, conduct, learning, and skills and encouraged the people, correcting their faults and wrongdoing and admonishing them. The Township Heads (dang zheng) assembled the people, read the laws to them, and recorded their virtue, conduct, learning, and skills. The Clan Preceptors (zu shi) recorded those who displayed filial piety, fraternal respect, harmony with kin, and amity with relatives by marriage, and those who had learning. The Ward Heads (lü xu) recorded those who were respectful, diligent, dependable, and compassionate. Such was the division of responsibility for instruction below. There were also Remonstrance Officials (si jian), charged with correcting and encouraging the virtue of all the people. How thoroughly their education prepared them in advance!
The people were made to recommend the worthy, who were sent out to lead them; the people were made to recommend the capable, who were brought in to administer affairs. Their employment of men thus already differed from that of later ages, which relied on formal qualifications and seniority. As for assessing them afterward, the Minister of State (tai zai) governed the offices through eight regulations, of which the seventh…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
曰官刑以糾邦治八曰官計以弊邦治總
之於上如此小宰以聽官府之六計弊羣
吏之治曰廉善曰廉能曰廉敬曰廉正曰
廉法曰廉辨分以理之於下如此而又太
宰歲終令百官府各正其治受其會聽其
致事詔王廢置三歲大計羣吏之治而誅
賞之所以考之者何如其嚴也夫惟教之
豫而人有所資以進於善也考之嚴而人
有所儆以益勵於善也此周之所由得人
===
以成治也執事謂選舉考課其法相因是
矣然又以論治者必歸唐虞而有疑於周
之考課以隋唐取士用人之陋而有取於
漢舉孝廉茂材之近古愚則以為考課之
法非至周始嚴也昔在有虞曰敷奏以言
明試以功車服以庸曰三載考績三考黜
陟幽明然則其來久矣彼論治者獨歸唐
虞夫豈皇降而帝帝降而王其時使然乎
未可為周病也漢武孝廉茂才之舉雖小
punctuated:
曰官刑，以糾邦治；八曰官計，以弊邦治。總之於上如此。小宰以聽官府之六計弊羣吏之治：曰廉善，曰廉能，曰廉敬，曰廉正，曰廉法，曰廉辨。分以理之於下如此。而又太宰歲終令百官府各正其治，受其會，聽其致事，詔王廢置；三歲大計羣吏之治，而誅賞之。所以考之者何如其嚴也！夫惟教之豫，而人有所資以進於善也；考之嚴，而人有所儆以益勵於善也。此周之所由得人以成治也。
執事謂選舉考課，其法相因，是矣。然又以論治者必歸唐虞，而有疑於周之考課；以隋唐取士用人之陋，而有取於漢舉孝廉茂材之近古。愚則以為考課之法，非至周始嚴也。昔在有虞，曰：「敷奏以言，明試以功，車服以庸。」曰：「三載考績，三考黜陟幽明。」然則其來久矣。彼論治者獨歸唐虞，夫豈皇降而帝，帝降而王，其時使然乎？未可為周病也。漢武孝廉茂才之舉，雖小
translation_en:
… is called official penalties, by which the governance of the realm is corrected; the eighth is called official accounting, by which the governance of the realm is assessed. Such was the overall direction exercised above. The Junior Steward assessed the administration of the various officials by hearing the six criteria of evaluation applied to government offices: integrity and goodness, integrity and ability, integrity and diligence, integrity and uprightness, integrity and adherence to law, and integrity and discernment. Such was the division of responsibilities for managing affairs below. Furthermore, at the end of each year the Grand Steward ordered all government offices to put their administration in order, received their accounts, heard their reports on completed business, and advised the king on dismissals and appointments. Every three years he conducted a comprehensive assessment of the officials’ administration and punished or rewarded them. How rigorous were the means by which they were assessed! Precisely because instruction was provided beforehand, people had resources upon which to draw in advancing toward goodness; because assessment was rigorous, they had warnings that spurred them to greater efforts toward goodness. This was how the Zhou obtained worthy men and achieved good government.
You say that the methods of selection and performance assessment depend upon one another. This is correct. Yet because those who discuss good government invariably turn to Tang and Yu, you entertain doubts about Zhou performance assessment; and because of the shortcomings of recruitment and appointments under the Sui and Tang, you approve of the Han recommendation of the filial and incorrupt and of outstanding talents as approaching ancient practice. In my humble view, however, methods of performance assessment did not first become rigorous under the Zhou. In the time of Yu, it was said: “Have them present their proposals in words, clearly test them through their accomplishments, and grant them carriages and robes according to their service.” It was also said: “Every three years assess their achievements; after three assessments, dismiss the unenlightened and promote the enlightened.” Thus these practices had a long history. Those who discuss government turn exclusively to Tang and Yu; but could it be that the august sovereigns declined into sage emperors, and the sage emperors into kings, simply because their times made it so? This cannot be counted as a fault of the Zhou. Although Emperor Wu of Han’s recommendation of the filial and incorrupt and of outstanding talents differed slightly …

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
異於隋唐也顧在當時挾書之律再世始
除禮樂之請謙讓未遑然則爲敎可知矣
彼其屢詔邦國夫亦因董仲舒之對慕古
之名姑爲是文具乎未可與周並也審如
是選舉之義考課之方大略可知矣我
國家取士以文而三試之若循文詞之舊矣
其用人稽其年勞而叙遷之若循資格之
舊矣然社有學郡縣有學而其爲敎又皆
宗六經首德行是黨正閭胥敎民之意也
===
郡縣有守令提調之而總於藩司是州長
攷勸糾戒之意也畿輔諸省有憲臣督視
之是司諫糾民之意也士三歲試於鄉論
其秀者而升之禮部是鄉長鄉大夫大司
徒賓興之意也而選舉即周之法矣況懷
材抱德賢良方正之士訪延徵辟不專爲
文夫豈倚於文詞者所可擬乎內外百司
三載一考績各書其功過而奏之銓曹是
受會致事之意也考功第其殿最而黜陟
punctuated:
異於隋唐也。顧在當時，挾書之律再世始除，禮樂之請謙讓未遑，然則爲敎可知矣。彼其屢詔邦國，夫亦因董仲舒之對，慕古之名，姑爲是文具乎？未可與周並也。審如是，選舉之義、考課之方，大略可知矣。
我國家取士以文，而三試之，若循文詞之舊矣；其用人，稽其年勞而叙遷之，若循資格之舊矣。然社有學，郡縣有學，而其爲敎又皆宗六經、首德行，是黨正、閭胥敎民之意也。郡縣有守令提調之，而總於藩司，是州長攷勸糾戒之意也。畿輔諸省有憲臣督視之，是司諫糾民之意也。士三歲試於鄉，論其秀者而升之禮部，是鄉長、鄉大夫、大司徒賓興之意也。而選舉即周之法矣。況懷材抱德、賢良方正之士，訪延徵辟，不專爲文，夫豈倚於文詞者所可擬乎？內外百司三載一考績，各書其功過而奏之銓曹，是受會致事之意也。考功第其殿最而黜陟
translation_en:
… differed from the Sui and Tang. Yet at that time, the law against possessing books was not abolished until two reigns had passed, while proposals concerning rites and music were deferred with modest disclaimers that there had been no leisure to undertake them. From this we can judge the state of instruction. As for the repeated edicts issued throughout the realm, were these not merely prompted by Dong Zhongshu’s response to the throne—a desire for the reputation of emulating antiquity, provisionally satisfied through empty formalities? This cannot be ranked alongside the Zhou. Once this is understood, the principles of selecting men for office and the methods of assessing their performance become broadly clear.
Our dynasty selects men through written compositions and examines them three times, seemingly following the old reliance on literary expression. In employing men, it reviews their years of service and promotes them in sequence, seemingly following the old reliance on qualifications and seniority. Yet there are schools in local communities and schools in prefectures and counties, and their instruction universally takes the Six Classics as its foundation and moral conduct as its foremost concern. This embodies the intent of the Zhou Neighborhood Heads (dangzheng) and Ward Heads (lüxu) in instructing the people. In prefectures and counties, prefects and magistrates oversee these schools, under the overall authority of the Provincial Administration Commission. This embodies the intent of the Zhou District Chiefs (zhouzhang) in examining, encouraging, correcting, and admonishing. In the metropolitan region and the provinces, censorial officials supervise them. This embodies the intent of the Zhou Admonishers (sijian) in correcting the people. Every three years, scholars sit the Provincial Examination; those judged outstanding are advanced to the Ministry of Rites. This embodies the intent of the Zhou township heads, Township Grand Masters (xiangdafu), and Minister of Education (dasitu) in honoring worthy men as guests and recommending them for advancement. Thus our selection of men follows the Zhou method. Moreover, men possessing talent and virtue, men of worth and upright character, are sought out, invited, summoned, and appointed: selection does not depend exclusively on writing. How could this be compared with a system that relies on literary expression alone? The officials of all central and local offices undergo a performance evaluation every three years. Their merits and faults are individually recorded and reported to the Ministry of Personnel. This embodies the intent of receiving aggregate accounts and reports of official business. The Bureau of Evaluations ranks their performance from worst to best and demotes or promotes …

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之是六計弊治之意也其在內者復五年
一考察之在外者復三年一考察之是三
歲大計之意也又臺諫時以所聞舉劾之
太宰請於
上而去留之是歲終詔王廢置之意也而考課
即周之法矣況竒才異能精忠大節之士
超遷特拜不專以資又豈倚於資格者所
可擬乎百六十年士有成材官有成績而
海內乂安有由然矣而執事猶欲講求其
===
法者愚以為成周之法未必不可行於今
也隋唐之事又非所以為訓也為今之計
豈可以他求哉亦惟守吾
祖宗之法而時振飭之而已矣是故學校之教
或隳於士習之浮薄或敗於師儒之怠弛
則
申勅中外本實必敦遴選必慎去其害吾教
者可也黜陟之典或亂於毀譽之失真或
誤於形迹之疑似則
punctuated: 之，是六計弊治之意也。其在內者，復五年一考察之；在外者，復三年一考察之，是三歲大計之意也。又臺諫時以所聞舉劾之，太宰請於上而去留之，是歲終詔王廢置之意也。而考課即周之法矣。況竒才異能、精忠大節之士，超遷特拜，不專以資，又豈倚於資格者所可擬乎？百六十年，士有成材，官有成績，而海內乂安，有由然矣。而執事猶欲講求其法者，愚以為成周之法未必不可行於今也，隋唐之事又非所以為訓也。為今之計，豈可以他求哉？亦惟守吾祖宗之法，而時振飭之而已矣。是故學校之教，或隳於士習之浮薄，或敗於師儒之怠弛，則申勅中外，本實必敦，遴選必慎，去其害吾教者可也。黜陟之典，或亂於毀譽之失真，或誤於形迹之疑似，則
translation_en:
…them: this embodies the intent of judging administration by the six criteria. Those serving in the capital undergo an additional scrutiny every five years, and those serving outside it every three years: this embodies the intent of the triennial grand assessment. Moreover, censors and remonstrance officials periodically recommend or impeach officials on the basis of what they have learned, and the Minister of Personnel petitions the emperor to dismiss or retain them: this embodies the intent of advising the king at year’s end on dismissals and appointments. Thus, performance evaluation follows the methods of the Zhou. Furthermore, men of extraordinary talent and exceptional ability, of perfect loyalty and outstanding integrity, receive accelerated promotion and special appointments, without exclusive reliance on seniority. How could those who depend on seniority and formal qualifications compare with them?

For a hundred and sixty years, scholars have developed their talents and officials have achieved results in office; there are thus reasons why all within the seas enjoys peace and order. Yet you still wish to investigate these methods. In my humble view, the methods of the consummate Zhou need not be impracticable today, while the practices of the Sui and Tang are not suitable models. In devising a policy for the present, why should we seek elsewhere? We need only preserve the institutions of our imperial ancestors and periodically reinvigorate and put them in order.

Thus, if instruction in the schools is undermined by scholars’ frivolous habits or spoiled by teachers’ negligence, renewed injunctions should be issued to officials in the capital and throughout the provinces: substantive learning and conduct must be earnestly cultivated, and teachers must be selected with care. It will suffice to remove whatever harms our teaching. If the system of demotion and promotion is thrown into disorder by untruthful blame and praise, or misled by outward appearances that admit of doubt, then…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
申勅所司事求其實聽求其公去其害吾政
者可也如是則選舉考課豈復有失人之
患而成周之治有不可再見於今哉愚不
敏敢執此以復
第三問
張志淑
同考試官教諭陳批書生談兵亹亹若老將
他日為文武全才者子豈其人邪主司為
國得賢可預慶矣庸執此以驗
===
考試官教授何批六韜左氏互相為用孔
明武穆各有所長子兼指而言之有見矣錄之
考試官教授高批是亦胸中有甲兵者
平邦國之治存乎兵備之不可不豫馭天
下之兵存乎法講之不可不明備不豫則
倉卒應變無以成折衝禦侮之功講不明
則淺率寡謀何以收戰勝攻取之效是故
先王謀其始也睽乖取象則弧矢利夫天
下師嚴以律則地水制于剛中皆以潛消
punctuated:
申勅所司，事求其實，聽求其公，去其害吾政者可也。如是，則選舉考課豈復有失人之患，而成周之治有不可再見於今哉？愚不敏，敢執此以復。
第三問
張志淑
同考試官教諭陳批：書生談兵，亹亹若老將。他日為文武全才者，子豈其人邪？主司為國得賢，可預慶矣。庸執此以驗。
考試官教授何批：《六韜》、《左氏》互相為用，孔明、武穆各有所長。子兼指而言之，有見矣。錄之。
考試官教授高批：是亦胸中有甲兵者。
平邦國之治，存乎兵備之不可不豫；馭天下之兵，存乎法講之不可不明。備不豫，則倉卒應變，無以成折衝禦侮之功；講不明，則淺率寡謀，何以收戰勝攻取之效？是故先王謀其始也，睽乖取象，則弧矢利夫天下；師嚴以律，則地水制于剛中。皆以潛消
translation_en:
…renew the injunctions to the responsible offices: ascertain the facts in every matter, ensure impartiality in hearings, and remove whatever harms our government. That will suffice. If this is done, how could selection and appointment, and assessments of officials, still suffer from failures to obtain the right men? Could the good government of the Zhou in its flourishing days not appear again today? Though I am slow of understanding, I venture to offer this in reply.
Third Question
Zhang Zhishu
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: This scholar discusses military affairs fluently, like a veteran general. Might you be the man who will one day possess complete mastery of both civil and military affairs? We may already congratulate the chief examiners on securing a worthy man for the state. Let these words stand as a prediction to be tested.
Comment by Examiner He, Professor: The Six Secret Teachings (Liu tao) and Zuo’s Commentary (Zuo shi) complement one another; Kongming [Zhuge Liang] and Wumu [Yue Fei] each had their particular strengths. In discussing them together, you show insight. Accept this answer.
Comment by Examiner Gao, Professor: Here, too, is a man who carries armor and troops within his breast.
The governance that brings peace to the realm depends on military preparations, which must be made in advance; command of the armies of All-under-Heaven depends on the study of military methods, which must be thoroughly understood. Without advance preparations, a sudden response to an emergency cannot succeed in repelling aggression and resisting insult. Without clear understanding gained through study, how can superficiality, rashness, and scant planning yield victory in battle and success in taking objectives? Thus the former kings laid their plans at the outset: taking their image from the estrangement represented by the Kui hexagram, they made bows and arrows beneficial to All-under-Heaven; making armies strict through discipline, they embodied in earth and water the control exercised by the firm central line of the Shi hexagram. All this was intended quietly to eliminate…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
暴亂陰奪不軌輔弼敎化宣昭文德歸于
無亂以成君之仁初非必於用武以毒天
下也是故泥焉者敗變焉者神弛焉者弗
可振也然則備之其可以弗豫講之其可
以弗明邪執事以文策士而以武事相與
講明豈以書生亦有識達時務者乎請試
言之兵也者天地之義氣也天無是氣則
不成歲功人無是氣則不成人道故宋子
罕曰天有五財民並用之廢一不可何能
===
去兵夫兵金象也五財無金則木煩而不
制水煩而不化五行擧乖其用則兵固天
道之不可廢者聖人明於天道故五射五
御之學備於周官而夾谷之會雖孔子大
聖亦具左右司馬以從則兵尤儒者事也
自軒轅制五陣以生克爲勝負太公爲六
韜以極陰陽之變化而兵法始著於天下
矣夫五陣五行之理也六韜八卦之象也
其法出于河圖洛書後世兵家者流雖出
punctuated:
暴亂，陰奪不軌，輔弼敎化，宣昭文德，歸于無亂，以成君之仁，初非必於用武以毒天下也。是故泥焉者敗，變焉者神，弛焉者弗可振也。然則備之，其可以弗豫；講之，其可以弗明邪？執事以文策士，而以武事相與講明，豈以書生亦有識達時務者乎？請試言之。
兵也者，天地之義氣也。天無是氣，則不成歲功；人無是氣，則不成人道。故宋子罕曰：「天有五財，民並用之，廢一不可，何能去兵？」夫兵，金象也。五財無金，則木煩而不制，水煩而不化，五行擧乖其用，則兵固天道之不可廢者。聖人明於天道，故五射五御之學備於周官，而夾谷之會，雖孔子大聖，亦具左右司馬以從，則兵尤儒者事也。
自軒轅制五陣，以生克爲勝負，太公爲六韜，以極陰陽之變化，而兵法始著於天下矣。夫五陣，五行之理也；六韜，八卦之象也。其法出于河圖洛書。後世兵家者流，雖出
translation_en:
… violent disorder, forestall illicit designs in secret, assist moral instruction, and make civil virtue manifest, bringing about freedom from disorder and thereby fulfilling the ruler’s benevolence. The original purpose was certainly not to insist on using military force to afflict all under Heaven. Thus, those who cling rigidly to military methods fail; those who adapt them achieve marvelous results; and those who let military preparedness lapse cannot restore it. Can preparations, then, be left until too late, or military methods be studied without attaining clarity? You, honored examiners, test scholars through literary policy essays, yet invite us to examine military affairs together. Is this because you believe that even among bookish scholars there are some whose understanding encompasses the affairs of the time? Allow me to attempt an explanation.
Military force is the righteous vital energy of Heaven and Earth. Without this energy, Heaven could not accomplish the work of the year; without it, human beings could not fulfill the human Way. Thus Zihan of Song said: “Heaven has five resources, and the people use them all together. Not one can be discarded. How, then, could weapons be abolished?” Weapons embody the image of metal. If the five resources lacked metal, wood would proliferate unchecked, and water would become excessive without undergoing transformation; all five phases would fail to perform their functions. Military force is therefore something that the Way of Heaven cannot dispense with. The sages understood the Way of Heaven; hence instruction in the five techniques of archery and the five techniques of chariot driving is fully provided for in the Offices of Zhou. At the meeting at Jiagu, even Confucius, great sage though he was, had Marshals of the Left and Right accompany him. Military affairs are thus especially a concern of Confucian scholars.
Xuanyuan devised the five battle formations, making victory and defeat depend on the mutual generation and conquest of the five phases; the Grand Duke composed the Six Secret Teachings, exploring to the utmost the transformations of yin and yang. From then on, the methods of warfare became known throughout the world. The five battle formations embody the principles of the five phases; the Six Secret Teachings embody the images of the eight trigrams. Their methods derive from the River Chart and the Luo Writing. Military strategists of later ages, although they brought forth …

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
奇效詭縱横經緯至于百千萬變不可勝
窮然終不能有出於五行八卦之外者迨
夫一變而爲春秋則左氏得其意觀其叙
晉敗狄曰兩於前伍於後專爲右角參爲
左角偏爲前拒則步戰之五陣也其叙楚
敗晉曰軍行右轅左追前茅慮無中權後
勁則車戰之五陣也其法純用軒轅蒙馬
遁荆採樵致絞左氏以叙事寓兵法用之
於戰其可乎哉左氏去周未遠古法猶存
===
故有車戰而無騎戰當時有車而無騎也
自鄭莊公用徒兵中行穆子毁車崇卒趙
武靈王用胡騎而車騎步卒始並用于天
下矣又變而爲戰國則武經七書得其精
觀其載太公論戰騎有必走必懼必敗必
饑必亂可克可擒可虜之十勝焉有敗地
圍地死地没地竭地艱地困地患地隅地
之九敗焉其法載于六韜然而不用于周
不見于春秋其深謀妙法反出于孫武子
punctuated: 奇效詭，縱横經緯，至于百千萬變，不可勝窮，然終不能有出於五行八卦之外者。迨夫一變而爲春秋，則左氏得其意。觀其叙晉敗狄曰：「兩於前，伍於後，專爲右角，參爲左角，偏爲前拒。」則步戰之五陣也。其叙楚敗晉曰：「軍行，右轅左追，前茅慮無，中權後勁。」則車戰之五陣也。其法純用軒轅。蒙馬遁荆，採樵致絞，左氏以叙事寓兵法，用之於戰，其可乎哉？左氏去周未遠，古法猶存，故有車戰而無騎戰，當時有車而無騎也。自鄭莊公用徒兵，中行穆子毁車崇卒，趙武靈王用胡騎，而車騎步卒始並用于天下矣。又變而爲戰國，則《武經七書》得其精。觀其載太公論戰騎，有必走、必懼、必敗、必饑、必亂、可克、可擒、可虜之十勝焉；有敗地、圍地、死地、没地、竭地、艱地、困地、患地、隅地之九敗焉。其法載于《六韜》，然而不用于周，不見于春秋，其深謀妙法反出于孫武子
translation_en:
…extraordinary stratagems and displays of deception, maneuvering in every direction through hundreds, thousands, and myriads of inexhaustible variations, ultimately none can go beyond the Five Phases and Eight Trigrams. When circumstances changed and the Spring and Autumn period arrived, Master Zuo grasped their meaning. Consider his account of Jin’s defeat of the Di: “Place units of twenty-five in front and units of five behind; concentrate forces on the right flank, divide them into three on the left flank, and deploy a detachment as the forward defense.” These are the five formations for infantry warfare. His account of Chu’s defeat of Jin says: “On the march, chariots on the right and pursuit troops on the left [?]; scouts ahead guard against the unexpected, the command occupies the center, and strong troops bring up the rear.” These are the five formations for chariot warfare. These methods follow Xuanyuan entirely. Covering horses to put the troops of Jing to flight, and gathering firewood to lure out the men of Jiao—Master Zuo embeds military methods in his narration of events. Could these be applied in battle? Master Zuo lived not long after the Zhou, and ancient methods still survived. Thus there was chariot warfare but no cavalry warfare: at that time there were chariots but no cavalry. Only after Duke Zhuang of Zheng employed infantry, Zhonghang Muzi destroyed chariots and promoted foot soldiers, and King Wuling of Zhao employed Hu cavalry did chariots, cavalry, and infantry begin to be used together throughout the realm.

When circumstances changed again and the Warring States period arrived, the Seven Military Classics captured the essence of these methods. Consider their account of the Grand Duke’s discussion of cavalry warfare: there are ten conditions for victory, under which the enemy must flee, must become fearful, must suffer defeat, must go hungry, must fall into disorder, or can be overcome, captured, or taken prisoner. There are nine conditions for defeat: unfavorable ground, encircled ground, deadly ground, sinking ground, exhausting ground, difficult ground, confining ground, dangerous ground, and cornered ground. These methods are recorded in the Six Secret Teachings, yet they were not employed under the Zhou and do not appear in the Spring and Autumn period. Their profound plans and ingenious methods nevertheless rank below those of Master Sun Wu…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之下蘇子謂六韜非周書則其所言亦有
據矣誠爲戰國知兵之士祖其餘論而推
廣之設爲問答以極兵家之變也然躙轢
彊陣遏禦奔衝不可以無車乘亂搗虛追
敗結離不可以無騎短戟相交投石超距
不可以無卒而車騎歩卒不可偏廢于天
下矣是故用兵貴乎有紀尚節制也決勝
至于無形尚權變也二者兵家之大權左
氏多古法尚近節制之兵六韜多變法已
===
極權謀之秘武侯八陣本六韜而其節制
則得諸左氏故武侯之兵極天下之至深
岳飛兵法本左氏而其運用則得諸六韜
故岳飛之兵極天下之至變兵志曰凡兵
之道莫貴乎一一者能獨往獨來階於道
幾於神用之在於機顯之在於勢所謂奇
正相生循環無端者也此又兵家之至要
二公之所獨得也今觀武侯八陣擊首則
尾至擊尾則首至擊中則首尾皆至岳飛
punctuated:
之下。蘇子謂《六韜》非周書，則其所言亦有據矣。誠爲戰國知兵之士，祖其餘論而推廣之，設爲問答，以極兵家之變也。然躙轢彊陣，遏禦奔衝，不可以無車；乘亂搗虛，追敗結離，不可以無騎；短戟相交，投石超距，不可以無卒。而車騎歩卒不可偏廢于天下矣。
是故用兵貴乎有紀，尚節制也；決勝至于無形，尚權變也。二者，兵家之大權。《左氏》多古法，尚近節制之兵；《六韜》多變法，已極權謀之秘。武侯八陣本《六韜》，而其節制則得諸《左氏》，故武侯之兵極天下之至深。岳飛兵法本《左氏》，而其運用則得諸《六韜》，故岳飛之兵極天下之至變。
《兵志》曰：「凡兵之道，莫貴乎一。一者，能獨往獨來，階於道，幾於神。用之在於機，顯之在於勢。」所謂奇正相生，循環無端者也。此又兵家之至要，二公之所獨得也。今觀武侯八陣，擊首則尾至，擊尾則首至，擊中則首尾皆至。岳飛
translation_en:
…below that of Master Sun Wu. Master Su said that the Six Secret Teachings (Liutao) was not a Zhou work; his statement thus has grounds. It was indeed composed by men of the Warring States period who understood warfare: they took the master's surviving discussions as their foundation and elaborated upon them, casting them as questions and answers to explore fully the variations of military practice. Yet to trample strong formations and check charging assaults, chariots are indispensable; to exploit disorder, strike undefended positions, pursue defeated troops, and join or separate forces [?], cavalry is indispensable; to engage at close quarters with short halberds, hurl stones, and leap across distances, foot soldiers are indispensable. Thus none of the three—chariots, cavalry, or infantry—can be discarded in warfare anywhere under Heaven.
Therefore, in employing troops, orderly organization is prized: this means valuing discipline and control. In securing victory without discernible form, adaptability is prized. These two are the great governing principles of military practice. The Zuo Commentary contains many ancient methods and remains close to warfare governed by discipline and control; the Six Secret Teachings contains many adaptable methods and has already probed the deepest secrets of stratagem. The Eight Formations of the Marquis Wu were based on the Six Secret Teachings, but their discipline and control came from the Zuo Commentary. Thus the Marquis Wu's warfare attained the utmost profundity under Heaven. Yue Fei's military methods were based on the Zuo Commentary, but his practical deployment of them came from the Six Secret Teachings. Thus Yue Fei's warfare attained the utmost adaptability under Heaven.
The Military Records states: “In all the ways of warfare, nothing is more precious than unity. Through unity, one can advance and withdraw independently, ascend to the Way, and approach the divine. Its application rests on the critical opportunity; its manifestation rests on strategic advantage.” This is what is meant by the unorthodox and orthodox generating each other in an endless cycle. This, moreover, is the highest essential of military practice, which these two men uniquely grasped. Now consider the Marquis Wu's Eight Formations: strike the head, and the tail comes to its aid; strike the tail, and the head comes; strike the center, and both head and tail come. Yue Fei…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
行陣兵識將意將識士情人人各自爲戰
此皆會于一而幾于神者也摧敵制勝有
以哉法異功同一者基之矣是故以兵法
言則左氏不如六韜之盡而深六韜不如
左氏之約而大以知兵言則岳飛不如武
侯之深而安武侯亦當以岳飛之兵爲變
且神也使今之爲兵者學六韜皆如武侯
之得其深學左氏皆如岳飛之得其變則
用左氏可也用六韜可也使學六韜而徒
===
得其數學左氏而徒尚其辭則左氏固陳
言也六韜亦陳言也所謂徒讀父書者耳
其何以應天下之變哉洪惟我
朝稽古定制擇將備邊其置兵也內設兵部
五府以統之外設都司衛所以翼之大小
相維犬牙相制備至豫矣其訓兵也內則
嚴團營操練之典外則慎考較演習之法
調度有時開闔有方講至明矣一或有變
則又命將出師擇人任勢使騎步相參五
punctuated:
行陣，兵識將意，將識士情，人人各自爲戰，此皆會于一而幾于神者也。摧敵制勝有以哉！法異功同，一者基之矣。是故以兵法言，則左氏不如六韜之盡而深，六韜不如左氏之約而大；以知兵言，則岳飛不如武侯之深而安，武侯亦當以岳飛之兵爲變且神也。使今之爲兵者學六韜，皆如武侯之得其深；學左氏，皆如岳飛之得其變，則用左氏可也，用六韜可也。使學六韜而徒得其數，學左氏而徒尚其辭，則左氏固陳言也，六韜亦陳言也，所謂徒讀父書者耳。其何以應天下之變哉！
洪惟我朝稽古定制，擇將備邊。其置兵也，內設兵部、五府以統之，外設都司、衛所以翼之，大小相維，犬牙相制，備至豫矣。其訓兵也，內則嚴團營操練之典，外則慎考較演習之法，調度有時，開闔有方，講至明矣。一或有變，則又命將出師，擇人任勢，使騎步相參，五
translation_en:
…in Yue Fei’s battle formations, the soldiers understood their commanders’ intentions, and the commanders understood their men’s dispositions; every man fought on his own initiative. All these practices converged upon unity and approached the divine. There was indeed a basis for crushing the enemy and securing victory! Their methods differed, but their achievements were alike: unity underlay them. Thus, in terms of military methods, the Zuo Commentary (Zuozhuan) falls short of the Six Secret Teachings (Liutao) in comprehensiveness and depth, while the Six Secret Teachings falls short of the Zuo Commentary in concision and breadth. In understanding warfare, Yue Fei falls short of the Marquis Wu (Zhuge Liang) in profundity and steadiness; yet the Marquis Wu, too, would surely have regarded Yue Fei’s use of troops as adaptable and divinely skillful. If those who conduct military affairs today studied the Six Secret Teachings and all grasped its profundity as the Marquis Wu did, and studied the Zuo Commentary and all grasped its adaptability as Yue Fei did, then either the Zuo Commentary or the Six Secret Teachings could serve them. But if they study the Six Secret Teachings merely to acquire its techniques, and study the Zuo Commentary merely to prize its language, then the Zuo Commentary is indeed nothing but stale words, and the Six Secret Teachings is likewise nothing but stale words. Such men are merely what is called ‘those who only read their fathers’ books.’ How could they respond to the changing circumstances of the world?
We reverently reflect that our dynasty has examined antiquity to establish its institutions, selected commanders, and provided for frontier defense. In organizing its forces, it established the Ministry of War and the Five Chief Military Commissions at the center to command them, and Regional Military Commissions, Guards, and Battalions in the provinces to support them. Greater and lesser units sustain one another, their jurisdictions interlocking like dogs’ teeth to provide mutual checks: preparations are made thoroughly in advance. In training its forces, it strictly enforces the regulations for drilling the capital’s regimental camps, while carefully observing the procedures for assessment and exercises in the provinces. Mobilization and deployment have their appointed times, and opening and closing formations follow proper methods: instruction is fully explicit. Should any disturbance arise, it further appoints commanders to lead armies into the field, selecting suitable men and making use of the strategic circumstances, so that cavalry and infantry support one another, and the five…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
兵互用兵識將意將識士情百六十年以
來兵威强盛邊境肅清有由然矣然而承
平日久邊卒漸驕日者雲中之變至厪
宵旰之憂屯兵易將始克底平豈兵威未豫而
使之狎兵謀不素而使之縱邪故愚謂宜
於學校之中別立戎教科舉取士試以兵
務又於武學武舉之外別立講武一司隷
諸禁籍博采天下文臣武將謀略智勇之
士延置其中使之日講韜略推演八陣極
===
深研幾制器尚象皆可以施於實用如孔
明之深也以盡天下之變又時以其法閱
練軍士使皆知將意而識士情有若一身
之於四肢如岳飛之變也以盡天下之神
則今之兵猶夫古也而古今人豈不相及
哉矧我
國家至仁有道神武不殺威德所加無遠弗
届若蒞戎者法自昭明而不可犯事有豫
備而不失宜則赳赳武夫足為公侯腹心
punctuated: 兵互用，兵識將意，將識士情。百六十年以來，兵威强盛，邊境肅清，有由然矣。然而承平日久，邊卒漸驕，日者雲中之變，至厪宵旰之憂，屯兵易將，始克底平。豈兵威未豫而使之狎，兵謀不素而使之縱邪？故愚謂宜於學校之中別立戎教，科舉取士，試以兵務；又於武學武舉之外，別立講武一司，隷諸禁籍，博采天下文臣武將謀略智勇之士，延置其中，使之日講韜略，推演八陣，極深研幾，制器尚象，皆可以施於實用，如孔明之深也，以盡天下之變。又時以其法閱練軍士，使皆知將意而識士情，有若一身之於四肢，如岳飛之變也，以盡天下之神。則今之兵猶夫古也，而古今人豈不相及哉？矧我國家至仁有道，神武不殺，威德所加，無遠弗届。若蒞戎者法自昭明而不可犯，事有豫備而不失宜，則赳赳武夫足為公侯腹心。
translation_en:
…weapons employed in combination, the soldiers understanding their commanders’ intentions and the commanders understanding their men’s circumstances. There is thus good reason why, for a hundred and sixty years, our military power has been strong and our frontiers tranquil. Yet after prolonged peace, the frontier troops have gradually grown arrogant. The recent upheaval in Yunzhong caused His Majesty anxiety from before dawn until late at night; only after troops were stationed there and commanders replaced could peace finally be restored. Could it be that military authority had not been established beforehand [?], allowing the troops to become insolent, and that military plans had not been prepared in advance, allowing them to run unchecked?

I therefore humbly propose that separate military instruction be established within the schools, and that candidates recruited through the civil-service examinations be tested on military affairs. Beyond the existing military schools and military examinations, a separate bureau for the study of warfare should also be established and entered on the imperial guard registers [?]. Civil officials and military commanders throughout the realm possessing strategic ability, intelligence, and courage should be widely sought out and invited to serve there. Let them discuss military strategy daily, develop the eight battle formations, plumb the depths and investigate the first stirrings of change, and fashion implements according to exemplary forms—all for practical application. With profundity like that of Kongming, they could encompass every transformation under Heaven. Moreover, let them periodically inspect and train the soldiers according to these methods, so that commanders’ intentions and soldiers’ circumstances are mutually understood, like the relationship between a body and its four limbs. With adaptability like that of Yue Fei, they could exhaust the possibilities of marvellous efficacy under Heaven.
