Then the armies of today would be like those of antiquity: how could men of the present fail to equal the ancients?

All the more so since our dynasty is supremely benevolent and possesses the Way, displaying divine martial power without killing: wherever its might and virtue extend, no place is too distant to be reached. If those directing military affairs maintain clear regulations that cannot be violated, and prepare affairs in advance so that their actions remain appropriate, then our valiant warriors will be worthy to serve as the trusted confidants of dukes and lords.

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
善為治者法古之意而不泥其迹者也夫
意也者制作之所由出也迹也者制作之
所由寓也是本非二物也而何以曰意可
法迹不可泥哉蓋天下之勢其變無常形
而吾之治之不可以膠於一定故古昔帝
王之有所制作也由其初言之治如其時
事如其意固所謂名實相副者及行之既
久勢以時變向之制作有所窒礙而不可
復行則雖帝王身當其任亦且視為陳迹
===
推其意而更為之矣況治於其後者尚可
以泥乎是故法其意則雖事不相沿無所
往而非實泥其迹則雖行之舉相似無所
往而非名是名實之辯也請因明問所及
而陳其槩世之論名實者其於名類能知
之至所謂實則吾猶惑焉立官而命之曰
是冢宰是司徒是宗伯司馬司宼司空以
為六官之實在是矣取民之田而限之曰
母過百畝割其贏以畀鄉里九族以為井
punctuated:
善為治者，法古之意而不泥其迹者也。夫意也者，制作之所由出也；迹也者，制作之所由寓也。是本非二物也，而何以曰意可法、迹不可泥哉？蓋天下之勢，其變無常形，而吾之治之，不可以膠於一定。故古昔帝王之有所制作也，由其初言之，治如其時，事如其意，固所謂名實相副者。及行之既久，勢以時變，向之制作有所窒礙而不可復行，則雖帝王身當其任，亦且視為陳迹，推其意而更為之矣。況治於其後者，尚可以泥乎？是故法其意，則雖事不相沿，無所往而非實；泥其迹，則雖行之舉相似，無所往而非名。是名實之辯也。
請因明問所及而陳其槩。世之論名實者，其於名，類能知之；至所謂實，則吾猶惑焉。立官而命之曰：「是冢宰，是司徒，是宗伯、司馬、司宼、司空。」以為六官之實在是矣。取民之田而限之曰：「母過百畝。」割其贏以畀鄉里九族，以為井
translation_en:
Those skilled in governing follow the intent of antiquity without clinging to its outward forms. Intent is that from which institutions arise; outward forms are that in which institutions find expression. These are fundamentally not two separate things. Why, then, do we say that intent may be followed, but outward forms must not be rigidly maintained? Circumstances in the world change without any constant pattern, and our governance cannot remain bound to a single fixed arrangement. Thus, when the emperors and kings of antiquity established institutions, at the outset their governance suited the times and their undertakings accorded with their intentions. This was indeed what is meant by names and substance corresponding. But after these institutions had long been in use, circumstances changed with the times, and the institutions previously established encountered obstructions and could no longer be implemented. Even if those emperors and kings themselves were still in charge, they would regard these institutions as relics of the past, work out their underlying intent, and remake them. How much less could those governing afterward still cling to them? Thus, if one follows their intent, even though one's undertakings do not perpetuate earlier practices, everything has substance. If one clings to their outward forms, even though every action resembles theirs, everything is merely a name. Such is the distinction between names and substance.
Allow me to outline the matter with reference to the points raised in your discerning question. Those today who discuss names and substance generally understand names; as for what they call substance, I remain perplexed. They establish offices and designate them, saying, “This is the Minister of State; this is the Minister of Education; these are the Minister of Rites, Minister of War, Minister of Justice, and Minister of Works.” They suppose that herein lies the substance of the Six Offices. They take the people's fields and impose a limit, saying, “Do not exceed one hundred mu.” They cut off the excess and give it to fellow villagers and members of the nine degrees of kinship, supposing that herein lies the substance of the well-field …

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
田之實在是矣嗚呼此其所謂實乃正吾
所謂名也夫六官之所由設何爲也哉以
治民焉耳井田之所由畫何爲也哉以養
民焉耳治也養也是帝王制作之實也而
其曰六官曰井田陳迹之存乎簡編者皆
所謂名也使爲國家者興賢而用之擇能
而使之邦治果修也邦教果敷也邦禮果
秩也邦政果舉也邦禁果章也邦土果奠
也雖不立六官其實六官也不然獨名而
===
已矣因民之利而興之擇民之害而去之
强不得凌弱也衆不得暴寡也富不得兼
倂於貧也吏不得多取於下也雖不畫井
田其實井田也不然亦名而已矣古之帝
王有見於此是故唐虞建官惟百夏商官
倍周官三百六十周固無所襲於夏商而
夏商亦自不襲唐虞之舊夏貢殷助周徹
文王九一武王十一三代固不相沿而武
王亦自不沿其父之制苟益於民則帝王
punctuated:
田之實在是矣。嗚呼！此其所謂實，乃正吾所謂名也。夫六官之所由設，何爲也哉？以治民焉耳。井田之所由畫，何爲也哉？以養民焉耳。治也，養也，是帝王制作之實也。而其曰六官、曰井田，陳迹之存乎簡編者，皆所謂名也。使爲國家者興賢而用之，擇能而使之，邦治果修也，邦教果敷也，邦禮果秩也，邦政果舉也，邦禁果章也，邦土果奠也，雖不立六官，其實六官也。不然，獨名而已矣。因民之利而興之，擇民之害而去之，强不得凌弱也，衆不得暴寡也，富不得兼倂於貧也，吏不得多取於下也，雖不畫井田，其實井田也。不然，亦名而已矣。
古之帝王有見於此，是故唐虞建官惟百，夏商官倍，周官三百六十。周固無所襲於夏商，而夏商亦自不襲唐虞之舊。夏貢，殷助，周徹；文王九一，武王十一。三代固不相沿，而武王亦自不沿其父之制。苟益於民，則帝王
translation_en:
…the substance of the well-field system lies in this. Alas! What they call substance is precisely what I call name. Why were the Six Offices established? Simply to govern the people. Why were the well-fields laid out? Simply to provide for the people. Governing and providing: these are the substance of the institutions created by emperors and kings. As for what are called the Six Offices and the well-fields—the surviving traces of the past preserved in books—these are all what I call names. Suppose those who govern a state promote and employ the worthy, select and appoint the capable, and thereby truly put the state's administration in order, spread its moral instruction, regulate its rites, carry out its governance, make its prohibitions clear, and secure its territory. Even if they do not establish the Six Offices, they have the Six Offices in substance. Otherwise, they have only the name. If they develop what benefits the people and identify and remove what harms them, so that the strong cannot oppress the weak, the many cannot tyrannize over the few, the rich cannot engross the holdings of the poor, and officials cannot exact excessive levies from those below, then even without laying out well-fields, they have the well-field system in substance. Otherwise, this too is merely a name.
The emperors and kings of antiquity understood this. Thus, under Tang and Yu there were only one hundred offices; under Xia and Shang, twice that number; and under Zhou, three hundred and sixty. Zhou did not simply inherit the arrangements of Xia and Shang, nor did Xia and Shang simply inherit the old arrangements of Tang and Yu. Xia used the tribute system, Yin the labor-assistance system, and Zhou the che assessment system. King Wen took one part in nine, and King Wu one part in ten. The Three Dynasties did not simply follow one another, and King Wu did not even follow his own father's institutions. If something benefits the people, then it accords with the emperors' and kings'…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之意也昔者周公之思兼三王以施四事
也其有不合仰而思之坐以待旦而孟子
之論井地曰若夫潤澤之則在君與子變
通以盡利神化以宜民聖賢之所為蓋如
此至於後世時益以降則勢宜益以殊而
顧泥六官井田之迹思舉而復之於數千
載之下狥其名不責其實此其為莽歟此
其為宇文歟夫莽之事自其迹觀之不可
謂非井田也宇文之事自其迹觀之不可
===
謂非六官也然卒之六官無救於周之亡
而井田適以促新之滅然則其效可覩矣
自孟子以下善論治者愚於漢得董仲舒
焉其告武帝曰三王之道所祖不同非其
相反將以捄溢扶衰故王者有改制之名
無變道之實斯言也非無所見而云也殷
因於夏禮所損益可知周因於殷禮所損
益可知是魯論之旨而精於名實之辯者
也周公以下善為治者愚於唐得太宗焉
punctuated:
之意也。昔者周公之思兼三王以施四事也，其有不合，仰而思之，坐以待旦。而孟子之論井地曰：「若夫潤澤之，則在君與子。」變通以盡利，神化以宜民，聖賢之所為蓋如此。至於後世，時益以降，則勢宜益以殊，而顧泥六官井田之迹，思舉而復之於數千載之下，狥其名，不責其實，此其為莽歟？此其為宇文歟？夫莽之事，自其迹觀之，不可謂非井田也；宇文之事，自其迹觀之，不可謂非六官也。然卒之，六官無救於周之亡，而井田適以促新之滅。然則其效可覩矣。
自孟子以下善論治者，愚於漢得董仲舒焉。其告武帝曰：「三王之道，所祖不同，非其相反，將以捄溢扶衰。故王者有改制之名，無變道之實。」斯言也，非無所見而云也。「殷因於夏禮，所損益可知；周因於殷禮，所損益可知。」是魯論之旨，而精於名實之辯者也。
周公以下善為治者，愚於唐得太宗焉。
translation_en:
…is the intent of the emperors and kings. In former times, when the Duke of Zhou sought to draw together the practices of the Three Kings in implementing four matters, whenever something did not accord with his purpose, he looked up in reflection and sat awaiting dawn. And when Mengzi discussed the well-field system, he said: “As for refining and adapting it, that rests with your ruler and yourself.” Adapting institutions to realize their full benefits, bringing about wondrous transformations to suit the people: such, indeed, were the practices of sages and worthies. In later ages, as time advanced, circumstances necessarily differed ever more greatly. Yet some clung to the outward forms of the Six Offices and the well-field system, seeking to revive them thousands of years later, pursuing their names without demanding their substance. Was this not what Wang Mang did? Was this not what Yuwen did? Judged by its outward form, Wang Mang’s undertaking could certainly be called the well-field system; judged by its outward form, Yuwen’s undertaking could certainly be called the Six Offices. Yet in the end the Six Offices did nothing to save the Zhou dynasty from falling, while the well-field system merely hastened the destruction of the Xin dynasty. Their results are thus plain to see.
Among those after Mengzi who discussed government well, I humbly find Dong Zhongshu in the Han dynasty. He told Emperor Wu: “The ways of the Three Kings differed in what they took as their models, but this does not mean that they contradicted one another. Their purpose was to remedy excess and shore up decline. Thus kings nominally change institutions, but in substance do not alter the Way.” These words were not spoken without insight. “Yin followed the rites of Xia; what it subtracted and added can be known. Zhou followed the rites of Yin; what it subtracted and added can be known.” This is the purport of the Lu Analects, and it shows a precise grasp of the distinction between names and realities.
Among those after the Duke of Zhou who governed well, I humbly find Taizong in the Tang dynasty.

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
口分世業以授民租庸調以取民而天下
稱治斯義也非無所本而然也聖人不先
天以開人各因時以立政是春秋之旨而
深有得於名實之辨者也執事發策乃不
能無疑於仲舒之論而惜太宗之不竟其
施其亦小泥焉矣至謂三代制作不可行
於後世意若有深諱焉者愚以為是無損
於三代也蓋今所謂三代制作皆其迹也
未有能得其意也誠得其意則豈惟今之
===
世行之無弊哉雖千百世可矣故愚嘗竊
譬之帝王制作之意歷千百世而可行者
猶天之元氣流通運行無有止息者也其
制作之迹隨時改易者猶天之五行二象
始終升降循環而不窮者也而烏能一之
是故善為治者法古之意而不泥其迹如
是而止矣雖然欲法古必先自治使徒欲
得帝王之意而巳之所以為意者或牽於
有我則不能舍以從天下之公或敢於自
punctuated: 口分、世業以授民，租庸調以取民，而天下稱治。斯義也，非無所本而然也。聖人不先天以開人，各因時以立政，是春秋之旨，而深有得於名實之辨者也。執事發策，乃不能無疑於仲舒之論，而惜太宗之不竟其施，其亦小泥焉矣。至謂三代制作不可行於後世，意若有深諱焉者，愚以為是無損於三代也。蓋今所謂三代制作，皆其迹也，未有能得其意也。誠得其意，則豈惟今之世行之無弊哉？雖千百世可矣。故愚嘗竊譬之：帝王制作之意，歷千百世而可行者，猶天之元氣流通運行，無有止息者也；其制作之迹，隨時改易者，猶天之五行二象，始終升降，循環而不窮者也。而烏能一之？是故善為治者，法古之意而不泥其迹，如是而止矣。雖然，欲法古，必先自治。使徒欲得帝王之意，而巳之所以為意者或牽於有我，則不能舍以從天下之公；或敢於自
translation_en:
…He allotted land to the people as per-capita holdings and hereditary estates, and levied grain tax, labor service, and textile payments upon them; the realm was acclaimed as well governed. This principle, too, had a foundation. The sages did not anticipate Heaven in enlightening the people, but each established government in accordance with his times. This is the purport of the Spring and Autumn Annals, and it shows a profound grasp of the distinction between names and realities. Yet in setting this policy question, you express doubts about Dong Zhongshu’s argument and regret that Taizong did not fully carry out his measures. This, too, seems somewhat inflexible. As for the assertion that the institutions of the Three Dynasties cannot be implemented in later ages, you seem to regard it as something deeply taboo. In my humble view, it does no discredit to the Three Dynasties.

What are now called the institutions of the Three Dynasties are merely their outward forms; no one has yet grasped their underlying intent. If that intent were truly grasped, could it be put into practice without ill effects only in the present age? It could endure for hundreds or thousands of generations. Thus I have ventured to draw this analogy: the intent underlying the institutions of emperors and kings, which remains practicable through hundreds or thousands of generations, resembles Heaven’s primordial vital force, circulating and moving without cessation. The outward forms of their institutions, which change with the times, resemble Heaven’s Five Phases and its two manifestations, yin and yang: beginning and ending, rising and falling, cycling endlessly. How could these be made uniform? Thus those skilled in government emulate the intent of antiquity without clinging to its outward forms. That is all.

Nevertheless, anyone wishing to emulate antiquity must first govern himself. Suppose one merely wishes to grasp the intent of emperors and kings, while one’s own intentions are bound by attachment to the self: then one cannot relinquish that attachment to follow the common good of the realm. Or if one is bold in relying on oneself…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
用則不能虛以稽衆論之是或狃於柔懦
則不能斷以袪浮議之惑或蔽於近小則
不能明以燭幽隱之情彼其執以爲古之
意者將出於一己之見而非帝王之本然
其因仍故事也必失於偷惰變易法制也
必失於紛更雖有過人之資必爲之志亦
終爲漢文之謙讓未遑宋神之偏信獨斷
而可不戒哉故爲人君者必有格致之學
以明乎天下之理必有誠正之功以踐乎
===
天下之理然後能識古帝王之意而所謂
致三代之隆建萬世之長策者可得而言
焉是又執事未發之意也謹對
第五問
潘仲驂
同考試官教諭馬批足食足兵國政之大也
子能區處得宜是有先憂之志者詞亦足以發之
參之他策俱優錄此鼎嘗一臠矣
考試官教授何批其人存則其政舉識之
punctuated:
用，則不能虛以稽衆論之是；或狃於柔懦，則不能斷以袪浮議之惑；或蔽於近小，則不能明以燭幽隱之情。彼其執以爲古之意者，將出於一己之見，而非帝王之本然。其因仍故事也，必失於偷惰；變易法制也，必失於紛更。雖有過人之資、必爲之志，亦終爲漢文之謙讓未遑、宋神之偏信獨斷，而可不戒哉？故爲人君者，必有格致之學，以明乎天下之理；必有誠正之功，以踐乎天下之理。然後能識古帝王之意，而所謂致三代之隆、建萬世之長策者，可得而言焉。是又執事未發之意也。謹對。
第五問
潘仲驂
同考試官教諭馬批：足食足兵，國政之大也。子能區處得宜，是有先憂之志者，詞亦足以發之。參之他策，俱優，錄此鼎嘗一臠矣。
考試官教授何批：其人存，則其政舉。識之
translation_en:
…acting on his own judgment, he will be unable to empty his mind and examine what is right in the opinions of others. If he has grown accustomed to weakness and timidity, he will be unable to act decisively to dispel the confusion of frivolous discussion. If his vision is confined to what is near and petty, he will lack the clarity to illuminate hidden circumstances. What he insists is the intention of antiquity will then spring from his own individual views, rather than from the authentic intentions of the ancient emperors and kings. In adhering to established precedents, he will inevitably lapse into indolence; in altering laws and institutions, he will inevitably lapse into incessant changes. Even with exceptional abilities and a determination to act, he will ultimately fall into Emperor Wen of Han’s modest deference and failure to find time to act, or Emperor Shenzong of Song’s partial trust and unilateral decisions. Can one fail to guard against this?
Thus a ruler must study the investigation of things and extension of knowledge to understand the principles of the world, and must work at making his intentions sincere and rectifying his mind to put those principles into practice. Only then can he understand the intentions of the ancient emperors and kings, and only then can one speak of attaining the flourishing rule of the Three Dynasties and establishing enduring policies for ten thousand generations. This, too, is an intention that you, honored examiners, have left unexpressed. I respectfully submit my reply.
Fifth Question
Pan Zhongcan 潘仲驂
Comment by Associate Examiner Ma, Instructor: Ensuring sufficient food and sufficient troops is a major concern of state government. You can make appropriate arrangements for both, showing the resolve to take thought for troubles before others do; your language, too, adequately expresses this resolve. Compared with your other policy essays, all are excellent. Recording this one is like tasting a single morsel from the cauldron.
Comment by Examiner He, Professor: “When the right men are present, their government is put into effect.” Recognize this [?] …

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
弊何患焉此文盡之
考試官敎授高批是識時務者
對財猶水也水勢易渙以蓄之而爲利兵
猶火也火勢易焠以煽之而爲明夫亦因
其勢而利導之非有求於水火之外者也
明此則可與論救弊之理不必求新於常
法之外苦用力於其法之所無而更張之
唯於常法之所有者順遂而整齊之則因
地之利可以足國因人之力可以足兵執
===
事愛民體國之心可無終慮矣何則海育
地產財賦充饒浙固東南之富區也乃今
一遇水旱輒議勸借夫勸借之法亦黃香
之不得已於漢者耳追呼之苦倍于徵需
濡沫之利豈堪賑貸毋亦有因其勢而順
導之者乎蓋浙之民浮而侈夫其道之以
質乎專逐末者驅之於田畝尚奢侈者敎
之以節儉而又以身先之痛加抑損力爲
節制用民之財若取諸家用民之力若出
punctuated:
弊何患焉？此文盡之。

考試官敎授高批：是識時務者。

對：財猶水也，水勢易渙，以蓄之而爲利；兵猶火也，火勢易焠，以煽之而爲明。夫亦因其勢而利導之，非有求於水火之外者也。明此，則可與論救弊之理，不必求新於常法之外，苦用力於其法之所無而更張之。唯於常法之所有者順遂而整齊之，則因地之利可以足國，因人之力可以足兵，執事愛民體國之心可無終慮矣。何則？海育地產，財賦充饒，浙固東南之富區也。乃今一遇水旱，輒議勸借。夫勸借之法，亦黃香之不得已於漢者耳。追呼之苦倍于徵需，濡沫之利豈堪賑貸？毋亦有因其勢而順導之者乎？蓋浙之民浮而侈，夫其道之以質乎？專逐末者驅之於田畝，尚奢侈者敎之以節儉，而又以身先之，痛加抑損，力爲節制。用民之財若取諸家，用民之力若出
translation_en:
…what need be feared of abuses? This essay treats the matter fully.

Examiner Gao, Prefectural Confucian School Instructor, comments: This is someone who understands the needs of the times.

In reply: Wealth resembles water: water readily disperses, but storing it makes it beneficial. Military forces resemble fire: fire readily scorches [?], but fanning it makes it bright. This is simply a matter of guiding their inherent tendencies to beneficial ends, without seeking anything beyond water and fire themselves. Once this is understood, one can discuss the principles of remedying abuses. There is no need to seek innovations beyond established methods, laboriously pursuing what those methods do not contain and altering the system accordingly. Simply facilitate and put in order what established methods already provide. Then the advantages of the land can supply the state adequately, and the strength of the people can adequately sustain its forces. You, sir, with your concern for the people and devotion to the state, need no longer remain anxious. Why is this so? The sea nurtures and the land produces; wealth and tax revenues are abundant. Zhejiang has always been a wealthy region of the southeast. Yet nowadays, whenever flood or drought strikes, proposals immediately arise to solicit loans. Soliciting loans was itself only a last resort for Huang Xiang under the Han. The hardship of pursuing and summoning contributors is twice that of ordinary fiscal exactions. How could such meager assistance suffice for relief grants and loans? Might there not instead be a way to guide existing tendencies in a favorable direction?

The people of Zhejiang are frivolous and extravagant. Should they not be guided toward simplicity? Those devoted exclusively to secondary occupations should be directed into the fields; those who prize extravagance should be taught frugality. Moreover, officials should lead by personal example, drastically curtailing expenditure and vigorously exercising restraint. Use the people's wealth as though taking it from your own household; use the people's labor as though it came from …

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
諸身所謂冗役冗費凡可以蠹吾財者皆
盡去而不靳又必於預備倉之法而廣之
如李悝之平糴熟則斂之於官饑則散之
於民耿壽昌之常平賤則增價以糴貴則
減價以糶隨處可設也若然則民財可阜
倉廩可實有備無患而勸借之議容可免
矣枕山臂江果悍自負浙固東南之巨鎮
也乃今一遇有警輒稱招募夫招募之法
亦韓愈之不得已於唐者耳供給勞費倍
===
于養兵經歷騷擾比諸剽掠毋亦有因其
法而整齊之者乎蓋浙之兵惰而驕夫其
整之以經乎壯者在伍毋役以私富者在
行毋縱以賄而又必身先之甲胄與同甘
苦與同月給之餉無後其時日練以法無
惰其力而其為商為賈凡所以荒武事者
皆痛懲而必革又必合吾民兵而教之如
吳子所謂一人教十人十人教百人百人
教千人千人教萬人孫子所謂教目知形
punctuated:
諸身。所謂冗役冗費，凡可以蠹吾財者，皆盡去而不靳。又必於預備倉之法而廣之，如李悝之平糴，熟則斂之於官，饑則散之於民；耿壽昌之常平，賤則增價以糴，貴則減價以糶，隨處可設也。若然，則民財可阜，倉廩可實，有備無患，而勸借之議容可免矣。
枕山臂江，果悍自負，浙固東南之巨鎮也。乃今一遇有警，輒稱招募。夫招募之法，亦韓愈之不得已於唐者耳。供給勞費，倍于養兵；經歷騷擾，比諸剽掠。毋亦有因其法而整齊之者乎？蓋浙之兵惰而驕，夫其整之以經乎？壯者在伍，毋役以私；富者在行，毋縱以賄。而又必身先之，甲胄與同，甘苦與同。月給之餉，無後其時；日練以法，無惰其力。而其為商為賈，凡所以荒武事者，皆痛懲而必革。又必合吾民兵而教之，如吳子所謂一人教十人，十人教百人，百人教千人，千人教萬人；孫子所謂教目知形
translation_en:
…from one’s own person. All the redundant services and expenses that drain our resources must be eliminated without hesitation. Moreover, the system of reserve granaries must be expanded. There is Li Kui’s equitable grain-purchasing system: in plentiful years, grain is collected by the authorities; in famine years, it is distributed to the people. There is also Geng Shouchang’s ever-normal granary system: when grain is cheap, the purchasing price is raised; when it is dear, the selling price is lowered. These arrangements can be established everywhere. In this way, the people’s wealth can increase and the granaries can be filled. With preparations made, calamity need not be feared, and proposals to solicit loans from the people may be avoided.
With mountains at its back and rivers at its flanks, bold and fierce in its self-confidence, Zhejiang is indeed a great stronghold of the southeast. Yet nowadays, whenever an alarm arises, there is immediately talk of recruiting troops. Recruitment was merely an expedient to which Han Yu was compelled to resort under the Tang. The labor and expense of supplying recruits are twice those of maintaining regular troops, while the disturbances they cause wherever they pass are comparable to plundering. Might there not be a way to restore order by working through the existing military system? Zhejiang’s soldiers are indolent and arrogant: should they not be brought into order through established rules? Keep the able-bodied in the ranks; do not employ them on private errands. Keep the wealthy in the files; do not let them evade service through bribes. Those in command must also lead by personal example, sharing the wearing of armor and helmets, and sharing hardships and comforts. Monthly pay must not be late; daily training must follow prescribed methods, with no slackening of effort. Their engagement in trade, and everything else that causes military duties to be neglected, must be severely punished and decisively reformed. Moreover, our militia must be assembled and trained, as Master Wu says: ‘One man trains ten, ten train a hundred, a hundred train a thousand, and a thousand train ten thousand’; and as Master Sun says, train the eyes to recognize shapes…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
色之旗敎耳知號令之數敎足知進退之
度敎手知長短之兵敎心知賞罰之用者
無日可廢也若然則習熟藝精志定氣飽
有備無患而招募之議容可免矣乃若鹽
徒起於商販海寇起於番舶皆以死覓利
愈撲而不可滅者也漢人牢盆之法旣不
足以盡其奸則整齊之不可以已也何則
鹽法之弊所禁不在於鹽徒當在於竈戶
鹽徒之禁又不當在於所治當在於他方
===
故在所治則當盡弛挑負之禁凡欲市者
皆給之引輕其直以抵引報之數其在竈
戶當嚴私賣之法凡欲市於人者皆驗之
引時其直以為竈戶之利捕鹽徒兵不必
獲挑負之鹽徒特令查私賣之竈戶仍令
出鹽地方一切居民得互相舉發有私賣
者治以重典則他方鹽徒入吾境已無可
市之鹽出其境又有盤獲之禁無利可趨
有害可畏自將歸干故土以業生矣若海
punctuated:
色之旗，敎耳知號令之數，敎足知進退之度，敎手知長短之兵，敎心知賞罰之用者，無日可廢也。若然，則習熟藝精，志定氣飽，有備無患，而招募之議容可免矣。
乃若鹽徒起於商販，海寇起於番舶，皆以死覓利，愈撲而不可滅者也。漢人牢盆之法旣不足以盡其奸，則整齊之不可以已也。何則？鹽法之弊，所禁不在於鹽徒，當在於竈戶；鹽徒之禁，又不當在於所治，當在於他方。故在所治，則當盡弛挑負之禁，凡欲市者，皆給之引，輕其直，以抵引報之數。其在竈戶，當嚴私賣之法，凡欲市於人者，皆驗之引，時其直，以為竈戶之利。捕鹽徒兵，不必獲挑負之鹽徒，特令查私賣之竈戶，仍令出鹽地方一切居民得互相舉發。有私賣者，治以重典，則他方鹽徒入吾境，已無可市之鹽；出其境，又有盤獲之禁。無利可趨，有害可畏，自將歸干故土以業生矣。若海
translation_en:
…the colors of flags; teach the ears to recognize the patterns of commands, the feet to know the proper measures of advance and retreat, the hands to know long and short weapons, and the mind to understand the application of rewards and punishments. Such training must not be neglected for a single day. If this is done, practice will become familiar and skills refined, resolve will be firm and morale full. With preparation, there will be no cause for anxiety, and proposals for recruiting additional troops may be dispensed with.
As for illicit salt dealers, they arise from commercial trafficking, while maritime raiders arise from foreign shipping. All risk death in pursuit of profit; however vigorously they are suppressed, they cannot be eradicated. Since even the Han system of salt-boiling pans was insufficient to put an end to all their fraud, efforts to regulate them must not cease. Why is this? To remedy abuses in the salt administration, restrictions should target the salt-producing households, rather than the illicit dealers. Restrictions on the dealers themselves should be enforced elsewhere, rather than within the jurisdiction under one's administration.
Within that jurisdiction, therefore, all prohibitions on carrying salt should be relaxed. Everyone wishing to buy it should receive a salt certificate, and its price should be reduced to meet the quantities reported under the certificates [?]. As for the salt-producing households, the laws against private sales should be strictly enforced. Whenever they wish to sell to someone, the buyer's certificate should be checked, and the price adjusted according to the season [?], so as to benefit the producing households. Soldiers charged with apprehending illicit salt dealers need not seize those carrying salt; they should simply be ordered to investigate producing households that sell privately. All inhabitants of salt-producing areas should also be allowed to report one another's violations. Those making private sales should be punished under severe statutes. Then illicit salt dealers from elsewhere, upon entering our territory, will find no salt available for them to buy; on leaving it, they will also face inspection and apprehension under the prohibitions. With no profit to pursue and harm to fear, they will naturally return to their native places [?] to earn their livelihoods. As for maritime…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
冦弗靖則武職之罪也泊蒙衝于近地拍
威望不著老弱守舟而巡警不嚴又有陽
爲詰捕而陰受其賂者是以海冦時生無
所忌畏使船皆在鎭軍皆在船又時習水
戰以示之威時出遊䑲而警之備則何萑
澤之弗靖哉乃若小民稱貸起於饑寒地
利未獲由之兼併皆忍死求生欲已而不
能自己者宋人青苗之法既不可行之於
官則利導之不可以已也何則民窮之弊
===
在官居其十九富豪居其十一法外徴求
剥膚椎髓則其勢不得不稱貸而輸之官
非時之役勞筋苦骨而其力不得以自盡
於南畝終歳勤動少有所獲則追呼之吏
峻其科所貸之家索其息則又哀呼求假
於富豪之前矣負息既多勢必有訟大吏
則臨之刑威而責償旦夕小吏則受人賄
賂而淹禁逾年二者相因展轉交害如之
何民不窮且盜也則民財就盡非長吏之
punctuated: 冦弗靖，則武職之罪也。泊蒙衝于近地，拍威望不著，老弱守舟，而巡警不嚴，又有陽爲詰捕而陰受其賂者，是以海冦時生，無所忌畏。使船皆在鎭，軍皆在船，又時習水戰以示之威，時出遊䑲而警之備，則何萑澤之弗靖哉？乃若小民稱貸起於饑寒，地利未獲由之兼併，皆忍死求生，欲已而不能自己者。宋人青苗之法既不可行之於官，則利導之不可以已也。何則？民窮之弊，在官居其十九，富豪居其十一。法外徴求，剥膚椎髓，則其勢不得不稱貸而輸之官；非時之役，勞筋苦骨，而其力不得以自盡於南畝。終歳勤動，少有所獲，則追呼之吏峻其科，所貸之家索其息，則又哀呼求假於富豪之前矣。負息既多，勢必有訟。大吏則臨之刑威，而責償旦夕；小吏則受人賄賂，而淹禁逾年。二者相因，展轉交害，如之何民不窮且盜也？則民財就盡，非長吏之
translation_en:
…if the pirates are not quelled, the fault lies with the military officers. They moor their assault ships nearby, yet their authority inspires no awe [?]; the old and weak guard the vessels, and patrols are lax. There are also those who outwardly investigate and arrest the pirates while secretly accepting their bribes. Thus maritime pirates continually arise, with nothing to fear. If all ships were stationed at their garrisons and all troops aboard their ships, if they regularly practiced naval warfare to display their might and regularly sent out patrol boats to keep their defenses alert, how could these bands of brigands remain unquelled?
As for the common people, their borrowing arises from hunger and cold; their failure to reap the benefits of the land stems from its engrossment by the wealthy. They all endure the threat of death in their struggle to survive, wishing to stop borrowing but unable to do so. Since the Green Sprouts system of the Song cannot be implemented by the authorities, efforts to guide the people toward their own advantage must not cease. Why is this? Of the abuses that impoverish the people, officials account for nine-tenths and the rich and powerful for one-tenth. Exactions beyond the law strip their skin and pound their marrow, leaving them no choice but to borrow in order to pay the authorities. Untimely labor service exhausts their sinews and torments their bones, preventing them from devoting their full strength to their fields. After toiling throughout the year, if they obtain even a small yield, the clerks pursuing payment press their assessments harshly, while the households from which they borrowed demand interest. They must therefore once again cry pitifully before the rich and powerful, begging for loans.
Once their accumulated interest debts become large, lawsuits inevitably follow. Senior officials confront them with the threat of punishment and demand repayment within a day; petty clerks accept bribes and keep them imprisoned for more than a year. These two practices reinforce one another, inflicting harm in an ever-repeating cycle. How could the people fail to become impoverished and turn to banditry? If the people's resources are thus nearly exhausted, is this not the responsibility of the chief local officials…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
責乎必於山鄉水區凡可以厚其生者與
之無禁使得以盡自然之利賦稅徭役凡
所以需于上者徵之以時使得以受一分
之賜事為之制曲為之防無名征求一切
可罷也貪暴多取悉力與裁也則又何民
瘼之弗蘇哉是故財以裕民非推所有以
與之也兵以止盜非取諸外以昌之也民
自有財導之則源開國自有兵整之則威
振特患濟之者之無其人耳有其人矣或
===
病於職業之弗專有其職矣又病於遷徙
之無常或以議論之不一或以奉行之弗
稱是以法久弊生財殫兵弱以至於此苟
忠患公清上下皆有其人節制奉行上下
皆一其心相與利導而整齊之則兵寓于
農緩急得有所賴富藏于民水旱不能為
災此其可行之道固不在遠也未識以為
何如
punctuated: 責乎？必於山鄉水區，凡可以厚其生者，與之無禁，使得以盡自然之利；賦稅徭役，凡所以需于上者，徵之以時，使得以受一分之賜。事為之制，曲為之防，無名征求，一切可罷也；貪暴多取，悉力與裁也。則又何民瘼之弗蘇哉？是故財以裕民，非推所有以與之也；兵以止盜，非取諸外以昌之也。民自有財，導之則源開；國自有兵，整之則威振。特患濟之者之無其人耳。有其人矣，或病於職業之弗專；有其職矣，又病於遷徙之無常；或以議論之不一，或以奉行之弗稱。是以法久弊生，財殫兵弱，以至於此。苟忠患公清，上下皆有其人；節制奉行，上下皆一其心，相與利導而整齊之，則兵寓于農，緩急得有所賴；富藏于民，水旱不能為災。此其可行之道，固不在遠也。未識以為何如？
translation_en:
…responsibility? In mountain villages and waterside districts, whatever can enrich the people's livelihood must be made available to them without restriction, so that they may fully enjoy nature's benefits. Taxes and labor services—everything required by those above—should be exacted at the proper times, allowing the people to receive some measure of relief. Establish regulations for each matter and safeguards for every contingency. All exactions without legitimate grounds can be abolished; every effort should be made to curb the excessive demands of greedy and violent officials. What suffering among the people would then remain unrelieved?

Thus, using wealth to enrich the people does not mean handing over one's own possessions to them; using troops to suppress bandits does not mean drawing resources from outside to strengthen the forces. The people already have resources: guide their use, and the sources of wealth will open. The state already has troops: put them in order, and their might will be renewed. The only concern is the absence of suitable men to carry this out. Even when suitable men are available, their duties may not be sufficiently focused; even when they hold the appropriate posts, they may suffer from unpredictable transfers. Sometimes deliberations lack agreement; sometimes implementation falls short. Thus, as institutions endure, abuses arise, resources are exhausted, and military strength declines, bringing us to the present situation.

If loyal, conscientious [?], impartial, and incorruptible men could be found at every level, and if those above and below were united in directing and implementing these measures, together guiding resources to beneficial use and bringing matters into order, then troops would be embedded among the farming population, providing a dependable force whenever needed. Wealth would be stored among the people, and floods and droughts could not bring disaster. The practicable way to achieve this is surely not far to seek. I wonder what you think of this?

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
浙江鄉試錄後序
嘉靖甲午八月癸亥浙江鄉
試錄成故事元述宜有言以
勗多士曰夫士幸而生
聖明之世又幸以其藝升於有司
將進而立於
天子之廷以其氏名與其文詞梓
===
而爲錄將登諸
天府傳示海內及於無窮若爾多
士今日之事其可謂至榮也
已雖然人榮之則必有以責
之責之而不副則必罪且尤
之是故其升於有司進而立
於
punctuated:
浙江鄉試錄後序

嘉靖甲午八月癸亥，浙江鄉試錄成。故事，元述宜有言以勗多士，曰：「夫士幸而生聖明之世，又幸以其藝升於有司，將進而立於天子之廷，以其氏名與其文詞梓而爲錄，將登諸天府，傳示海內，及於無窮。若爾多士今日之事，其可謂至榮也已！雖然，人榮之，則必有以責之；責之而不副，則必罪且尤之。是故其升於有司，進而立於
translation_en:
Postface to the Zhejiang Provincial Examination Record

On the guihai day of the eighth month of the jiawu year of the Jiajing reign [1534], the Zhejiang Provincial Examination Record was completed. Following precedent, I, Yuan Shu, ought to offer some words to encourage the assembled scholars. I say: “A scholar is fortunate to be born in an age of sagely and enlightened rule, and fortunate again to be selected by the responsible officials for his literary accomplishments. He will advance to stand at the court of the Son of Heaven. His name and writings are printed from woodblocks to form a record, which will be deposited in the imperial archives, circulated throughout the realm, and transmitted for all time. What has happened today to you assembled scholars may indeed be called the highest honor!

“Nevertheless, when people honor someone, they necessarily make demands upon him. If he fails to meet those demands, they will surely condemn and blame him. Thus, when he is selected by the responsible officials and advances to stand at …

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
天子之廷也善固藉以顯而惡亦
因之以彰其梓而為錄登諸
天府傳示廣遠也善固資之有聞
而惡亦無以自覆然則夫人
之所謂榮乃吾所深懼者也
爾多士亦嘗思所以居其榮
者乎古稱太上有立德其次
===
有立功其次有立言三者謂
之不朽
國家之制每三歲一舉士每舉
合海内之衆蓋千餘人至考
其所終有能具是三者寡矣
夫然吾未見榮之能居也而
况反道敗德自速戾以負於
punctuated:
天子之廷也，善固藉以顯，而惡亦因之以彰。其梓而為錄，登諸天府，傳示廣遠也，善固資之有聞，而惡亦無以自覆。然則夫人之所謂榮，乃吾所深懼者也。爾多士亦嘗思所以居其榮者乎？古稱太上有立德，其次有立功，其次有立言，三者謂之不朽。
國家之制，每三歲一舉士，每舉合海内之衆，蓋千餘人。至考其所終，有能具是三者寡矣。夫然，吾未見榮之能居也，而况反道敗德，自速戾，以負於
translation_en:
…at the Son of Heaven’s court, their goodness is indeed brought to light, but their wickedness is likewise exposed. When their names and writings are printed in a record, deposited in the imperial archives, and circulated far and wide, their goodness thereby becomes known, but neither can their wickedness remain concealed. Thus what others call an honor is precisely what I deeply fear. Have you, assembled scholars, ever considered how to prove worthy of this honor? As the ancients said, the highest achievement is to establish virtue; next is to establish meritorious deeds; next is to establish enduring words. These three are called imperishable.
Under the institutions of our state, scholars are selected once every three years. Each selection brings together more than a thousand men from throughout the realm. Yet when we examine what they ultimately achieve, few have been able to attain all three of these. Such being the case, I have yet to see that they can prove worthy of their honor. How much less can those who turn against the Way, corrupt their virtue, and bring guilt upon themselves, thereby failing…

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
聖明者歟爾多士勉之毋溺於榮
知以爲懼焉可也夫浙天下
首藩也
聖天子在上豈弟作人觀文成化
浙之漸被尤深士養於庠序
旣充然有所蘊乃試之日監
臨御史于立朝夕儆于簾內
===
外之吏惟公惟愼以仰副
聖天子側席求賢之心爾多士又
皆選而拔其尤固足以居其
榮而無慊者元述獨慮夫志
之怠也故有以勗多士其尚
毋以予言爲贅也哉遂次其
說書諸末簡
punctuated: 聖明者歟？爾多士勉之，毋溺於榮，知以爲懼焉可也。夫浙，天下首藩也。聖天子在上，豈弟作人，觀文成化，浙之漸被尤深。士養於庠序，旣充然有所蘊，乃試之日，監臨御史于立朝夕儆于簾內外之吏，惟公惟愼，以仰副聖天子側席求賢之心。爾多士又皆選而拔其尤，固足以居其榮而無慊者。元述獨慮夫志之怠也，故有以勗多士，其尚毋以予言爲贅也哉！遂次其說，書諸末簡。
translation_en:
…the sagely and enlightened sovereign? You scholars must exert yourselves. Do not become absorbed in honor; recognize in it a reason for apprehension. That will suffice.

Zhejiang is the foremost province under Heaven. Our sagely Son of Heaven reigns above, nurturing men of talent with gracious benevolence and bringing about transformation through the cultivation of culture. Zhejiang has been especially deeply imbued with his influence. Its scholars, nurtured in the schools, have already accumulated substantial learning. When the examination took place, Censor Yu Li, the Supervising Official, admonished the officials within and outside the examination curtain morning and evening to be impartial and circumspect, thus answering the sagely Son of Heaven’s earnest desire to seek worthy men—a desire that keeps him from sitting at ease. You scholars have all been selected as the outstanding among your peers, and certainly deserve to enjoy this honor without misgiving. I, Yuanshu, fear only that your resolve may slacken. Therefore I offer these exhortations to you scholars. May you not regard my words as superfluous! I have accordingly set these remarks in order and written them on the final leaves.

title: 嘉靖十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
廣東惠州府儒學敎授何〔元〕
〔述〕謹序
